name: Agudo
title: Agudo Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The gorge's only beast-taming marksman, fighting alongside befriended monsters. Mount-and-split mechanics and a CC-blocking roll give her durability few other marksmen have.
playstyle: The gorge's only beast-taming marksman, fighting alongside befriended monsters. Mount-and-split mechanics and a CC-blocking roll give her durability few other marksmen have.
bestFor: players drawn to heroes outside the textbook: a marksman who stands in the middle of the fight, deciding on every engage whether Furball carries her or gets thrown.

tips.earlyGame: Agudo is a jungle marksman whose Passive lets her vacuum camps at a speed few junglers match. Take both buffs, race to level 4, and keep collecting the seed mines your basic attacks drop to maintain the attack and movement speed stacks (max 6). Skill 2's roll negates one hard crowd control effect, so even a face-check against the enemy jungler leaves you one free escape. Her early dueling is average, though — if an invade is coming, just call teammates. When you gank, pick lanes with walls where the bounce stun can actually land.
tips.midGame: The 4-minute Tyrant is where Agudo shines brightest. Drop Skill 1's paradise to boost your own and your companion monsters' attack and movement speed by 15%, and the pack melts the objective before a contest can even form. Mid-game skirmishes also start with Skill 1: a zone of healing and speed turns even-numbered fights lopsided. The Ultimate throws Pom-Pom for a ranged area stun, but your body is fragile once the throw is out, so only light the fuse on a brawl when your frontline is actually there.
tips.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, where you throw Pom-Pom decides the result. Toss the Ultimate at the enemy marksman's or mage's feet for the stun, let the detached Pom-Pom maul them, and run a second front with your own basic attacks from the very back. Recast to recall Pom-Pom when the damage piles up. After the throw, your body is a plucked bird — check your escape wall and your teammates' positions before committing it. If Pom-Pom dies, half your power is gone until it recovers, so skip the solo side-lane pushes and keep shooting from under your team's umbrella.
tips.teamfight: Your teamfight starts before the fight: sow Skill 1's field where the fight is going to happen. The 15% Attack Speed and Movement Speed and the healing land on Agudo and her animal companions only — allied heroes get nothing from it. The companions that gather there still stand in front of the enemy, so the extra bodies translate straight into board pressure. When the enemy engages, roll with Skill 2 to negate one hard crowd control while you reposition, and bounce off a wall to answer with the empowered basic attack's triple seed-mine burst. Save Skill 3's Pom-Pom toss as the finisher for the moment an enemy backliner ends up isolated. Between her summons and her own attacks she covers a wide front, so the longer a face-to-face fight drags on, the further it tilts toward Agudo.

strengths: Companion summons plus Skill 1's buffs create numbers and board pressure
Skill 2 negates one hard crowd control and stuns off walls — great in attack or defense
The Ultimate's Pom-Pom toss is a ranged area stun you can throw from safety
Seed-mine stacks and the Passive make her jungle clear exceptionally fast
weaknesses: The body is an assassin magnet while Pom-Pom is detached
Losing Pom-Pom guts her power until it finishes recovering
Before summons and stacks come online, her early dueling is merely average

counteredBy.name: Han Xin
counteredBy.reason: Han Xin still holds a second leap once Agudo has spent her only roll, leaving her no way out.

counteredBy.name: Lam
counteredBy.reason: Lam's Death From Below drags Agudo in, and once she is low the Prey mark adds true damage.

synergies.name: Dr Bian
synergies.reason: Dr Bian's poison pool slows whoever stands in it, so Agudo's Tumble, Furball! is much harder to dodge.

synergies.name: Zhang Fei
synergies.reason: Zhang Fei's shield covers Agudo, so she can stay on the front line and keep landing Basic Attacks.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Stacked crit for bigger hits
builds.condition: When the enemy has one frontliner at most and you want their backline down fast.
builds.notes: Shadow Ripper third and Eternity Blade fourth put 40% crit rate up early. Eternity Blade turns every 2% crit rate into 1% more critical damage, so the earlier Agudo stacks rate, the harder each hit lands. Bloodweeper fifth adds 25% physical lifesteal and +500 max HP, and Daybreaker's Virtue with its penetration comes sixth. Gear and arcana finish at 71% crit rate and +419 physical attack, 135 more than build 2.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: HP and defense to keep firing
builds.condition: When the draft puts two or more high-HP frontliners on the enemy team.
builds.notes: Deepfrost Siege third and Doomsday fourth stack bonus basic-attack damage together with max HP. Doomsday's extra hit scales with 7% of the target's bonus HP, so the more health a frontliner carries, the more it strips away. Daybreaker's Virtue moves up to fifth at 9,570G for earlier penetration, and Ominous Premonition closes with +300 physical defense and +1200 max HP. Totals of +105% attack speed and +2450 max HP let Agudo hold a more forward position than build 1 and keep firing.

name: Alessio
title: Alessio Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A sky-pirate marksman with splash cannonballs and a smoke screen that cloaks his whole team. His aerial missile ultimate executes one named target — carry, trickster, and support in one hat.
playstyle: A sky-pirate marksman with splash cannonballs and a smoke screen that cloaks his whole team. His aerial missile ultimate executes one named target — carry, trickster, and support in one hat.
bestFor: players bored of orthodox shootouts: grounded shells get body-blocked, so the smoke bomb and the flight window are how the damage reaches the backline.

tips.earlyGame: Head to the farm lane and aim to have level 4 plus your first attack item before the Tyrant fight at 4:00. Your Passive shells deal splash damage plus bonus damage equal to 0.5% of the target's max Health at level 1, so simply angling shots to clip the enemy marksman through the minion wave wins you trades. The catch: grounded basic attacks can be blocked by enemy heroes, so when their frontline wedges itself in between, take the farm instead. When things get dicey, reach for Skill 2. The smoke cloud stealths you and nearby allies for 3.5 seconds, and the blast carries you airborne — a burst of Movement Speed for 0.8s plus free passage over terrain is enough to break away.
tips.midGame: Between 8 and 10 minutes, with your crit core online, you become the centerpiece of every fight. When rotating to objectives, drop Skill 2's smoke (3.5 seconds of stealth) over your team and the whole rotation vanishes off the enemy's screen — ambushes practically set themselves up. In fights, save Skill 1's three enhanced shells for the moment enemies clump: the bigger splash plus 1% max HP bonus shreds groups. That smoke is your lifeline for both attack and escape, so never burn it just to walk somewhere faster.
tips.lateGame: By the late game you are the fire source the enemy most wants gone, which is exactly why you stand one step behind your frontline at all times. When someone dives you, Skill 2 into the air and cast your Ultimate while airborne: five missiles rain down under crowd control immunity, each adding 6% of the target's missing HP as bonus damage — as a finisher on softened targets, it's as reliable as they come. Another enemy hero can soak exactly one missile for the target, so the moment your mark stands alone is the moment you fire.
tips.teamfight: Open from behind your frontline, farming splash damage onto the clump with enhanced shells, and only step up once the enemy's engage tools are spent. If you're already airborne from the Ultimate, recasting Skill 2 in the air trades the smoke for unblockable basic attacks — you shoot straight past the frontline into their carries. Stack missiles onto anything escaping low. Here's a positioning habit worth stealing: place the smoke half a step behind you rather than at your feet, so you vanish right in front of the assassin who just jumped in — the survival difference is night and day.

strengths: Splash basic attacks with max-HP scaling put real damage into tanks
Smoke stealth and airborne movement cover both self-peel and ambushes
Airborne shots ignore body-blocking and reach the enemy backline directly
Missing-HP scaling on the Ultimate reliably finishes softened targets
weaknesses: With Skill 2 and the Ultimate down he has no escape and melts on the ground
Grounded basic attacks get body-blocked by the enemy frontline
Another enemy can soak one Ultimate missile, blunting it in brawls
The airborne game plan is punished hard by lock-on skills and anti-air CC

counteredBy.name: Li Bai
counteredBy.reason: Li Bai cannot be targeted during his ultimate, so Alessio's attacks find nothing at all.

counteredBy.name: Lady Sun
counteredBy.reason: Lady Sun's Frag Grenade slows Alessio hard, so her Ultimate Shell is far harder for him to dodge.

synergies.name: Yaria
synergies.reason: Yaria attaches and shields Alessio, so he can hold a forward position and keep firing.

synergies.name: Guiguzi
synergies.reason: Guiguzi pulls enemies into one stunned cluster, so Alessio's area shots hit the whole group at once.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Crit first, Doomsday last
builds.condition: When the enemy front line stacks high max HP
builds.notes: Shadow Ripper lands second and Eternity Blade third, so item crit rate hits 40% by 4,850G. Seven Calamity slots and three Unparalleled slots add +10.8% crit damage on top. Doomsday closes the build, adding 80-160 plus 7% of the target's bonus HP to every basic attack. Totals: 68.3% crit rate, 115% attack speed, 45% physical lifesteal and +17.5% movement speed.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Tempest second for early bulk
builds.condition: When you want to push the lane from the early game
builds.notes: Tempest goes second, so 2,780G already brings +600 max HP and 30% attack speed. Shadow Ripper and Eternity Blade each slide back a slot, so ten Calamity slots carry crit rate to 71%. Bloodweeper only lands at 11,500G, so five Reaver slots hold 8% physical lifesteal until then. Totals: 120% attack speed, 379 physical attack, +1,100 max HP.

name: Allain
title: Allain Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A swordsman who deals physical, magical, and true damage all at once — there is no right defense against him. Knock-up chains flow into an untargetable ultimate that resets the exchange.
playstyle: A swordsman who deals physical, magical, and true damage all at once — there is no right defense against him. Knock-up chains flow into an untargetable ultimate that resets the exchange.
bestFor: players who want an all-rounder that resists counter-building, and who like calling Skill 3 in the moment — chase the kill, or jump to an ally and shield them.

tips.earlyGame: Allain's first rule in the clash lane: never commit before your marks are stacked. Marks build from basic attacks and Ultimate hits, and at three stacks Skill 1 becomes a different move entirely — true damage, crowd control immunity, and a wide knock-up. Until level 4, build marks through short basic-attack exchanges, fire Skill 1, and step back without chasing. His Passive heal at full rage scales with missing HP — up to triple — so a slightly bruised Allain wins brawls that look even on paper.
tips.midGame: From about 10 minutes, once a lifesteal item finishes, Allain stops losing side-lane 1v1s. His Passive cuts item lifesteal to 75% of its effect, but in exchange it drains from his magical and true damage as well. Each basic attack lands one magical and one physical hit, with true damage added on every third — damage that would normally heal him for nothing now feeds the drain. The base pattern is split pushing to bait defenders, then running them down with Skill 2 dashes. Join teamfights late from a flank bush, and time Skill 3's 1.5-second untargetable window against the enemy's biggest skill to make it hit nothing but air.
tips.lateGame: Your late-game job is diving the enemy carry — but always on the counterpunch. Wait for enemy CC to land on your teammates, then close with Skill 2 and deliver basic attacks into a three-stack Skill 1. The Ultimate can finish a chase, but the play that wins late games is casting it on an ally the instant you're focused: you vanish for 1.5 seconds, share the landing shield, and reset the exchange. The one thing to never forget — the moment marks and rage lapse, Allain turns abruptly soft.
tips.teamfight: Pick the single most dangerous enemy and refuse to leave them alone. Skill 2 holds two charges, so spend the first to close and the second to cut off the escape route. Three basic attacks into Skill 1 pushes through most interrupts thanks to crowd control immunity, lifting everyone around the target. Because rage grants penetration and damage reduction as it builds, Allain is at his strongest in a fight's second half — surviving the opening volley is the entire job description.

strengths: Physical, magic, and true damage; no defensive build blanks him
Lifesteal runs at 75% effect but drains from his magical and true damage too
Three-stack Skill 1 is a wide-area knock-up with crowd control immunity
One Skill 3 covers chasing, dodging, and shielding an ally
weaknesses: His real damage only arrives once marks and rage are stacked
Chained slows and kiting starve his stacks and his healing
Basic attacks apply item effects at only 60%, demanding build knowledge
Mobility lives on Skill 2; with charges spent he can't chase or run

counteredBy.name: Donghuang
counteredBy.reason: Donghuang's Forsaken Contract suppresses Allain outright, cutting off his attack chain and the Fury it builds.

synergies.name: Lam
synergies.reason: Lam drags enemies into one spot, and Death at Sunset hits harder the closer they are.

synergies.name: Yaria
synergies.reason: Yaria attaches to Allain with a shield and stays untargetable, following him straight through his dashes.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Attack speed first, shield for CC
builds.condition: When the enemy team is loaded with hard CC and you want early attack speed to push the lane.
builds.notes: Sparkforged Dagger goes second, so +35% attack speed and +7.5% movement speed are online at 2,740 gold. Every third basic attack arcs for 160-400 magic damage, which speeds up lane pressure. Frigid Charge in the fifth slot answers any hard CC other than suppression with a shield worth 10% of Allain's max health, once every 15 seconds. Cooldown reduction totals 13.5%, and the finished build reads +603 physical defense and +5,487 max health.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Defense first, damage last
builds.condition: When enemy physical damage is heavy and the clash lane chips you down early.
builds.notes: Blazing Cape goes second here, locking in +1,100 max health plus +150 physical defense and +150 magic defense by 2,740 gold. Its 375-range burn cuts enemy health recovery and lifesteal by 35%, so drawn-out trades tilt Allain's way. Cuirass of Savagery closes the build at +663 physical defense and +166 physical attack, 60 and 35 above the other list. Every hit taken stacks up to 10 times for extra damage dealt and movement speed.

name: Angela
title: Angela Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A turret mage whose burn stacks make every follow-up hit harder, finished by a steerable beam that chases runners down. Point her at the fight and she is the damage plan.
playstyle: A turret mage whose burn stacks make every follow-up hit harder, finished by a steerable beam that chases runners down. Point her at the fight and she is the damage plan.
bestFor: pure damage duty, with no complicated kit attached. Every skill is a skillshot, so learn to lead a strafing target — after that, the team's damage plan is simply you.

tips.earlyGame: Start Skill 1 in the mid lane. All five fireballs deal full damage to non-heroes, giving Angela some of the fastest waveclear in the game — prioritize the clear until level 4 and spend leftover fireballs poking your opponent. Skill 2's 1-second stun is your lifeline, but the projectile is straightforward and easy to read; throwing it early and missing turns you into a free target, so only aim it when the enemy stops to last-hit. Your Passive stacks burn and movement speed as skills land, so keep the output flowing.
tips.midGame: From around 7 minutes with Savant's Wrath complete, almost anyone hit by Skill 2 is coming home with you. Shove mid, show yourself along the river, and time Skill 2 with your jungler's ganks. At Tyrant fights, the fire vortex's damage-over-time and slow let you seal off chokepoints, so you have a job even when you'd rather not take a straight shootout. Your Ultimate is your damage centerpiece, but you can only steer it while firing — while enemy blinks are unaccounted for, choose your starting position carefully.
tips.lateGame: Once Void Staff joins the build after 15 minutes, a full combo off Skill 2 evaporates everything short of a tank. But enemy assassins are also complete, so stand diagonally behind your frontline at all times. Getting dove is actually your moment: the Ultimate grants an 850 shield with crowd control immunity, and dumping all twelve beam ticks point-blank means the assassin who came for a kill melts instead — the signature Angela experience. In the tight paths near Shadow Tyrant, pre-place Skill 2 to watch the entrance.
tips.teamfight: The single biggest teamfight rule: don't spend Skill 2 at the start. Hitting a frontliner wastes the stun into shields and armor. Wait until the enemy divers jump onto your allies, then land it on their stalled backline or the assassin coming for you. From the stun, chain a burn-stacked Skill 1 and the Ultimate — nothing non-durable survives the sequence. The beam can be cancelled 0.5 seconds after it starts, so build the habit of cutting it the moment your target drops and saving the rest for the next exchange.

strengths: One landed Skill 2 stun lets her solo-delete an enemy backliner
Ultimate's shield and crowd control immunity let her finish the beam uninterrupted
Passive burn stacks make consecutive skill hits snowball her damage
Five-projectile Skill 1 gives extremely fast waveclear
weaknesses: Every skill is a skillshot — strafing enemies are hard to hit
No blink, so self-defense is paper-thin right after Skill 2 misses
The Ultimate only steers while firing; a bad starting position is fatal
Skill 1 fireballs decay after the first hit on a hero, so single-target damage is inconsistent

counteredBy.name: Han Xin
counteredBy.reason: Han Xin leaps in and launches Angela before she can even start firing, pinning her down.

counteredBy.name: Daji
counteredBy.reason: Daji stuns Angela, shreds her Magical Defense while she is held, and wins the trade outright.

synergies.name: Zhuangzi
synergies.reason: Zhuangzi's slow keeps enemies from escaping, so Angela's Chaos Cinder vortex keeps ticking on them.

synergies.name: Zhang Fei
synergies.reason: Zhang Fei's shield covers Angela as she steps up, letting her keep firing instead of retreating.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Reverberation and lifesteal
builds.condition: When you want to shove the lane early and still hold up in teamfights.
builds.notes: The Scepter of Reverberation lands second at 2,800G, adding a 140-280 + 28% magic attack blast on skill hits, once every 5 seconds. Fourth is the Insatiable Tome: 24% magic lifesteal, +750 max HP, plus 1% cooldown reduction for every 2% of that lifesteal. Void Staff comes fifth, so the 45% magic defense penetration is online by 9,040G. Totals come to +1182 magic attack, +1250 max HP and +17.5% movement speed.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Anti-heal with a safety net
builds.condition: When the enemy team leans on healing or lifesteal to stay alive.
builds.notes: Venomous Staff arrives second and cuts enemy healing and lifesteal by 35% for 2.5 seconds on every hit. Ardent Dominion follows fourth, clearing crowd control below 30% HP and granting a 4-second shield that also adds 30% movement speed (90s cooldown). Sage's Tome is bought fifth at 9,530G for the early +350 magic attack and 10% cooldown reduction, which leaves Void Staff's penetration for last. The build totals +22.5% cooldown reduction, +25% movement speed and +1192 magic attack.

name: Annette
title: Annette Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A support who literally cannot stand still — movement refunds her cooldowns. She accelerates allies through her circles, hands out shields, and her barrier ultimate bounces entire engages back.
playstyle: A support who literally cannot stand still — movement refunds her cooldowns. She accelerates allies through her circles, hands out shields, and her barrier ultimate bounces entire engages back.
bestFor: players who want to support at a sprint — movement itself refunds her cooldowns, and the orb's recoil has to be measured before it is fired.

tips.earlyGame: Shadow your marksman from the start and support the farm-lane scraps with Skill 2's orb. Hit an ally and it shields; hit an enemy and it damages; and you bounce backward on every cast — one aiming decision covers offense and defense at once. Before the 4-minute Tyrant, your job is tagging along on ganks: Skill 1's formation stacks slows on enemies who cross it and speeds up allies who do, a ready-made chase engine. Since the Passive refunds cooldowns and restores mana as you move, walking the river beats standing still in lane — Annette performs best in motion.
tips.midGame: Once your support item upgrade and cooldown boots are in, skirmishes start brewing around mid. Annette's spot is half a step ahead of her carry. The instant an enemy fighter telegraphs a dive, open Skill 3: every enemy inside the radius at that moment is knocked back. Anyone who walks into the barrier afterwards is not pushed away — they take damage and a 1.25-second stun instead. Teammates standing inside gain crowd control immunity. Because the knockback fires on cast, you can wait and watch their engage before committing. The trick of pushing your formation forward with the orb is also worth practicing for chipping enemies who hide under tower.
tips.lateGame: The late game is an exercise in patience: hold the Ultimate for the one enemy who decides fights. With your defensive capes stacked, you won't fall over even standing forward. The ideal sequence at a fight's entrance is Skill 1 first to control the ground, then catching the enemy assassin mid-leap with the barrier as they jump your marksman. While it's active you become untargetable but your move speed is halved, so opening in the wrong spot strands you away from your team while the fight is decided. Open it right beside the person you're protecting — no exceptions.
tips.teamfight: Stand next to your carry. The job is three tasks: lay Skill 1 across the enemy frontline's path to blunt the charge; thread Skill 2's orb through your most-focused teammate to keep shields flowing; and when the real dive arrives, meet it with the Ultimate — knockback, stun, and crowd control immunity for everyone inside. Keep that order and you'll tilt teamfights while dealing almost no damage yourself. The one hazard is the orb's recoil: bounce backward into a flanker and the story ends badly. Glance behind you before every cast — make it a reflex.

strengths: The Ultimate's knockback, stun, and crowd control immunity erase entire dives
Skill 2 is damage, shielding, and a reposition in a single button
Movement refunds her cooldowns, so skills keep cycling as long as she moves
Layered speed-ups and slows control the tempo of chases and retreats
weaknesses: Minimal personal damage — she can't convert her setups into kills alone
No healing, so teammates who are already chunked stay chunked
The barrier halves her move speed; a bad opening spot means instant separation
Forget the orb's recoil and it bounces you straight into trouble

counteredBy.name: Gan & Mo
counteredBy.reason: Gan & Mo instantly refill their flying swords with Freshly Forged, closing the window Annette needs to step up.

counteredBy.name: Kongming
counteredBy.reason: Kongming's Spirit Bomb hits harder the more Health Annette has lost, so a chipped Annette only gets easier to kill.

synergies.name: Hou Yi
synergies.reason: Hou Yi has to stand still to keep firing, and Hurricane Wall covers exactly that window.

synergies.name: Consort Yu
synergies.reason: Consort Yu needs a wind-up before Oak Bolt fires, and Annette's shield carries that charge through.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Redemption shield and early speed
builds.condition: When enemy burst is heavy and you need the speed to arrive in time
builds.notes: The opening buy, Crimson Shadow - Redemption, drops a 4-second shield on allies in range worth 240-480 plus 10% of max HP, on a 60-second cooldown. Boots of Deftness come second for 700G, adding 70 movement speed and up to 70 more once you have been out of combat for five seconds. Items three through six match the other build, so the totals land at +5887 max HP and 31% cooldown reduction.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Starspring healing and cooldowns
builds.condition: When trades drag on and the team needs HP and MP topped back up
builds.notes: Crimson Shadow - Starspring opens instead, linking to your lowest-HP ally and restoring 500-1060 plus 20% of max HP, along with 25% of max MP, over five seconds. The effect drops to 20% the moment you attack an enemy hero or take a hit from one, so the window for it sits between fights. Boots of Tranquility take the second slot, pushing cooldown reduction to 46% in total while max HP settles at +5587, three hundred under the other build.

name: Ao'yin
title: Ao'yin Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A twin-blade marksman whose Dragon Souls change with his recent casts, his main and off-blade striking separate targets at once. His real output in brawls exceeds what the numbers suggest.
playstyle: A twin-blade marksman whose Dragon Souls change with his recent casts, his main and off-blade striking separate targets at once. His real output in brawls exceeds what the numbers suggest.
bestFor: theory-minded marksman players who read cast order as a recipe, since fire, water, or wind decides what the enhanced Basic Attack does.

tips.earlyGame: Ao'yin spends the early farm lane playing around Skill 2. It sweeps up to three targets with sword energy and restores Health on hit, and with a Water Dragon Soul on his primary sword every strike of the enhanced Basic Attack heals him again. Recovery is halved against non-hero units, so the real refund comes from landing it on the enemy laner. Refunding poke on his own is what separates him from most marksmen. Every skill cast banks a Dragon Soul mark (up to three), and the enhanced Basic Attack spends them all in one flurry, so waves die faster if you stack marks before swinging. Until your first attack-speed core item is done, your job is collecting CS from behind your support's shoulder, nothing more.
tips.midGame: Around 10 minutes with two core items, Ao'yin's engine revs up. Skills 1 through 3 all cast faster as his Attack Speed rises, so the more speed you build, the tighter the loop between casts and enhanced Basic Attacks. Open trades with Skill 1 — the true damage folded into it goes through armor — then cash in an enhanced Basic Attack while holding three marks. If someone sticks to you, Skill 3's sword energy knocks them back and buys the space. Skill 4's flight and dive is the control window: the landing Dread drives enemies away from him, and for the next 10 seconds he gains 25 Attack Range and bonus Attack Speed. Hold it as the trump card for taking or defending towers.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Ao'yin wins through flexibility: heal with Skill 2 when you get chipped, take Skill 3's speed boost when you need to disengage, lead with Skill 1 when you want damage through. His last two casts decide which Dragon Souls sit on his primary and secondary swords, and those decide what the next enhanced Basic Attack does. Taking one beat to ask which element you actually want is what separates good Ao'yin players from great ones. Matching the same soul on both swords amplifies its effect by half, so repeating a skill is a legitimate choice. At Overlord standoffs, hold a spacing where enemy CC can't reach you and shove diving frontliners off with Skill 3's knockback.
tips.teamfight: In teamfights, Ao'yin sits behind the frontline and keeps the damage flowing. Never start the fight yourself — wait out one or two enemy dash skills first. If someone sticks to you, answer with Skill 3: the sword energy knocks them back, and with a Wind Dragon Soul on his primary sword all three strikes of the enhanced Basic Attack knock back as well. Heal the chip damage off with Skill 2. The moment the enemy's momentum fully dies is the cue for Skill 4 — the dive and the landing Dread scatter them, and the True Dragon Sword gives you 10 seconds of extra range, Attack Speed, and up to two additional targets per swing. His secondary sword strikes a second nearby enemy on its own, so the messier the brawl, the higher his real output. Simply walking around holding two or three marks changes your burst when a pick appears.

strengths: His skills cast faster as Attack Speed rises, so speed items buy raw volume
Skill 2's healing lets him refund poke himself, rare for a marksman
Skill 3's knockback shoves off anyone who sticks to him
Banked marks and Skill 4's dive cover both burst and area control
weaknesses: Skill order changes his buffs, and a misplay directly cuts his damage
The loop is slow before attack-speed items, muting his early pressure
Disengage means Skill 3's speed boost or a long-cooldown Skill 4; layered CC runs him down
Busy piloting; sloppy mark management leaves him a jack of no trades

counteredBy.name: Arli
counteredBy.reason: Arli blinks off with the speed she gains from dropping her parasol, then shoves Ao'yin back out of range.

counteredBy.name: Consort Yu
counteredBy.reason: Consort Yu can go immune to physical attacks, and nearly everything Ao'yin deals is physical.

synergies.name: Zhang Fei
synergies.reason: Zhang Fei's shield and knockback hold the front line, letting Ao'yin attack through all of True Dragon Sword.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Crit build with defensive boots
builds.condition: When two or more enemy heroes deal magic damage
builds.notes: It opens on Eternity Blade and stacks to +455 physical attack and +71% crit rate once the arcana are counted in. Daybreaker's Virtue in the fourth slot doubles up on a ranged hero, so it lands 30% physical penetration and +50 basic attack damage. The only change from Build 2 sits in the second slot: Boots of Resistance add +50 physical defense and +100 magic defense, and raise tenacity by 25%. Total attack speed stops at +85%.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Crit build with attack-speed boots
builds.condition: When enemy magic damage is light and you can keep auto-attacking
builds.notes: The other five items and the buy order match Build 1; only the second slot changes. Boots of Dexterity bring +20% attack speed and heal 30-60 HP on every basic attack. Total attack speed climbs to +105%, but the build picks up no physical or magic defense from its items. The +455 physical attack, +71% crit rate and +64 physical penetration are shared with Build 1.

name: Arke
title: Arke Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An executioner whose strikes always crit from behind. Her ultimate's stealth lets her heal while flanking, deleting a backline hero before they see her. She is at her worst in a straight brawl.
playstyle: An executioner whose strikes always crit from behind. Her ultimate's stealth lets her heal while flanking, deleting a backline hero before they see her. She is at her worst in a straight brawl.
bestFor: players who hunt the map for whoever is standing alone — Arke only crits from behind, so a face-up trade is already lost and most of the game is the walk around and the wait before it.

tips.earlyGame: Arke is a below-average assassin until her first kill, so commit to a clean jungle route from the start. Her Passive grants 20% bonus damage when hitting monsters from the front, so there's no need to circle behind camps while farming. The goal is both buffs and level 4 — unlocking your Ultimate — before the 4-minute Tyrant. Until then, ganks lean entirely on Skill 2's blink with no follow-up mobility, and a failed gank sets your whole game behind, so only touch targets you can actually kill.
tips.midGame: Once the Ultimate is up, stealth approaches out of bushes become your job. The 4-second stealth grants 40% move speed, so path around enemy vision and always open from behind. Arke simply cannot crit from the front, so the extra second spent flanking converts directly into damage. Around 10 minutes, with two crit items done, you can solo the enemy backline, and the kill-resets-all-cooldowns mechanic becomes the engine of your chain kills.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Arke is all about patience before the first kill. At Shadow Tyrant or Overlord, lurk in a bush, confirm the enemy's stuns and locks have been spent on your teammates, then Ultimate behind their carry. Kill one and every cooldown resets — re-stealth with the healing and line up the second. Dive at the opening horn instead and one piece of CC (crowd control) exposes your paper HP bar. Enemies hugging walls deny your backstab, so pick victims standing in the open.
tips.teamfight: Always enter last. Two to three seconds after the enemy's eyes and skills commit to your frontline is your cue. Stealth around the back with the Ultimate, close from behind with Skill 2 to apply the mark, then unload basic attacks and Skill 1. Every hit on the marked target refunds a second of Skill 2's cooldown and you take 30% less damage from them, so tunneling one target down actually keeps you tougher than switching. Once the kill lands, don't stop moving — take your reset skills to the next backline target.

strengths: Every attack from behind crits — once ahead, she erases backlines in seconds
Kills and assists reset all cooldowns, giving explosive chain-kill potential
Ultimate's stealth and per-tick healing allow both re-engages and clean exits
30% less damage taken from her marked target makes her surprisingly scrappy in duels
weaknesses: No crits from the front — head-on trades cut her damage in half
No hard CC and paper durability; a single stun usually means death
Weak until the first kill lands, making it hard to create openings from behind

name: Arli
title: Arli Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The umbrella dancer — placing, throwing, and swapping to her parasol in the game's most unorthodox movement kit. The umbrella's position is her health bar and her damage; mastery gaps show brutally.
playstyle: The umbrella dancer — placing, throwing, and swapping to her parasol in the game's most unorthodox movement kit. The umbrella's position is her health bar and her damage; mastery gaps show brutally.
bestFor: players willing to drill one tool to its limit — every skill doubles as a jump back to the parasol, so a single bad placement drops you in the middle of the enemy team.

tips.earlyGame: Arli is a farm lane marksman who dances with her umbrella. From minute one, internalize the rhythm: skills leave the umbrella behind, and recasting within 4 seconds blinks you back to it. Dash in with Skill 1, tag the enemy with an empowered basic attack for maple marks, then recast home before the counterattack arrives. Repeat this harass and your opponent can forget about last-hitting. That said, she lacks damage until her first attack item is done, so never overstay. Marks detonate at 4 stacks for AoE physical damage — two round trips for 4 stacks is the right level of greed.
tips.midGame: Once two attack items are finished, she becomes unreasonable in river skirmishes. The trump card is Skill 2's projectile destruction: casting it erases enemy projectiles in range, letting you brawl straight through a marksman's shots or a mage's barrage. The catch is that the destruction only happens on the instant of the cast, so the expert habit is saving it for their biggest skill. In Tyrant fights, always leave the umbrella on the safe side, weave in and out, and stack mark detonations to grind down their frontline.
tips.lateGame: Full-build Arli's razor's-edge dance decides matches. Her base durability is rock bottom — a single targeted stun and she evaporates — so fight exclusively on the fight's outer edge. Against diving assassins, the two-layer defense is your lifeline: knock them back with the Ultimate, then change angles with Skill 1 and slip away. As long as you're breathing, your mark detonations keep splashing AoE physical damage every 4 hits and will chew through even tanks. Picking the angle where you don't die, over and over, IS how you maximize her damage.
tips.teamfight: Never stand in the same spot for a full second — that's the iron rule. Blink around with Skill 1 while spreading marks, keeping your next position unreadable from the enemy's screen. When you spot a lethal projectile skill coming, shoot it down with Skill 2. If a frontliner dives you, shove them off with the Ultimate and recast to the umbrella to resume kiting. The most dangerous moment in her kit is losing track of the umbrella, so while you're learning her, simply commit to one rule — the umbrella always stays on your team's side — and your accidental deaths will plummet.

strengths: Every skill doubles as an umbrella blink, giving her the game's best evasion
Skill 2 erases enemy projectiles outright at the moment of cast
Mark detonations plus empowered basics deliver heavy AoE burst
The Ultimate's knockback peels assassins off her without any help
weaknesses: Rock-bottom durability; targeted CC deletes her before she can react
Misplacing the umbrella can blink her straight into the enemy team
Rated Very Hard for a reason — mastery takes serious time
Damage stays underwhelming until her attack items come online

The six items and 30 arcana slots are identical to Build 1, so the finished stat line matches.

name: Arthur
title: Arthur Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The textbook fighter: passive regeneration, a silencing charge, and a percent-Health ultimate. Nothing complicated, and he does an above-average job in every phase of the game.
playstyle: The textbook fighter: passive regeneration, a silencing charge, and a percent-Health ultimate. Nothing complicated, and he does an above-average job in every phase of the game.
bestFor: a first hero. No mana bar, steady self-healing, nothing fiddly to track — which leaves you free to think about lane position and when to take a tower.

tips.earlyGame: Arthur takes any clash lane matchup. He has no mana, and his Passive restores 100 Health every 2 seconds. While his Movement Speed is impaired, that same amount is restored a second time every 2 seconds, so getting chunked never forces him out. The regen also carries 2.5% of his extra Health, which turns every HP item straight into staying power. From level 1, trade with Skill 1's dash plus its 1.25-second silence and follow up with the Skill 2 spin. Against melee fighters, let Skill 2 handle the wave and hit level 4 first. At the 4-minute Tyrant, rotate to the river as the designated silence-bot for enemy interrupt skills.
tips.midGame: Once the Ultimate unlocks, his gank follow-up becomes elite. It's a point-and-click leap with a knock-up that cannot miss — when your jungler shows up, stacking Ultimate into Skill 1 chains nearly 2 seconds of lockdown, and kills usually just happen. Make roaming mid a habit after every shove. A failed Arthur roam costs almost nothing thanks to the Passive's regen and move speed, and a successful one hands you mid priority outright. It's simply good investment.
tips.lateGame: Late game, you're the frontline trigger for engages. The Ultimate deals 16% of the target's HP as magic damage, so HP-stacked enemies actually take more — the jump works whether you point it at a carry or a frontliner. The prime target is the enemy mage: slam Skill 1's silence onto their cast animation and their big spell fizzles entirely, which is miserable to play against. Just confirm your team is actually following before you go in, or you're volunteering as the death vanguard.
tips.teamfight: The teamfight plan is refreshingly simple: Ultimate the priority target, Skill 1 to silence the retaliation, keep Skill 2 spinning, keep swinging. Because the mechanics are easy, target selection is your entire contribution — default to the enemy backline, but if your side is collapsing, switch to bouncing the assassin who dove your own carries. Skill 2 keeps dealing damage while you move, so spin it on the chase and the retreat alike; it's never wasted.

strengths: No mana plus constant regen makes him impossible to shove out of lane
The point-and-click Ultimate and silence make every catch stick
16% HP damage on the Ultimate hurts even stacked frontliners
A simple kit that doubles as the best classroom for fighter macro
weaknesses: Ranged kiting can whittle him down before he ever closes the gap
No shields or immunity — his only answer to focus fire is regen
Flat damage scaling; he can't become the late-game carry
Spending Skill 1 to engage leaves him no tool to disengage

Spikemail, the fourth buy, spends three seconds reflecting 35% of the damage you take as true damage. name: Ata
title: Ata Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A tank who reclaims lost Health by hitting people — offense as defense. His ghost-ship wall partitions fights, and his low-Health recovery punishes anyone who leaves the job half done.
playstyle: A tank who reclaims lost Health by hitting people — offense as defense. His ghost-ship wall partitions fights, and his low-Health recovery punishes anyone who leaves the job half done.
bestFor: players who find passive tanking dull — lost Health comes back only through damage dealt, so the job is anchoring enemies into walls and cutting the field with Ghost Ship.

tips.earlyGame: The lane badge at the top of this page reads Clash, following the official stats. The advice below assumes a roaming pick. Roam from the opening minutes — Ata can meaningfully gank as early as level 2. When Skill 2's anchor clips a wall, it charges in and slams enemies into the terrain for a 0.5-second stun (the classic wall-slam), so simply herding someone toward lane-side walls manufactures kills. And thanks to his Passive, every hit on an enemy hero claws back 40% of your stored lost HP, which means slightly reckless trades actually work in your favor. Manufacture even one kill before the 4:00 Tyrant and your jungler takes off running.
tips.midGame: In skirmishes, you dive first — no exceptions. Skill 1's double jump deals damage on both hops, knocks up on the second landing, and grants crowd control immunity throughout, so you can shrug off enemy CC and press their backline. After casting Skill 2, your next empowered basic attack drags its target right in front of you: wall-slam, drag, team focus fire — that chain is the standard play. As anti-heal items start showing up in enemy builds, your Passive sustain thins out, so slot an early defensive item to compensate.
tips.lateGame: When the Shadow Tyrant and the Overlord become the stakes, everything starts with Skill 3's barrier. It raises a cone-shaped wall that heroes cannot pass for 4 seconds — lay it between the enemy frontline and backline and you get to hit one half with all five. Around boss pits, the tight corridors make the detour it forces that much longer. Dive the carry you cut off with Skill 1: both landings deal damage, but only the second one launches enemies for 0.5s. Line your team's damage up with that launch and the target does not walk away. The barrier's angle has to be decided in a split second, so rehearse the placement in your head before the fight breaks out.
tips.teamfight: Lead the charge alongside your team's engage and treat getting hit as part of the job description: lost HP banks into your Passive, and every strike on an enemy hero recovers 40% of it, which makes the center of the brawl Ata's healing zone. Alternate the crowd control immunity windows on Skill 1 and the Ultimate and CC barely touches you, while the barrier severs escapes and reinforcements at once. From experience: angling the barrier to shut reinforcements out beats trying to cage enemies in — your team moves more freely and you avoid the classic own-goal.

strengths: Passive converts lost HP back through attacks — brawling makes him tankier
Deep CC kit: a wall-slam stun, an empowered-attack drag, and a 0.5s launch
Crowd control immunity on Skill 1 and Skill 3 lets him work straight through CC
Skill 3's barrier reshapes terrain for splits and cutoffs on demand
weaknesses: Anti-heal purchases gut the Passive's sustain
Short reach with little answer to long-range kiting
No solo burst — kills depend on allied damage arriving
A misangled barrier can lock your own team out of the fight

Physical defense stacks to +1053, 390 above the other build, and movement speed reaches +12.5%. Spikemail, bought fifth, spends three seconds returning 35% of incoming damage as true damage. Blood Rage adds +75 physical attack, plus an active that trades 30% of current HP for a four-second shield worth 40% of max HP. Succubus Cloak finishes up with a 400-800 magic damage shield every 15 seconds, carrying magic defense to +680. Max HP lands at +6,837, 400 above build one, while physical defense sits 390 lower at +663.

name: Athena
title: Athena Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A shield-and-dash fighter who doesn't stop at death — she remains on the field as a divine spirit, supporting her team, and her respawn descent hits like a skill. Dying is part of her kit.
playstyle: A shield-and-dash fighter who doesn't stop at death — she remains on the field as a divine spirit, supporting her team, and her respawn descent hits like a skill. Dying is part of her kit.
bestFor: players who want to dive deeper than anyone else — landing Skill 1 or Skill 3 refunds the leap, and being killed leaves you on the field as a spirit rather than out of the fight.

tips.earlyGame: Athena's laning is a level-2 trade loop: jump in with Skill 2, land the empowered basic attack, dash out with Skill 1 — and because a connected Skill 1 refunds Skill 2's cooldown, you immediately get another round trip. Run that cycle and only your opponent's health bar moves. The empowered hit adds 6% of the target's missing HP, so the more chipped they are, the harder it lands. Level 4 unlocks the full all-in: two shields with crowd control immunity layered on top. The only real way to throw it is whiffing, so pick your jump target with care.
tips.midGame: Around 7-8 minutes, one core item in, Athena's mobility starts cashing checks. Shove your side wave, then use Skill 2's leap to cut through the river and hit the 4:00 Tyrant or any skirmish from the flank. Before diving, count the enemy's key lockdown skills — if one is still up, time Skill 1's one second of crowd control immunity to slide through it and reach the backline safely. Do not rush the Ultimate out either. Its retaliation grows every time enemies strike the braced shield, so the moment they focus you is the moment it starts printing damage.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Athena is a time bomb strapped to the enemy backline. As long as Skill 1 and the Ultimate keep connecting, Skill 2 keeps refreshing, and no amount of running rescues a marksman you have decided to keep. Do not overlook the Passive: on death she respawns at the nearest allied tower with a knock-up burst, so in defensive scenarios even a death converts into a play. That insurance barely functions when you are the one diving deep, so measure your entry. At Shadow Tyrant, slide in from behind after both sides have traded skills — that is where she cuts deepest.
tips.teamfight: Decide one thing before every teamfight: whose face are you living in. Athena's damage is stacked empowered basics, so swapping targets mid-fight means killing no one. The ideal is single-minded pursuit of the enemy marksman. Slip the first lockdown with Skill 1's crowd control immunity, raise the Ultimate against their counterattack so every hit feeds the retaliation, then dump it back on them. One detail everyone forgets in practice: you can walk while the shield is braced. Drifting toward your escape route during those seconds is often the difference between a reset and a respawn.

strengths: Skill 1 and Ultimate hits refund Skill 2, so her mobility never runs dry
Shields with crowd control immunity slip enemy lockdown on demand
Missing-HP empowered basics give her a real answer to tanks
Tower respawn passive turns defensive deaths into tempo, not losses
weaknesses: A whiffed Skill 1 or Ultimate stalls the reset engine mid-combo
No burst, so disciplined enemies can recover before she finishes them
Respawn is fixed to the nearest allied tower — weak while sieging
Reset bookkeeping is expert-level; sloppy play accomplishes nothing

The finished build totals +368 physical attack, +52.8% attack speed, +89.2 physical penetration, +23.2% physical lifesteal, +1900 max HP and +300 physical defense.

name: Augran
title: Augran Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A fighter who links souls with his halberd and partitions the battlefield with walls of life and death. Enemies caught in his territory take escalating damage — he doesn't chase, he encloses.
playstyle: A fighter who links souls with his halberd and partitions the battlefield with walls of life and death. Enemies caught in his territory take escalating damage — he doesn't chase, he encloses.
bestFor: anyone who likes setting the ground before a fight — walls down to bend the path first, then executing whoever falls under 10% Health.

tips.earlyGame: Augran's jungle clear runs on never letting the Passive's soul link drop. Basic attacks tether souls, and weaving in Skill 2's empowered attack pushes damage and healing into several targets at once — double camps barely scratch your HP bar. Full clear to a fast level 4, then lay down Skill 1's path and gank from an angle the terrain was supposed to forbid. Pick the lane where the enemy is overextended rather than the one being shoved in; the success rates aren't close. Take the 4-minute Tyrant off the momentum of a converted gank.
tips.midGame: From level 4, Skill 1's path becomes the axis of your game. On the path you ignore terrain and move 50% faster, and touching a wall builds a bridge that accelerates you further — arriving behind someone from a route that never appears on their screen is a feeling no other jungler offers. In fights, Skill 2's wall marks multiple enemies so your empowered attacks drain all of them at once; that healing is your lifeline. When a target runs low, recast Skill 1 for the execute stance and finish anyone under 10% HP with a basic attack. Learn to harvest that final sliver and your kill count doubles.
tips.lateGame: In late teamfights, the correct Augran timing is right after the opening burst exchange ends. Your burst is modest, but as long as links and walls keep touching multiple enemies, the healing never stops — the longer the brawl runs, the harder you are to remove. Once low-HP enemies start piling up, drop the Ultimate into their midst. Its healing scales with every enemy hero struck, up to double, and the landing grants 8 seconds of execute stance to cull dying targets in sequence. The phantom that mirrors an enemy even papers over a numbers disadvantage now and then.
tips.teamfight: Position where the soul link can reach at least two enemies at all times. Place Skill 2's wall across predicted paths so every marked enemy eats the empowered attack's echo and feeds you healing. The Ultimate also doubles as an emergency heal button — cast even after the focus fire lands, it often stands you back up. The only real fear is chained CC. Both the links and the executes require standing next to enemies, so against multiple stunners, wait until your teammates have baited the CC out before stepping forward.

strengths: Soul links and empowered attacks heal off several enemies at once
Execute stance culls anyone who drops below 10% HP
The terrain-ignoring path hides his gank angles completely
Ultimate's huge heal and phantom flip losing brawls
weaknesses: Low burst; enemies who disengage early escape his damage
Healing and executes demand melee range, so chained CC ruins him
Link damage needs time to ramp and loses short exchanges
Managing the path and recasts is busy work that takes practice

synergies.reason: Sun Bin's slow clumps enemies, so Augran can mark them with Death's Precipice and link Soul Resonance to several.

name: Bai Qi
title: Bai Qi Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The taunt tank: he forces enemies to attack him, embodying aggro control. His scythe pulls and self-healing sustain the frontline — rated easy, but the craft runs deep.
playstyle: The taunt tank: he forces enemies to attack him, embodying aggro control. His scythe pulls and self-healing sustain the frontline — rated easy, but the craft runs deep.
bestFor: players at peace with being the one who gets hit — the taunt pulls enemy damage off your team and runs longer the more bonus Health you carry, so everything rides on where you jump in.

tips.earlyGame: The lane badge at the top of this page reads Clash, following the official stats. The advice below assumes a roaming pick. Bai Qi roams from the opening minutes, but his taunt only comes online at level 4 and lasts barely a second while his bonus HP is low, so deep dives backfire. Hold the space between mid and farm lane and play interceptor: thread Skill 2's scythe through ganking enemies and drag them back. The scythe returns 1.2 seconds after the throw, so aim it across the target's walking path rather than at their feet and it connects far more often. Taking damage has a chance to auto-cast Skill 1's heal, so tanking minion aggro to hold ground is less painful than it looks.
tips.midGame: Two HP items done around 10 minutes is Bai Qi's power spike. Every 1000 bonus HP adds 0.2 seconds of taunt, and by now you're holding enemies for close to 2 seconds. When setting up vision at Tyrant or Shadow Tyrant, the real play is your Ultimate from a bush: the taunt forces enemies to attack Bai Qi, instantly sealing away the enemy carry's skills and combos. After landing, drag retreating targets back with Skill 2 and charge Skill 1 to heal while your team arrives.
tips.lateGame: Full-build Bai Qi taunts for up to 2.5 seconds, and late-game teamfights come down to who eats it. The ideal is dropping it on the enemy marksman or mage — if your team burns them during 2-plus seconds of lockdown, the fight becomes 5v4. Miss the Ultimate, though, and your gap closers are spent, leaving a walking target. Discipline yourself to hold it until you've seen the enemy's dashes. Skill 2 also deals bonus damage to enemies below 30% HP, so you can finish runners yourself more often than you'd expect.
tips.teamfight: In teamfights, one thought is enough: land your Ultimate on the enemy's most dangerous hero. Catch several with the AoE taunt and their entire damage output points at Bai Qi for seconds while your team swings freely, essentially untouched. Every hit you take stacks Shadow Power through the Passive, boosting your healing, and Skill 1's auto-proc stacks on top — melting mid-taunt is rarer than it looks. As the taunt expires, scythe their squishiest survivor toward your team as a parting gift and the numbers advantage keeps rolling.

strengths: AoE taunt scaling to 2.5 seconds with bonus HP seals away entire enemy combos
Auto-proc Skill 1 and the healing-boost Passive make him tougher the deeper the brawl
Skill 2 hits harder below 30% HP, letting him finish fleeing targets himself
weaknesses: The scythe's 1.2-second return delay makes it dodgeable once the path is read
Missing the Ultimate leaves no gap closer — he becomes a walking target
Early taunts last about a second, so early dives tend to backfire

counteredBy.reason: Lu Bu's enchanted halberd adds true damage on top, which Bai Qi's stacked defense cannot cut down.

counteredBy.name: Mozi
counteredBy.reason: Mozi's barrier stuns anything touching it, so Bai Qi's Lay Waste jump leaves him locked in place.

synergies.reason: Yaria's shield scales with the target's extra Health, so it grows thickest on a Health-stacking Bai Qi.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Shield and freeze in slot five
builds.condition: When the enemy team stacks hard CC and you want to lock fights down
builds.notes: Only the fifth slot differs — the other five items, and the order they are bought in, match across both builds. Build one puts Frigid Charge (2,030G) there for 150 physical defense and 7.5% cooldown reduction. Any hard CC short of suppression grants a shield worth 10% of max HP, and the active frost field freezes enemies after 0.75s. Totals come to +6,987 max HP and +893 physical defense, with cooldown reduction at 13.5% — 7.5 points clear of the other build.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: More HP and healing in slot five
builds.condition: When enemy damage is mostly magic and fights run long
builds.notes: Slot five is the only change — Eye of the Phoenix (2,020G) — while the other five buys and their order match build one. It adds 180 magic defense and 1,350 max HP, and every 10% of HP lost raises healing received by 5%. Overlord's Platemail restoring 0.5% Health every second and Longnight Guardian's 10% max HP heal both scale up as the health bar drops. Totals reach +7,437 max HP and +600 magic defense — 450 HP and 180 magic defense over build 1.

name: Biron
title: Biron Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An armored bruiser who charges his mace and discharges it in electrified slams. Shields and area slows hold the frontline while his charge cycle creates waves of burst.
playstyle: An armored bruiser who charges his mace and discharges it in electrified slams. Shields and area slows hold the frontline while his charge cycle creates waves of burst.
bestFor: players who like a charge-and-release rhythm — at 30 energy every skill upgrades, the empowered dash stuns, and the shield lets you hold the middle of a brawl.

tips.earlyGame: Biron pushes hard in the clash lane early — as long as his gauge is up. Basic Attack hits accumulate 5−10 charge and skill hits accumulate 8−16. At 30 or more the mace goes Electrified and every skill gains an enhancement. Punch a few minions to clear 30 before you start anything with your opponent. Charge stocks up to 90, so loading extra before you commit is never wasted. Enhanced Skill 1 heals 1% more for every 1% of HP you are missing. That is what makes low-HP slugfests survivable, and the moment your opponent thinks they have chunked you down and steps in is usually where you win.
tips.midGame: From level 4, once empowered Skill 2's knockup and stun come online, Biron transforms into a premier gank-followup hero. Clear waves while banking Energy, and the second your jungler arrives, dash in with Skill 2 and lock the target down for a full second with the empowered basic attack — that's essentially a guaranteed kill. The iron rule before the 4-minute Tyrant: fill your gauge before walking down to the river, because empty-gauge Biron is just a target. After shoving your lane, hit the enemy's jungle camps to keep the gauge topped up while you raid.
tips.lateGame: Late game you are the frontline diver and disruptor. Enhanced Skill 3 raises its area damage from 450 to 580 and its shield from 900 to 1,450 absorbed (level 1 values). Soak the enemy's opening burst with that 6-second shield and buy your team the window to counterattack. The enhanced version also sends out an electric wave that steals 25 Movement Speed from every hero it hits and grants it to Biron, so the more enemies surround you, the faster you move — good for the dive and good for the exit. Healing comes from enhanced Skill 1 and Electrified basic attacks, not from Skill 3. The shield buys the time; the swings bring the HP back. The only thing to fear is being kept at range. Against comps that stack slows from distance, save Flash as your instant gap-closer until the very end. Charge and Flash: managing those two is the whole late game.
tips.teamfight: The fight starts 30 seconds before the fight. Hit nearby minions or jungle camps to bank Energy, then walk in loaded. Engage with Skill 2's dash, stop their momentum with the empowered basic attack's knockup, and immediately follow with the Ultimate's shield and AoE slow. Close with empowered Skill 1 in the middle of their clump — the more enemies it hits, the more you heal. And once you're below half HP, empowered Skill 1's healing spikes hard, so the longer you persist in the scrum, the harder you become to kill.

strengths: With all three empowered skills up, few clash laners match his overall kit
Empowered Skill 1's healing scales with missing HP for dramatic comebacks
Empowered Skill 2 chains a dash into a reliable stun to start plays
Empowered Ultimate's 1500 shield lets him live in the middle of the brawl
weaknesses: At zero Energy his damage, healing, and CC all turn mediocre at once
Short skill range leaves him helpless against long-range kiting
Needs pre-fight gauge charging, so he reacts poorly on short notice
Skill 2's dash is his only mobility, leaving few retreat options

counteredBy.name: Menki
counteredBy.reason: Menki stacks Dream Bubble slows and walks away from Biron before he can catch up.

counteredBy.name: Lu Bu
counteredBy.reason: Lu Bu's enchanted halberd deals true damage that ignores defenses, so Biron's bulk counts for nothing.

synergies.reason: Liu Bang's shield and arrival heal stack onto Biron's own shield, letting him hold the front line.

Frigid Charge in the fifth slot grants a shield worth 10% of max HP for 5 seconds whenever a hard CC other than suppression lands (15s cooldown). Starbreaker closes with +30% physical penetration, for totals of +170 physical attack, 43.5% cooldown reduction and +17.5% movement speed.

name: Butterfly
title: Butterfly Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A snowballing assassin: takedowns build marks, and at three stacks her next skill has no cooldown. Every kill fuels the next — once she's rolling, nobody stops the chain.
playstyle: A snowballing assassin: takedowns build marks, and at three stacks her next skill has no cooldown. Every kill fuels the next — once she's rolling, nobody stops the chain.
bestFor: players chasing momentum itself: patient early, then closing hard the instant a health bar drops, because the first kill shapes the whole match.

tips.earlyGame: You're the jungler. Skill 1 gains 25% bonus damage for every additional enemy it hits, so casting from the center of each camp is free clear speed. The opening route is both buffs plus the river camps, aiming for Level 4 around the 3-minute mark. Passive stacks build from monster kills too, and at three stacks your next skill costs no cooldown — bank them before a gank and you walk in with an extra cast. As for the 4-minute Tyrant: touch it only when you've reached Level 4 before the enemy jungler has. Otherwise it's bait.
tips.midGame: Once your jungle item and first damage item are finished, the real work begins: erasing chipped enemies. The ideal prey is a backliner under half HP. Death Dealer's leap applies the mark, converts 35% of your damage into healing, and — the headline — resets its own cooldown instantly on a takedown. Open ganks with Skill 2: the first enemy hit takes 1.5x damage and a 50% slow, and the attack speed and crit buffs it grants let your basics finish the job. The one rule that never changes, even in this window: do not walk into a healthy enemy team from the front.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Butterfly is the cleanup crew, not the opening act. Even when the 5v5 starts, hold your side bush until the enemy's CC and attention are committed to your frontline. The Ultimate adds true damage equal to 12% of a marked target's lost HP, so anyone already chipped dies — armor stacked or not. One kill refunds the Ultimate on the spot, a hero takedown banks two passive stacks, and the chain reaction begins. The flip side: without that first kill, nothing starts. Whatever else you compromise on, never compromise on your entry timing.
tips.teamfight: Your brawl loop is enter, kill, reset, next. Lead with Skill 2 before committing — the slow keeps them in reach, the attack speed buff quickens your swings, and each basic on a marked target shaves a second off both Skill 1 and Skill 2. When focus piles up, Skill 1's shield and decaying 50% speed boost carry you back to the edge of the fight. While your mark is active you take half damage from basic attacks, so a chasing marksman often can't actually finish you. One nuance: enemy support shields can rob your takedown reset, so start with the softest unshielded target — that's the correct kill order.

strengths: Takedown-triggered Ultimate resets give unmatched chain-kill power in brawls
35% damage-to-healing plus halved basic-attack damage while the mark runs
Lost-HP true damage finishes chipped targets through any amount of armor
Skill 1's shield and speed burst keep her entries and exits cheap
weaknesses: Without a first kill the resets never spin up and she fades hard
No CC of her own to start fights — she depends on teammates' lockdown
Hard CC exposes pure assassin fragility the moment it lands
Lacks a decisive answer to full-HP targets and healthy frontlines

counteredBy.name: Lu Bu
counteredBy.reason: Lu Bu's ring of slaughter raises both his defenses, so Butterfly struggles to trade with him.

counteredBy.name: Diaochan
counteredBy.reason: Diaochan keeps trimming Petals in the Wind's cooldown, so she blinks away before Butterfly can close.

synergies.name: Mozi

builds.notes: Destiny takes the fourth slot, so by 7,010G Butterfly survives one lethal hit and goes invulnerable instead. Finished with Pure Sky, the totals reach +407 physical attack, +41.6% attack speed and +27.5% cooldown reduction. Pure Sky also carries an active that cuts incoming damage by 30% for 3 seconds, taking the edge off the return fire after a dive. One Mutation slot is swapped for Red Moon, lifting critical rate to 20.5%.

builds.title: Defense first, built to trade
builds.condition: When the enemy damage is mostly physical and fights run long
builds.notes: Spikemail goes fourth, so +300 physical defense and +700 max HP arrive at 6,970G. It also brings an active that reflects 35% of the damage taken as true damage for 3 seconds. Closing with Eye of the Phoenix pushes the totals to +3150 max HP, +440 physical defense and +280 magic defense, with physical attack at +299, 108 below build 1. All ten Mutation slots are kept, holding physical defense penetration at 100.

name: Cai Yan
title: Cai Yan Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The fundamental healer: she walks and heals simultaneously, defends herself with a bouncing stun, and tilts every extended fight through sheer sustained restoration.
playstyle: The fundamental healer: she walks and heals simultaneously, defends herself with a bouncing stun, and tilts every extended fight through sheer sustained restoration.
bestFor: healers who read their team's health bars as their own scoreboard — there is no damage here, so where you stand while the heals go out is the entire job.

tips.earlyGame: Cai Yan's assigned seat is directly beside her marksman from minute zero. The early job is not damage — it is making sure your partner cannot die. When the enemy commits, answer with Skill 2's ricochet stun; if they are tangled up with their minion wave, the bounces chain-stun and the trade collapses in your favor. After every exchange, walk alongside with Skill 1 running and the chip damage simply refunds itself, letting your partner keep farming instead of recalling. Until the Ultimate arrives at level 4, check bushes, hold position, and refuse to be the one caught forward.
tips.midGame: Cai Yan's presence grows from the 4:00 Tyrant onward. While your team burns the boss, the flank is the most dangerous moment on the map — meet whoever walks in with Skill 2, and the ricochet stuns stall the contest cold. Her Ultimate spends five seconds auto-targeting the lowest-HP ally in range with healing and a defense buff, so rather than panic-casting mid-brawl, open it just before the enemy's burst lands. Between the Passive's speed surge on taking damage and her self-heal, she is far harder to catch than the health bar suggests.
tips.lateGame: Late fights become a staring contest over Cai Yan's Ultimate — the enemy wants it forced early, you want it perfectly timed. Absent anti-heal, its five seconds of rolling heals and defense buffs absorb an entire round of enemy focus. Stand diagonally behind your carry, and cast it where only the ally you intend to save sits inside the ring; that placement is the entire skill expression of this hero, because a frontliner soaking the heal is a wasted Ultimate. Fill your slots with team utility items and forget your own scoreline entirely.
tips.teamfight: Cai Yan's teamfight reduces to two real decisions: spend Skill 2 on the enemy's entrance or on their retreat, and choose whose feet the Ultimate covers. The ricochet multiplies against clustered enemies, so its highest value is meeting the opening dive; if it misses, drop back and wait out the cooldown. A teamfight where the healer dies first is close to an automatic loss — never surrender the backmost position, no matter how won the fight looks. And triage coldly: the ally who can still fight outranks the ally who is already doomed.

strengths: Ultimate auto-locks the lowest-HP ally with heavy healing and defenses
Ricochet stuns multiply against clumped divers
Passive speed burst and self-heal make her deceptively hard to catch
A simple kit that delivers steady value in every single game
weaknesses: Near-zero damage of her own; she cannot create a win condition alone
Anti-heal items cut her entire reason for existing in half
Ricochet targets are uncontrollable; pinning one specific enemy is hard
Caught by CC first, she dies before a single heal goes out

counteredBy.name: Musashi
counteredBy.reason: Musashi's Duel to the Death delays all recovery on his target, so Cai Yan's healing arrives only after the duel ends.

counteredBy.name: Lady Zhen
counteredBy.reason: Lady Zhen's Destructive Deluge pool denies Cai Yan a place to heal from, and its slow keeps her from leaving.

synergies.name: Gao

builds.notes: Crimson Shadow - Redemption opens the build with an aura of 20% attack speed and 15% cooldown reduction, half of which reaches allies within 800 range. Venomous Staff fills the fourth slot at 2,040G, cutting HP regeneration and lifesteal by 35% for 2.5 seconds on any enemy you connect with. Totals come to +745 magic attack, +29.5% cooldown reduction and +27.5% movement speed. Those two items are the only gap to build two, and they buy the faster cooldowns and the faster feet.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Shared defense, extra damage
builds.condition: When enemy damage comes from both physical and magic sources
builds.notes: Guardian - Redemption leads, adding 65-130 physical and magic defense, and half of that aura reaches allies within 800 range. Equipment and arcana together come to +725 magic attack, +22% cooldown reduction and +20% movement speed. Savant's Wrath in the fourth slot, 2,140G, adds a further 30% magic attack on top of that sum. The same two items are the whole gap to build one: 7.5% less movement speed, traded for defense that covers nearby allies too.

name: Chano
title: Chano Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A hunter who charges empowered leaps by lurking in brush, ringing the battlefield with wolf-spirit traps. His ambush angles decide who fires first — and firing first is most of the fight.
playstyle: A hunter who charges empowered leaps by lurking in brush, ringing the battlefield with wolf-spirit traps. His ambush angles decide who fires first — and firing first is most of the fight.
bestFor: hunters who set the board before they take the shot — charging concealment in a bush, leaping out at an angle nobody covers, and ringing off the retreat with traps.

tips.earlyGame: Chano defaults to the farm lane, but his Passive's 25% bonus monster damage inside bushes makes jungle a well-established alternative. Either way, one rule governs everything: touch a bush before you swing. Entering one empowers your next basic attack into a double shot, and leaving one converts stored stealth value into a jump whose distance scales with how long you lurked. In lane, weave between the river and your own bushes — land the double shot, jump away, repeat — and you'll hold an HP lead through nothing but hit-and-run. Also get in the habit of placing Skill 2 traps at the river entrances before level 4.
tips.midGame: From six or seven minutes, with your first attack speed item done, trap management becomes the center of your job. Skill 2 holds up to four charges, and each trap is vision, damage, and a wolf-spirit attacker in one package. Seed them around Tyrant, Overlord, and the enemy jungle entrances, and gank detection and gank punishment become the same action. When someone closes in, escape skyward with Skill 1 and shove pursuers back with the powerful arrow's knockback. The recoil trick — inputting away from your target as the arrow fires to slide backward — is worth drilling in the practice room until it's muscle memory.
tips.lateGame: Late teamfights are decided by the setup, not the fight. Lay two to four traps around the Shadow Tyrant pit, then wait in a bush with full stealth value — that's the ideal opening stance. On engage, detonate everything at once with your Ultimate, send the wolf-spirit pack charging in, and kite backward through the eight seconds of mounted archery. That rolling barrage while sliding away from their front line is Chano's whole kit in one motion. Whatever you do, avoid flat open ground: without bushes, he loses most of his mobility and turns into an ordinary marksman.
tips.teamfight: Chano's teamfight starts from the side bushes, not the front line. Chip from the outside with stealth jumps and double shots, and when heads turn toward you, take to the air with Skill 1. Slide your landing spot with the recoil movement so nobody can pre-aim your touchdown. Save the Ultimate as a counter to the enemy's dive — the wolf pack plus its stacking slows flips the momentum in one cast. Keep steering enemies toward wherever your traps still sit. Chano's teamfight is half over the moment the battlefield has become his backyard.

strengths: Ultimate's mounted archery keeps damage flowing on the move
Bush stealth jumps and double shots enable pure hit-and-run
Four traps handle vision, zoning, and ambush punishment at once
Bonus monster damage in bushes makes jungle a genuine option
weaknesses: Lacks burst, so low targets often escape before they die
Loses most of his mobility on open ground without bushes
Damage leans on basic attacks and wolves, weak to attack speed debuffs
High mechanical demands — stealth and recoil tricks take practice

counteredBy.name: Gao Changgong
counteredBy.reason: Gao Changgong closes in from stealth, so the spacing Chano takes from the brush counts for nothing.

The other five items all carry Critical Rate or Attack Speed, finishing at +130% Attack Speed and +86% Critical Rate. Sunchaser caps the order with an active that adds 20% Movement Speed for 5s. Boots of Dexterity and Sunchaser are the two items Build 2 never buys, and they are where the 40% Attack Speed and 15% Critical Rate gap comes from.
