Every monster killed stacks +3 Physical Attack and 0.2% Cooldown Reduction on Rapacious Bite, up to 25 times. Those boots then add 50 Physical Defense, 100 Magical Defense and 25% Resistance, none of which Build 1 ever buys. Total Physical Attack reaches +379, 50 above Build 1, while Attack Speed stops at +90%.

name: Charlotte
title: Charlotte Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A duelist whose skills chain: any opener empowers the follow-up, turning three skills into a full combo table. The same kit produces different routes every fight.
playstyle: A duelist whose skills chain: any opener empowers the follow-up, turning three skills into a full combo table. The same kit produces different routes every fight.
bestFor: players who enjoy building combos for their own sake, since any skill can open and the next one lands enhanced; picking the right starter is the whole game.

tips.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Charlotte commits fully to touch-and-go trading until level 4. Skill 1 grants 80% movement speed on hit, so pre-cast it like a trap, close the gap the moment it connects, shave them down with Skill 2's six-stab heal, and leave. That one round trip is your winning trade pattern. The Passive's marks expire after 4 seconds, so resist any half-hearted engage that won't reach the third stack. Impose one condition on yourself — only step in deep right after your opponent whiffs a skill — and your early-game deaths plummet.
tips.midGame: From around 8 minutes, as cooldown reduction items come online, Charlotte enters her unbeatable-in-a-1v1 window. Shove side waves to bait out the enemy fighter, then run them over from the front with the 3-mark empowered basic attack: seven dashing strikes, a final hit dealing missing-HP percentage damage, and damage reduction while it runs. The follow-up strikes' attack speed slow hurts basic-attack-reliant heroes most, so any side lane holding a retreating enemy marksman is prime hunting ground. Arrive at Tyrant fights slightly late from a flank, cycling skills on the perimeter to pre-build marks before you touch anyone.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Charlotte dives second, aiming for the enemy backline's head. Open by waiting: once your team's engage soaks the enemy's attention and crowd control, enter with Skill 2, layer the Ultimate's crowd control immunity, complete your marks, and unload the seven-hit flurry. Missing a single skill severs the whole chain — her greatest weakness — so the composure to wait for a guaranteed-hit distance converts directly into damage. Anti-heal items thin out Skill 2's sustain considerably, so check the enemy's item builds every single fight.
tips.teamfight: The teamfight ideal is carving sword scars in the middle of the brawl while the Ultimate's crowd control immunity makes enemy lockdown whiff. Timing is everything: casting it on reaction, right as you see the enemy's stun animation start, is exactly fast enough. Fire it early and you're just a statue. The empowered basic attack carries damage reduction while it runs, so you survive the center of a scrum better than you'd expect. Even without kills, continually smearing the attack speed slow onto the enemy marksman visibly cuts the damage your frontline takes — there's always work to do.

strengths: The 3-mark seven-hit flurry carries missing-HP damage that shreds even frontliners
Follow-up attack speed slows cripple basic-attack-reliant enemies
Skill 2's healing and the Ultimate's crowd control immunity win extended brawls
The 80% on-hit speed boost from Skill 1 dictates every engagement
weaknesses: Whiffed skills sever the chain and the marks, and the damage evaporates
No real answer to long-range poke or disciplined kiting
The wound debuff is stripped by enemy basic attacks, so it fades against heavy single hits
Silence locks her out of ever reaching the empowered basic attack

counteredBy.name: Arthur
counteredBy.reason: Arthur's silence breaks the Follow-Up chain Charlotte relies on, and her own slow only speeds his healing.

counteredBy.name: Arli
counteredBy.reason: Arli's Autumn Storm knocks Charlotte away, cutting short the close-range pressure Charlotte needs to build.

synergies.name: Mai Shiranui
synergies.reason: Mai Shiranui's launch freezes enemies in place, letting Charlotte's enhanced Basic Attack land in full.

synergies.name: Guiguzi
synergies.reason: Guiguzi pulls enemies into one stunned clump, so Charlotte's Power Gradation catches several of them at once.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Pierce and physical defense
builds.condition: When the enemy team leans physical and you need to cut through a tanky front line.
builds.notes: Boots of Tranquility come first at 700G, locking in 15% cooldown reduction on the way to 45% across four items. Mutation and Eagle Eye arcana take physical pierce to +100, more than double Build 2's +36. Eye of the Phoenix and Ominous Premonition close things out, bringing the totals to +3450 max HP and +840 physical defense. Anything that damages Charlotte loses 20-40% attack speed for 2.5 seconds.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Soak magic with resist and shields
builds.condition: When two or more enemy heroes deal magic damage.
builds.notes: Boots of Resistance open at 700G with 100 magic defense and 25% tenacity. Those boots carry no cooldown reduction, so three items and ten Void arcana bring the total to 36%. Succubus Cloak in the fifth slot throws a 400-800 magic damage shield every 15 seconds, and Cuirass of Savagery stacks bonus damage up to 10 times as Charlotte takes hits. Magic defense finishes at +400, more than double Build 1's +180, with max HP at +3310.

name: Chicha
title: Chicha Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A shapeshifting fighter who cycles five ancestral weapons with every basic attack; whichever weapon is in hand sets her form — Defense, Offense, or Overkill. Skills 1 and 2 change outright with the form, so what comes next is decided by your current weapon. Skill 3 wields all five at once.
playstyle: A shapeshifting fighter who cycles five ancestral weapons with every basic attack; whichever weapon is in hand sets her form — Defense, Offense, or Overkill. Skills 1 and 2 change outright with the form, so what comes next is decided by your current weapon. Skill 3 wields all five at once.
bestFor: drilling until you can name the next weapon without looking. Learn the cycle and one pick hands you three heroes' worth of tools.

tips.earlyGame: Chicha is a fighter whose brawling literally heals her. Every basic attack restores Health and cycles her to the next, longer-ranged weapon, so in the farm lane the first rule is simple: never stop swinging. Fighting Spirit stacks expire after four seconds, so keep the gaps between attacks short. The polearm and spear of Defense Form are her shortest reach, and overextending there is how you die. Step to an enemy hero only when the bow's Overkill Form comes around. Learning that rhythm is your lifeline until level 4.
tips.midGame: From level 4, one question drives everything: can you cast Skill 3 while in Overkill Form? Cast it with the bow in hand and the form stays locked in, and she can attack while moving. Entering Overkill Form also cuts the cooldowns of Skill 1 and Skill 2 by half the instant it triggers. Once your first attack speed item finishes around six minutes, start showing up to Tyrant fights. Health comes back on every basic attack, so extended damage races rarely go against you. One quiet trick that wins real games: pre-cycle your weapon on minions until you are two or three swings from the bow before the fight starts.
tips.lateGame: With three or four items done past the ten-minute mark, Fighting Spirit pushes her attack speed past the normal cap and her sustained trading gets hard to beat. She is also the first target in any teamfight, so open behind your front line and use Skill 3 as the counterpunch once the divers commit. At Shadow Tyrant standoffs, prioritize a position where you can keep swinging over hiding and waiting. The moment your attacks stop, Fighting Spirit drops and the healing stops with it. Never stopping is the best defense she has.
tips.teamfight: Half of Chicha's teamfight is decided by which weapon she is holding when it starts. The ideal is the bow's Overkill Form: entering it halves the cooldowns of Skill 1 and Skill 2, and layering Skill 3's move-and-shoot on top lets her kite backward while grinding the enemy line down. Every basic attack heals her mid-brawl, so a chunk of the damage she takes can simply be punched back. When an assassin jumps her, fighting back and cycling the weapon forward often keeps her alive longer than running would. The six seconds where Fighting Spirit has no stack limit hold her entire teamfight in miniature.

strengths: Healing on every basic attack wins brawls and sustains her lane
Fighting Spirit stacks push attack speed past the normal cap
Skill 3's move-and-shoot keeps damage flowing while kiting
Five cycling weapons adapt her range to any situation
weaknesses: Weapons cycle in fixed order, making a specific form hard to hold
Four seconds without attacking drops Fighting Spirit and craters her damage
Hit-count design makes attack speed debuffs and hard CC brutal
Form management takes real practice before she comes online

name: Cirrus
title: Cirrus Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An assassin who gains permanent flight at level 4 and crosses terrain as if it weren't there. His power is the angle of attack — appearing from over a wall no one was watching.
playstyle: An assassin who gains permanent flight at level 4 and crosses terrain as if it weren't there. His power is the angle of attack — appearing from over a wall no one was watching.
bestFor: junglers who read walls as doorways — flight is permanent from level 4, so a gank angle can come from over anything, and Skill 1 only ever goes forward.

tips.earlyGame: Level 4 is the first real checkpoint. That is when Cirrus takes flight, and from then on he permanently ignores terrain — there is no upkeep, so once you get there it never drops. The flip side: through level 3 he is a grounded assassin who cannot cross walls, and that stretch is his weakest. Camp clearing runs on Lacerate, the 2-second debuff (up to 5 stacks) his basic attacks and skills apply. Lacerated targets take damage every 0.2s, and minions and monsters take the full amount whether or not they are moving. Camps melt, and level 4 arrives early. Until then keep deep invades rare, since an ambush leaves you no escape route. Only touch the 4-minute Tyrant when your team can collapse on it from both sides.
tips.midGame: Level 4 is where Cirrus comes online. Approach from over-the-wall angles that wards rarely cover. Skill 1 builds 60% Movement Speed while you hold it (level 1) and dashes forward when you release, stunning whatever it hits for 0.5s. The dash travels straight ahead — it does not swing you around behind the target, so set up the angle yourself before you commit. Only after hitting a hero can you jump a set distance in any direction. Use it to disengage, or to land on the side they are running toward. Canceling the charge-up refunds 20% of the cooldown, so pull out instead of forcing a read that has gone wrong. Basic attacks grant Breath, worth up to 60 Movement Speed, but it drains quickly. You are fast for a few seconds after swinging rather than stacking speed the longer you fight. Finish a core item by 10 minutes and farm isolated side laners to widen the lead.
tips.lateGame: A frontal late-game collision is a death sentence for Cirrus. Wait at a flank or behind a wall, and commit to the back line only after one or two enemy CC skills have been burned. The order is Skill 1's stun into basic attacks, then Skill 2. Once the wind blades land their slow, you get 4 seconds of 20% Attack Speed with extended basic attack range and three feathers per swing. When everyone turns on you, that is Skill 3. It cuts incoming damage by 30% (level 1; 60% at level 3), clears the crowd control on you, and sweeps the target into the air. While airborne you cannot be targeted and can still move — that is the window that makes their return fire whiff, and it ends in your landing hit. Landing damage rises 10% per stack of Lacerate on the target, so how much you carved before the lift is how hard it lands. Lacerate deals percent-HP damage to enemies while they move, which means a tank trying to run bleeds the most.
tips.teamfight: Never call the engage yourself. After your tank absorbs the opening, come in from fog straight onto the enemy marksman or mage. Stun with Skill 1 and stack Lacerate with basic attacks. If you get chased, cut their speed with Skill 2's slow and leave straight over a wall — terrain does not apply to you. Skill 3 works as a finisher or as an escape hatch. Landing damage grows 10% per stack of Lacerate, so swinging first and lifting second makes the hit land far heavier. Used defensively, the value is simply the airborne window where nothing can target you. One target at a time. Greeding for a second kill is how you never make it home.

strengths: Terrain-ignoring flight opens gank angles wards cannot cover
Lacerate's percent-HP damage bleeds moving targets, tanks included
Skill 3's untargetable window makes enemy burst whiff
Every basic attack grants Breath for a short burst of chase speed
weaknesses: Paper-thin defenses; eating CC first usually means dying first
Skill 1 only dashes straight forward; over-committing leaves no way back
Cannot join teamfights head-on; entry timing is unforgiving
Open ground with no walls strips away his mobility edge

builds.notes: Four of the six items are shared with build 2; only the slot-2 boots and the sixth item differ. Max HP finishes 500 higher at +1500, while cooldown reduction sits 10 points lower at +22.5%.

name: Consort Yu
title: Consort Yu Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A duelist marksman whose signature skill nullifies physical damage for two seconds — the mirror-matchup specialist. Her charged arrow hits like a siege weapon, and the immunity mind-game decides the trade.
playstyle: A duelist marksman whose signature skill nullifies physical damage for two seconds — the mirror-matchup specialist. Her charged arrow hits like a siege weapon, and the immunity mind-game decides the trade.
bestFor: counter-punchers who want the carry-versus-carry duel. Time the physical immunity to their biggest swing; it does nothing against magic, so choose who you trade with.

tips.earlyGame: Treat Consort Yu's early game as a waiting room until attack speed items come online. Her charged shots fire faster the more attack speed she has, so with a bare inventory the wind-up is clumsy and forced poke just bleeds HP and mana. Focus on clean last-hits, and only fight back with Skill 2 when the enemy physical marksman starts a trade — for a short window she takes no physical damage at all, turning their confident all-in into a total whiff. At the four-minute Tyrant, simply follow your team's call; you have nothing to force there yet.
tips.midGame: From six or seven minutes, one finished attack speed item turns her into a different hero. The charge visibly speeds up, and the Ultimate's volley count grows with attack speed too, so every item purchase translates directly into damage you can feel. Against a physical lane opponent, fight face-to-face around Skill 2 and shove them off the tower. When the enemy mage shows up instead, the immunity means nothing — take your positioning a full step deeper. At objective fights, the iron rule is to hold Skill 2 until the actual engage.
tips.lateGame: After ten minutes, decide in advance whose skill your Skill 2 is answering — plan it before the fight, not during. If the enemy carry is physical, canceling their main burst with one well-timed immunity breaks the entire teamfight math. During Shadow Tyrant standoffs, charge your shot from the very back row and commit to punishing anyone who backs off too slowly. The Ultimate returns you to your starting position after the pounce, so even a deep catch has a guaranteed ride home. Magic burst is the one thing you can't answer, though — never give the enemy mage a clean angle on you.
tips.teamfight: Consort Yu stands in teamfights holding a few seconds that erase physical damage entirely. The highlight play is timing Skill 2 the instant the enemy's physical assassin or marksman commits, then beating them down with the empowered basic attack while their damage does nothing. With the Passive's follow-up shots and slow layered on, you can kite them to death from there. Hold the Ultimate until the enemy's plan shows itself, then use the stun to set up your team's focus fire. Charged shots root you briefly, so pick windows when enemy CC is pointed somewhere else.

strengths: Skill 2's physical immunity dominates physical-heavy lineups
Attack speed uniquely converts into faster charges and bigger volleys
Passive follow-up shots and layered slows make her a natural kiter
Ultimate returns her to her starting spot, keeping catches safe
weaknesses: Immunity blocks physical only — helpless against magic damage
Mistiming Skill 2 leaves her with no self-defense at all
Charged shots are hard to land on mobile targets without practice
Underwhelming damage and skill uptime until attack speed items finish

builds.notes: Eternity Blade goes right after Boots of Dexterity, so the crit damage bonus is live at 2,810 gold. Daybreaker's Virtue lands fourth and doubles on a ranged hero: 30% physical penetration and +50 basic attack damage. Fifth-item Mortal Punisher cuts enemy healing and lifesteal by 35%, and the closing Sunchaser buys 125 extra range for five seconds. Totals reach +86% crit rate, +132% attack speed and +22% movement speed — faster hands and feet than build 2.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Percent damage and sustain
builds.condition: When two or more high-HP frontliners are on the enemy side and fights drag on
builds.notes: Shadow Ripper goes second, banking +35% attack speed and +7.5% movement speed by 2,740 gold. Doomsday follows third and adds 80-160 plus 7% of the target's bonus HP to every basic attack, so the bulkier the target, the harder it melts. Once Bloodweeper is in, physical lifesteal sits at +49.8% and max HP at +1,000. Daybreaker's Virtue is held back to sixth, so the 30% physical penetration only arrives at 11,520 gold, well after build 1's 7,420.

name: Da Qiao
title: Da Qiao Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A support who builds transit networks — sending allies home and returning them through crystal warps. Her koi fish fight the skirmish while her logistics rewrite who is where on the map.
playstyle: A support who builds transit networks — sending allies home and returning them through crystal warps. Her koi fish fight the skirmish while her logistics rewrite who is where on the map.
bestFor: players who think in map states rather than duels — sending an ally home to heal to full and warping them back, always answering the question of who should be where.

tips.earlyGame: Early Da Qiao rides shotgun in the farm lane, using koi knock-ups to widen her marksman's safe farming pocket. The real product is Skill 2: an elevator that ships a wounded ally to base, refills them completely, and warps them straight back to the line. With that running, your partner can spend HP in trades like it grows back — because it does — and no war of attrition is losable. If nobody takes the ride, the cooldown refunds by half, so placing it on spec costs nothing. One genuinely critical prep step: explain the circle to your duo in the first minute, or the first accidental trip home will be theirs.
tips.midGame: Midgame Da Qiao turns both edges of the map into simultaneous fronts. Hand Skill 2 to whoever is pushing a side lane, and the push, full-heal, and warp-back cycle forces the enemy to over-commit defenders every single time. That distortion converts directly into a numbers advantage at the 4:00 Tyrant and the 10:00 Shadow Tyrant. In skirmishes the pairing is Skill 1 and Skill 3: send one koi through the tide the other left behind, and the Passive detonates it for extra damage and a one-second slow. Her koi range also grows by 50 per 250 magic attack, up to 200, so sneak some AP into the build alongside the usual support items.
tips.lateGame: The late-game siege is Da Qiao's private stage. Lay Skill 2 behind the siege line before committing, and a rotation forms on its own: chipped allies cycle home, refill, and warp back, while the defenders burn damage into a five-stack that never stays hurt. The circle takes four seconds to fire, so the entire skill is deciding early — it will never save someone already inside a burst window. See an ally dip below half, and place it even if they look fine to keep fighting. That one habit quietly drags your late-game win rate upward.
tips.teamfight: Da Qiao manages the entrance to the fight from the very back row. The instant an assassin leaps at your carry, flip them with Skill 1's knock-up, then sweep Skill 3's koi across for a second launch plus the slow from the tide explosion — most dives simply end there, unfinished. Skill 4 launches nobody; its job is to leave an 8-second circle allies can teleport into, shielding them and her while they stand in it. She has no engage of her own, so walking forward to farm damage numbers is banned. Keep Skill 2 away from healthy allies' feet while winning — that is exactly when accidental trips home happen. Once both koi are spent, fall back on the Passive's movement speed and kite the gap out politely.

strengths: Skill 2 sends allies home for a full refill and warps them right back
Two knock-ups plus current explosions shut down backline dives
Skill radius scales with magic attack, stretching her control zone
An untaken Skill 2 refunds half its cooldown — a free safety net
weaknesses: Minimal personal damage; her impact never shows on the scoreboard
Skill 2's four-second delay cannot answer sudden burst
Uninformed teammates trigger accidental trips home mid-fight
Self-peel is knock-ups only; two divers at once will run her down

builds.title: Bulk and physical defense

builds.notes: Crimson Shadow - Redemption opens the build, passing half of its +20% attack speed and 15% cooldown reduction aura to nearby allies. Ominous Premonition comes fourth, so the full +583 physical defense is up by the 6,840G mark. Damage taken slows the attacker by up to 15% for 2.5 seconds, so you hold up when the enemy focuses you. Augur's Word closes at +6487 max HP, 1,500 more than the other line.

builds.title: Cooldowns cut by 43.5%
builds.condition: Against healing-heavy enemies, or when you want to roam the map nonstop
builds.notes: Guardian - Redemption starts things off with up to +130 physical and magic defense plus 0.6% max HP healed every 5 seconds, half of it shared with allies nearby. Cooldown reduction reaches +42.5% and movement speed +20%, against +16% and +11.5% on the other line. Glacial Buckler carries 20% of that reduction and slows nearby enemies by up to 30% whenever a single hit takes more than 10% of your current HP. Venomous Staff finishes the build, cutting enemy healing and lifesteal by 35% for 2.5 seconds.

name: Daji
title: Daji Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The most direct mage in the game: stun, then burst, and one enemy disappears. Follow the 2-1-3 sequence and the job is done — her magic-defense shred makes the numbers hit harder than they read.
playstyle: The most direct mage in the game: stun, then burst, and one enemy disappears. Follow the 2-1-3 sequence and the job is done — her magic-defense shred makes the numbers hit harder than they read.
bestFor: players who prefer one reliable combo to a deep toolkit — the stun is targeted so it lands, and with no escape button, choosing the target before you leave the brush is the whole job.

tips.earlyGame: Daji's early game is a patience test: push waves with Skill 1 and wait for level 4. Her fox fires fly at random targets, so her clear is slower than most mages' — don't try to win the shove war, because you won't. What you do have is Skill 2, a targeted stun that cannot miss. The instant your opponent drifts into range, Skill 2 into Skill 1 takes a third of their HP with zero aim required. With no mobility skill, build the habit of stepping back whenever the enemy jungler vanishes from the minimap. Skip forcing the 4:00 Tyrant — holding your mid tower and soaking experience is a perfectly good outcome.
tips.midGame: From 5-7 minutes, with level 4 and some cooldown reduction online, Daji's best play is roaming for picks. Shove the mid wave, slide into a side brush, and wait. During the 1.5-second guaranteed stun, dumping all five fox fires and Skill 1 — with your Passive shredding their magic defense — erases any mage or marksman on the spot. After a full combo you're staring at long cooldowns, so take the kill and leave immediately; greed is how fed Dajis die. Since landing skills takes no mechanical skill, all your brainpower goes into the real question: when, and on whom.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Daji doesn't win teamfights — she makes them start 4v5. Past ten minutes, lurk in the brushes around Overlord and execute whoever comes to check vision: a support face-checking alone or a carry a step too far forward is a guaranteed kill. With four or more items, her single-target burst is among the best in the game, and anything short of a tank is inside the one-combo threshold. Open 5v5s are a different story — fox fires scatter randomly across multiple targets, so your damage evaporates. Bet everything on the pick before the fight.
tips.teamfight: If a straight-up teamfight is unavoidable, park Daji in the very back as the counter-assassin. Never fire your Ultimate into a clump — random targeting means it won't find the enemy you actually want dead. What you're waiting for is an isolated target, ideally the assassin who dove your backline: a guaranteed stun into full combo turns their engage into a death sentence. Burn Skill 2 early and you have no self-defense left, so keep asking yourself mid-fight who the stun is being saved for. Positioning alone decides whether Daji ends the game as the MVP or the liability.

strengths: Skill 2 is a targeted, unmissable stun — the chosen victim does not get away
Magic defense shred from her Passive synergizes with fox fires for elite single-target burst
The combo is so simple that anyone can reproduce her full damage once items are done
One ambush from a brush can decide a teamfight before it starts
weaknesses: Random fox fire targeting makes multi-enemy fights and wave clear genuinely bad
No mobility skill — outside of Flash, there is no escape plan
After dumping the full combo, long cooldowns leave her nearly helpless

counteredBy.reason: Mulan stacks Balance until it detonates and silences Daji, cutting off her skills entirely.

counteredBy.name: Gao Changgong
counteredBy.reason: Gao Changgong strikes out of stealth, and Daji has nothing but her stun to answer with.

synergies.reason: Wukong's enhanced Basic Attack is hard to land, but Daji's stun holds the target still for it.

synergies.name: Arke
synergies.reason: Arke only crits from behind, and Daji's stun freezes the target long enough for her to get there.

builds.notes: Boots of the Arcane come first at 700G, putting 60-120 magical pierce on the board straight away. The fourth slot goes to Insatiable Tome, so its 24% magic lifesteal arrives 2,040G earlier than in build 2. Sage's Tome is exclusive to this build: +350 magic power, and its Enlightenment passive adds 0.5% damage reduction per 100 magic power. builds.notes: Void Staff moves up to the fourth slot, so 45% magical pierce is online by 6,980G. Ten Nightmare arcana carry another 24 magical pierce, which frees the boot slot for Boots of Deftness and its +70 movement speed. Venomous Staff closes the build, cutting an enemy's health recovery and lifesteal by 35% for 2.5 seconds on hit. Totals land at 21% movement speed and +1550 max HP, with magic power at +1093.6, about 121 below build 1.

name: Devara
title: Devara Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A thunder fighter who builds power through close-range attacks, unlocking a second cast of his basic skills. His ultimate lifts him into a floating barrage at the heart of the brawl.
playstyle: A thunder fighter who builds power through close-range attacks, unlocking a second cast of his basic skills. His ultimate lifts him into a floating barrage at the heart of the brawl.
bestFor: players who accept the grind of point-blank range — melee Basic Attacks bank Thunder Resolve, and a full gauge buys a second cast of a basic skill.

tips.earlyGame: In the clash lane, everything about Devara flows from one rhythm: one skill, one empowered basic attack. Every skill cast empowers your next basic attack with area magic damage and healing attached, so simply keeping that weave going wins the lane's war of attrition. Until level 4, treat Skill 1's shielded dash as your answer to being jumped, not as an engage tool. Basic attacks bank Passive stacks, and hitting the cap of 6 triggers thunder that lets you cast one bonus basic skill — so the iron rule is to only take trades from a full gauge.
tips.midGame: From around 8 minutes, with one or two magic core items finished, Devara's skirmish power transforms. The Ultimate grants crowd control immunity and terrain-ignoring movement during its 1.5-second levitation, letting you drop into river scraps from over a wall. The transformed state lasts 8 seconds after landing: your empowered basic attacks grow in area and each basic attack banks 2 Passive stacks, raising both your damage and your healing a full tier. Cast it from behind a wall rather than in the enemy's face — floating in the open invites focus fire.
tips.lateGame: In teamfights past 15 minutes, Devara is a semi-carry whose frontline rank jumps a tier for the transformation's 8 seconds. Float with the Ultimate as the fight opens, collect the lightning strikes and shields on the way down, and land near the enemy's squishiest members. Your transformed ranged basic attacks carry chain bolts that ricochet between clustered enemies, spiking your damage into grouped teams. The danger is post-landing isolation: drop deeper than your support can reach and the focus fire ends you. Cap your landing depth at a spot allies can reach within 3 seconds.
tips.teamfight: In the brawl, your job is cycling in and out with Skill 1's shielded dash while keeping the empowered basic attacks' area damage and healing rolling. Against enemies glued to you, the answer is Skill 2 point-blank: the closer the target, the farther the knockback sends them, so the more suffocating the pressure, the calmer you should be about firing it in their chest. The Ultimate's crowd control immunity also answers an enemy engage, so decide from their composition whether it's your sword or your shield. Whatever happens, never break the basic attack rhythm — it carries both your damage and your survival.

strengths: Empowered basic attacks after every skill deliver area magic damage and healing at once
The Ultimate's levitation pairs crowd control immunity with terrain-free entry angles
Max Passive stacks grant a bonus basic skill cast for extra tempo
Thick shields and sustain let a magic build brawl toe to toe
weaknesses: Break the attack-weave rhythm and damage and healing dry up together
Engaging on an empty gauge means no empowered hits and lost trades
Mobility lives entirely in Skill 1 — spend it engaging and the exit is gone
A melee-centric core that suffers under sustained long-range poke

counteredBy.name: Gan & Mo
counteredBy.reason: Gan & Mo knock enemies back while stepping away, so the melee range Devara relies on disappears.

counteredBy.name: Arli
counteredBy.reason: Arli blinks away and speeds up with her parasol down, so Devara struggles to hold melee range.

synergies.name: Kongming
synergies.reason: Kongming's magic fields slow enemies to a crawl, letting Devara stay in the melee range he wants.

synergies.name: Li Bai

name: Dharma
title: Dharma Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A boxer whose knockback punches deal bonus damage when enemies hit walls. Terrain is half his weapon — the same skill is trivial in the open and lethal in a corridor.
playstyle: A boxer whose knockback punches deal bonus damage when enemies hit walls. Terrain is half his weapon — the same skill is trivial in the open and lethal in a corridor.
bestFor: players who track wall positions on instinct — a knockback into a wall stuns and opens the flying kick, while in open ground neither happens, so check the geometry before you punch.

tips.earlyGame: In the Clash Lane, your first teammate is the terrain — the walls — and the early game tests how well you use them. Level 1-3 trades lean on Skill 1's dash and the Passive's defense buff, and since Skill 1 holds two charges, the standing rule is one for offense, one banked for the exit. The only green light is the moment your opponent stands near a wall; otherwise, just soak the wave. Your empowered basic also slows on hit, so stack small hit-and-run chips to open an HP gap while you wait for level 4 to unlock the wall-slam game.
tips.midGame: Once you have the Ultimate, every wall on the map becomes a Dharma kill zone. The recipe is simple: knock the target into a wall, the collision stuns for a second with bonus damage, and within eight seconds Skill 1 converts into a flying kick that adds 15% of their missing HP. Land the full string and most victims don't walk away. Riverbanks and jungle corridors are nothing but walls, so your presence at Tyrant fights is actually stronger than your laning. Skill 2's punch flurry doubles as healing and percent-HP damage, giving you surprising staying power in monster tug-of-wars.
tips.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, Dharma's grade depends entirely on forcing fights into tight terrain. Start a fight in the corridor outside Overlord or around a jungle corner and you get the dream play — wall-stunning the enemy carry right in front of your team. In the wide-open river center, though, your knockback is just a shove and half your threat disappears. Claiming the strong bush early to control where the fight happens is your hidden late-game job. Keep three Passive stacks rolling and you hold your own in frontline slugfests too.
tips.teamfight: You have exactly one objective: put an enemy backliner into a wall. Enter with Skill 1's dash, set your angle, then fire the Ultimate — and take the half-second before casting to confirm a wall actually sits behind them, because that pause is the difference between a kill and a whiff. Once the stun lands, finish with the flying kick and Skill 2's punch flurry. Skill 2 lets you steer mid-channel, but your movement is still restricted, so swinging it out in front of an enemy holding burst is asking to die. Canceling early is always on the table — take the kills that are actually there.

strengths: Huge burst from the wall stun into the flying kick conversion
Strong brawling stats via the Passive's defense buff and Skill 2 healing
Percent-HP damage on Skill 2 chews through high-health targets
Two Skill 1 charges give him flexibility on offense and escape
weaknesses: Loses half his threat in open terrain with no walls
Restricted movement during Skill 2 makes him a target for big skills
A misjudged knockback angle shoves the enemy to safety instead

Demonsbane closes the build, adding magic defense equal to 50% of physical attack and topping the totals at +445 physical attack, +500 physical defense, +1800 max HP and 30% cooldown reduction.

name: Di Renjie
title: Di Renjie Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A marksman who scatters homing tokens, hiding a master-class defensive tool inside an easy kit: Skill 2's brief immunity plus cleanse works as both a beginner's insurance and an expert's outplay.
playstyle: A marksman who scatters homing tokens, hiding a master-class defensive tool inside an easy kit: Skill 2's brief immunity plus cleanse works as both a beginner's insurance and an expert's outplay.
bestFor: players who want approachability and survivability at once — the tokens chase enemies so rough aim is fine, and Skill 2's immunity and cleanse cover the one hole: no way over a wall.

tips.earlyGame: In the Farm Lane, simply never letting your basic attacks stop is a strength in itself. The Passive stacks attack speed and move speed with every swing, and holding it at five stacks is the ideal state. Just by taking CS, the token that fires on every third attack chips your lane opponent for free — the lead builds without any deliberate harass. Skill 1 pulls double duty on wave clear and poke, but your mana is finite, so don't spam it. Skill 2's invulnerability is your lifeline; never let a greedy early trade bait it out of you.
tips.midGame: Level 4 hands Di Renjie a win-on-hit button. When the golden edict connects, it stuns for a second and cuts the target's physical and magic defense by 50% — with your jungler following up, even tanks don't survive it. When a gank arrives, the edict is the opening move, every time. Around 8 minutes, with two core items finished, you start beating your lane opponent in straight shootouts, so make every Tyrant fight. The no-mobility weakness never goes away, though: confirm where your teammates are before you ever step forward.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Di Renjie lives and dies on one decision: when to press Skill 2. An invulnerability that also cleanses debuffs is about the best self-peel any marksman gets — but it's one charge. Let the assassin's lockdown actually land, then cast it, and their whole engage evaporates; panic-press it early and the follow-up kills you every time. On offense, put the Ultimate on the enemy carry and focus-fire through the five seconds of halved defenses. One more trick worth keeping: the edict grants vision of whoever it hits, which makes it a fine tool for flushing out ambushes in bushes.
tips.teamfight: Your job is holding five Passive stacks and never stopping the shooting, all from the very back. The dream opener is landing the Ultimate on their engage hero — the stun blunts the dive, and the 50% defense cut invites your whole team to collapse. If you miss, no panic: steady basics and tokens over your frontline's shoulder are plenty of sustained damage. When someone finally jumps on you, that's the moment to stay calm — eat the CC first, then cleanse and go invulnerable with Skill 2. Land that reversal and the enemy has essentially nothing left that kills you. You can't cross walls, so never take a position where one blocks your exit.

strengths: Best-in-class self-peel: invulnerability plus a debuff cleanse on Skill 2
The Ultimate's 50% defense shred is a teamfight-opening button
Passive attack and move speed stacking for relentless sustained damage
Straightforward kit — an ideal first marksman
weaknesses: No mobility skill and no way to escape over walls
Missing the Ultimate loses both the stun and the shred, halving his impact
Random token colors make slow-based chase damage unreliable

Ominous Premonition fifth and Succubus Cloak sixth bring the totals to +3887 max HP, +423 physical defense and +350 magic defense. name: Dian Wei
title: Dian Wei Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A fighter whose every skill cleanses crowd control — and each cleanse raises his attack. The enemy's lockdown literally becomes his damage.
playstyle: A fighter whose every skill cleanses crowd control — and each cleanse raises his attack. The enemy's lockdown literally becomes his damage.
bestFor: players who want the enemy's lockdown to become their own damage — every skill cleanses crowd control and every cleanse raises attack and reach, so it comes down to landing Skill 2.

tips.earlyGame: Jungle is the standard assignment. Skill 2's 200% attack speed steroid works on monsters too, putting his clear speed near the top of the jungler class. Open on your two buffs and the riverside camps and race to level 4. Before that, only take ganks that Skill 1's 60% move speed lets you reach for free — Dian Wei doesn't truly come online until his Ultimate, so an incident-free farming start matters more than anything. One thing worth knowing: in early buff scraps, if Skill 2 connects you win most straight slugfests, so you can afford to play those confidently.
tips.midGame: Once the Ultimate's leaping strike is online, you become a gank machine. For five seconds after it lands, every instance of your damage adds true damage equal to 2% of the target's max HP — half-finished armor doesn't come close to absorbing it. The fun part: enemy CC actually feeds you. Every skill in your kit cleanses crowd control, and each cleanse stacks your Passive's Rage, growing your attack damage and attack range. See their stun come in, cleanse it with a skill, and hit back harder — master that rhythm and the players trying to catch Dian Wei are the ones who fall apart. Tyrant also melts quickly solo thanks to the attack speed buff.
tips.lateGame: Past the 10-minute mark, camp the fights that break out around Shadow Tyrant and Shadow Overlord. That 2% max-HP true damage bites deepest into late-game tanks with inflated health bars, making you one of the rare fighters who can melt the enemy frontline first. The catch: your only gap closers are Skill 1's empowered basic and the Ultimate, and getting kited at range with both down is your nightmare scenario — time your dives with allied CC. But when six Rage stacks come online mid-brawl, the rampage that follows can flip an entire fight on its own.
tips.teamfight: A chaotic brawl full of flying CC is exactly where Dian Wei belongs. Enter second, after your team commits, and drop the Ultimate on the squishiest target or a wounded frontliner. After landing, Skill 2 must connect — the difference between having and not having 200% attack speed plus 20% lifesteal decides every slugfest that follows. When enemy lockdown hits you, don't panic; cleanse it with a skill and convert it into Rage stacks. The only genuinely dangerous moment is when your cleanses run dry, so never stand in the middle of their team with every skill spent.

strengths: Comeback engine — every CC cleanse grows his attack damage and range
Skill 2's 200% attack speed and lifesteal make him a premier brawler
Percent-based true damage on the Ultimate shreds even late-game tanks
Fast jungle clear keeps him ahead on levels
weaknesses: Missing Skill 2 halves the steroid, gutting both damage and sustain
Few gap closers — nearly helpless against ranged kiting
Enemies who hold their CC deny him Rage stacks entirely

name: Diaochan
title: Diaochan Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A melee-range mage who dances through repeated blinks, her passive detonations healing her and dealing true damage. She fights from inside the enemy team — skill difference shows instantly.
playstyle: A melee-range mage who dances through repeated blinks, her passive detonations healing her and dealing true damage. She fights from inside the enemy team — skill difference shows instantly.
bestFor: mages who refuse to stay in the back line. Dive in, stack four marks, and live off the detonation heal; nerve matters more than range here.

tips.earlyGame: Mid lane, and until level 4 it's a patience game. Skill 1's lotus travels out and back, so catching an enemy with both halves stacks two marks in one cast — that alone covers your waveclear and poke. Skill 2 is Diaochan's only escape, so don't throw it away on offense while gank threat exists. Since four marks detonate for damage and healing, you can actually take extended HP trades more confidently than your frame suggests. Your first item goal is an early Holy Grail to erase your mana problems.
tips.midGame: From around 7-8 minutes, with Holy Grail and cooldown items online, Diaochan becomes a true close-range mage. On roams, close the gap instantly with Skill 2. Each petal that connects shaves up to 3s off Skill 2's cooldown, so landing all three point-blank strips nearly the whole 10-second timer and you can blink again right away. In skirmishes before Tyrant, lay down Skill 3's field first, then cycle Skills 1 and 2; the true damage and healing from mark detonations can push back even a numbers disadvantage. Diving while enemy stuns or silences are still up is suicide — count who has spent their CC before you go in.
tips.lateGame: In the late game, Diaochan's detonation true damage hits tanks and squishies alike, no matter how much armor they've stacked, so her relative damage actually rises. After 15 minutes, never take a teamfight without Skill 3's field down — inside it, your Skill 1 and 2 rotation speeds up, and with the healing included you become a different hero entirely. The one matchup to respect is burst: if an enemy assassin has the damage to delete you before your healing catches up, hold Purify or Flash and let a teammate take the first engage.
tips.teamfight: Teamfighting Diaochan comes down to one sentence: enter the middle the instant enemy CC is gone. With your field down, the enemy clump is your fuel — hitting multiple enemies chains mark detonations until your healing outpaces the damage coming in. The ideal is catching two or three enemies in the field and confusing their aim with Skill 2's teleports while you dance. The flip side: a single stun collapses everything, so before the fight starts, know exactly who on their team holds CC and what they haven't used yet.

strengths: The detonation loop of true damage and healing gives elite staying power in brawls
Skill 2's teleport refunds cooldown on every orb hit, so she never stops moving
Inside her Ultimate's field, faster skill cycling shreds multiple enemies at once
True damage core means her output never falls off against late-game tanks
weaknesses: A silence or stun that stops the combo gets her deleted instantly
Low base durability — burst damage before marks detonate is lethal
A melee-range mage at heart; long-range poke comps never let her touch them
Very Hard difficulty — below full mastery she's just a squishy melee

Augur's Word lands third for +900 max HP, and Twilight Stream after it builds magical pierce the more you damage heroes. Splendor buys 1.5 seconds of full immunity at the price of standing still.

name: Dolia
title: Dolia Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A mermaid support who lays down pools of water where allies standing in them recover Health and Mana. Skill 3 is unique in the game: it instantly refreshes one ally's skill — she hands out time itself.
playstyle: A mermaid support who lays down pools of water where allies standing in them recover Health and Mana. Skill 3 is unique in the game: it instantly refreshes one ally's skill — she hands out time itself.
bestFor: making other people's highlight plays. Read whose cooldown matters most, refresh it, re-lay the water — almost none of the damage is yours.

tips.earlyGame: Pick your contract partner at spawn — usually the marksman or jungler who'll be your late-game gun. Shadow that partner early and actively force skirmishes around the river, because Dolia in water is a different hero: Mermaid mode passively regenerates her HP and MP, and Skill 1 upgrades into an AoE knockback plus stun. The 4-minute Tyrant fight happens in the river, and it's her first showcase — simply standing in the water before the enemy arrives is already an advantage.
tips.midGame: Mid game is for drilling the Ultimate's timing into muscle memory. It resets the skill with the longest remaining cooldown in range, so casting it right after an ally fires their ultimate returns that ultimate almost every time. Shadow Tyrant and Overlord contests are her home turf — river terrain stacked with Skill 2's water field generation. Even on dry land, Skill 2's landing zone hands sustained healing to every ally standing in it.
tips.lateGame: Her late-game value collapses into one sentence: your ace's ultimate fires twice. Partner's ultimate lands, Ultimate immediately after — whether that single input happens determines the entire teamfight's math. From the enemy's perspective, the big skill they just played around is coming again, and there's essentially no answer. If you die, the reset supply stops, so position behind even your contract partner. Not dying is itself your biggest contribution — accept that fully.
tips.teamfight: Step one of fight prep: lay a water field at your feet with Skill 2 before it starts. On the water, you sustain while fighting, and diving assassins get bounced by Skill 1's knockback and stun. From there, just sync the Ultimate with your team's big cooldowns. It isn't flashy, but when your allies out-sustain everything on the field and every enemy engage gets bounced back, the fight turns more one-sided than any scoreboard suggests. Even retreats favor you — moving through water halves slows on her.

strengths: The Ultimate's instant reset of allied ultimates is unique support power
In water she gains healing, hard CC, and AoE attacks all at once
Skill 2 carries a water field anywhere, so she works far beyond the river
The contract system stacks resources on your ace and sharpens the win condition
weaknesses: The Ultimate's cooldown depends on ally skills, so it rotates poorly alone
Out of water, Skill 1 loses its CC and her self-defense collapses
Almost no personal damage — she creates nothing by herself
Her value craters when teammates don't understand the reset mechanic

name: Donghuang
title: Donghuang Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A suppression tank who seizes one enemy for two full seconds — sharing the damage he takes with his captive. His orbs sustain him on the frontline; the plan is simply: I hold, you hit.
playstyle: A suppression tank who seizes one enemy for two full seconds — sharing the damage he takes with his captive. His orbs sustain him on the frontline; the plan is simply: I hold, you hit.
bestFor: players willing to put their own health bar on the table — two seconds of suppression splits the damage with the captive, and Flash decides how far in you can go.

tips.earlyGame: Play Donghuang's roam aggressively from the opening seconds. Spin up three dark orbs with Skill 1 and walk into the enemy jungle alongside your own jungler — every orb touch deals percent max-HP magic damage and heals you, so even-numbers shoving matches in tight bushes are fights you simply do not lose. Contest every River Sprite to stunt the enemy jungler's curve. Your first real kill window opens the moment the Ultimate arrives at level 4, and here is the quiet truth: enemies still holding Flash are usually the careless ones.
tips.midGame: The midgame runs through the 4:00 Tyrant and Overlord control afterward. Camp the bushes around the pit early, flush corridors with Skill 2 for damage and slows, and fish for the third orb's stun. The headline play is Flash into the Ultimate: two seconds of suppression that nothing interrupts, with the damage share letting your team pour burst into their star while they carry part of the bill. Track your own Flash cooldown obsessively — whether that card exists changes how far the enemy backline dares to walk.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Donghuang is a walking arrest warrant with the enemy carry's name on it. Just pacing the frontline with the Ultimate available forces their marksman to hang at maximum range, halving their output before anything happens. Spend the suppression exclusively on marksmen and assassins — never tanks, because the damage-share math simply does not produce a trade against beefy targets. The counter-suppress is just as strong: when an assassin lands on your backline, clamp them, press your orbs into their face, and grind them down.
tips.teamfight: In teamfights Donghuang either authors the opening or erases the enemy's. Attacking, Flash plus the Ultimate binds their centerpiece for two seconds while your team's burst flows in. Defending, catch divers with orbs and Skill 2's stun. The critical caveat: you are rooted during your own suppression, so casting it in the middle of their team is a signed confession — the beating starts the instant the lock ends. Suppress inside your team's range, no exceptions. And since activating the Ultimate instantly refunds three orbs, your grind damage never stops ticking while you hold them.

strengths: Suppression shares damage, trading his life for their fed carry
Orb percent damage and self-healing dominate close-range brawls
Flash plus the Ultimate is a simple, nearly unmissable pick tool
A tank who moonlights as an early-game invade threat
weaknesses: Long-range poke comps never let his orbs touch anyone
He is rooted during suppression; casting beyond ally range is fatal
Skill 2's trajectory is honest and demands predictive casting
No mobility skill, so his Flash timer quietly decides fights
