Insatiable Tome follows with +24% Magic Lifesteal, which is why Sage's Tome can wait for the 11,780G mark.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Movement First, Pierce Last
builds.condition: When the enemy stacks Magic Defense and Donghuang needs to keep roaming between lanes
builds.notes: Scepter of Reverberation arrives second for +7.5% Movement Speed, and ten slots of the Hunt arcana add +10% more, for +17.5% in total. Every skill hit detonates around Donghuang for 140–280 plus 28% of Magic Attack as magic damage, on a 5s cooldown. Sage's Tome moves up to the fourth slot, putting +350 Magic Attack online by 7,550G. Void Staff closes the build with 45% more Magic Pierce, while the arcana carry flat Pierce to +88 against build one's +24.

name: Dr Bian
title: Dr Bian Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A dual-ledger mage who stacks poison marks on enemies and healing marks on allies, then detonates both at once. Every decision moves two scoreboards simultaneously.
playstyle: A dual-ledger mage who stacks poison marks on enemies and healing marks on allies, then detonates both at once. Every decision moves two scoreboards simultaneously.
bestFor: players who read offense and defense off one board — poison stacks on enemies while healing stacks on allies, and with no dash, the discipline is waiting out five stacks before setting both off.

tips.earlyGame: Dr Bian's early game is an exercise in patience. With no burst, mid lane trades are losing propositions until your first core item finishes, so clear waves with Skill 1's poison pools and manage your HP. Vials restock every 12.5 seconds up to a cap of three — always bank one for self-defense. Whenever the enemy jungler is off the map, dropping a pool at your feet before backing off cuts gank success rates dramatically. Basic attacks apply a poison stack through the Passive too, so keep tapping targets from safe range.
tips.midGame: Around 8 minutes, with one or two items done, you can drag fights into your arena: long skirmishes. In Tyrant standoffs, throw Skill 1 at their feet from behind your frontline, cycle Skill 2 for chip damage and ally healing, and once poison marks build up, detonate them with your Ultimate. Each stack adds 50% to the blast's damage and healing, so holding for 5 stacks instead of panicking at 2 changes what the fight looks like. Past the 10-second mark of any brawl, the poison-versus-healing math starts sinking the enemy team.
tips.lateGame: The later the game, the more Dr Bian wants to dodge coin-flip bursts and drag everyone into attrition. Line up three poison pools in front of Shadow Tyrant or Overlord and the enemy either fights while melting or gives up the spawn. In teamfights, stand near the center of your team and use the Ultimate's detonation for AoE damage and a team-wide heal in the same instant. Once enemies start buying anti-heal items, your edge shrinks — compensate with timing, detonating earlier, before allies drop below half HP.
tips.teamfight: Skip the flashy opener — you're the fight's accountant, keeping the books on marks. Open with Skill 1 into their clump, throw Skill 2 at whoever is easiest to hit (usually the frontline) while healing allies around you, and once both teams tangle, detonate everything with the Ultimate. Blowing 5-stack poison across multiple enemies at once is the comeback button: AoE damage and a team recovery in the same moment. When an assassin jumps you, crack a pool at your own feet and walk them across the 30% slow toward your team — that alone changes your survival rate.

strengths: Poisons enemies and heals allies at the same time — long fights snowball his way
Five-stack Ultimate delivers big AoE damage and a team-wide heal in one cast
Three stocked vials make him excellent at zoning objective pits
weaknesses: No mobility skill — an assassin who reaches him rarely lets him leave
Needs time to stack marks, so instant-burst shootouts are not his game
Anti-heal items erase half of what he brings

counteredBy.name: Yang Jian
counteredBy.reason: Yang Jian's damage scales with the Health Dr Bian has already lost, so every trade makes the next one worse.

counteredBy.name: Mai Shiranui
counteredBy.reason: Mai Shiranui strips magical defense before she dashes in, leaving Dr Bian no room to reset the distance.

synergies.name: Bai Qi
synergies.reason: Bai Qi taunts and pulls enemies into one clump, so Dr Bian's detonated marks hit the whole group.

synergies.name: Xiang Yu
synergies.reason: Xiang Yu cannot be defeated during his ultimate, so Dr Bian's healing has time to land and hold the line.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: HP into damage, damage into defense
builds.condition: When the enemy team has multiple divers and you want to hold your ground and keep casting
builds.notes: Cooldown reduction totals +40% from Boots of Tranquility through Sage's Tome, and max HP reaches +2300. Breakthrough Robe adds 20-40 magic attack plus 2% of bonus HP, and 30-60 magic penetration plus 3% of bonus HP. Augur's Word contributes 50-100 physical and magic defense plus 10% of magic attack. HP feeds damage and damage feeds defense, so bulk and output rise together.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Penetration and pace
builds.condition: When the enemy fields high magic defense or a healer you need to shut down
builds.notes: Boots of the Arcane opens with 60-120 magic penetration, and Void Staff closes the build by raising that penetration another 45%. Venomous Staff, third in the order, cuts an enemy's healing and lifesteal by 35% for 2.5 seconds once you land a hit. Movement speed reaches +17.5%, 7.5 points above build 1, and the full set costs 10,980G, 760G less. Less bulk, more penetration and pace.

name: Dun
title: Dun Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A defensive tank whose healing awakens below half Health — he wins by refusing to finish dying. A stunning chain-blade and area shield round out a kit built for weathering storms.
playstyle: A defensive tank whose healing awakens below half Health — he wins by refusing to finish dying. A stunning chain-blade and area shield round out a kit built for weathering storms.
bestFor: players strongest in the defensive hour — the healing only wakes below half Health and returns once every 25 seconds, so budget that window and pick your moment to throw the chain.

tips.earlyGame: Your Clash Lane game plan starts with landing Skill 1's shockwave. Connect the first hit and the second cast's knock-up follows, letting you clear the wave and harass your lane opponent in one motion — that is what makes Dun's laning so comfortable. Don't be afraid to take even trades below 50% HP, since your Passive kicks in and refunds the damage through on-hit healing. Just remember it only triggers once every 25 seconds; the moment it's spent, take a step back so you don't get run down. Once you hit level 4 and unlock your Ultimate, a coordinated dive with your jungler generates real kill pressure.
tips.midGame: From the 4-minute Tyrant fight onward, your Ultimate's stun and pull is your team's engage button. The priority targets are the enemy jungler or mid laner — but the chain blade stops on the first thing it touches, so never throw it through a screen of minions or frontliners. In fights, cycle Skill 2's shield and your empowered basic attacks: every hit shaves a second off your Ultimate's cooldown, setting up your next catch. With one or two defensive items online, Dun doesn't fold to a bit of focus fire.
tips.lateGame: By the time your third defensive item is finished, you're playing pure engage tank. Your single most important job is landing the one-second stun on the enemy carry and pulling your team in behind it. Decide your escape route before you throw, so a miss doesn't turn into a death. In standoffs before Overlord or Shadow Tyrant, an ambush from a bush lands far more often than a face-to-face throw. Even after dumping your full combo, the shield and Passive healing let you survive one more exchange — that's what makes late-game Dun so dependable.
tips.teamfight: Open every teamfight with an Ultimate catch. On hit, the pull puts you point-blank, so stack Skill 1's two-part knock-up on top, throw up Skill 2's shield, and simply refuse to leave the enemy's side of the fight. You're immune to crowd control while the Ultimate is active, so nothing they do can stop your entry. Keep landing empowered basics and the Ultimate comes back faster than you'd expect — throwing it twice in one fight is common. Staying alive is priority one: cutting off the enemy carry's escape route beats chasing kills every time.

strengths: Reliable pick potential with the Ultimate's one-second stun and pull
Excellent frontline staying power from stacking the shield with Passive healing
True damage on empowered basics punishes armor stackers
Crowd control immunity during the Ultimate makes his engage unstoppable
weaknesses: Skill 3 stops on minions and rarely reaches its real target in messy fights
Passive healing has a 25-second cooldown, leaving him weak in back-to-back fights
His only mobility is Skill 3's pull — miss it and long-range kiting goes unanswered

counteredBy.name: Lu Bu
counteredBy.reason: Lu Bu brings true damage or Physical Pierce either way, so Dun's Health and defense stop neither.

counteredBy.name: Diaochan
counteredBy.reason: Diaochan stacks floral marks from outside Dun's reach, and their true damage detonation ignores his defense.

synergies.name: Li Bai
synergies.reason: Li Bai can dash in on Dun's stun, build Sword Energy, and then return to where he started.

synergies.name: Arli
synergies.reason: Arli can spend her parasol-less speed window attacking rather than escaping, since Dun dives in ahead of her.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Physical Defense First, Regen Stacked
builds.condition: When the enemy's main damage is physical and you want to hold the front line.
builds.notes: Frostscar's Embrace lands third, so +300 physical defense and 10% cooldown reduction are up by 4,800G. Fourth comes Eye of the Phoenix, which raises HP recovery by 5% for every 10% of HP lost. Add the +25 HP regen every five seconds from five Harmony arcana and Dun recovers faster the lower his HP falls. Totals of +913 physical defense and +5537 max HP sit 90 and 450 above build 2.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Magic Shield First
builds.condition: When two or more enemies on the draft deal magic damage.
builds.notes: Succubus Cloak takes the third slot, locking in +300 magic defense by 4,760G. It also grants a 400-800 (+7% bonus HP) magic damage shield every 15 seconds. Frostscar's Embrace slips to fifth, so its 10% cooldown reduction waits until 8,840G. Magic defense totals +550, a full 120 over build 1, and ten Hunt arcana add +10% movement speed.

name: Dunshan
title: Dunshan Guide: Combos, Counters & Strategy - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A support who uses Bastion either to dash in and shield a teammate or to become a turret on a tower, and catches enemies by tossing them behind him with Collision Course. Official difficulty: Hard.
playstyle: A support who uses Bastion either to dash in and shield a teammate or to become a turret on a tower, and catches enemies by tossing them behind him with Collision Course. Official difficulty: Hard.
bestFor: players who are fine handing movement to a teammate and focusing on aim: while sheltering, holding Basic Attack charges it for more range and lets you steer its direction. If you want the toss, you also need the habit of casting Collision Course before Bastion, not during it.

tips.earlyGame: The official recommendation is to level Bastion (Skill 1) first. Select a teammate and Dunshan dashes over to shelter them, giving the pair a combined 900 shield for 6 seconds. It costs 60 Mana on a 10-second cooldown. While sheltered, your teammate steers both heroes at 95% of the pair's average Movement Speed. Meanwhile, Moving Mountain turns Dunshan's Basic Attacks into ranged attacks that slow by 10% for 0.5s (20% at Level 15). Hold the button to charge them for more range and to aim the direction. Stay on the teammate you're roaming with and keep the slows coming.
tips.midGame: Once your team starts moving together in the mid game, use Collision Course to throw enemy heroes toward your side. It charges forward, picks up enemy heroes in front of Dunshan and tosses them behind him, dealing 300 physical damage to nearby targets (600 at Level 6). The cooldown is 10 seconds, 8 at Level 6. On landing, nearby enemies are stunned for 0.5s and enemy heroes take collision damage equal to 5% of their max Health. The charge stops when it hits an enemy hero, so check that no one stands between you and your target. The toss lands behind you, so charge with your team at your back to drop the enemy on their side. Cast during Bastion, it pushes enemies on its path aside instead of tossing them.
tips.lateGame: At Level 3, Allshield's cooldown drops to 32 seconds, its base damage rises to 340 and the slow reaches 50%. Dunshan gains brief crowd control immunity on cast, so enemy CC can't stop the slam. More extra Health means more passive damage and a bigger Bastion shield. When you're holding your base towers late, cast Bastion on an allied tower. It also works on any tower ruins, turning Dunshan into a turret for 6 seconds. He's untargetable, and he and the tower recover 125 Health per second (250 at Level 6). The tower also gets a 600 shield (1,200 at Level 6). Turret mode has its own 15-second cooldown (12 at Level 6), and recasting ends it early.
tips.teamfight: Open fights by sheltering the teammate most likely to be focused. The shield totals 900 between the two of you (1,800 at Level 6) and lasts 6 seconds. Your teammate can end it by dismounting or by using a movement skill with very long range. After 3 seconds Dunshan can end it too, refunding up to 50% of the cooldown depending on how long the shelter lasted. Meet divers with Allshield. The slam slows by 25% for 1s (Level 1), then the shield travels forward and launches enemies it touches for 0.5s. It also knocks down projectiles, so aim it across the path of shots heading for your backline.

strengths: Bastion on a teammate dashes Dunshan to them and shields both for a combined 900 for 6s, with more going to whichever hero has less Health (Level 1)
Bastion on an allied tower or any tower ruins turns him into an untargetable turret for 6s and gives the tower a 600 shield (Level 1)
Collision Course tosses enemy heroes in front of him to his back, and their landing stuns nearby enemies for 0.5s
Allshield grants brief crowd control immunity, then the shield travels forward, launching enemies for 0.5s and knocking down projectiles
weaknesses: While sheltering, the teammate controls movement for both heroes, at 95% of their average Movement Speed
A movement skill with very long range from the teammate ends the shelter, and Dunshan can only cancel it himself after 3s
Collision Course used during Bastion does not toss enemy heroes; it only pushes enemies out of his path
Both the Collision Course stun and the Allshield launch last only 0.5s, so enemies are free again quickly unless teammates follow up

counteredBy.name: Garo
counteredBy.reason: Garo's Basic Attacks and skills deal 50% extra damage against shields, so she strips the shields Dunshan hands out with Bastion quickly.

counteredBy.name: Zhuangzi
counteredBy.reason: Zhuangzi's Butterfly Effect cleanses crowd control from his teammates and makes them immune for 1.5s, undoing the stun after a Collision Course toss and blanking Allshield's knockback during that window.

synergies.name: Hou Yi
synergies.reason: Hou Yi has no movement skill and struggles to escape divers on his own. While Dunshan shelters him, Dunshan's Basic Attacks turn ranged and slow each enemy they hit as it closes in.

synergies.name: Wang Zhaojun
synergies.reason: Allshield knocks enemies back and slows them by 25–50% for 1s, so if Wang Zhaojun drops Frigid Prison where they land, they struggle to walk out before the delayed freeze hits.

name: Dyadia
title: Dyadia Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A matchmaker who ties fates — blessing allies who stay close and cursing enemies who stray near. Her swing keeps her safe while her bonds teach the team that proximity is power.
playstyle: A matchmaker who ties fates — blessing allies who stay close and cursing enemies who stray near. Her swing keeps her safe while her bonds teach the team that proximity is power.
bestFor: players who like steering other people's spacing — pulling allies together to trigger the blessing, taxing gold off enemies, and running the team from backstage.

tips.earlyGame: Dyadia opens the game glued to her jungler, not to a lane. Tag enemies with Skill 2 as you roam: the curse ticks damage, taxes gold off them every second, and shuts off stealth for 5 seconds, exposing bush ambushes as you walk in. Recast it and she dashes to the target for a 0.75-second root — sync that with your jungler's gank and you're manufacturing kills from level 2 or 3. Add the Passive's gold bonuses on top and this is a support who out-earns laners simply by staying in motion.
tips.midGame: From 8 to 12 minutes the job is vision around objectives and catching strays. Land the Skill 2 recast root, then follow with Skill 3: enemies already carrying the curse eat an extra 1-second root, for 1.75 seconds of total lockdown — long enough for your team's damage to arrive. When an ally gets chunked, double-tap Skill 1. Dyadia runs to them mid-cast and delivers 600 base healing across the two stages. The taxed gold is only held, never owned: the marked target reclaims 100% of it by killing her, 50% by assisting. It also goes back if two cursed enemies meet and trigger Bitter Reconciliation. Protecting your income comes down to one rule — don't die to the person you taxed.
tips.lateGame: Late game, your address is next to the carry. When an assassin dives, answer with the Passive's empowered basic: the swing knocks them back while its momentum carries you backward — peel (bodyguarding your carry) and self-peel in a single input. Thread Skill 3 down the middle of a forming brawl and one line delivers ally healing, enemy damage, and the bonus 1-second root on cursed targets all at once. The Skill 2 recast root is not a ranged tool — she dashes to the target to trigger it, so only reach for it while your team's damage still covers that ground. Stop one key enemy from there and the whole fight redraws.
tips.teamfight: Stand half a step ahead of your backline. Job one is meeting the enemy engage with the Skill 2 recast root — you take 25% reduced damage during it (doubled against the rooted target), so you can play braver than her stats suggest. From there, cycle Skill 1's two-stage healing into wounded allies and keep flicking divers away with the empowered basic. A survival note from real games: if your team doesn't turn onto the enemy you rooted, don't force it — take the backward hop and reset the distance instead.

strengths: Taxes gold off enemies — staying in motion converts into an economy lead
Two roots plus the knockback basic add up to serious lockdown and peel
The curse's stealth shutdown exposes ambushes and invisible heroes
Recast dashes stretch her healing and catch range surprisingly far
weaknesses: The taxed target reclaims 100% of the gold by killing her, 50% by assisting
The recast-centric kit makes split-second reactions awkward
Near-zero personal damage — roots go to waste if allies don't respond
The bond system takes real time to internalize

counteredBy.name: Gao Changgong
counteredBy.reason: Gao Changgong stays in stealth far longer than the exposure from Bitter Farewell lasts, so it expires first.

counteredBy.name: Liang
counteredBy.reason: Liang's Power Word - Control locks Dyadia in place, and fated bond simply expires while she stands there.

synergies.name: Lady Sun
synergies.reason: Lady Sun's Ultimate Shell needs a target that cannot move, and Destined Encounter pins enemies already carrying bitter bond.

synergies.name: Jing
synergies.reason: Jing's Mirror Domain gathers enemies into one spot and pins them, so Destined Encounter sweeps the whole clump.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Team attack speed aura, physical defense
builds.condition: When the enemy threat is mostly physical and your team wins on volume of attacks
builds.notes: Crimson Shadow - Redemption goes down first for 20% attack speed and 15% cooldown reduction, with half of that passed to allies within 800 range. Ominous Premonition in the fourth slot adds 300 physical defense, taking the totals to +373 physical defense and +5687 max HP. Damage taken cuts the attacker's attack speed by 20-40% and movement speed by 7.5-15%, on a 3-second cooldown per target. Frozen Breath at fifth adds 75-150 plus 15% of magic attack as magic damage every 3 seconds, stacking a slow on top.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Guard aura, freeze, HP feeds penetration
builds.condition: When enemies stack magic defense and you want to open fights yourself
builds.notes: Guardian - Redemption leads, adding 65-130 physical and magic defense and passing half of it to allies within 800 range. Frigid Charge in the fourth slot carries an active that cuts enemy movement speed by 30-60% inside 450 range and freezes for 0.75 seconds. Breakthrough Robe at sixth adds 3% of bonus HP as magic defense penetration, and +5787 max HP pushes that straight to the 150 cap. Physical defense lands at +223 against build 1's +373 - the armor given up goes into penetration and lockdown.

name: Erin
title: Erin Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An elven archer cycling energy and laurel marks to keep her empowered shots flowing. When the gears mesh her damage soars; when management slips, the whole engine audibly stalls.
playstyle: An elven archer cycling energy and laurel marks to keep her empowered shots flowing. When the gears mesh her damage soars; when management slips, the whole engine audibly stalls.
bestFor: tidy players. Energy and Laurel stacks are the damage — keep the order of shoot, glide, refill intact and the output never dips.

tips.earlyGame: Spend the first four minutes in the farm lane doing nothing but securing last hits. Erin is built around an unusual scaling scheme — magic attack raises both her move speed and her skill rotation — so finishing that first magic item is her real first power spike. Skill 1 is your harass tool: it stacks laurel marks on hit and deploys a slowing ring. Manage energy on a rhythm of one glide per three basic attacks and you'll stay half a step faster than the opposing marksman at all times.
tips.midGame: Around the 10-minute mark, two completed magic items plus the Ultimate unlocking at 6 marks send her sustained damage through the roof. In Tyrant fights and skirmishes, gliding half a step off an enemy skill's flight path cuts your damage taken dramatically. When you get ganked, Skill 2 is the lifeline: it refills energy, grants slow immunity, and boosts attack speed all at once, which is enough to outrun one full rotation of chase. You're fragile while it's on cooldown, so pick the moment carefully.
tips.lateGame: Erin approaching full build is the whole point of picking her. Her penetration and lifesteal apply whichever of physical or magic is higher, so her damage goes through any defensive itemization and she rarely loses an extended DPS race. Always fight from behind your frontline. Don't overthink targeting either — hit the nearest safe enemy, and the Ultimate's leaves will chase down the lowest-HP target on their own. Her win condition is uptime, not burst: staying alive and firing is the play.
tips.teamfight: Hold the perimeter and settle into the rhythm of basic attack, glide, basic attack. When an assassin dives you, hit Skill 2 to speed up, ignore their slows, and slide behind your frontline. The Ultimate's leaves keep flying while you retreat, so your damage never actually stops. One habit worth building: don't glide just because you're pressured. Wait until you've seen one enemy dash skill before spending energy on movement, and you'll still have some banked when it really matters.

strengths: Magic attack raises her basic-attack damage and her glide speed at once
Glides plus slow immunity give her some of the best escapes of any marksman
Skill 3's leaves hunt the lowest-HP enemy and secure cleanup on their own
No mana - she camps lane indefinitely and out-farms her opposite number
weaknesses: Low burst, so out-damaging heals and shields takes real time
Loses all mobility the instant her energy runs dry
No answer to point-and-click CC — getting caught means dying
Heavily item-dependent, with little teamfight presence before 10 minutes

counteredBy.name: Lam
counteredBy.reason: Lam's pull drags Erin in regardless of her slow immunity, so she cannot hold her distance.

counteredBy.name: Mai Shiranui
counteredBy.reason: Mai Shiranui's low-cooldown KACHOUSEN strips Erin's magical defense and keeps chipping her down.

synergies.name: Dun
synergies.reason: Dun's stun and launch pin enemies in place, letting Erin fire freely from the back line.

synergies.name: Xiang Yu
synergies.reason: Xiang Yu peels divers off Erin and cuts enemy damage output, so she survives being focused.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Magic penetration first
builds.condition: When the enemy fields two or more frontliners and you need to keep firing through them.
builds.notes: The one difference is Void Staff, bought fourth with Tempest pushed back to fifth. That puts +210 magic attack and 45% magic penetration on the board at 6,880G. Stacked with the 60-120 from Boots of the Arcane and the +64 from ten Mind's Eye slots, the 160-400 jolt Sparkforged Dagger throws every third basic attack lands through magic defense. Ten Fate and ten Reaver slots take the totals to +2837 max HP and 36% physical lifesteal, so Erin can stand in the trade.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Crit and physical penetration
builds.condition: When the enemy front line is thin and the backline needs to die fast.
builds.notes: Tempest moves up to fourth here, bringing the attack speed and movement speed stacks online at 6,920G. Daybreaker's Virtue, the one item the other build lacks, costs 2,570G and waits until 9,490G. Erin is ranged, so the bow doubles: 30% physical penetration and +50 on basic attack damage. Ten Calamity slots on top of the bow's own 15% put crit at +31%, with +280 physical attack and +123% attack speed overall.

name: Fang
title: Fang Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A rhythm-based marksman who detonates dark marks on every fourth stack. His chakram dash turns him untargetable mid-fight, and his tornado claims ground with lasting damage.
playstyle: A rhythm-based marksman who detonates dark marks on every fourth stack. His chakram dash turns him untargetable mid-fight, and his tornado claims ground with lasting damage.
bestFor: shooting in four-counts. Four marks, detonate, repeat — and the chakram dash doubles as your dodge, so escaping and attacking come from one input.

tips.earlyGame: Fang works in the farm lane or the jungle, and either way the game plan is the same: four mark stacks, instant detonation. In lane, hit Skill 1 for the attack speed and range boost, land four basic attacks on your opponent, and watch the trade swing hard your way. His Passive adds bonus damage against monsters, so as a jungler he burns down the four-minute Tyrant about as fast as anyone in the game. That same Passive reveals enemy heroes lurking nearby, which makes bush ambushes far easier to smell out. Whatever you do, keep Skill 2 in reserve as your escape.
tips.midGame: From around seven minutes, with one or two damage items finished, you become an objective monster — the monster bonus and mark detonations stack up, and Tyrant and Overlord visibly melt a size faster under your shots. When a teammate catches someone, the standard play is dropping your Ultimate's tornado on their escape route to box them in. Damage inside the tornado is doubled and tornado ticks also stack marks, so layered with Skill 1, squishy targets rarely make it out. Just remember Skill 2 is your only self-defense tool; spend it with care.
tips.lateGame: Late game Fang designs teamfights around tornado placement. Pre-place it on the tight terrain in front of Shadow Tyrant and the enemy must either eat the doubled-damage core or break formation walking around it. Past ten minutes, cut back on solo play: Skill 2's untargetable dash is excellent, but the seconds after it's spent leave you genuinely defenseless, and getting caught there kills you through any item lead. In sieges, mark detonations splash onto enemies packed under the tower, so lean on your front line and grind forward together.
tips.teamfight: Open every teamfight with the tornado. Place it where the enemy back line will retreat — or where your front line will shove them — and let the five-plus seconds of doubled damage shrink the battlefield. From there, boost your attack speed with Skill 1 and stack marks off everything the tornado touches; a brawl with chained four-stack detonations is Fang's private playground. When assassins dive, slip through them with Skill 2, leave the burning trail's slow behind, and re-position behind your front line. The detonations are area damage — the tighter the enemy clumps, the harder you hit.

strengths: Mark detonations plus a monster bonus give elite objective speed
Skill 2's untargetable dash dodges burst skills outright
Doubled damage inside the tornado dominates tight-quarters fights
Passive reveals lurking enemies, defusing bush ambushes
weaknesses: Damage depends on stacking marks; single-hit burst is modest
Badly exposed after Skill 2 is spent and melts to focus fire
Late-game sustained damage trails pure basic-attack marksmen
If enemies sidestep the tornado, his teamfight control halves

counteredBy.name: Dun
counteredBy.reason: Dun chains a launch into a stun, leaving Fang no window to shoot back.

counteredBy.name: Di Renjie
counteredBy.reason: Di Renjie's Legal Immunity gives him a brief window where nothing lands, so Fang's burst whiffs on him.

synergies.name: Liu Shan
synergies.reason: Liu Shan's stun pins enemies in place, letting Fang land Bladestorm's double-damage center right on them.

synergies.name: Zhang Fei
synergies.reason: Zhang Fei's shield lets Fang hold his ground under fire and finish stacking Dark Marks.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: 70% attack speed and healing cut
builds.condition: When the enemy team heals or lifesteals its way through fights
builds.notes: Only the fourth slot differs across the six items. Mortal Punisher costs 2,080G and brings the running total to 7,030G, adding 20% attack speed. Anything it hits loses 35% of its health recovery and lifesteal for 2.5 seconds. Finished, the build carries +425 physical attack, +100 physical pierce and 70% attack speed, twenty points above build 2.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: 25% lifesteal and +1900 max health
builds.condition: When the enemy team has divers and you must keep firing while taking hits
builds.notes: Same build with Bloodweeper in the fourth slot. It costs 2,000G for 25% physical lifesteal and +500 max health, putting the running total at 6,950G. Its passive adds another 25% physical lifesteal on skill damage. Max health finishes at +1900, five hundred above build 1, while attack speed settles at 50% and physical attack at +405.

name: Fatih
title: Fatih Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A berserker who stacks empowered attacks by cycling skills, healing as he swings. His crowd-control-immune ultimate plants him in the center of the fight, out-sustaining the damage aimed at him.
playstyle: A berserker who stacks empowered attacks by cycling skills, healing as he swings. His crowd-control-immune ultimate plants him in the center of the fight, out-sustaining the damage aimed at him.
bestFor: players who want to be the last one standing in the middle — casts bank empowered attacks, the hits heal you back, and the ultimate grows with every enemy nearby, so never plan an exit.

tips.earlyGame: Fatih's Clash Lane edge is a healing trade: land Skill 2 on the enemy laner and 200 HP comes right back. Until level 4, the loop is simple — tag your opponent with the sword wave, win the sustain war, and reset with your Passive's empowered basic attacks whenever you get chipped. Skill 1 stores three casts, but burning all three every time is a mistake: stop at one or two and each unspent cast refunds 35% of the cooldown, letting you out-tempo your opponent on rotations. Bank the third cast's knock-up as self-defense for when the enemy jungler shows up — it visibly cuts down on early deaths.
tips.midGame: The moment you learn your Ultimate at level 4 is your first real power spike. It grants crowd control immunity, raises your max HP, and — crucially — the HP bonus grows another 20% per nearby enemy hero, so you can win skirmishes even against two opponents. While it's active, Skill 2 and your empowered basics each fire an extra sword wave, and your effective damage jumps to roughly 1.5 times normal. Be the first one into the Tyrant-fight scrum and brawl while you heal. Basic attacks also shave Skill 2's cooldown on hit, so never stop swinging — that's the secret to his staying power.
tips.lateGame: Late game you're a dual threat: side-lane pushing and teamfighting. Almost nobody stops a five-item Fatih head-on, so welcome anyone foolish enough to duel you. One catch: your healing only pays full value against heroes — it's halved on minions — so recovering HP by farming a lane takes longer than you'd think. Before a big fight, don't get greedy; recall and reset. You are at your absolute strongest during the Ultimate's 8-second window and noticeably softer once it drops, so commit to finishing fights inside it.
tips.teamfight: The advanced play is holding your Ultimate instead of opening with it — pop it the instant enemy CC is aimed your way, and the immunity lets you walk straight through their lockdown into the middle of their team. From there, spray long-range empowered basics and bonus sword waves; there are stretches where your healing genuinely outpaces their damage. Any nearby squishy target is a fine focus, but don't chase deep — the second your Ultimate expires, focus fire melts you. When in doubt, just stand next to your frontline and keep swinging. The enemy formation cracks on its own.

strengths: Every skill cast banks an empowered basic and 35% bonus attack speed
The Ultimate's HP bonus scales per nearby enemy — tankier when outnumbered
Outstanding sustain from Skill 2's on-hit healing plus empowered basics
Smart Skill 1 charge management massively compresses his cooldowns
weaknesses: Healing requires hitting heroes, so he slowly bleeds out in poke wars
Noticeably squishier whenever the Ultimate is down
Lacks a gap closer and has no answer to enemies who keep their distance

counteredBy.name: Lu Bu
counteredBy.reason: Lu Bu's ring of Tremble, Mortals hands him heavy defenses, so Fatih's purely physical damage cannot break him.

counteredBy.name: Mulan
counteredBy.reason: Mulan's Balance stacks detonate into a silence, and Fatih cannot answer with Sacred Tree Blessing.

synergies.name: Donghuang
synergies.reason: Donghuang's suppression freezes a target completely, so Fatih can land every slash of The King's Blade on it.

synergies.name: Guiguzi
synergies.reason: Guiguzi's pull bunches enemy heroes together, so Sacred Tree Blessing grants Fatih more max Health for each one nearby.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Cooldowns first, 45% total
builds.condition: When enemy slows and silences are scarce and you want more attacks going out early.
builds.notes: Boots of Tranquility open with 15% cooldown reduction, and the three cooldown items stacked on top of them take the total to 45%. Frostscar's Embrace lands third at 4,850G, adding 210-420 physical damage to the next basic attack within 5 seconds of a cast. Succubus Cloak moves up to fifth, one slot earlier than in build 2, so 300 magic defense and a shield every 15 seconds are up by 9,010G. Totals reach 303 physical attack and 96.4 physical defense penetration.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Resistances and tenacity first
builds.condition: When enemy slows and silences pile up and you plan to trade up front.
builds.notes: Boots of Resistance open with 50 physical defense, 100 magic defense and 25% tenacity, cutting how long crowd control holds Fatih. Pure Sky comes third rather than fourth, so the 20% damage reduction on a skill hit is up by 4,930G. Doomsday also moves earlier, giving 20% physical lifesteal from 9,090G onward. Defenses finish at 500 physical and 400 magic, a step above build 1.

name: Feyd
title: Feyd Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An assassin who walks on walls, claiming a vertical dimension no one else can use. Ranged attacks from above and sudden drops give him attack lines that simply don't exist for grounded heroes.
playstyle: An assassin who walks on walls, claiming a vertical dimension no one else can use. Ranged attacks from above and sudden drops give him attack lines that simply don't exist for grounded heroes.
bestFor: players who find value in the space nobody else uses — scouting and poking from the wall layer, and accepting that crowd control lasts 25% longer up there.

tips.earlyGame: Feyd's wall-walking Passive is one of a kind, and you should lean on it from minute one. Clear your jungle, then scout the enemy's farm state from the walls before level 4 — you get 15% wider vision up there and your basic attacks become ranged, so you're poking and gathering information at zero risk. The standard gank is Skill 2 onto a wall, then Skill 1 to drop down and land the 0.75-second knock-up. One caveat to burn into memory: slows and CC applied to you last 25% longer while you're standing on a wall.
tips.midGame: Around 8 minutes, once your first physical damage item is finished, the side-lane walls become your hunting grounds. Roam wall to wall with at least two Skill 2 stacks in reserve (you bank one every 10 seconds, up to four), and when you spot a low-HP target, unload the full kit: Skill 1, three empowered basic attacks, the Ultimate's mark, then its follow-up strike. Any enemy below 1/8 HP dies to that strike guaranteed — Feyd never knows the pain of a kill escaping on a sliver. Front-on brawls are not his game, so kill and leave, every time.
tips.lateGame: From 15 minutes on, commit to entering fights late. Dive in at the start and his lack of bulk gets exposed, so perch on a wall, wait for a few enemy CC abilities to be spent, then drop. Your target list is short: the isolated marksman or mage, nobody else. Skill 1's drop knock-up leads into empowered basics (which heal you at melee range), and the Ultimate's mark plus follow-up strike closes the deal. When you're down to your last Skill 2 stack, stop chasing and save it for the trip back to a wall — that discipline is what keeps you alive.
tips.teamfight: Skip the head-on collision entirely and time your entrance from the outer walls. The moment enemy eyes lock onto your frontline, drop in from the side and put Skill 1 into a backliner. Skill 3's sweep marks everything it touches, and the follow-up, Hardened Jade Strike, ignores untargetable states as it shatters those marks. An enemy who goes untargetable to slip away still takes it, so long as the mark is on them. Take the kill, Skill 2 back to a wall, and reset for the next pick. A trick that pays real dividends: choose a wall along the enemy's escape route before the fight starts — the kills you collect go up noticeably.

strengths: Wall movement plus ranged basics enable zero-risk scouting and poke
Skill 3's execute guarantees kills below 1/8 HP — nothing slips away
The follow-up strike shatters marks even through untargetable states
Skill 1's knock-up and 50% attack speed give brutal short-window stickiness
weaknesses: Slows and CC on him last 25% longer while he is standing on a wall
Mobility falls off a cliff once his Skill 2 stacks run dry
No stats for front-on brawling — late fight entries are mandatory
Struggles to show his identity in open areas with few walls

counteredBy.name: Liang
counteredBy.reason: Liang's suppression lasts even longer on Feyd while he stands on a wall, leaving him stuck.

counteredBy.name: Donghuang
counteredBy.reason: While Donghuang suppresses Feyd, the two share all damage, so even Feyd's allies end up hurting him.

synergies.name: Diaochan
synergies.reason: Diaochan's marks detonate into a slow, which is exactly when Feyd's dash lands cleanly.

synergies.name: Mulan
synergies.reason: Mulan's Balance detonation silences and heavily slows enemies, so Feyd can seal the whole group at once.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Attack speed first
builds.condition: When the enemy fields at most one magic damage dealer and you want long basic-attack windows.
builds.notes: Boots of Dexterity go second for 700G, putting 20% attack speed in hand by 2,860G. Pure Sky adds 150 physical defense fifth, along with an active that cuts incoming damage by 30% for 3 seconds. Totals reach 388 physical attack, 56.6% attack speed and 96.4 physical defense penetration, with magic defense still at zero. Only these two items differ from build 2 - the arcana are identical.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Thicker defense and HP
builds.condition: When two or more enemies deal magic damage and you get focused in fights.
builds.notes: Boots of Resistance cost the same 700G but bring 50 physical defense, 100 magic defense and 25% more tenacity. Dragon's Rage lands fifth, adding 1,350 max HP plus a passive that deals 3.5% HP as physical damage to enemy heroes. Totals come to 2,950 max HP, 210 physical defense and 180 magic defense. Physical attack sits 80 lower at 308, and attack speed stops at 36.6%.

name: Florentino
title: Florentino Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A fencer who scatters bouquets and weaves between them, each pickup refreshing his empowered strikes. He duels by designing routes through his own flowers — elegant to watch, demanding to pilot.
playstyle: A fencer who scatters bouquets and weaves between them, each pickup refreshing his empowered strikes. He duels by designing routes through his own flowers — elegant to watch, demanding to pilot.
bestFor: players who choreograph their footwork mid-fight, since every bouquet touched refreshes Triple Threat and the route between the flowers is the combo.

tips.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Level 1 starts with Skill 1. The 0.75-second stun sprouts three flowers around your target, so collect them mid-stun, then chain enhanced basic attack into Skill 2 for a trade loaded with true damage that your opponent simply cannot match. The enhanced basic heals 140 HP when it strikes a hero, which means the longer the slugfest runs, the wider the HP gap grows — that's the Florentino experience. Once the Ultimate arrives at Level 4, the mark's 10% bonus damage taken plus crowd control immunity makes your duels nearly unloseable. Just pick flower routes on the side ganks can't reach.
tips.midGame: Around nine minutes, with your first two core items finished, it's time to move. Chip the enemy tower down, then show up mid: Skill 3's dash into the flower loop makes you a one-man gank engine. In the standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, one Skill 1 threaded from a river bush is enough to take a pick. When nothing is happening, splitting side towers is genuinely one of your best uses of time. Watch your sustain, though — the enhanced basic's healing is halved against minions, so don't loiter in a lane at low HP expecting to heal it back.
tips.lateGame: With a frost gauntlet and a sustain piece rounding out your build, the late game rewards duels over head-on 5v5s. Pressure a side lane, then catch whoever comes to answer with Skill 3 and finish them — that's the golden pattern. At rank 3 the mark raises their damage taken by 20%, and cycling Skill 2's true damage through flower pickups on a target like that kills even tanks on a timer. The only real threat is getting surrounded. Crowd control immunity runs 3 seconds and extends 1 second per bouquet you touch, but that ceiling is real — CC timed for the moment it drops will still put you down.
tips.teamfight: You are not the frontal engage. Wait in a side bush, let the enemy's CC land on your frontline, then commit the Ultimate onto their backline. The dash blooms three flowers on arrival, so once you land, dance the loop — flower, Skill 2, flower, Skill 2 — and your damage never pauses. While the Ultimate runs, enhanced basic healing doubles, letting you shrug off a surprising amount of focus mid-combo. Your one losing script is getting burst before the first flower pickup. In the instant before you dive, check what skills the enemy still has up — every time.

strengths: Flower pickups reset Skill 2 endlessly, cycling true damage nonstop
Enhanced-basic healing — doubled during the Ultimate — wins any slugfest
The dash's crowd control immunity forces 1v1s on his terms
Constant dashes and bonus moves make roams and split pushes fast
weaknesses: Miss Skill 1 and no flowers bloom — the combo loses its front door
Flower spots are predictable; CC placed on the pickup path shreds him
Few answers to long-range poke and disciplined kiting
Flower tracking and micro-movement demand real practice time

counteredBy.name: Donghuang
counteredBy.reason: Donghuang's Forsaken Contract suppresses Florentino, cutting off Triple Threat's chain and his bouquet pickups.

counteredBy.name: Liang
counteredBy.reason: Liang's Power Word - Barrier walls off the approach, and the stun on contact cuts Florentino's dash short.

synergies.name: Zhuangzi
synergies.reason: Zhuangzi's Butterfly Effect strips crowd control from allies, so a pinned Florentino can move and fight again.

synergies.name: Guiguzi
synergies.reason: Guiguzi's The Animist pulls enemies into one spot, so Blossom's bouquets land right in that pile and keep refreshing Triple Threat.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Pierce and uptime to grind tanks down
builds.condition: When the enemy front line is thick and you need attrition to break it.
builds.notes: Boots of Tranquility open at 700G with 15% Cooldown Reduction, and the finished build reaches 50%. All 100 points of Physical Pierce come from the Mutation and Eagle Eye arcana, so it is live before the first item lands. Overlord's Might closes the build with 30% bonus damage against enemies under 50% HP. With 660 Physical Defense and 2000 Max Health behind him, Florentino can hold the front and finish the job.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Stacked health for long trades
builds.condition: When the enemy team leans physical and you want to keep trading up front.
builds.notes: Boots of Fortitude lead, cutting physical damage taken by 6-12% from 700G onward. Axe of Torment lands third, putting 90-180 Physical Pierce online at the 4,930G mark. Max Health reaches 2500, and Blood Rage converts it: every basic attack deals bonus physical damage equal to 1.5% of bonus health. Calamity and Compassion arcana finish it with 16% Critical Rate and 10% Cooldown Reduction.

name: Flowborn (Assassin)
title: Flowborn (Assassin) Guide: Combos, Counters & Strategy - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A jungle assassin that chains dashes which heal on landing near enemies, diving into ganks and teamfights. Official difficulty: Easy.
playstyle: A jungle assassin that chains dashes which heal on landing near enemies, diving into ganks and teamfights. Official difficulty: Easy.
bestFor: players who can land Claw Flurry right next to an enemy, since it only heals and strikes when one is near where it ends. If tracking Flow stacks and Skill 1's cooldown together still feels busy, cycling just Skill 1 and Skill 2 is enough to start.

tips.earlyGame: Official HoK Camp data lists Flowborn (Assassin) as a jungler. Start on the red or blue buff and head straight for Level 4, when your ultimate unlocks. Claw Flurry's healing is halved against monsters, but it still restores 150 at Level 1, so you keep your Health up as you clear. Cast alone in the jungle, Convergence gives only its base healing and Flow. Cast it while a teammate helps with your first camp, and both go up. Your first gank comes at Level 4 with Mortal Talons. You have no stun or slow of your own, so start with lanes where your laner has crowd control.
tips.midGame: Before a gank, cast Convergence next to your minions or your laner. The more of them nearby, the more Flow you gain, up to 9 stacks, and that decides how many bonus casts you get. With 8 stacks you can fire Claw Flurry three times in a row, and the third becomes Cutthroat. Cutthroat adds 10% of the target's lost Health, so it hits hardest on targets your team has already worn down. The Tyrant and Overlord both spawn at 4:00; stock up next to your team before contesting them too. Invade the enemy jungle alone and Convergence yields only 5 stacks, which covers a single bonus cast.
tips.lateGame: Late in the game, leave the initiation to your frontline. You fight at melee range with no way to hold an enemy in place, so going in first tends to get you surrounded before you reach the backline. Go for backliners your team has chipped, or anyone who has stepped too far forward. Mortal Talons gives you crowd control immunity as you dash, so you can still get in while the enemy holds crowd control. Keep 5 stacks of Flow in reserve and you can cast Mortal Talons again to get out after the kill. Claw Flurry works as an escape too, but fired away from enemies it restores no Health.
tips.teamfight: Before the fight, cast Convergence near your team and stock as much Flow as you can (up to 9). Let your frontline open, and wait on the flank. Dive the enemy backline with Mortal Talons; the knockback at the destination scatters anyone bunched up. Recast Claw Flurry within 2 seconds each time and finish the weakened target with Cutthroat. Each Claw Flurry that lands near an enemy restores 300 Health at Level 1, so you can hold out while surrounded as long as the casts keep coming. When you run dry, weave in Convergence: it pushes nearby enemies back, cuts the cooldowns of Claw Flurry and Mortal Talons by 50%, and returns at least 5 stacks of Flow.

strengths: Claw Flurry restores 300 Health (Level 1) each time it lands near an enemy, sustaining deep dives
Convergence cuts the cooldowns of Claw Flurry and Mortal Talons by 50%, bringing both dashes back sooner
Mortal Talons dashes in with crowd control immunity, so enemies holding CC can't stop the dive
Cutthroat adds 10% of the target's lost Health, making wounded targets easy to finish
weaknesses: Claw Flurry neither heals nor strikes without an enemy near its endpoint, so a miss is just movement
No stun or slow; Flowborn can only knock enemies back or pull them in slightly
Melee range, and every skill needs Flowborn close to the target
Bonus casts depend on Flow stacks; run dry and the chain gets shorter

counteredBy.name: Musashi
counteredBy.reason: Musashi's duel delays Flowborn's healing until it ends, so Claw Flurry's recovery can't keep them in the fight.

counteredBy.name: Arthur
counteredBy.reason: Arthur dashes in with a silencing strike, and Flowborn, whose healing and dashes all come from skills, loses both while silenced.

synergies.name: Guiguzi
synergies.reason: Guiguzi's ultimate camouflages nearby teammates too, so Flowborn can get within Claw Flurry range unseen.

synergies.name: Kui
synergies.reason: Kui hooks an enemy and keeps it stunned with his ultimate, so Flowborn can chain Claw Flurry on a pinned target.

name: Flowborn (Mage)
title: Flowborn (Mage) Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A turret mage who picks their own stat upgrades through Flow selection. The beam and the three-stage orb are simple area control — a polished template of the mage role.
playstyle: A turret mage who picks their own stat upgrades through Flow selection. The beam and the three-stage orb are simple area control — a polished template of the mage role.
bestFor: players who like re-picking their build direction match to match. The piloting stays light: recasting Skill 2 inside two seconds supplies its own stun. Fire without counting Flow stacks, though, and the bonus cast is missing exactly when it is needed.

tips.earlyGame: Your game starts before you leave the fountain: pick the Flow boon at base. The cooldown option (5-10% CDR) is the default for combo uptime, while the magic-pierce boon punishes opponents who stack magic defense. In mid lane, Skill 2's orb is the chip damage — it detonates on a hero or a monster, or when it reaches the end of its path. It passes through minions, but piercing one shortens the fuse, so clearing the wave and touching the laner behind it rarely happen in the same cast. Decide which one you want before you fire. Treat Skill 1 less as a weapon and more as fuel: it cuts the cooldowns of Skill 2 and the Ultimate by 50% and restocks Flow, so fire it during safe windows while the wave sits on your side and you will never run dry at the 4-minute Tyrant fight. Until the Ultimate arrives at Level 4, winning the chip war is the whole job — don't force kills.
tips.midGame: Around eight minutes, once cooldown boots and a magic-pierce staff are finished, a single orb starts taking frightening chunks out of people. The job now is recasting inside the two-second window to supply your own crowd control. The first cast slows 25% for 0.75s. The second, Dual Radiance, stuns for a third of a second; the third, Orb Volley, stuns for 0.5s and widens the radius by 25. Flow caps at nine stacks, so the iron rule is topping off with Skill 1 before every fight. Walk in empty and the four-stack bonus cast never comes, along with half your output.
tips.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, holding the full combo in reserve becomes the win condition. With magic attack scaled through the final core items, Orb Volley's 0.5s stun into Skill 3's beam drops anyone with marksman-grade durability. Skill 3 lets you cast other skills mid-channel, so the ideal picture is holding the beam while firing fresh orbs. If someone dives you, you are not empty-handed: Skill 1 knocks them back, Skill 2 slows, and the follow-up casts stun twice. Four Flow stacks keep Skill 2 off cooldown entirely, so how many times you can shove a diver away comes down to the stack count. What Flowborn does not have is a dash or a blink — the moment they stand ahead of the frontline is the moment they die. When setting up before Overlord, always keep a wall and your teammates at your back.
tips.teamfight: Open every fight from the absolute backline. Skip the enemy tank; land Skill 2 on the fighter pushing into your carries, then chain the second and third casts' stuns to freeze their front. Once you see an enemy blink go down, commit the Ultimate — its beam links to the enemies around it and keeps ticking every 0.2 seconds. A Skill 2 paid for with four Flow stacks never touches its cooldown, so you can keep firing as long as stacks remain; that loop is the whole point of this hero. When you're spent, don't chase — fall back and let Skill 1's healing patch you up.

strengths: Spending Flow stacks lets Skill 2 and the Ultimate ignore cooldowns entirely
Recasting Skill 2 supplies two stuns with no outside help
Casting other skills during the Ultimate's beam packs absurd damage density
Skill 1's healing and cooldown cut give far more staying power than expected
weaknesses: No mobility skill — once Skill 1's small knockback is baited, nothing else peels
Damage ceiling depends heavily on precise nine-stack Flow management
Skill 1's stack income and healing shrink without teammates nearby
Skill 2 is a straight-line orb, so stepping sideways lets it pass by

counteredBy.name: Jing
counteredBy.reason: Jing's paired marks reset the dash she engages with, so Flowborn can never keep her at range.

counteredBy.name: Liang
counteredBy.reason: Liang's circles claim the ground, and a turret mage like Flowborn gets whittled down standing in them.

synergies.name: Zhang Fei
synergies.reason: Zhang Fei's shield and his wind's stun buy the stationary Flowborn the time to finish Arcane Arts.

synergies.name: Lian Po
synergies.reason: Lian Po's crowd control immunity guarantees the launch at the end of Tremor Smash, pinning targets for Starflow Cascade.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: HP and lifesteal to keep casting
builds.condition: When two or more high-HP frontliners are on the enemy team and fights run long
builds.notes: Boots of the Arcane go down first at 700G, locking in 60-120 magic penetration and 50 movement speed before anything else. Twilight Stream in slot four adds 20-40 penetration every time you damage an enemy hero, reaching 240 at six stacks. Insatiable Tome in slot five brings 24% magic lifesteal, and its Mana Conversion passive turns that into 12% more cooldown reduction. Mask of Agony closes the build, dealing 3% of the target's current HP four times over three seconds, and +2650 max HP keeps you in range.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Stacking magic attack for the burst
builds.condition: When the enemy has at most one frontliner and fights are settled quickly
builds.notes: Sage's Tome at 2610G in slot three and Savant's Wrath in slot four put raw magic attack ahead of everything else. Savant's Wrath raises magic attack by 30%, so the Venomous Staff and Void Staff bought after it are worth more than their listed numbers. The total reaches +1222 magic attack, 350 above build 1, and Void Staff finishes by raising magic penetration 45%. Slot one is Boots of Deftness at 70 movement speed rather than the penetration boots, with another 35-70 after five seconds out of combat.

name: Flowborn (Marksman)
title: Flowborn (Marksman) Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A clean, honest marksman whose individuality lives in Flow selection — choose your own stat growth, then fight with a big arrow and an arrow storm anyone can understand.
playstyle: A clean, honest marksman whose individuality lives in Flow selection — choose your own stat growth, then fight with a big arrow and an arrow storm anyone can understand.
bestFor: learning marksman fundamentals at a low execution cost — a big arrow, an arrow storm, and one real choice: the Flow you pick back at base.

tips.earlyGame: Pick your Flow boon at base, then head for the farm lane. Take the max-HP option (300 HP) into aggressive matchups, and borrow damage with the physical attack boon when the lane looks safe. Until Level 4 your base damage is genuinely poor, so this is not a trading window — quietly collect last hits and experience and nothing else. If an enemy closes the gap, Skill 1's knockback and healing reset the exchange more often than not. It also halves the cooldowns of Skill 2 and the Ultimate, so spending it defensively never feels like a waste.
tips.midGame: From 8 to 10 minutes, once attack-speed boots and your first damage item are online, Flowborn's signature mechanic starts spinning: attack speed accelerates your skill animations too. You're still not the main character of teamfights, so shove the lane, sweep open jungle camps, and rush your second core item. When called to Tyrant, join from the very back — planting Skill 2's giant arrow into the closest enemy is a full shift on its own. Each cast tacks on a short move afterward, so build the habit of stepping back half a pace every time you fire. It quietly prevents most deaths.
tips.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, at four items and up, the lead role changes hands. Weaving bonus casts of Skill 2 and the Ultimate between basic attacks — paid for with Flow stacks — creates the damage spikes that define this hero's endgame. Fire Skill 2 three times within 1.5 seconds and the third becomes an aerial attack at 50% bonus damage, so the moment your frontline pins someone is the moment to unload the triple. Skill 1 restocks five stacks, more with allies or minions nearby; never let the tank run empty between fights. And never walk anywhere alone — stay close enough to see a teammate's back at all times.
tips.teamfight: Your position is locked to the very back, and your target is whoever stands closest. When chased, Skill 1's knockback peels them off while the heal and the 50% cooldown refund on Skill 2 and the Ultimate set up your next burst. Arrowstorm's volley also grants 10% move speed, tailor-made for kiting backward. Once the enemy front cracks, spend your saved Flow stacks on the Skill 2 triple volley into whatever remains of their backline. You are softest right after dumping everything — at zero stacks, sit at max range and refuse to get greedy. That's how this hero grows old.

strengths: Attack speed uniquely accelerates skill animations, double-dipping every point
Skill 1's knockback, healing, and cooldown refund make elite self-peel
Flow-stack bonus casts create burst windows that ignore cooldowns
Post-cast movement and aerial attacks on Skill 2 and the Ultimate make kiting exceptional
weaknesses: Weak base damage before Level 4 — early trades are nearly always losses
The piercing arrow loses 30% damage after passing through a target, so long-range poke rarely finishes anyone
Sloppy stack management removes the bonus casts and flattens the damage spikes
Targeted CC is lethal once Skill 1 is down, with no second escape

counteredBy.name: Gao Changgong
counteredBy.reason: Gao Changgong opens from stealth and stuns Flowborn through his dagger mark, leaving no room to fire back.

counteredBy.name: Jing
counteredBy.reason: Jing pressures from two sides at once, and every mark shatter refreshes her skills, so the chase never stops.

synergies.name: Zhang Fei
synergies.reason: Zhang Fei's shield and stun let Flowborn stand in the fight and finish a full arrow chain.

synergies.name: Cai Yan
synergies.reason: Cai Yan's sound wave chains stuns down the enemy line, opening a clean window for Arrowstorm.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Finishing with 439 physical attack
builds.condition: When the enemy team fields two or more high-HP front-liners
builds.notes: Doomsday moves up to second, locking in 500 max HP and 20% physical lifesteal by 2,800G. Its passive adds 80-160 plus 7% of the target's bonus HP to every basic attack, biting hardest into stacked HP. Daybreaker's Virtue also comes early, fourth at 7,410G, for 15% physical penetration (doubled on ranged heroes). Overlord's Might closes the set with 30% extra damage to enemies below 50% HP, taking physical attack to 439 in total.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Extra range and attack speed
builds.condition: When enemies dive you often and you want to hold your distance
builds.notes: Shadow Ripper second puts 20% crit rate and 7.5% movement speed on the board at 2,740G. Eternity Blade then comes fourth to raise crit damage early, pushing Daybreaker's Virtue back to fifth. Sunchaser closes the set with an active that adds 125 basic-attack range and 20% movement speed for 5 seconds, on a 75-second cooldown. Totals reach 86% crit rate and 130% attack speed, trading 110 physical attack against build 1 for more shots landed.

name: Flowborn (Roamer)
title: Flowborn (Roamer) Guide: Combos, Counters & Strategy - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A roamer that hands out shields and range from a platform at their feet, and uses sound waves to damage and heal at the same time. With no hard crowd control, the kit leans into protection and support.
playstyle: A roamer that hands out shields and range from a platform at their feet, and uses sound waves to damage and heal at the same time. With no hard crowd control, the kit leans into protection and support.
bestFor: players happy to stay glued to a teammate. The shield and range only exist on the platform, so long stretches of scouting alone waste them. Mechanically, the habit to build is checking that you still hold 4–5 stacks of Flow before each extra cast.

tips.earlyGame: Official HoK Camp data lists Flowborn (Roamer) as a roamer. Convergence restores more Health and grants more Flow the more teammates and minions are nearby, so early on it gets the most value beside a minion wave and your laner. Each stack of Flow can be spent on an enhanced Basic Attack. Its sound wave ricochets to nearby units twice, and a ricochet that reaches an allied hero restores 80 Health (at hero Level 1). With no allied hero nearby, it heals no one. Once Lingering Melody unlocks at Level 4, move with your jungler's ganks. You have no way to hold enemies in place, so let your teammates call the engage.
tips.midGame: The Tyrant and Overlord both spawn at 4:00. Before contesting them, stock at least 8 stacks of Flow with Convergence. Protection Melody costs 4 stacks for an extra cast, so recasting twice on the platform takes it to its third stage, Harmonious Song. Each recast extends the platform and raises the shield by 25%, then 50%. The platform only appears beneath your own feet, so stand next to the teammate you want to protect before you cast. Teammates on it gain 75 attack and skill range and can fire from further back than usual.
tips.lateGame: Late in the game, your place is beside your marksman or mage. Nothing in your kit stops an enemy, so you answer divers with knockbacks and shields. Protection Melody serves both offense, stretching your team's range, and defense, pushing divers away. Cast it to attack, and its knockback is gone until the cooldown ends. Keep 4 stacks of Flow in reserve and you can cast it again on the spot. Teammates leaving the platform dash in the direction they are moving, so after a knockback, step off together with your backliner to fall back.
tips.teamfight: Fights start with you standing just behind your frontline and dropping Protection Melody. Backliners who step onto the platform fire with the shared shield and 75 extra range. When enemies close in, push them back with Convergence, which also cuts the cooldowns of Protection Melody and Lingering Melody by 50% and returns at least 5 stacks of Flow. Lingering Melody fires 8 sound waves, damaging enemies and healing allies they hit. Aim it where both teams are tangled up, and one cast reaches both sides. Waves that hit a wall ricochet into new waves (up to 3, at 75% damage), so in jungle corridors, aiming at a wall gives you more waves.

strengths: Protection Melody hands a shared shield and 75 extra range to every ally on the platform
Convergence heals more and grants more Flow the more teammates and minions are nearby
Lingering Melody's 8 sound waves damage the enemies they hit and heal the allies they hit
The enhanced Basic Attack ricochets to nearby units twice, healing the allies it reaches
weaknesses: Every knockback applies no crowd control, and the kit has no stun or launch
The shield and range bonus only reach allies standing on the platform at Flowborn's feet
Extra casts cost 4–5 stacks of Flow, and once they are spent you get fewer casts until Skill 1 is back
The shield and self-healing scale with extra Health, while damage and ally healing scale with magical attack, so item stats get split between the two

counteredBy.name: Musashi
counteredBy.reason: Musashi's duel delays all of the target's recovery, so Flowborn cannot lean on self-healing to outlast him.

counteredBy.name: Wang Zhaojun
counteredBy.reason: Wang Zhaojun's snowstorm lingers on the ground, grinding down Flowborn and allies who hold position on the casting platform.

synergies.name: Huang Zhong
synergies.reason: Huang Zhong is immobile in Turret Mode, so he can sit on the casting platform and keep its shield and range.

synergies.name: Lady Zhen
synergies.reason: Lady Zhen's launch and heavy slow leave enemies barely moving, so Flowborn's stream of sound waves is hard to dodge.

name: Flowborn (Tank)
title: Flowborn (Tank) Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A clean, well-built tank with Flow customization on top. His charge knockback and leaping knock-up open fights exactly as a frontliner should — the easy rating is honest.
playstyle: A clean, well-built tank with Flow customization on top. His charge knockback and leaping knock-up open fights exactly as a frontliner should — the easy rating is honest.
bestFor: learning the tank role — the engage call is the only hard part, and spending Flow to recast Skill 2 and the ultimate is the one extra layer.

tips.earlyGame: The game starts before the gates open: pick your Flow enhancement at base, and if you're frontlining, the dual-defense option is the safe default. The early rule that matters most: cast Skill 1 near allies or minions. Flow stacks scale with the bodies around you (up to 9) and the healing climbs with them, so the same button is a different skill depending on where you press it. Roam or clash lane both work. When the Ultimate unlocks at level 4, syncing its knock-up with your jungler's gank is your first highlight moment.
tips.midGame: Through the 8-to-12-minute objective fights, your Flow bank is your voice in the game. Skill 2 recasts free of cooldown for 4 stacks and the Ultimate for 5, so at full stacks you're effectively a tank with double the spellbook. Engage with the Ultimate's center hit (50% bonus damage plus a 0.75-second knock-up), then chain Skill 2 into the same target: the second and third strikes add escalating knock-ups on top. Land the full chain and the average carry simply does not walk away.
tips.lateGame: When the game settles into 5v5 set pieces, your edge is initiating twice by yourself: once with the normal rotation, once more with stack-funded recasts. The most lethal Ultimate of the night is the second one — cast right as the enemy steps forward believing you're out of cooldowns. Hold the frontline with Flow-empowered basic attacks: each one heals, so as long as you keep swinging you're genuinely hard to bring down. Just remember Skill 1's stack income depends on nearby bodies — never drift into isolated fights.
tips.teamfight: You take the front, but top off with Skill 1 before committing — a full Flow bank changes how brave you're allowed to be. Enter on the Ultimate's center hit, then run Skill 2 three times into one target: the chained knock-ups juggle them while your team pours in damage. If the backline gets dived, Skill 2's charging knockback carves the assassin off your carry while the shield absorbs the exchange. A habit worth building: keep at least 4 stacks in reserve at all times, so a surprise engage can always be answered with an instant recast.

strengths: Flow stacks buy cooldown-free recasts of Skill 2 and the Ultimate
Chained, escalating knock-ups deliver exceptional lockdown
Empowered-basic healing and shields sustain a long frontline shift
The pre-game Flow choice tunes him against any enemy comp
weaknesses: With an empty Flow bank he's an ordinary tank with ordinary CC
Skill 1's income scales with nearby bodies, so isolated fights starve him
No mobility beyond the charge; long-range poke drains him for free
Stack accounting plus chained inputs make him busier than he looks

counteredBy.reason: Lu Bu ignores crowd control while diving with Tremble, Mortals, so Flowborn's launches cannot stop him.

synergies.name: Kongming
synergies.reason: Kongming's Spirit Bomb needs a channel, and Flowborn's launch buys exactly that window.

Frigid Charge at fifth hands you a shield worth 10% of max HP whenever hard CC other than suppression lands on you. The totals reach +6687 max HP, +943 physical defense and +520 magic defense, 1800 more HP than the first build.

name: Fuzi
title: Fuzi Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A brawler who powers up through repeated basic attacks, pulls enemies in with his ruler, and reflects the first attack that hits his stance. He is built to win while being hit.
playstyle: A brawler who powers up through repeated basic attacks, pulls enemies in with his ruler, and reflects the first attack that hits his stance. He is built to win while being hit.
bestFor: patient brawlers happy to win while taking hits. Stacking five basic attacks takes discipline; the payoff is turning the enemy's opening blow back on them.

tips.earlyGame: Take Skill 2 first in the clash lane — the damage reduction and bonus-attack procs let you clear the opening wave and trade at the same time. Fuzi's lifeline is his Passive: whether you have five stacks banked from hitting minions before you commit changes the fight entirely. The empowered state adds true damage and shaves the cooldowns of Skills 1 and 2, so at even HP you win most slugfests on math alone. Don't chase before level 4, and any time the enemy jungler disappears from the map, assume the river brush and back off.
tips.midGame: At the 4-minute Tyrant fight, your job is to open by binding the enemy fighter or jungler with your Ultimate. Five seconds of restricted movement plus 20% reduced damage output means they fight the whole skirmish at a disadvantage. In lane, lean on your 1v1 strength to push the side, and drag anyone who collapses on you into melee with Skill 1. Skill 2 reflects 50% of the first basic attack you take while it's active — read the tell on an enemy's empowered attack and pop it in response, and you win the trade on that alone.
tips.lateGame: True to his late-game label, Fuzi peaks once Doomsday and Blood Rage come online after 15 minutes. Five-stack true damage all but ignores armor, so almost nobody wins a straight brawl against you. But games are decided at Shadow Tyrant and Overlord, not in a side lane. Leave the 1v1 thirty seconds before the objective spawns, regroup with your team, and claim the position that lets you land your Ultimate as the fight's opening move.
tips.teamfight: The dream scenario: bind the enemy carry right before the brawl starts and turn it into a 5v4. The dash latches onto the first hero it touches, so when their frontline is walling you out, look for a flank angle. Once the bind lands, activate Skill 2's 45% damage reduction and never stop swinging — as long as your basics connect, the stacks and cooldown refunds keep cycling, and Fuzi only gets stronger the longer the fight runs. Standing around without a target is the one thing that kills you.

strengths: Five-stack true damage makes him one of the game's best 1v1 brawlers
Skill 2's 45% damage reduction and reflect turn enemy aggression against them
The Ultimate's 5-second bind and 20% damage cut shuts down the enemy ace
A late-game power curve that keeps climbing as items complete
weaknesses: Needs uninterrupted basic attacks to function — kiting shuts him down hard
His only real gap-closer is the Ultimate; missing it leaves a long window
Skill 1's pull radius is small and whiffs against high-mobility targets
Without stacks, both his damage and durability are merely average

name: Gan & Mo
title: Gan & Mo Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An extreme-range artillery mage whose paired blades both strike wherever he aims — one act of aim, double the payload. Accuracy converts directly into multiplied damage.
playstyle: An extreme-range artillery mage whose paired blades both strike wherever he aims — one act of aim, double the payload. Accuracy converts directly into multiplied damage.
bestFor: snipers who trust their aim — one cast sends two blades, and landing them where they cross is how accuracy turns into damage from outside anyone's reach.

tips.earlyGame: Gan & Mo outrange the entire mid lane from level 1. Everything about the duo's damage flows from crossing Skill 2's short-range blades with Skill 3's long-range blades at a single point, so the second volley detonates the Sword Energy the first one left behind — spend the opening waves calibrating that intersection distance on stationary minions. Blade skills draw from a shared usage cap that only restores one charge every five to six seconds, which means never stepping forward right after emptying it. If someone jumps you, Skill 1's knockback-and-hop-back buys exactly one reset. That is the only insurance policy you own; price it accordingly.
tips.midGame: From about 7-8 minutes, with your first core item finished, one clean intersection removes close to half of an enemy mage's HP. Before the 4:00 Tyrant or the 10:00 Shadow Tyrant, simply raining blades from maximum range onto anyone entering the pit forces the enemy to open the fight pre-chipped — that is Gan & Mo's brand of pressure. Skill 1 banks bonus magic attack on every kill and assist, so involvement snowballs the damage curve on its own. Skip the roams. Push mid, step back, carve sword qi into whoever contests, repeat.
tips.lateGame: With Skill 1 grown to 15-20 stacks, a single intersection deletes a marksman outright — which is precisely why the enemy will spend everything to reach you. Two non-negotiables: stand behind every teammate, and never fight with a wall at your back. Do not hunt with Skill 1 either; hold it as the reaction card you play the instant someone commits to the jump. During Overlord fights, dropping blades from outside the pit's perimeter slowly bends the enemy formation out of shape until someone makes the mistake you have been waiting for.
tips.teamfight: Gan & Mo never need to walk forward in a teamfight. From the deepest backline, punish any enemy frontliner who stops moving by crossing the short and long blades on their feet — that alone is a full shift's work. Priority targets: pre-fight clumps and anyone locked down by your team's CC. Chasing sprinting targets with blades is wasted ammunition. Skill 1's 150 magic defense shred also boosts your allied mage, so land it on the focus target first. Empty the charges, take one step back, wait for the refill. Guard that rhythm and you survive.

strengths: Crossed blade intersections burst enemies from beyond retaliation range
Skill 1 banks up to 20 stacks of magic attack off kills and assists
Knockback plus hop-back on Skill 1 is genuine anti-assassin insurance
The 150 magic defense shred amplifies every magic dealer on the team
weaknesses: Damage tracks intersection accuracy one-to-one; the skill floor is steep
No mobility skill, so a closed gap almost always means death
Blade charges are finite and the pressure vanishes once they are spent
No hard CC of their own, so they cannot lock anyone down solo

Savant's Wrath lands fourth: its passive adds 30% Magical Attack, and the +350 from Sage's Tome is already there to be multiplied.
