The trade is Max Health, which sits at 1250 — 180 lower than Build 1.

name: Gao
title: Gao Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A sound mage whose notes ricochet between enemies and whose ultimate is a five-second concert that hits harder the closer the audience. He plays a mage from a frontliner's position.
playstyle: A sound mage whose notes ricochet between enemies and whose ultimate is a five-second concert that hits harder the closer the audience. He plays a mage from a frontliner's position.
bestFor: mages willing to stand where mages should not — the ultimate hardens with every enemy nearby, so hanging back throws it away and holding the concert for five full seconds is the job.

tips.earlyGame: Until level 4, Gao's only escape tool is Skill 2, so don't force anything in mid lane. Skill 1's notes ricochet to nearby enemies, so land them on the minion wave and let the bounces chip the enemy laner from safety. Every third performance turns your next basic attack into a piercing energy chord thanks to the Passive, so make a habit of finishing each wave clear with a basic attack to speed up your rotations. Skill 2's heal is cut in half when it hits non-heroes, so unless you're escaping, angle the dash to clip the enemy laner.
tips.midGame: The moment your Ultimate comes online at level 4, Gao becomes a different hero. At the 4-minute Tyrant, wait behind your frontline, then dash in with Skill 2 the instant the enemy clumps up and start spinning your Ultimate. Its damage reduction stacks an extra 5% for every nearby enemy hero, so counterintuitively, performing in the middle of three enemies keeps you alive longer than half-committing onto one. Casting Skill 1 during Skill 2's dash lets you move again — save it to correct your entry angle.
tips.lateGame: Once three core items are done around 15 minutes, a single full Ultimate rotation can decide a teamfight. The flip side: while it's on cooldown, Gao is just a squishy mage with a healing dash, so stay off the frontline until it comes back. Before you commit, check which enemy is holding the stun, and only dive after you see it land on your frontline — that's how you finish the channel. The tight corridors around Shadow Tyrant and Overlord suit your bouncing notes, so you contribute plenty with pre-fight poke too.
tips.teamfight: Open at range with Skill 1 poke — the real play comes when the enemy stacks up. Skill 2 into a Skill 1 recast lands you in the center of their team, and if you survive the Ultimate's full 5 seconds, damage ticks every 0.5 seconds into everyone around you. The 50% move speed on activation decays over 3 seconds, so settle your positioning within the first second or two. If you're about to get dropped mid-performance, don't force the full channel — simply walking back toward your team baits the chase and buys time.

strengths: Ultimate's damage reduction grows with nearby enemies — the deeper the brawl, the longer he survives
Skill 2's heal and dash recast give rare engage-and-exit mobility for a mage
Passive's piercing basic attack handles wave clear and poke at the same time
weaknesses: With the Ultimate down, both damage and durability are ordinary — he can't start fights
Max damage requires diving the enemy team, and one stun ends the performance
Skill 1's repeat hits on the same hero are heavily reduced, so single-target burst is low

counteredBy.reason: Liang can suppress Gao outright, cutting off Rock Out! long before the drawn-out performance finishes.

counteredBy.name: Donghuang
counteredBy.reason: Donghuang's suppression shares all damage taken, so allies rushing in to free Gao end up hurting him instead.

synergies.reason: Bai Qi's pull and taunt hold enemies in one clump, so Rock Out! and Wild Chord's ricochets keep landing.

synergies.name: Sun Bin

Ardent Dominion, bought third, clears crowd control below 30% HP and grants a 4-second shield with +30% movement speed. Breakthrough Robe grants magic power worth 2% of bonus health and magic defense penetration worth 3%, which pays off at +3,150 max HP. Savant's Wrath and its 30% boost wait until the fifth slot, so magic power finishes at 862 — 260 below build 1. Staves of Sorcery closes the build, adding magic damage to the next basic attack within 5 seconds of a cast.

name: Gao Changgong
title: Gao Changgong Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A classic stealth assassin: approach unseen, mark the target, and end it in one burst. The fight is mostly decided before he becomes visible.
playstyle: A classic stealth assassin: approach unseen, mark the target, and end it in one burst. The fight is mostly decided before he becomes visible.
bestFor: planning the entrance rather than the fight. Most of your game happens while invisible — pick the bush, pick the moment; once you are seen it is already decided.

tips.earlyGame: Start on your own buffs and rush level 4. The reason is simple: Gao Changgong's assassination kit only comes online once the Ultimate's dash links into Skill 2's follow-up stun. His Passive grants 15–30% bonus movement speed (it scales with level) only while moving toward enemy heroes, so approach ganks through bushes rather than down the lane. Touch the bottom side of the map at least once before the Tyrant spawns at 4:00 — showing up with a numbers advantage decides that first objective more often than the smite does.
tips.midGame: Your assassination power peaks around 8-10 minutes, when two core physical and penetration items are done. Skill 2's mark lasts 3 seconds, and the moment it disappears the target takes 152 (140 + 12% lost Health) physical damage. The scaling is on health already lost, not max health, so the mark pays out more the longer you chip at them first — and every 50 extra physical attack adds another 1% on top. Re-attacking a marked enemy stuns for 1 second and heals you, which makes even greedy dives surprisingly survivable. Before the Shadow Tyrant arrives at 10:00, walk the enemy jungle bushes once to map out your ambush routes.
tips.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, tanks get too beefy and your value in front-to-front fights drops. Hunt the enemies who leave the group instead: the side laner pushing alone, the support walking out for vision. If Skill 2 connects, the stun plus percent damage almost always converts into a kill. Deleting one enemy right before the Overlord contest is your real win condition — treat full 5v5s as a last resort and only fight with a numbers edge.
tips.teamfight: Never be the first one in. You are paper-thin, and a single crowd-control effect will end you, so wait until the enemy dumps their lockdown on your frontline before circling to the backline. Always open with Skill 2: a hit slows the target immensely for 2 seconds, and because that slow diminishes as it runs, the first second is when you close. Skill 3 covers the rest of the gap and sets up the 1-second stun from re-attacking the mark. Skill 1's clone automatically hunts the lowest-HP enemy hero, so in a scrum it cleans up chunked targets you can't physically reach.

strengths: Single-target burst from Skill 2's 1s stun plus a mark that detonates for 12% of lost Health
Passive move speed makes chases and bush ganks reliably stick
Healing off marked targets lets him survive aggressive dives and chain fights
The clone auto-targets the lowest-HP enemy hero and cleans up scraps
weaknesses: Paper-thin defenses — a single CC chain usually kills him
Missing Skill 2 deletes the stun and percent damage, half his kit
No frontal fighting tools, so his impact fades in late 5v5s
The Ultimate is his only mobility, making exits after deep dives rough

counteredBy.name: Shouyue
counteredBy.reason: Shouyue builds Ambush stacks while out of combat, so his pierce-boosted shots chip Gao Changgong down as he approaches.

counteredBy.name: Ata
counteredBy.reason: Ata heals back from the damage he deals, so trading blows with him gets Gao Changgong nowhere.

synergies.reason: Guiguzi strips their armor and pulls them into a stun, so Gao Changgong's dive lands on a helpless target.

synergies.name: Zhang Fei

Cuirass of Savagery follows at 9,540G with 210 physical defense and 900 max HP, and every hit taken raises Gao Changgong's damage and movement speed for 3 seconds. No attack speed in this line, but the armor keeps him swinging through a long fight.

builds.notes: Boots of Deftness are the second buy: 70 movement speed, and 35-70 more after 5 seconds out of combat. Master Sword slots in fourth, so 15% attack speed and 20% critical rate arrive at 7,050G. Overlord's Might drops to fifth, pushing the 30% bonus against targets below 50% HP back to 9,590G. Cooldown reduction stops at 22.5%, so this line puts its 503.6 physical attack through raw swing count.

name: Garo
title: Garo Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The anti-shield specialist: her attacks deal 50% bonus damage to shields. Longbow stance extends her reach while silencing arrows enforce her terms from afar.
playstyle: The anti-shield specialist: her attacks deal 50% bonus damage to shields. Longbow stance extends her reach while silencing arrows enforce her terms from afar.
bestFor: drafters who pick to answer a composition — damage lands 50% harder against shields, and the longbow buys range at the cost of a slower interval and more mana.

tips.earlyGame: Garo's early game in the farm lane is an exercise in restraint. Skill 1's longbow adds 125 attack range, but every arrow that lands costs 50 Mana and her attack interval stretches by 25%, so leaving it on permanently runs you dry. Use the longbow for wave clear and a few pokes, then stow it — attacks with the bow stowed restore Mana, at triple value against heroes. The faster that toggle becomes a habit, the faster she improves. She has no mobility skill, so stay off the river bushes whenever the enemy jungler is unaccounted for. Until your first crit item finishes, farm beats fighting every time.
tips.midGame: Garo's game starts around 10 minutes, once one or two crit items are done. The Ultimate's passive slows targets on every critical hit, so as long as you keep landing arrows, nobody closes the distance. When sieging, abuse the longbow's range to chip towers from beyond any retaliation. The moment an enemy initiator shows their face, stop them cold with Skill 2's 0.5-second silence. Walking anywhere alone, however fed you are, remains a death sentence.
tips.lateGame: A full-build Garo is a stationary artillery platform that deletes everything in reach. Drop Skill 3 underfoot and, while she stands inside the circle, she gains 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate — the bonus is hers, not the team's. From maximum longbow range the chained crit slows alone keep enemies from ever walking to you. If someone does close in, recast Skill 3 while you are still inside it: destroying the circle grants the same 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate and deals area damage on the way out. Collapse it from outside and you only get half. Before Overlord fights, glance at your Mana bar first. A Garo who can't afford her longbow is just a slow marksman.
tips.teamfight: Open teamfights by dropping your Ultimate underfoot and shooting the nearest frontliner from inside the circle. Don't force shots at their backline; hitting whatever is in range is how the crit slows stay unbroken. When an assassin dives, answer with Skill 2's silence and 50% slow, collapse the circle for the speed burst, and kite behind your tank. Her Passive deals 50% bonus damage to shields, so shielded carries — normally the hardest targets on the map — melt fastest of all against Garo.

strengths: Longbow range is among the longest of any marksman for one-sided poke
Critical hits apply slows that stall anyone walking toward her
Passive deals 50% bonus damage to shields, shredding shield-heavy comps
Standing inside Skill 3's circle gives her 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate
weaknesses: No mobility skill whatsoever; once touched, her team is the plan
The longbow devours MP, and sloppy management switches her damage off
Longbow mode stretches her attack interval by 25%, losing close-range duels
Little presence before crit items; the early game is pure survival

name: Garuda
title: Garuda Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A mage who burns both lines and areas — piercing basic attacks plus a 90-arrow barrage he can fire on the move, with his other skills still usable during it. He pressures the whole fight while walking backwards.
playstyle: A mage who burns both lines and areas — piercing basic attacks plus a 90-arrow barrage he can fire on the move, with his other skills still usable during it. He pressures the whole fight while walking backwards.
bestFor: players who enjoy never stopping the shooting — the barrage moves with you, leaving one call to make over and over: dump the remaining arrows for the fear, or hold and keep firing.

tips.earlyGame: Garuda's lane revolves around basic attacks that pierce and deal magic damage. Angle yourself so the enemy laner stands behind their own minions and your autos farm and poke in the same swing. Lay the Skill 1 feather field on the enemy's escape path rather than under their feet — that's where the slow earns its keep — and treat Skill 2 as insurance for when damage is incoming. Until your Ultimate arrives at level 4, farming and HP discipline beat hero plays. You have speed but no self-peel CC, so once ganks pick up around the four-minute mark, check the minimap more, not less.
tips.midGame: Mid-game Garuda is about area denial with the Ultimate. Ninety feather arrows over five seconds turns any narrow contest — the Tyrant pit, a mid tower siege — into ground the enemy simply cannot hold. With two AP items around 7-9 minutes, run the mobile-turret loop: feather field down, barrage into the clump, Skill 2 speed to hold your range. One discipline matters above all — don't recast the Ultimate casually. The fear plus physical attack bonus nullification is your trump card against assassins, and while that threat exists, they can't touch you.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Garuda is the worst matchup the enemy's physical carries can face. When an assassin or fighter dives you, the Ultimate recast answers with a two-second fear and nullifies their equipment's physical attack bonus — the assassination just doesn't happen. Past ten minutes, merely holding that button unspent keeps enemies from committing. Set up diagonally behind your frontline, at the angle where piercing basics travel through their tanks into the backline. You have no hard CC to lock down runners, so leave the executions to teammates and do the one thing only you do: keep firing.
tips.teamfight: Garuda's teamfight is measured in seconds of uninterrupted shooting. On engage, stack the Skill 1 feather field on the frontline and pour the Ultimate's arrows into the thickest part of the enemy team, weaving piercing basics between them. When someone closes the gap, kite out with Skill 2's speed — and if they stick anyway, the Ultimate recast dumps every unfired arrow around you while the fear buys the reset. Self-peel and burst damage on the same button is deeply satisfying, but it's also your whole defense: confirm the threat is real before you press it.

strengths: Piercing magic basic attacks deliver relentless damage into clumped enemies
The Ultimate recast's fear and physical attack bonus nullification is elite self-defense
Skill 2's shield and speed let him kite and keep shooting at the same time
Feather fields and the barrage dominate the tight spaces around objectives
weaknesses: No guaranteed hard CC, so he struggles to catch anyone on his own
Using the fear means sacrificing the Ultimate's remaining damage — a genuinely hard call
No blink, so chained hard CC will eventually run him down

Both builds land the same +1037.8 magic attack, so the gap is uptime and bulk — paid for with movement speed dropping to +10%.

name: Guan Yu
title: Guan Yu Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A cavalry hero whose power is his run-up: 2,000 units of movement puts him in charge state, where his skills split formations with knockbacks. A stationary Guan Yu is barely a hero at all.
playstyle: A cavalry hero whose power is his run-up: 2,000 units of movement puts him in charge state, where his skills split formations with knockbacks. A stationary Guan Yu is barely a hero at all.
bestFor: anyone happy never to stand still. Keep the run-up alive and choose the angle that splits the enemy formation; stop moving and the hero stops working.

tips.earlyGame: Guan Yu starts in the clash lane, but after the first two waves your top priority is simple: never stop moving. His Passive enters the charge state after 2000 units of travel, so every second spent standing in a lane staring at your opponent is a second spent being weak. Loop through the river and your own jungle to build a runway, then knock enemies flying with the charged basic attack, disengage, and repeat. Until level 4, resist every urge to chase — hit, knock them back, and leave. That alone wins you lane priority.
tips.midGame: The game becomes Guan Yu's around the 4-minute Tyrant. Objective standoffs hand you runways for free, and a single blindside knockback into their backline can decide the fight before it starts. Cast Skill 3 in Normal Stance and you are enhanced for 10s, with the distance required to enter Charge Stance reduced by 75% — 2,000 units becomes 500, so re-engages come around far faster. When ganking, angle your approach so enemies get knocked toward your tower or your teammates — punting them to safety in their own territory is the classic first mistake every new Guan Yu makes.
tips.lateGame: With two or three defense items like Overlord's Platemail and Blazing Cape done by 15 minutes, Charge Stance Skill 1 becomes your main tool. It charges forward, knocking enemies back for 360 (360 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage, and the slash at the end of the charge adds 500 (500 + 160% extra physical attack) on top. Your enhanced basic attack is flat, not percentage — an extra 500 (1,000 at level 15) plus 125% extra physical attack — so items are what scale it. At Shadow Tyrant and Overlord, your job is to crash sideways into the brush they're holding, wedge yourself between the boss pit and their team, and split their formation. You lack solo kill power, so leave knocked-back targets to your teammates and immediately start building the next runway. While an enemy with strong slows is alive, take the long way around and come from behind — never the front.
tips.teamfight: Your teamfight prep starts 30 seconds early: run the perimeter and keep the charge state alive. The ideal entry clips their marksman and mage in a single line, and once you've run someone over, do not stop — Skill 2 cleanses crowd control and re-accelerates you for a second and third pass. Planting your feet in the middle of the scrum is the worst thing you can do. Keep making passes back and forth through their team, and the enemy never reforms their line while your own backline shoots for free.

strengths: Charge Stance Skill 1 lands twice — the charge itself and the slash at the end — so even tanky lines break
Skill 2 self-cleanses CC, making him extremely hard to pin down
Elite formation-breaking; he creates teamfight openings single-handedly
Gets stronger just by running, so his farm dependency is low
weaknesses: Standing still drops the charge state, leaving him weak in tight scrums
Stacked slows or chained CC stop his feet and get him focused down
Demands runway knowledge and heavy mechanics — a genuinely hard hero
Lacks solo kill power; his knockbacks need teammates to convert

Succubus Cloak closes it out, converting 15% of the extra magic defense into physical defense and refreshing a 400-800 magic damage shield every 15 seconds.

name: Guiguzi
title: Guiguzi Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The architect of ambushes: he cloaks his entire team and delivers an invisible squad to the enemy's doorstep, with a mass pull and shields to finish the design.
playstyle: The architect of ambushes: he cloaks his entire team and delivers an invisible squad to the enemy's doorstep, with a mass pull and shields to finish the design.
bestFor: shot-callers who want to design the opening — you cloak the whole team, walk it to the enemy's door, and land the pull before the two-second channel gets read.

tips.earlyGame: Guiguzi should have walked half the map before his first recall — that is the correct pace. Touch the mid wave for a moment, then slide toward a side lane under Skill 1's camouflage and 40% movement speed. Ghost through the enemy laner's back, and merely brushing them carves 25% off both defenses; your laner collapsing onto that debuff turns into a kill from thin air. One rule above all: attacking anything breaks the camouflage. The touch already did the work, so keep your hands to yourself.
tips.midGame: Guiguzi's busiest window is the thirty seconds before each Tyrant spawn. Tuck into the pit-side bush with your jungler, and anyone who wanders up eats Skill 2's pull-and-stun — objective and numbers advantage in one motion. The Ultimate's team-wide camouflage can hand your side the opening of an entire teamfight, but spending it casually on travel leaves nothing for the moment that matters; commit it to engages, full stop. The free vision of the nearest enemy hero it grants sharpens every ambush you set.
tips.lateGame: In the late game a single engage decides everything, which makes Guiguzi's stealth the trump card of trump cards. The script: cloak all five with the Ultimate, spread across the objective approach, and land Skill 2's pull on the enemy's structural piece — usually the carry. But understand that your durability is paper against late-game damage, and the two-second channel can be burned through, shield and all. Always start the play from inside your team's effective range. Solo hero-ball adventures are this hero's number one loss condition.
tips.teamfight: The ideal sequence never changes: vanish the team with the Ultimate, thread Skill 1 through the enemy line to stamp the 25% defense shred on priority targets, then channel Skill 2 in the thick of their formation. Two seconds later the pull and stun compress them into one tidy package for your team's AoE. The shield on hero contact absorbs some of the opening fire, but the channel is your single point of failure — start it while their attention is fixed on your frontline, in that stolen instant when nobody is looking at you.

strengths: Team-wide camouflage lets him dictate exactly when fights begin
Pull-stun engage plus ally shields makes his openings devastating
Skill 1's 25% dual-defense shred raises the whole team's damage
Stealth and speed give him unmatched roaming range for ambushes
weaknesses: Paper durability — a failed engage usually costs him his life
Skill 2's two-second channel whiffs badly against anyone who reads it
His openings evaporate if teammates do not follow up instantly
Close to zero solo damage or kill threat

name: Han Xin
title: Han Xin Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A spear fighter who lives in motion, chaining double-jump engages and knock-ups so the target never gets a turn. Kill, reposition, flow to the next target.
playstyle: A spear fighter who lives in motion, chaining double-jump engages and knock-ups so the target never gets a turn. Kill, reposition, flow to the next target.
bestFor: hands that enjoy moving. Double-jump in, reverse-dash out, and close the kill before the mobility runs dry — precision here is survival.

tips.earlyGame: Han Xin junglers almost always open from the blue buff side. The Passive's fourth-hit knock-up and 20% lifesteal mean that simply spacing out clean four-hit sequences keeps your HP topped while you clear at speed. Once your Ultimate unlocks at level 4, start ganking the lane being shoved in or any enemy slow to back off. Skill 1's double jump crosses walls, so appear from the wall behind your target rather than the river — suddenly there is no correct direction for them to run.
tips.midGame: From around 7 minutes with your first core item done, Han Xin's hunting ground moves to the enemy jungle. Bounce through unwarded territory on double jumps, catch farmers alone, and vanish — that loop alone visibly stunts the whole enemy team's growth. Skip the opening exchanges at Tyrant and mid; your role is entering from the side once both teams are worn down and collecting what's left. And before every invade, decide your exit route first. Skip that step, and all the mobility in the game won't carry you home.
tips.lateGame: After 15 minutes, Han Xin loses half his value the moment he stands in a front-on 5v5. Instead, push a side lane deep: two enemies come, hop a wall and vanish; one comes, kill him. That single repeated decision keeps the map in your team's hands. At Overlord, lurk in a flanking position and dive their backline after the fight starts. Your Ultimate carries crowd control immunity and 30% damage reduction while spinning, so committing under a tower or through a wall of enemy CC is a play you're allowed to make with confidence.
tips.teamfight: Wait on the perimeter until the enemy's CC and attention are committed to your frontline, then take Skill 1 into their isolated backline. Land three basics, then time Skill 2's sweep as the fourth hit for a guaranteed knock-up, and spin your Ultimate through them to finish — that's the ideal script. When the target drops, don't chase; leave on Skill 1's remaining jump. A Han Xin who spent every movement skill on the way in is just a fragile spearman, so always keep one in the tank for the road home.

strengths: Double jumps and the reverse dash give mobility few heroes can match
Passive knock-up and 20% lifesteal keep his HP healthy through repeated fights
Ultimate's crowd control immunity and 30% reduction let him finish combos through CC
Elite wall-hopping makes enemy jungle invades and escapes routine
weaknesses: Fragile base stats — one CC chain after his jumps are spent is lethal
Skill 2's reverse input is unique, and precision directly equals survival
Damage is built around reaching the fourth hit, so split-second trades underwhelm
Long stretches of solo play mean vision-starved games blunt his edge

name: Haya
title: Haya Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A lunar mage who spends three moon rings on her casts and halves incoming damage through her linking ultimate. The skill ceiling lives in hiding the vulnerable moment when the rings run dry.
playstyle: A lunar mage who spends three moon rings on her casts and halves incoming damage through her linking ultimate. The skill ceiling lives in hiding the vulnerable moment when the rings run dry.
bestFor: players willing to drill: covering the gap after the third moon ring is spent, then picking one target apart imprint by imprint.

tips.earlyGame: In the mid lane, Haya's bread and butter is landing Skill 1 at max range, then hitting the imprinted target again to stack true damage on top. While you still hold moon rings, Skill 1 and Skill 2 cycle on very short cooldowns, but spending all three drops you onto normal cooldowns — so keep one cast of Skill 2 in your pocket for escapes whenever the enemy jungler's shadow appears. Skill 2 also grants a shield and a speed boost, so until you unlock the Ultimate at level 4, avoid overextending and fight around the imprint stun as a counter tool.
tips.midGame: Around the 4-minute Tyrant spawn, the Ultimate starts paying off. Group with your jungler and link onto an enemy support warding the river or an isolated mid laner. Hold the link for 1.5 seconds and you drag them into the mirage, where the 50% cooldown reduction lets you dump Skill 2's stun and Skill 1's true damage on them one-sidedly. A practical tip worth remembering: cast the link right after the enemy burns their blink, and it's far harder to break. Once your first magic core item is done, the imprint combo alone puts enemy mages at death's door.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Haya is all about choosing who disappears into the mirage. Isolate the enemy marksman or mage with the Ultimate before a teamfight starts and you've effectively created a 4v5. Link a tank by mistake, though, and you can lose the brawl inside the mirage — pick your target carefully. After spending all three moon rings, your empowered basic attack fires three orbs' worth of damage, so always tack it onto the end of a combo. The vision fights before Shadow Tyrant after 10 minutes are exactly where a single-target catch hits hardest.
tips.teamfight: Don't join the opening scrum head-on. Sit behind your frontline, spread imprints, and keep Skill 2's shield in reserve. If an enemy assassin dives your backline, link Skill 3 onto that assassin — hold it for 1.5 seconds and the two of you drop into the mirage together, which is what pulls them off your carries. Recast Skill 3 inside the mirage and Haya herself moves 700 units away from the target, resetting the spacing. When attacking, punish whoever steps up out of position with the Skill 1 into Skill 2 imprint stun and focus them down with your team. You have no area damage, so committing everything to deleting one target beats spraying into a clumped enemy team.

strengths: Repeated single-target burst through imprint true damage and stuns
The Ultimate isolates one enemy in the mirage, forcing a pseudo-1v1
Moon rings enable low-cooldown spam plus a shield and speed for self-defense
The link's displacement doubles as peel to protect your carries
weaknesses: Everything flows through imprints, so whiffing the first hit stalls the kit
The link breaks at range, making high-mobility heroes miserable matchups
Thin area damage means weak waveclear and zone control
Juggling rings, imprints, and links earns the Very Hard difficulty tag

name: Heino
title: Heino Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A hybrid whose skills change between ranged and melee forms. His power source is always being the one who chooses the distance — the matchup is a duel over range control itself.
playstyle: A hybrid whose skills change between ranged and melee forms. His power source is always being the one who chooses the distance — the matchup is a duel over range control itself.
bestFor: players who like denying opponents their preferred range, swapping forms on the fly and treating the trip out and the rewind home as one move.

tips.earlyGame: Start with the lane decision. Heino runs mid as a ranged poke machine or the clash lane as a melee brawler with built-in healing and max HP growth — a genuinely dual-purpose hero. Either way, the through-line is mark management: skills and melee basic attacks apply a 7-second mark, and that mark is the precondition for Skill 1's healing and rapid recasts. Keep it running or your numbers fall apart. Until the Ultimate unlocks at level 4, skip the deep plays and use the time to get a feel for Skill 2's form swapping.
tips.midGame: The moment the Ultimate clicks, Heino transforms. Switching to ranged form with Skill 2 records that spot, and the Ultimate returns you there after 1.5 seconds — which enables an almost unfair loop: record somewhere safe, wade in and brawl, then when you're at your limit, pop the domain, heal, and vanish home. Make it a habit before every objective fight from 8 to 10 minutes: record in the back, then commit in melee form. The lower your HP, the bigger the heal (up to double), so every second you stall makes the payoff larger.
tips.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, form choice becomes your tactical dial. Thick frontline in front of you? Stay ranged and keep throwing Skill 1 with its phantom bolts. Thin frontline? Go melee, stack Skill 2's healing and max HP growth, and be the frontline yourself. In tower defenses, know this trick: if an allied tower stands inside the Ultimate's domain, the tower rewinds to its state 5 seconds earlier — a last-second save that decides siege after siege. Knowing that one interaction visibly changes your win rate in defensive games.
tips.teamfight: Before every fight, without exception, record a ranged-form point somewhere safe. That single habit converts your melee dives from gambles into round trips. Once in, hold the brawl with Skill 2's healing and Skill 1, and when the focus fire arrives, cast the Ultimate: 15% damage reduction and crowd control immunity for 1.5 seconds, an AoE burst as the parting gift, and you're gone to the recorded point. From experience, the safest pattern is tanking the enemy's burst through the domain and then leaving — panic-casting it early wastes the low-HP healing bonus.

strengths: Form swapping retunes his role to match the comp and the fight
The Ultimate's return converts aggression into guaranteed round trips
Healing scales up at low HP, giving him remarkable clutch survivability
Rewinding an allied tower 5 seconds is a defensive tool no one else has
weaknesses: Damage and healing both hinge on applying and maintaining marks
Rooted in place during the domain — bad casts invite focus fire
Dying before the return erases his entire gimmick; chained CC is lethal
Tracking forms and the record point at once keeps your hands busy

name: Hou Yi
title: Hou Yi Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The embodiment of sustained fire: at full stacks every attack looses three arrows. If your position is right the piloting is simple — DPS as a raw, physical experience.
playstyle: The embodiment of sustained fire: at full stacks every attack looses three arrows. If your position is right the piloting is simple — DPS as a raw, physical experience.
bestFor: shooting, plainly. There is no dash to bail you out, so positioning is the entire skill — get it right and three arrows per attack do the rest.

tips.earlyGame: Your first job in the farm lane is building those three Passive stacks cleanly. Chastising Shot empowers Hou Yi after three basic attacks, turning each shot into a spread of three arrows, so the laning rhythm is simple: step up and trade only while empowered, back off when it drops. With zero mobility skills, stay away from the river bushes around the four-minute Tyrant whenever you've lost track of the enemy jungler. Skill 2 grants vision at range, so fire it into bushes ahead of time — it's your cheapest insurance against ganks while you farm.
tips.midGame: Once you hit level 4, Hou Yi joins fights he isn't even standing in. The Ultimate's stun scales up to 3.5 seconds with flight distance, and a cross-map arrow flipping a skirmish is a regular occurrence — when your teammates start posturing at mid, line one up from an off-angle. From around seven minutes, with one or two attack speed items finished, you become the primary teamfight damage source: lay Skill 2 across the enemy's escape path for the slow, and learn to hold ground behind your front line pumping triple arrows.
tips.lateGame: At Shadow Tyrant and Overlord standoffs, the single most important question is whether your Ultimate is still in your pocket. Land it on the enemy carry from long range and the extended stun hands you a free numbers advantage; miss it, and Skill 2's slow is your only anti-dive tool left. So the iron rule: only fire once the enemy formation has settled. Empowered Skill 1 also sends 50% damage into two enemies in front of you and towers, so keep three stacks rolling and melt turrets with it during sieges. Hold your position one step behind the front line, no exceptions.
tips.teamfight: Hou Yi's spot is the very back row, yet his damage reaches the whole battlefield. Opening the fight with your own Ultimate is perfectly fine — if it tags the mage lurking behind the enemy tank, your win condition is all but locked in. Once the brawl starts, lean on the triple arrows' natural spread and shred the front line together with everyone stacked behind it. When an assassin dives you, drop Skill 2 at your own feet, let them walk into the slow, then re-space. Save Flash as your final trump card instead of burning it at the first sign of danger.

strengths: Empowered triple arrows shred multiple enemies and towers at once
Ultimate's cross-map stun picks off targets from outside the screen
Skill 2 scouts bushes safely with long-range vision
Simple mechanics make him an ideal first rapid-fire marksman
weaknesses: No mobility skills whatsoever — once caught, he can't escape alone
Damage lives in basic attacks, so attack speed debuffs cripple him
Skill 2's delayed impact makes it hard to land on its own
Missing the Ultimate leaves almost nothing to stop divers

builds.notes: Doomsday comes before the boots at 2,100G, locking in 20% physical lifesteal and +500 max HP. Its Destruction passive adds 80-160 plus 7% of the target's bonus HP to each basic attack, so the more HP the enemy stacks, the more comes off. Daybreaker's Virtue moves up to the fourth slot at 7,410G, so the 30% physical pierce a ranged hero draws from it arrives 4,210G earlier than in build 1. Three Reaver arcana push physical lifesteal to 24.8% against build 1's 20%, enough to hold a forward position longer.

name: Huang Zhong
title: Huang Zhong Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A deployable-turret marksman who chooses between mobility and mounted dominance. Once planted, few heroes match his zone control — the real skill is deciding where and when to plant.
playstyle: A deployable-turret marksman who chooses between mobility and mounted dominance. Once planted, few heroes match his zone control — the real skill is deciding where and when to plant.
bestFor: players who want the siting call to be theirs — planting the turret buys 200 of each defense at the price of every step, and knowing when to pack up is on you.

tips.earlyGame: Huang Zhong is a hyper-late-game marksman who farms up in the farm lane. Until level 4, don't force trades — just collect last hits, because his turret only hits like a truck once crit items come online. Gank protection is entirely Skill 2's job: drop a mine in the river bush and you get 3 seconds of vision, a slow, and a shield all in one cast. Whenever the enemy jungler is missing from the map, hold your mines for defense instead of poke.
tips.midGame: Start rotating to your team around the 10-minute mark, once two crit cores are finished. The turret deals 50% less damage to towers, so during sieges the right call is shooting the heroes defending it, not the building. Shove the wave in, set up behind your teammates, and the enemy simply can't step forward while the tower chips away. Always place a Skill 2 mine on your escape route before you sit down — deploying while three or more enemies are missing from the map is suicide.
tips.lateGame: The clumped-up fights around Shadow Tyrant and Overlord in the final minutes are where Huang Zhong takes over. In turret mode his Passive buff doubles and he gains 200 physical and magic defense, so just parking one step behind your frontline and firing melts the enemy line. The catch: you cannot move at all. If an assassin flanks you, don't get greedy — hit Skill 1 to instantly exit turret mode and retreat with the 70% speed boost. Also remember that re-entering turret mode resets Skill 1's cooldown; that detail alone changes your survival rate.
tips.teamfight: The single most important rule: never set up where you'll be hit first. Wait until the enemy's dive skills have been burned, then deploy behind your frontline. The bombardment deals full damage at the center of its area and 40% less on the edges, so aim at the middle of the enemy clump and your damage jumps dramatically. Put mines at your own feet or in a side bush — enemies who touch them get slowed and armor-shredded while you get a shield, so one mine doubles as assassin insurance and damage support.

strengths: Turret mode adds 200 to both defenses and doubles his Passive, turning him into a fortress
A single Skill 2 mine covers vision, a shield, armor shred, and a slow
Skill 1's 70% speed boost makes disengaging from turret mode fast
Best-in-class AoE damage among marksmen once crit items are complete
weaknesses: Completely immobile while the turret is deployed, helpless against hard CC and dives
No mobility skill; mines are his only answer to ganks
The turret deals 50% less to towers, so his solo siege power is poor
Mediocre fighting power until two core items are finished forces a patient early game

Mortal Punisher slides back to fifth, and the three Reaver slots go to Hunt instead, so physical lifesteal stops at 20%. Sunchaser closes the build with +125 attack range and +20% movement speed on a 75-second cooldown, while ten Hunt slots hold movement speed at +25% and ten Calamity slots push crit rate to +86%.

name: Jing
title: Jing Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An assassin who fights alongside her mirror image, marking targets from two directions and swapping positions mid-fight. Every swap breaks the enemy's aim — mastered, she feels uncatchable.
playstyle: An assassin who fights alongside her mirror image, marking targets from two directions and swapping positions mid-fight. Every swap breaks the enemy's aim — mastered, she feels uncatchable.
bestFor: players who like playing against the enemy's screen — the image hits harder the farther it stands from her, and one mistimed swap costs the whole life.

tips.earlyGame: Jungle Jing lives or dies on understanding the mirror image. With no image on the field, casting Skill 1 or Skill 2 spawns one for 2s, and it replicates everything you do except Skill 4. Your body and the image apply two different types of mark, and when both sit on the same enemy the marks shatter. The shatter deals physical damage equal to 4% of the target's lost Health and refreshes the cooldowns of Skill 1 and Skill 2, once every 5s. Drill that reset rhythm on jungle camps first, then hit level 4 as fast as you can. For early ganks, Skill 1's dash and 1.5s slow to stop their feet, plus the mirror's overlapping damage to complete the marks, is already plenty of chip. Practicing clean reset patterns beats greedy invades.
tips.midGame: From around 7 minutes, with your first physical core item finished, Jing's burst puts squishy targets inside one-combo range. Hunt lone enemies in their jungle or on the side lanes: enter with Skill 1, complete the marks with the mirror, take the reset, re-dash with the refreshed Skill 1 — chain that loop and they never get a turn. Skill 2 hits everything around you and pushes your own Movement Speed up by 50%, diminishing over 1s. The heal is biggest on the first enemy struck, with each additional target adding 25% of that amount. Swing it once you are fully inside their space and you get the damage, the heal, and the speed to leave on. Before the 4-minute Tyrant and the 10-minute Shadow Tyrant, deleting the enemy support who comes for vision frees up your whole team.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Jing is the flanking blade aimed at the enemy marksman's throat. With durability that folds in a few hits, diving the front of a 5v5 unplanned is suicide, so you spend long stretches waiting. Watch which target the enemy's point-and-click crowd control gets used on, then enter with Skill 1. Skill 3, Dimensional Shift, swaps you with your mirror image and covers both extending a kill and getting out. It stocks 1 charge every 10s and caps at 4. Even with a full hand, impose one rule on yourself — always keep one for the road home — and your deaths drop. Skill 4, Mirror Domain, flies forward pulling enemies along, then opens a Mirror Vortex at the stopping point and immobilizes whoever is at its center for 1s. Inside the vortex you also take reduced damage, so the dive comes with a layer of extra durability. Getting your swap read and answered with crowd control is the number one killer, so vary your swap timing every time.
tips.teamfight: Hold the perimeter until your tank draws the enemy's crowd control, then slide in the moment the backline's feet are exposed. Skill 1 into empowered basic attack into Skill 2 completes the marks; once they shatter and the reset lands, swap with your mirror using Skill 3 to make their counterattack whiff, then re-enter on the refreshed Skill 1 — that in-and-out loop is the ideal form. Because the shatter scales off the target's lost Health, your execution speed climbs as the brawl wears on and health bars drop. While Skill 4 is active the shatter's cooldown falls from 5s to 2s, and inside the Mirror Vortex every hit you land stocks another charge of Skill 3. Every second spent hitting a full-HP tank is wasted, so keep your eyes locked on the softest target alive.

strengths: Dual-mark cooldown resets multiply both tempo and burst
The missing-HP slash makes her a premier executioner of chipped targets
Skill 3's swap covers re-engage and escape in a single motion
On-hit healing from Skill 2 lets her brawl longer than she looks
weaknesses: Damage falls off a cliff whenever marks fail to complete
The mirror image starts at 30% of her damage — keep it hugging her and output stalls
Paper durability; a predicted swap into crowd control is a death sentence
Mirror management piles on the workload and stretches the learning curve

name: Kaizer
title: Kaizer Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A duel-specialist whose attacks hit 50% harder against lone targets. His demon-armor ultimate transforms him — isolate one enemy and few heroes in the game match his kill pressure.
playstyle: A duel-specialist whose attacks hit 50% harder against lone targets. His demon-armor ultimate transforms him — isolate one enemy and few heroes in the game match his kill pressure.
bestFor: duelists who go out and manufacture the 1v1 — basics and Skill 2 hit 50% harder when only one enemy is in range, with the ultimate's eight seconds stacked on top.

tips.earlyGame: The clash lane 1v1 is where Kaizer shines brightest. Start trading with Skill 1's thrown blade from level 1 — when the blade returns to you it heals and refunds 30% of its cooldown, so you consistently come out of trades with the HP lead. Keep his Passive in mind: basic attacks and Skill 2 deal 50% more damage when they hit only a single target. Don't chase enemies hiding inside their minion wave; manage the push to drag your opponent into an isolated spot, then start swinging.
tips.midGame: Once you learn your Ultimate, those 8 seconds of +500 max HP, +100 physical attack, and +60 damage block are pure stat-check violence — almost nobody beats you 1v1. At the 4-minute Tyrant fight, don't walk in through the front. Catch isolated enemies from the river bushes instead: knock them up with Skill 2's second slash and chase with the empowered basic attack's dash and they're not getting away. But once the buff expires you're a different, far weaker hero — if you can't finish the kill within 8 seconds, don't commit at all.
tips.lateGame: You're still a duelist late, not the guy who runs face-first into five enemies. Enter teamfights late from the flank, transform, and beeline straight for their marksman or mage — a fed Kaizer deletes squishy backliners in two or three hits with the empowered basic attack. Before Overlord, deliberately showing yourself so the threat of your Ultimate forces their formation backward is part of the job. When your transformation has under 2 seconds left, stop chasing and disengage while picking up Skill 1's heal.
tips.teamfight: Rotate to a side bush before the fight starts, and go in the instant your team draws the enemy's attention. Skill 1 slows the target while speeding you up, then transform with your Ultimate and close the gap with Skill 2's knockup. Commit to exactly one target. Even in a scrap, pick the moment your victim is standing alone — the Passive's 50% bonus kicks in and they drop noticeably faster than they expect. While the enemy is still clumped, sometimes the right call is chipping them with the transformation's aura damage and waiting.

strengths: Passive adds 50% damage to basics and Skill 2 against isolated targets
Ultimate's 8-second stat surge makes him one of the best 1v1 heroes in the game
Skill 1's heal and cooldown refund win extended trades and sustain the lane
Skill 2's knockup plus dash lets him complete picks entirely on his own
weaknesses: Drops back to base stats when the Ultimate ends and folds to counterattacks
Single-target damage profile struggles against clumped frontline fights
Skill 2 is his only gap-closer, so ranged kiting shuts him down
Every engage depends heavily on whether his Ultimate is off cooldown

It also grants a 400-800 (+7% bonus HP) magic damage shield every 15 seconds and turns 15% of bonus magic defense into physical defense. Physical attack finishes at +279, 90 short of build 1.

name: Kongming
title: Kongming Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A tactician mage who orbits auto-attacking orbs at five marks and blinks in and out of range. His lock-on ultimate needs its channel protected — choosing when and where to cast is the skill.
playstyle: A tactician mage who orbits auto-attacking orbs at five marks and blinks in and out of range. His lock-on ultimate needs its channel protected — choosing when and where to cast is the skill.
bestFor: mages who build a play in steps — five marks for the orbs, two blink charges for the angle, and an ultimate whose channel someone else has to be protecting.

tips.earlyGame: How the midgame treats Kongming is decided by how cleanly he plays before level 4. Fan Skill 1 through waves to farm seal stacks, keep the five-stack orbs orbiting, and take short trades while they hover — the orbs fly at the nearest enemy automatically, so your opponent stepping up for a last hit is your cue to chip them. Skill 2 carries two charges, but the arithmetic is fixed: spend one aggressively, and the other is your ticket home, always. Finish this phase without dying once and you have already passed.
tips.midGame: Kongming's show starts when the Ultimate comes online. Hunt anything below half HP — the missile scales with missing health, so a chipped target eats far more than the tooltip suggests. Land the kill and 80% of the cooldown refunds with seals instantly maxed, and the hunt loops straight into the next victim. Shove mid, show up to the 4:00 Tyrant, and fan Skill 1 from the perimeter to pre-chip the fight. One discipline: while the enemy still holds two or more lockdown skills, forcing entries with Skill 2 stays in the pocket.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Kongming demands almost unreasonable patience. Enemies walk in tight packs with magic defense stacked, and a casual entry is nothing but food for their lockdown. So orbit the fight, cycle Skill 1 to keep the seals alive, and watch the blinks and CC leave their hands. The instant someone's HP crosses the execute line, cut an angle with Skill 2 and let the Ultimate fly. After the first kill, resets start flowing with a full orbit of orbs — flip from statue to storm and keep pressing. That toggle between stillness and violence is the entire hero.
tips.teamfight: Kongming starts every teamfight outside its walls. Sprinkle Skill 1 to hold the seals, let the orbs freelance in the frontline scrum, and study which target is bleeding. The Ultimate gets blocked by whoever stands in between, so create diagonal firing lines with Skill 2 or Flash before releasing. A detail most players miss: even if an ally finishes the target during your charge-up, the 80% refund still triggers — never hesitate over kill-secure anxiety. The moment after firing is your most defenseless; confirm the exit before you ever commit.

strengths: Kills refund 80% of the Ultimate's cooldown and instantly max his seals
Two blink charges create angles and escapes on demand
Auto-attacking orbs apply constant pressure while he stays out of reach
Missing-HP scaling on the Ultimate erases anything left low
weaknesses: The Ultimate is body-blocked by enemies standing in the way
Paper-thin the moment both blink charges are spent
Ordinary damage whenever his seal stacks lapse
Misjudge the execute line and he becomes a decoration

Ardent Dominion, the third buy, clears crowd control below 30% HP and puts up a 4-second shield. The fourth item, Venomous Staff, cuts enemy healing and lifesteal by 35% for 2.5 seconds on every hit. builds.title: Runeblade as the opening buy

builds.notes: Runeblade takes the 2160G opening slot and Boots of the Arcane slides to second. Every monster Kongming or a nearby ally kills feeds Runeblade 6 magical attack, stacking up to 25 times. Savant's Wrath and its 30% magical attack bonus lands fourth at 7,060G, a full 1,920G sooner than in the first build. Splendor finishes the build with 1.5 seconds where nothing can touch Kongming — though he cannot move, attack, or cast either — and cooldown reduction totals +22.5%.

name: Kui
title: Kui Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A fisherman support who hooks one enemy and serves them to his team. Every landed hook is the starting gun of a fight, and his void-gate ultimate swallows entire groups.
playstyle: A fisherman support who hooks one enemy and serves them to his team. Every landed hook is the starting gun of a fight, and his void-gate ultimate swallows entire groups.
bestFor: living and dying by one skillshot. A landed hook starts the fight, a missed one leaves you useless for several seconds — and that is on you.

tips.earlyGame: Kui roams as an aggressive support, but the early job isn't landing hooks — it's standing where a hook is possible. Fade into the mid bushes or along the river, and the moment an enemy steps forward, drag them in with Skill 2. One connected hook becomes a first-blood setup for your team, and every kill or assist permanently grows Kui's HP. The punishment for whiffing is severe, so until level 4, only pull targets who aren't hiding behind their minion wave. The four-minute Tyrant spawn is also prime time for an ambush hook on anyone rotating in.
tips.midGame: Level 4 completes the lockdown script. Skill 2's hook marks the first enemy it hits with Into the Void, and Skill 3 stuns marked targets continuously — up to 16 devours land on someone who cannot move. Before Tyrant or Overlord, a single hook from outside vision forces the enemy to start the fight a player down. Choose the target well: the enemy marksman or mid laner. Nobody on your team celebrates a hooked tank. Keep stacking kill participation and Void Devour climbs with it; 20 stacks is 3,600 extra Health, and Kui quietly ends up as durable as a front-liner.
tips.lateGame: Late game Kui bets entire matches on one hook. During Shadow Tyrant standoffs, lurk in a bush half a step behind your front line and wait for the enemy carry's positioning mistake — patiently, for as long as it takes. When the pull lands, chain your Ultimate and Skill 1 for lockdown and damage while your team collapses on the target. The reverse is just as true: with no mobility skill, getting caught means dying on the spot. The Passive does splash damage around you when you take a massive hit or die, so even your worst moments carry a threat — but play careful, and make the one hook count.
tips.teamfight: The ideal teamfight starts before the teamfight: one clean pull. Yank a back-liner out of formation with Skill 2 and you open five against four. Once the brawl is live, land Skill 1 at point-blank range to spread the mark — enemies right next to Kui take 250% magical damage and are marked with Into the Void. Stack Skill 3 onto them and the mark holds them in a continuous stun through all 16 devours. Because his effects cluster around his own body, you will wade into the enemy's half of the fight, and whether you survive it depends on the Health you banked earlier. When the hook whiffs, don't linger trying to salvage it; fall back into your lines immediately.

strengths: One hook creates a numbers advantage before the fight even starts
Skill 3 keeps anyone marked with Into the Void in a continuous stun
Kills and assists permanently stack HP toward front-liner bulk
Deals damage around him even in death, so he's never a free kill
weaknesses: No mobility skill — once caught, he usually just dies
Whiffing the hook leaves him nearly useless for several seconds
His effects center on his own body, forcing risky positioning
A pull without allied follow-up is just a one-way ticket

Its active hits four times, each hit stripping 3% of current HP and cutting movement speed by 25-50%. Dropping Glacial Buckler pulls every later slot forward by one, so Frigid Charge is finished at 4,810G. Overlord's Platemail closes the build at 2450G and takes max HP to +7187, 1200 above build 1.

name: Lady Sun
title: Lady Sun Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A tumbling gunner whose basic attacks refund her roll — the more she shoots, the more she moves. Her life depends on never losing damage while never standing still.
playstyle: A tumbling gunner whose basic attacks refund her roll — the more she shoots, the more she moves. Her life depends on never losing damage while never standing still.
bestFor: carries who refuse to stand still — basic attacks pay the roll back, so shooting is what buys the mobility, and spending the roll on aggression leaves no way home.

tips.earlyGame: Farm-lane Lady Sun is banking for a payoff that arrives after the ten-minute mark. Farm cleanly, and above all, never stop attacking — every basic attack that connects cuts Skill 1's cooldown by 10%, so the roll is always coming back as long as you're swinging. The roll into empowered basic into extended-range basic is a real trade pattern, but early on it's better held as insurance for when the enemy jungler goes missing. If your team contests the 4:00 Tyrant, contribute from the back of the river — no heroics required.
tips.midGame: Once one or two crit items finish around 7-9 minutes, the roll-and-shoot style becomes real damage. Push side waves, and trade with the full package: the Skill 2 bomb shreds 10% of their physical defense and applies a mark, which your empowered basic then cashes in. Rolling near an enemy hero also grants a burst of movement speed, so your hit-and-run game is quicker than it looks. The habit to build now is roll direction: forward only when the kill is certain, sideways or backward everything else, shooting while the cooldown ticks back. That's the whole secret to a long life.
tips.lateGame: With four or five items, Lady Sun's sustained fire melts frontliners and everything behind them. At Overlord fights past ten minutes, the ideal picture is you at maximum range, cycling empowered basics while your frontline absorbs attention. Choose the Ultimate's job case by case: opening poke before the fight, or a long-range execute on a runner. The ballista travels through walls and brush, and a kill shot arriving from somewhere invisible does real psychological damage. The one iron rule: for a few seconds after you spend the roll aggressively, play one step further back than feels natural.
tips.teamfight: Lady Sun's greatest teamfight contribution is uninterrupted output from a position nobody can reach. Open by firing the Ultimate past the enemy frontline — the cone explosion carries the damage into their backline. From there, keep basic attacks flowing to recycle Skill 1, and roll laterally to keep breaking the dive angles of enemy assassins. When someone does get close, drop Skill 2 at your feet: the slow plus defense shred makes your counterattack start winning immediately. Think of it as shooting first and rolling as a consequence — that ordering is what lets damage and survival coexist.

strengths: Basic attacks refund Skill 1's cooldown, letting her roll and shoot indefinitely
Empowered and extended-range basics give her burst and sustained damage in one kit
Skill 2's defense shred and mark keep her damage honest against tanks
The Ultimate's ballista flies through walls and executes fleeing enemies
weaknesses: Spending the roll aggressively opens a defenseless window with no escape
All her mobility lives in one skill — layered CC leaves her with no answer
Heavily item-dependent, so a rough early game delays her damage badly

With arcana counted, +87% attack speed and +1600 max HP both beat the other build, and the damage grows with the HP the enemy stacks.

name: Lady Zhen
title: Lady Zhen Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A lockdown mage who freezes enemies at three ice marks and reshapes the map with an impassable ice pillar. Her value is measured in seconds of stopped enemies, not damage.
playstyle: A lockdown mage who freezes enemies at three ice marks and reshapes the map with an impassable ice pillar. Her value is measured in seconds of stopped enemies, not damage.
bestFor: players who count their game in seconds of enemy downtime rather than kills — three frost marks freeze a target, and the pillar no hero can walk through makes placement matter more than aim.

tips.earlyGame: Start your mid lane by clearing with Skill 2. The water current bounces between minions on its own, so firing it the moment the enemy laner steps near their wave turns clear and harass into one cast. Your Passive's frost marks last seven seconds, and three stacks trigger a 0.75-second freeze — land two or three bounces, follow with Skill 1, and you can freeze targets as early as level 2. That said, the ice pillar comes out slowly and gets sidestepped on its own, so treat it as a placement tool for the moment your opponent steps forward. Don't force plays before level 4; keeping your lane opponent at half HP is a job well done.
tips.midGame: Once you learn your Ultimate, Lady Zhen becomes a gank-assist specialist. The water current slaps a 90% slow — a near-total stop — on the first hero it hits for a full second, so firing it as your jungler arrives all but guarantees the catch. Chain Skill 1 and Skill 2 behind it and you ride straight into a three-stack freeze. From the 4-minute mark, rotate toward the river about 30 seconds before Tyrant spawns and lay your Ultimate's flood zone across the narrow river paths to seal off the enemy's approach entirely. Anyone who steps in bleeds damage every second, forcing a choice between a long detour and walking through the pain.
tips.lateGame: With three core items finished, chained freezes alone let you dictate teamfights — but your own body stays paper-thin, so always operate from behind your frontline. When an enemy assassin dives you, the trump card is self-freezing: cast Skill 1 on top of your Ultimate's flood zone to become invulnerable for three seconds and let their whole combo whiff. The pillar's collapse damage on exit even sets up your counterattack. You can't move while frozen and everyone knows exactly where you are, so save it for moments your teammates can collapse as you thaw. Narrow-corridor standoffs before Overlord are where Lady Zhen has no equal.
tips.teamfight: Before the fight starts, fire your Ultimate down a narrow approach to break the enemy's formation with the flood zone. Pour Skill 2 into anyone caught standing still — the bouncing current farms frost marks across clumped enemies and can freeze several of them at once. A frozen target eats your team's entire damage output without answering back, so landing the chain effectively ends the fight. If you get dived, self-freeze with Skill 1 inside the zone and wait the three seconds for help. The one thing to respect: miss your Ultimate and you've lost your pick tool until it returns, so back off rather than gamble.

strengths: Every skill applies frost marks, chaining lockdown through three-stack freezes
Bouncing water damage that gets stronger the more enemies clump together
Elite zoning — the flood zone and ice pillar seal off narrow corridors
A self-freeze escape hatch worth three seconds of invulnerability
weaknesses: Skill 1 is slow to arm and hard to land without a slow set up first
Missing the Ultimate removes her pick threat almost entirely
No mobility skill — one positioning mistake is usually fatal
Enemies who time her thaw can delete her before the counterattack comes

name: Lam
title: Lam Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An execution specialist: enemies below 30% Health are marked as Prey and take bonus true damage from his skills and Basic Attacks. He closes the gap on the +40 Movement Speed of Submerge mode and finishes wounded targets one by one — he has almost no tools for a fair fight.
playstyle: An execution specialist: enemies below 30% Health are marked as Prey and take bonus true damage from his skills and Basic Attacks. He closes the gap on the +40 Movement Speed of Submerge mode and finishes wounded targets one by one — he has almost no tools for a fair fight.
bestFor: players who read health bars before they read fights, surfacing from Submerge the moment a target drops under 30% and never taking a fair duel.

tips.earlyGame: As a jungler, Lam's first goal is using Skill 1's dive mode (+40 movement speed) to cut travel time between camps and secure level 4 plus the Ultimate before the 4-minute Tyrant spawns. The on-hit healing from Skill 2 keeps your HP topped up mid-clear, so you can often full-clear without recalling. Pick gank targets around the Passive: enemies below 30% HP take bonus true damage, so hit lanes where the enemy is already chipped. Train your eyes on that 30% line on every health bar — the number of kills you convert changes visibly.
tips.midGame: Mid-game Lam owns the river. Use dive mode's speed to slip into the enemy jungle and drag isolated targets to the dash endpoint with the Ultimate, delivering them into your team's arms. Cast during dive mode, the Ultimate hauls every enemy along its path, so the dream opening at objectives is abducting the enemy jungler before the fight starts. Around 10 minutes, with two physical core items done, the mark-chase combo alone chips squishy enemies to 30% HP — then the Passive's true damage zone finishes the job.
tips.lateGame: The late game is an exercise in patience. Lam is not a first-engage piece; he's a finisher who slips into the backline seconds after enemy targeted crowd control and attention lock onto your frontline. Stack marks with Skill 2, weave the empowered basic attack's dash and healing, and execute enemies in order as they cross below 30% HP. Resetting after each kill matters too — whether you can ride out cooldowns in dive mode is the difference between life and death. In Overlord standoffs, keep showing the enemy marksman the threat of a dive-mode Ultimate abduction.
tips.teamfight: Lam's teamfight motto: enter second, outlast everyone. Circle the perimeter in dive mode at the start, and the moment enemy crowd control is spent, drag out their squishiest member with the Ultimate. From there, cycle Skill 2 into empowered basic attack dashes, healing through the on-hit sustain while you execute targets one at a time. The Passive works harder as health bars drop across the fight, so simply surviving the early chaos is itself a damage steroid. If chasing deep means ending up 1v3, dive out and wait for the next victim instead — that composure defines good Lam play.

strengths: True damage below 30% HP means chipped targets never escape
Chained dashes from dive mode and mark chases make him hard to pin down
Skill 2's on-hit healing keeps him brawling on the frontline
The dive-mode Ultimate hauls enemies to the dash endpoint — a premier catch
weaknesses: Missing the Ultimate strands him alone in the middle of the enemy team
Hard crowd control breaks the dash chain and his thin frame melts fast
Managing dive mode, marks, and empowered attacks at once demands high APM

name: Lapulapu
title: Lapulapu Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A walking aura: he armors himself and whichever ally is lowest, automatically. His sweeping ultimate interrupts channels — a breakwater built to crush the enemy's biggest cast.
playstyle: A walking aura: he armors himself and whichever ally is lowest, automatically. His sweeping ultimate interrupts channels — a breakwater built to crush the enemy's biggest cast.
bestFor: anyone who values quiet work. Simply standing with your team raises their defenses, and cutting one enemy channel short with the third skill can turn the fight.

tips.earlyGame: Start the game glued to your marksman in the farm lane. Lapulapu's Passive, Sea Beast's Favor, raises defenses for both himself and the lowest-HP ally nearby, so simply standing next to your carry does work — camping a bush alone wastes the buff. Once you have Skill 2, punish any enemy who steps up by dashing in for a short trade with the knock-up. Skill 1's tap slash comes back fast and heals you on every hit, so spam it freely whenever a brawl breaks out. And don't forget to rotate toward mid before the Tyrant spawns at four minutes.
tips.midGame: From level 4 onward, Lapulapu's hidden strength is that his Ultimate interrupts enemy skill casts. One charged strike can cancel a channeled ultimate or a Recall mid-cast, so at Tyrant fights, time it on top of the enemy jungler's Punish attempt. Between roams, you can also pre-throw your weapon with Skill 1 (hold) to tag enemies with the 50 physical defense shred before your team commits. You're the one eating hits at the front of every fight, so start playing forward in earnest around the six-minute mark, once your first core defensive item is finished.
tips.lateGame: The Shadow Tyrant fights after ten minutes are where you earn your keep. Skill 2 into Ultimate chains two knock-ups for roughly 1.75 seconds of total airtime — whether your team's damage lands inside that window decides the fight, so only engage within range of your allies. The rift lingers for five seconds, and dropping it across a narrow chokepoint in front of the Overlord pit dramatically slows any enemy approach. The Passive does boost your defenses by another 50% when you're alone, but you have no kill threat, so never chase deep. In retreats, cover the back line with the weapon throw's slow.
tips.teamfight: Skill 2 is your signal to start the fight. Drag the knocked-up target into your Ultimate's charge and force the brawl on top of the rift — that's the ideal shape. Once the scrap starts, keep landing Skill 1's tap slash; the healing and cooldown refunds make you far harder to kill than you look. Be picky about who you launch: aim for an overextended mage or marksman, never the enemy tank. And the instant you see a healing or recall channel start, cancel it with your Ultimate's interrupt. It's unglamorous work, but it wins games.

strengths: Passive raises defenses for himself and the lowest-HP nearby ally at once
Ultimate interrupts enemy skill casts, shutting down channeled abilities
Skill 1's healing and cooldown refunds make him excel in extended brawls
Skill 2 into Ultimate chains a punishing double knock-up
weaknesses: Low personal damage — his lockdown is wasted without allied follow-up
Ultimate needs a charge-up and often misses high-mobility targets
Skill 2 is his only dash, leaving no escape after he commits
No answer to long-range poke and gets chipped down for free

Frigid Charge adds a 0.75-second freeze in the third slot, and Ominous Premonition strips up to 40% attack speed off anyone who damages you. Succubus Cloak then refreshes a 400–800 (+7% bonus HP) magic shield every 15 seconds and converts 15% of bonus magic defense into physical defense. Gear and arcana total +7,387 max HP and +490 magic defense — 1,000 more HP and 120 more magic defense than build 1, paid for with 180 physical defense and 12.5 points of cooldown reduction.

name: Li Bai
title: Li Bai Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A swordsman with a charge-and-release rhythm: basic attacks build sword energy that unlocks his ultimate. Dash in, phase through the counterattack with his untargetable sword formation, and exit on the return dash.
playstyle: A swordsman with a charge-and-release rhythm: basic attacks build sword energy that unlocks his ultimate. Dash in, phase through the counterattack with his untargetable sword formation, and exit on the return dash.
bestFor: players who decide the way out before going in — four stacks of sword energy unlock the ultimate and the third cast of Skill 1 snaps you back where you started, a routine that pays for drilling.

tips.earlyGame: Jungle, no debate — and early Li Bai is genuinely weak. Your Ultimate stays locked until basic attacks build four Sword Qi stacks, and your clear speed is nothing special. Concede the opening buff scrap to your team and quietly farm safe routes until level 4. Weave basic attacks between skills even while clearing to keep Sword Qi topped up — it prevents the classic beginner disaster of reaching a kill window with your Ultimate still locked. If the enemy jungler invades, don't fight; use Skill 1's third cast to blink back to your origin point and leave. Surviving this phase is the whole assignment.
tips.midGame: From level 4 on, there's one non-negotiable pre-gank ritual: hit a nearby minion or monster until Sword Qi is full, then go in. That's the Li Bai law. The sequence is Skill 1's double dash for the stun, Skill 2 to strip 150 physical defense, then the unlocked Ultimate for the five-slash flurry. Kill secured, take Skill 1's third cast back to your entry point and the counterattack never comes. Delete the enemy mid laner or marksman two or three times before the 10-minute mark and the item lead snowballs into full map control. Until Shadow Tyrant spawns, you should always be hunting your next mark.
tips.lateGame: A five-item Li Bai is a nightmare for the enemy backline — but diving at a teamfight's opening bell is strictly forbidden. Both untargetability windows are strong, yet getting caught while enemy CC is still up means dying in one rotation. Wait in a flanking bush until two enemy lockdown skills are spent, then enter with Skill 1 and unload. Remember your Ultimate loses up to 30% damage per target when it strikes multiple heroes, so it's a scalpel for one isolated carry, not a bomb for their clumped frontline. Once the target drops, don't get greedy — take the exit.
tips.teamfight: Li Bai's teamfight is 90% waiting. Fight the itch to enter on the engage; watch until enemy stuns and hooks are burned on your teammates, then move. Enter with Skill 1's dash, drop Skill 2's 150-defense shred under their feet, and carve the priority backliner with your Ultimate — two layers of untargetability mean almost nothing touches you in between. Kill confirmed, take Skill 1's third cast out of the fight. The moment right after, with Sword Qi empty, is your only true weakness, so hit a minion to rebuild stacks before you look for round two.

strengths: Two layers of untargetability nullify enemy retaliation
Skill 1's return blink makes him nearly impossible to pin down
Massive single-target burst off a 150 defense shred into the flurry
weaknesses: The Ultimate stays locked without four Sword Qi stacks — setup is mandatory
Slow early clear; falling behind before coming online is hard to fix
Ultimate damage decays against multiple targets, so clumped fights hurt him
Demanding mechanics — mismanage the return blink and he kills himself

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Antiheal and slow

name: Li Xin
title: Li Xin Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A fighter who alternates between the Domination (light) and Revenge (dark) modes. Light converts attack speed into damage reduction and shortens his cooldowns for a durable, grinding style; dark converts physical attack into attack speed and opens with a knock-up field. Switching transfers energy between the two, so you are always choosing which side to lean on.
playstyle: A fighter who alternates between the Domination (light) and Revenge (dark) modes. Light converts attack speed into damage reduction and shortens his cooldowns for a durable, grinding style; dark converts physical attack into attack speed and opens with a knock-up field. Switching transfers energy between the two, so you are always choosing which side to lean on.
bestFor: players who want both answers on one hero — light turns attack speed into damage reduction, dark turns attack into attack speed, and the timing of the swap is the skill.

tips.earlyGame: Until level 4, Li Xin is one of the last heroes in the clash lane you want brawling with. His base mode hits soft, so stick to flicking Skill 2's sword qi from range for last hits and harass, and dash out with Skill 1 the moment someone commits onto you. The Passive's base mode grants bonus EXP whenever a basic attack or Skill 2 tags a hero, so even safe poke pays out experience. Against a lane bully, conceding waves under tower is exactly the right amount of cowardice.
tips.midGame: At level 4 you leave base mode behind: Skill 3 awakens Light (Domination), Skill 4 awakens Dark (Revenge). Domination turns bonus attack speed into physical damage reduction and holds up in a straight brawl. Revenge turns bonus physical attack into attack speed and drowns people in swings. Neither choice is locked for the match. Once awakened, Skill 4 becomes the mode swap — no cooldown, uninterruptible by crowd control, and it deals 200 damage (level 1) to nearby enemies on the switch. What carries over, though, is only (100 − your current energy), so swapping on a full gauge wastes the transfer; spend the mode you are in first. Energy drains 10 per second, so awaken right before contact instead of burning the gauge on the walk over.
tips.lateGame: Late game, Domination Li Xin holds the front during tower defenses and Overlord standoffs, using the damage reduction to eat the enemy's opening swing. Revenge Li Xin skips the main fight entirely, split pushing and deleting whoever peels off to stop him in a 1v1. Energy only fills to the cap of 100 when he awakens out of base mode with Skill 3 or Skill 4 — swapping between the two forms hands him just (100 − his current energy). Time the awakening to the engage call and save the swap for when the gauge is already low. Get that order wrong and you run dry mid-fight, back to something close to base-mode Li Xin.
tips.teamfight: In Domination, fight half a step behind your tank, sliding Skill 2's sword qi into the crowd and deciding on every cooldown whether to chase with Skill 1 or hold it. The damage reduction is real, but you are not an actual tank — stay out of stacked CC zones. In Revenge, enter from the fight's outer edge and use your attack speed to delete an isolated backliner first. Your best window is the first fight, before the enemy has read your mode — show them steel or show them speed, and warp how they play the rest of the game.

strengths: Picks Domination or Revenge to fit whatever the draft needs
Domination converts attack speed into damage reduction for brawls
Revenge converts attack into attack speed and drowns 1v1s in swings
Skill 2 sword qi clears waves from a safe distance
weaknesses: Feeble before level 4; a lost lane is slow to repair
Each mode burns 10 energy per second and gases out in long fights
A form swap only grants (100 - current energy), so swapping on a full gauge wastes it
Skill 1 is his only mobility, so layered CC leaves no exit
