Blood Rage, bought fourth, trades 30% of current HP for a four-second shield worth 40% of max HP. Physical attack lands at +209 against build one's +339, trading damage for staying power.

name: Lian Po
title: Lian Po Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A tank who has crowd control immunity during every skill — enemy lockdown simply does not apply. His Battle Spirit stacks make him tougher as brawls drag on, plowing the enemy line in repeated passes.
playstyle: A tank who has crowd control immunity during every skill — enemy lockdown simply does not apply. His Battle Spirit stacks make him tougher as brawls drag on, plowing the enemy line in repeated passes.
bestFor: players who want to drive their own plan straight through enemy crowd control, cycling in and out of a brawl that only makes them harder the longer it runs.

tips.earlyGame: Lian Po starts the clash lane weaker than he looks. His Battle Spirit gauge is empty at level 1, so the damage reduction from his Passive isn't online yet — don't force extended trades before level 3. Instead, take short exchanges with the Skill 1 dash and the third-hit heavy strike from its passive, and soak waves behind the Skill 2 shield. Here's the trick: if an enemy is standing inside your Skill 2 charge zone, Skill 1's cooldown resets instantly, so you win trades on sheer number of touches. Once you hit level 4, rotate to the river for the 4:00 Tyrant and play knock-up bot next to your jungler.
tips.midGame: Around the eight-minute mark, with two defensive items done, Lian Po gets to start fights on his own terms. You have crowd control immunity for the entire duration of your skill animations, so enemy stuns and knock-ups simply don't matter mid-cast — that's your license to dive. Drop out of a mid-lane brush with your Ultimate, use the first two slams to cut off the escape route, and land the third-slam knock-up on your real target. Win or lose the skirmish, leaving combat converts your Battle Spirit into HP, so you arrive at the next objective healthy. When teams start shadowboxing before Shadow Tyrant, volunteer to be the one who face-checks brushes.
tips.lateGame: Past ten minutes, when Shadow Tyrant and Overlord decide games, your entire job comes down to one decision: who eats the first hit. Before the fight breaks out, smack a nearby minion or jungle camp to pre-stack Battle Spirit, so you enter with the damage reduction and attack speed already rolling. Your Ultimate lets you adjust the slam position through the first two hits — aim the third slam where the enemy is running to, not where they are, and it stops missing. You don't need kills; peeling two enemy backliners out of the fight is a full day's work. The one true loss condition is overchasing and dying alone.
tips.teamfight: The dream engage is a Skill 3 that clips two or three members of the enemy midline. Land, then start charging Skill 2 on the spot — any enemy inside the zone refunds Skill 1 instantly, and the 15% slow while charging drags out their retreat. The blast hits hardest at the epicenter, so the closer you plant yourself, the better it pays. One caveat: the pull only grabs non-hero units. Enemy heroes never get dragged in, so the clumping has to come from your own footwork. Dash, charge, dash again — that loop draws enemy fire onto you while carving their formation in half. You're there to split the fight, not to secure kills; leave those to your carries. When your HP dips, disengage for a moment, let Battle Spirit convert back into HP, then walk right back in. From the enemy's side, the tank they thought they killed just keeps coming back.

strengths: Crowd control immunity during every skill animation lets him engage straight through enemy CC
Battle Spirit stacks make him tankier as fights drag on — brawls are his home turf
Skill 2 refunds Skill 1 when it catches an enemy, fueling relentless in-and-out pressure
Battle Spirit converts to HP out of combat, so he re-enters fights faster than expected
weaknesses: With zero Battle Spirit right after spawning, he's far squishier than his frame suggests
The Skill 2 blast and the Ultimate's third slam are slow to land and easy for agile enemies to dodge
Poor base movement speed means he's often a step late to the fight

name: Liang
title: Liang Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The definitive single-target suppressor: his ultimate holds one enemy helpless for over two seconds. Barriers and repeating true damage soften targets; the suppression converts them.
playstyle: The definitive single-target suppressor: his ultimate holds one enemy helpless for over two seconds. Barriers and repeating true damage soften targets; the suppression converts them.
bestFor: the job nobody volunteers for. Your team asks you to remove one hero, so you stand still for 2.2 seconds and take that ace out of the fight.

tips.earlyGame: Skill 2 runs Liang's early mid lane. The circle deals 50% bonus damage to non-heroes for fast waveclear, and since two can be maintained at once, parking one in a river bush doubles as vision. Once the wave is shoved, use that vision to move with your jungler, and hit level 4 as fast as possible — the 2.2-second suppression is one of the longest lockdowns in the game, and from the moment it unlocks, your mid lane carries constant kill threat.
tips.midGame: Mid game, your biggest job is picks with your jungler — catching an isolated enemy before objectives. Suppress whoever walks up for vision before the Tyrant or Shadow Tyrant and the objective is yours without a fight. One caution: Liang is rooted for the entire suppression. Only cast it within reach of your team's damage, or you'll land a perfect lockdown and then get left behind alone. Also, walk through your own Skill 2 circles when rotating — the move speed boost is a small habit with real mileage.
tips.lateGame: Late game, who you suppress IS the match. The default target is the enemy's main carry, but the Ultimate is also a first-class counter to assassins diving your backline: read the landing spot of their dash, wait, and suppress on contact — they melt without taking a single action. Use Skill 1's four barriers to zone retreat paths and chokepoints, and let the Passive's true damage grind down even the frontline tanks.
tips.teamfight: Stay behind your frontline at the very edge of Ultimate range. Open by dropping Skill 1 across the enemy's approach to stagger their entry with the multi-stuns, and lay Skill 2 at your feet to claim ground for your team. Don't rush the Ultimate — hold it for the most dangerous enemy, like the assassin the instant he commits. A stun zone lingers at the target's feet when suppression ends, so tell your team in advance to burst during that 0.75-second window; the kill rate difference is night and day.

strengths: The 2.2-second suppression reliably removes one enemy ace from any fight
Passive true damage keeps hurting even fully stacked tanks
Two circles deliver vision control and fast waveclear for mid priority
Barrier multi-stuns excel at zoning chokes and holding sieges
weaknesses: Rooted and defenseless during the Ultimate, which is hard to place in a scrum
No mobility skill, leaving him soft to ganks and assassin flanks
Barrier stuns don't re-apply to the same target, so lockdown can't be chained
Low burst — closing out kills alone is a struggle

With no pierce items in the list, Cooldown Reduction reaches 40% (against 22.5% on build 1) and Max Health +1700.

name: Liu Bang
title: Liu Bang Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A tank whose shields explode and whose ultimate teleports him to any ally on the map. The mere fact that Liu Bang is missing from vision is pressure — the split-map specialist.
playstyle: A tank whose shields explode and whose ultimate teleports him to any ally on the map. The mere fact that Liu Bang is missing from vision is pressure — the split-map specialist.
bestFor: split-map thinkers. Being absent from the minimap is the threat, the 2.2-second channel is the price, and you alone choose whose fight to land in.

tips.earlyGame: Liu Bang's default home is the clash lane. Until level 4, Skill 1's shield and delayed blast handle the waves, while the Passive's four-stack ranged empowered basic lets you chip melee opponents without ever being touched. Skill 2's charged dash is your only stun and it's precious — through the early game, hold it as the counter-punch for enemy jungler ganks. Liu Bang's real value unlocks with his Ultimate and its map-wide reach, so through this window, simply banking experience without dying earns a passing grade.
tips.midGame: After the 4-minute Tyrant, your two-front war begins. Shove side waves, and the moment a teammate gets touched anywhere on the map, channel your Ultimate and warp to them. You arrive delivering shields, and for 10 seconds after warping, Skill 2 sits at max charge — meaning an immediate full-range stun dash the second you land. The 2.2-second channel is a complete opening, so always cast from brush or behind a tower. Your goal is planting one thought in every enemy's head: if Liu Bang is off the map, this could be a 5v6.
tips.lateGame: With three or more defense items after 15 minutes, split push and make two defenders deal with you. A detail worth banking: your Ultimate's shield scales with the target's bonus HP, so it lands biggest on your beefiest tank or fighter. The gold-standard pattern is pushing a side lane until seconds before Overlord, then warping in as it spawns. And if five enemies start collapsing on you, the warp to a distant ally is itself your escape hatch.
tips.teamfight: Fighting with your team from the start, the job is catching the enemy carry with Skill 2's stun and layering Skill 1's blast on top. The shield can be manually detonated 1.5 seconds after casting, so when enemies glue themselves to you, pop it yourself and waste nothing. Arriving from a side lane instead, drop onto their backline mid-fight and let the max-charge Skill 2 flip the board. Engage together or arrive late — read the enemy comp and pick your policy in the first half, and the hesitation disappears.

strengths: The Ultimate projects pressure onto any fight from anywhere on the map
One warp delivers shields, healing, and his own escape in a single skill
A guaranteed max-charge Skill 2 stun for 10 seconds after every warp
Passive ranged empowered basics let him poke melee laners for free
weaknesses: The 2.2-second channel is a total opening and struggles when watched
Low personal burst — he rarely closes out a kill alone
Built around split play, so one bad Ultimate creates instant man-down fights
No CC beyond the single stun, so mobile enemies slip away repeatedly

name: Liu Bei
title: Liu Bei Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A shotgun brawler who walks his damage forward. His ultimate cleanses CC and grants a huge shield, letting him force the range where every pellet connects.
playstyle: A shotgun brawler who walks his damage forward. His ultimate cleanses CC and grants a huge shield, letting him force the range where every pellet connects.
bestFor: dictating the range of every exchange. Cleanse through the crowd control, walk into point-blank, and land every pellet — distance is the only thing that beats you.

tips.earlyGame: Liu Bei is played jungle first. His Passive shotgun fires four pellets and all four only connect at point-blank range, so hug every buff monster while you clear — your camp speed improves visibly. Level 4 and the Ultimate unlock is your first real decision point; until then, don't force anything and just bank your second buff rotation. When you do gank, enter with Skill 2 from the enemy's escape side so the knockback shoves them toward your teammates. Every pellet that lands stacks physical defense shred, so make it a rule: fight inside their face and empty everything.
tips.midGame: Six to eight minutes, when your core damage item finishes, is when Liu Bei runs wild. Skill 3 cleanses CC, grants three seconds of crowd control immunity, and converts 60% of the damage you deal to enemy heroes into shield. Press it the moment enemy CC turns toward you and the brawl becomes one-sided. At Tyrant and Overlord, keep the stack condition straight: Combat Instinct only builds when a pellet hits an enemy hero, so hammering the boss adds nothing. What the boss does feed is the shield — 20% of the damage dealt to minions and monsters comes back as shield points. Open Skill 3 to thicken the shield while you burn the objective, then turn the pellets onto whoever contests. Sequenced that way, the shred is stacked in time for the Smite duel. When you spot an isolated target, walk them down while saving Skill 2 for the chase — holding the dash in reserve is what separates good Liu Bei players from impatient ones.
tips.lateGame: Past ten minutes, switch to entering fights second. The moment enemy CC and attention lock onto your front line, flank with Skill 2 onto their back line and delete a squishy with point-blank pellets — that's Liu Bei's signature win condition. The Ultimate's shield rebuilds as long as you keep shooting, so answer panicked CC chains with your immunity window and simply out-damage them. Once it expires, though, you're just a melee hero; don't get greedy after a kill. Secure the Shadow Tyrant buff, then close out with the numbers advantage.
tips.teamfight: In teamfights, Liu Bei becomes the star a few seconds after the opening, not at it. Wait until the enemy dumps skills and CC on your front line, then Skill 2 onto something soft and unload — pellets, Skill 1's double shot, more pellets. If they try to stop you, cleanse instantly with your Ultimate and keep firing. The outer two pellets whiff at range, so your teamfight position is permanently inside the enemy's pocket. From their perspective, the fight is basically lost the moment lockdown stops working on you. Cycling shields in the middle of the scrum, he plays like a fighter wearing a marksman's tag.

strengths: Devastating point-blank burst when all four pellets connect
Ultimate's cleanse and 3-second immunity walk through enemy CC
Damage dealt converts into shield, so he gets tankier as he swings
Pellet hits stack armor shred, keeping damage high even into tanks
weaknesses: Damage falls off sharply at range as the outer pellets stop connecting
Skill 2 is his only dash; miss it and he can neither chase nor leave
Extremely vulnerable to CC the moment his Ultimate wears off
Only the two center pellets crit, making item efficiency awkward

It brings 35 physical attack, 210 physical defense and 900 max HP, and every hit taken raises damage dealt by 1%, up to 10%. Cutting Red Moon and Hunt to make room for five slots of Mutation and three of Reaver lifts the totals to +319 physical attack, +82 physical penetration and +24.8% physical lifesteal. The arcana swap costs 11 points of attack speed, leaving +70%, and the sixth-slot difference leaves max HP 300 lower at +2,500.

name: Liu Shan
title: Liu Shan Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A siege-specialist support tank who jams towers, breaks them, and heals off the scrap. He attacks the enemy's win condition at the structural level, with a stun and charge for ordinary fights.
playstyle: A siege-specialist support tank who jams towers, breaks them, and heals off the scrap. He attacks the enemy's win condition at the structural level, with a stun and charge for ordinary fights.
bestFor: players who put tower destruction at the center of the win plan — jam one, break it, heal off every swing, and answer only the question of which tower falls and when.

tips.earlyGame: Liu Shan roams with his team while constantly shopping for the next structure to touch — a habit no other support needs. His Passive lets skills damage towers, CC skills jam them for 1.2 seconds, and every skill hit on a structure refunds 280 HP. Early on, though, the star is Skill 2: time the tip of the fan-shaped stun with your jungler's gank and the kill is all but booked. His range is short, so always approach behind Skill 1's shield and speed boost. At the 4:00 Tyrant, stand at the front and use the stun to shut down anyone contesting.
tips.midGame: Liu Shan's mid game peaks in the seconds right after a won fight. The moment the enemy backs off, march to the nearest tower, jam it with Skill 2, and start swinging: the tower's counterattack stops for 1.2 seconds, your skills damage it directly, and the HP refunds let you finish sieges other teams would abandon. With two defensive items around eight minutes, you're also a real engage threat — Skill 1 in, empowered basic knock-up, Skill 2 stun. Take mid's first tower early and your roaming radius explodes.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Liu Shan closes matches with a two-part threat: the CC chain and the siege. In fights, rotating Skill 1's empowered knock-up, Skill 2's stun, and the Ultimate's spinning slow locks enemies down for over two seconds singlehandedly. But what makes him genuinely scary past ten minutes is what happens after the fight. Win at Overlord and he jams towers and the crystal into silence while dismantling them — ending games at the moment other teams would recall to heal. Decide what you're breaking after you win before you ever commit to the engage. That's the Liu Shan way.
tips.teamfight: Your role is to hold enemies in place where your team's damage can reach them. Enter behind Skill 1's shield and speed, open with the empowered basic knock-up, land the Skill 2 fan stun on the enemy carry, then keep the Ultimate spinning for the area slow. Since other skills stay castable during the spin, the CC never has to stop. The thing to fear is distance: every tool in the kit is point-blank, so chasing deep and dying alone is the classic Liu Shan mistake. Meeting the enemies who dive your backline is the far more reliable version of the same fight.

strengths: One-of-a-kind siege power — he jams towers while tearing them down directly
Knock-up and stun in one kit make his CC chain fully self-sufficient
Skill 1's shield and speed make the first step of every engage a safe one
HP refunds on every structure hit keep him healthy through long sieges
weaknesses: Every skill is point-blank — good kiting means he never touches anyone
Skill 1's speed boost is his only gap-closer, so mobile enemies slip away
His personal damage is modest; without allied follow-up, the CC achieves nothing

name: Lorion
title: Lorion Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A mage defined by where his projectile is: outside him it's a placed turret, inside him it fuels his own casts. One orb, two identities — and his wide launch ultimate opens teamfights.
playstyle: A mage defined by where his projectile is: outside him it's a placed turret, inside him it fuels his own casts. One orb, two identities — and his wide launch ultimate opens teamfights.
bestFor: players who enjoy a management puzzle inside a clean-looking kit — one orb, a turret outside him or fuel inside him, and where it sits decides the fight.

tips.earlyGame: In mid lane, clear waves with the orb held inside your body. Activated there, it strikes everything around you at double frequency and even heals you, which makes Lorion shockingly durable in lane scraps. When you want to harass, send the orb out with Skill 1 — and the moment it connects, don't leave it lying there. Recall it with Skill 2 and collect the 20% move speed. Repeat that send-and-recall rhythm patiently until Level 4 and you'll walk into the 4-minute Tyrant contest with a visible HP lead over your lane opponent.
tips.midGame: From about eight minutes, once cooldown boots and a magic-pierce staff are complete, orb placement starts deciding fights. In the standoffs before Tyrant, your job is shipping the orb into enemy escape routes and narrow corridors with Skill 1, booking the Ultimate's detonation in advance. After a 2-second charge it erupts for heavy damage and a 1.25-second knock-up, so enemies simply cannot stand in that zone. Time the blast with your team's engage — detonating early is just an expensive scare. And since the activated orb auto-targets the lowest-HP enemy in range, parking it near someone chipped forces a recall all by itself.
tips.lateGame: Your late-game role is zone control from the backline. With your magic attack fully built, a rank-3 Skill 4 detonation lands 1,200 base damage — enough to take a huge bite out of anything squishy. The discipline that matters here: never spend Skill 3 offensively. Flying to your orb carries 25% damage reduction and crowd control immunity, and the reduction lingers for 2 seconds after you land. In practice that flight is your last lifeline. When the enemy assassin is missing from vision, pre-place the orb toward your escape side before stepping up; if they jump you, you fly straight out of their reach. Let the orb project the threat while your body stays safe. That's the iron rule of late-game Lorion.
tips.teamfight: Teamfight prep starts 30 seconds before the fight. At Overlord or Shadow Tyrant, set the orb at the pit entrance, then rake Skill 1's start-to-end line damage and slow through their formation. The moment they clump, detonate for the knock-up and let your team's follow-up turn it into a numbers win. If the brawl swallows you, recalling the orb into your body with Skill 2 is a real option — the double-frequency damage around you plus the self-healing makes you far harder to kill than you look. Lorion's teamfight is one continuous choice: which do you show the enemy, the orb or yourself?

strengths: The orb swaps whole playstyles inside versus outside his body, covering any range
Planted detonation knock-ups own every chokepoint on the map
Damage-reduced flight with crowd control immunity is elite escape for a mage
The outside orb hunts the lowest-HP enemy, projecting free closing pressure
weaknesses: Everything hinges on orb placement — one bad spot stalls the entire kit
The 2-second detonation delay gives mobile enemies time to dodge
Spending the flight offensively leaves him with no way out afterward
Straying too far force-recalls the orb and erases its zone threat

name: Lu Bu
title: Lu Bu Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A fighter whose enchanted halberd deals true damage that no armor answers. His ultimate descends with a knock-up and claims the ground — where he lands becomes the center of the fight.
playstyle: A fighter whose enchanted halberd deals true damage that no armor answers. His ultimate descends with a knock-up and claims the ground — where he lands becomes the center of the fight.
bestFor: players who light up when the enemy stacks armor — the enchanted halberd deals true damage armor cannot answer, and with the ultimate as your only way in, picking where you land is the game.

tips.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Lu Bu lives and dies by landing Skill 1 on enemy heroes. A hit enchants his halberd for 8 seconds, adding true damage to basic attacks and skills plus healing per swing — but whiffing it on heroes removes the enchant entirely, so never burn it on a minion wave out of habit. Open trades with Skill 2: the more enemies it clips, the more shield stacks you bank (up to three), each ticking back into HP. Keep trades even until level 4, then hit the gas once your Ultimate unlocks.
tips.midGame: From level 4, Lu Bu headlines the 4-minute Tyrant fight. The Ultimate is a descending 1-second knock-up with crowd control immunity until landing — a reliable counter-engage you can throw after seeing the enemy's first move. Inside the kill zone you gain 150 physical and 150 magical defense, so the iron rule is: fight inside the circle. Enchanted true damage ignores armor, so your damage doesn't fall off as the lane opponent stacks defense — build tanky yourself and let the true damage carry the numbers.
tips.lateGame: Late game you play two roles: frontline and backline diver. Before fights, load three Skill 2 shields off minions or their frontline, then drop the Ultimate at the enemy marksman's feet. The zone's defensive bonus plus true damage means tanks and squishies both count as valid targets. Watch out for the mobility void after the Ultimate is spent — land at the edge of a fight and you're stuck walking back into relevance. Drop only when they clump and stop moving: the late-game mantra.
tips.teamfight: The ideal script: bank shields with Skill 2, wait for their formation to lock in place, Ultimate into the center, then unload Skill 1 and basic attacks with true damage during the 1-second knock-up. Keep the 8-second enchant timer in mind — as long as you're hitting any enemy hero, the healing never stops. Getting shredded in the scrum? Re-cast Skill 2 into three enemies and a 1000-plus shield rebuilds you. The zone's rim slows anyone leaving, so land the Ultimate a half-step toward their escape route.

strengths: Enchanted true damage cuts through stacked armor — even tanks aren't safe
Ultimate descends with crowd control immunity and a knock-up, so his engage rarely gets interrupted
Skill 2 shields plus healing basic attacks sustain him through long brawls
weaknesses: Whiffing Skill 1 on heroes drops the enchant — damage and healing die together
The Ultimate is his only movement; once it's spent, he walks everywhere
No lockdown beyond the Ultimate and slows, so kiting marksmen frustrate him

name: Luara
title: Luara Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A marksman who carries up to two serpent blades: every basic attack sends them slicing at the target, and three blade hits count as one basic attack. The blades also grant vision of whatever they cut, so her damage and her scouting run on the same track.
playstyle: A marksman who carries up to two serpent blades: every basic attack sends them slicing at the target, and three blade hits count as one basic attack. The blades also grant vision of whatever they cut, so her damage and her scouting run on the same track.
bestFor: players who like running two damage streams at once — her own shots and the blades already in the air — and who would rather win on placement than on reaction speed.

tips.earlyGame: Take the farm lane and let the serpent blades do the early work until your first attack speed item is finished. Pick up a blade with Skill 1, land a basic attack, and the blade cuts the target continuously while granting vision of it — an enemy who ducks into a bush stays visible and keeps bleeding. Feel a gank coming? Skill 1 again: 60 bonus Movement Speed (up to 120 at max rank) and one free wall vault while it lasts, which most junglers cannot answer. The boost diminishes over 1.5 seconds, so pick your exit before you press it. She has no burst this early, so prioritize last-hitting over hero kills.
tips.midGame: Around 10 minutes, with two attack speed core items online, her sustained damage starts to bite. Every skill cast raises her Attack Speed for 3 seconds, stacking up to three times, so keep Skill 1 and Skill 2 rolling instead of hoarding them. Three serpent blade hits count as one basic attack, which means your attack speed directly sets how fast the blades cut. In skirmishes, drop Skill 2's fire serpent behind the enemy: it charges back toward you, carving through everyone in its path, slowing them by 25% at rank 1 (up to 50%) and pulling them back slightly — that pull is not a crowd control effect. Hold a blade when it lands and the blade immediately attacks every enemy the serpent hit. Jumped by a basic-attack jungler? Skill 3. Their attacks deal nothing for 1.5 seconds, and that window is enough to turn the fight around.
tips.lateGame: With full build in sight, build your marksman duels around Skill 3. A blinded enemy cannot deal damage with basic attacks, and their skill projectiles deviate from their path at random, so for those 1.5 seconds you are effectively fighting a player up. The same cast hands her a serpent blade and enhances her. While enhanced, every point of damage she deals with basic attacks and skills charges Energy — damage dealt, not damage taken — and each time the bar fills, fire rains down and launches nearby enemies for 1/3s. That is genuine self-peel against an assassin glued to your back. The catch: Energy only builds while you are attacking, so backing out of range turns the buff into a dead card. Knowing exactly when to step out is where Luara players separate.
tips.teamfight: Your job is steady area damage: keep two serpent blades cycling from behind your frontline. Land Skill 3 on the enemy marksman as the fight opens and their basic attacks deal nothing for 1.5 seconds while you push in with the buff running. If someone dives you, do not just retreat — keep attacking, fill the Energy bar, and the fire rain's 1/3s launch pries them off. Once there is space, take Skill 1's speed and wall vault to reset. One escape trick: when running, drop the fire serpent behind your pursuer. It charges back to you straight through them, leaving a slow behind as it goes.

strengths: Blades that keep cutting the target and grant vision of it, beating bushes and escape attempts
The 1.5s blind shuts off the damage of any basic-attack hero
Skill 1's 10s cooldown keeps the speed boost and wall vault coming, making her hard to catch
The 1/3s knock-up from the fire rain during her enhanced state doubles as anti-assassin self-peel
weaknesses: Zero burst; targets often walk away before she can finish the job
Cashing in the self-buff means staying forward and eating damage
Skill-heavy comps blank the blind and cut deep into her identity
Heavily attack-speed dependent — underwhelming until the core is built

builds.notes: Boots of Dexterity open with +20% attack speed, and Sparkforged Dagger plus Doomsday keep raising the rate of fire. From the fourth slot on, Master Sword, Daybreaker's Virtue and Overlord's Might push the totals to +125% attack speed, 51% crit rate and +369 physical attack. Daybreaker's Virtue doubles its penetration bonus for a ranged hero, so Luara reads 30% physical penetration, and Overlord's Might adds 30% damage against any enemy under 50% HP. No defensive item goes in at all: gear and arcana add zero physical defense, and max HP tops out at +1100.

name: Luban No.7
title: Luban No.7 Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A stubby-legged siege cannon whose every fifth shot sprays percent-max-Health damage. Nearly the least mobile hero in the game — pure firepower cultured on the premise of being protected.
playstyle: A stubby-legged siege cannon whose every fifth shot sprays percent-max-Health damage. Nearly the least mobile hero in the game — pure firepower cultured on the premise of being protected.
bestFor: players content to be escorted and set on being worth the escort — with no dash and no speed, position is the entire defense, and the strafe every fifth attack is what you give back.

tips.earlyGame: Let's be honest: Luban No.7's early game is about survival. He has no mobility skill and slow legs, so don't fight for lane priority — hug your tower and collect last hits. The good news is that the Passive strafe and the Skill 1 bomb clear waves quickly, so your farm rarely falls behind even from a defensive posture. Skill 1 also grants vision of anything it hits, which makes it a cheap brush-check when something feels off. The most dangerous moments are when the enemy support disappears from the minimap. Don't chase anything, and leave the 4:00 Tyrant to your teammates.
tips.midGame: Around eight minutes, with two or three items done, the patience starts paying out. Your strafe deals physical damage scaling with the target's maximum HP, so unlike other marksmen, you only hit harder as their tanks get bigger. In fights, the damage rotation is about strafe frequency: Skill 1, strafe, Skill 2, strafe — every skill cast loads another burst. Your legs haven't gotten any faster, though, so step forward only after your frontline has the enemy's full attention. The Ultimate airship pays for itself even as a pure scouting tool thrown before a fight.
tips.lateGame: Approaching full build, Luban No.7 is the strongest stationary gun in the game — one strafe visibly moves an enemy HP bar, tanks included. At Shadow Tyrant and Overlord fights past ten minutes, cycling strafes from the absolute backline is your entire job, and the enemy melts front to back. Luban wins by not dying, full stop — always choose the safe position over the kill. Skill 2's knockback is your only self-peel; save it for the assassin, every time. Throw the Ultimate airship at the enemy's staging area before the fight for vision and free pressure.
tips.teamfight: Everything depends on holding your spot two or three steps behind the frontline. On engage, drop the Skill 1 slow on the clump and run the loop — strafe, skill, strafe — working through whoever stands in front. The strafe fires in a straight line, so when enemies spread out, just aim at the widest target available, usually their tank: the max-HP scaling means that damage is never wasted. The single non-negotiable is the flank. The instant an enemy assassin appears behind you, Skill 2 them away and run toward your team — no hesitation, no exceptions.

strengths: Strafe damage scales with the target's maximum HP — even tanks melt late game
Skill 1 and the airship supply their own vision, blunting brush ambushes
Skill 2's knockback is a reliable last line of defense against divers
Rapid wave clear makes him hard to siege out even when pushed in
weaknesses: No mobility skill and slow movement — among the easiest marksmen to catch
Weak early skirmishing forces a patient, defensive start until items arrive
The strafe fires in a straight line, losing value when enemies spread out

builds.notes: Shadow Ripper takes the second slot for 20% critical rate, bringing the build to +56%. Starbreaker lands at 6,930G, so its 30% physical penetration comes online about 500G earlier than Build 1's fourth item. Overlord's Might also moves up a slot, putting the 30% bonus damage against enemies under half HP in play at 9,470G. Bloodweeper closes the build out at +1,200 max HP and +33% physical lifesteal, enough to hold position instead of backing off.

name: Luna
title: Luna Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The moonlight duelist with a theoretically infinite combo: her ultimate resets whenever it hits a marked enemy. Maintain the mark-dash-mark loop and she never stops; drop it once and she's mortal again.
playstyle: The moonlight duelist with a theoretically infinite combo: her ultimate resets whenever it hits a marked enemy. Maintain the mark-dash-mark loop and she never stops; drop it once and she's mortal again.
bestFor: combo drillers. Mark, dash, reset, repeat — break the chain once and you are just squishy melee again, so hundreds of practice reps are the entry fee.

tips.earlyGame: Luna is a jungler first. Open on both buffs and the camps between them and race to level 4, drilling the Skill 1 → Ultimate → third basic attack order into muscle memory as you clear. Everything Luna does rests on one rule: hitting a marked enemy with the Ultimate resets its cooldown. On your first ganks after level 4, resist the urge to show off a long chain — landing Skill 2's pull and stun to hold the target for your laner succeeds far more often than a greedy solo play.
tips.midGame: From around 8 minutes, with one or two magic attack items done, Luna headlines every skirmish. The base pattern at Tyrant and mid: tag from range with Skill 1, enter with the Ultimate, refresh the mark with your third basic and Skill 2, and keep weaving in and out. Marks stick to minions too, so learn to chain Ultimates through waves and camps as transportation — it puts your chases and escapes in a different dimension. As long as you don't die, nobody out-farms you.
tips.lateGame: Teamfights after 15 minutes are won before you enter. A Luna walking in the front door is just a squishy melee, so always start from a flank or the rear with a mark already on a perimeter enemy. Touch once and leave before their stuns and silences turn your way, then start the real dance once their CC is down. Skill 2's shield and 0.5-second stun erase hundreds of damage in a scrum — when you feel surrounded, restart from the pull rather than the attack and your survival rate climbs.
tips.teamfight: A dropped chain is death, full stop. Throughout the fight, keep the next marked Ultimate target decided two steps ahead, and the instant one dies, switch to another enemy or a minion. While a mark lives, you enter and exit the fight at will — from the enemy's seat, an uncatchable nightmare. But one missed reset deletes your escape plan, so build the habit of confirming your exit mark one step before every overextension. Luna returns exactly what you put into her, and she demands commitment.

strengths: Endless Ultimate resets grant mobility no one else in the game matches
Skill 2's pull, stun, and shield keep her alive in the center of brawls
Free entry and exit lets her bait enemy CC before the real engage
At full mastery, she can win a teamfight single-handedly
weaknesses: The instant the reset chain breaks, her escape disappears with it
A stun or silence mid-loop reduces her to a squishy melee
One of the hardest heroes in the game — low mastery means zero output
Tunnel vision mid-combo makes her slow to react to counter-ganks

counteredBy.name: Heino
counteredBy.reason: Heino heals more the more enemy heroes stand near him, so Luna's own melee pressure feeds his sustain.

builds.notes: Runeblade goes down first: every monster kill adds 6 magic attack, reaching +150 at 25 stacks. The 700G Boots of Resistance slot in second for +50 movement speed and 25% tenacity early. Augur's Word, Insatiable Tome and Breakthrough Robe push max HP to +2550, and the Robe adds 3% of that bonus HP on top of its base 30-60 magic pierce. Ten Mind's Eye arcana contribute a separate 64, and Savant's Wrath closes the gear at +770 magic attack before raising it another 30%.

name: Mai Shiranui
title: Mai Shiranui Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A close-range burst mage who weaves empowered attacks and dashes while managing an energy bar. The hands are busy, but a clean sequence simply deletes the target.
playstyle: A close-range burst mage who weaves empowered attacks and dashes while managing an energy bar. The hands are busy, but a clean sequence simply deletes the target.
bestFor: busy hands. Dashes and rolls have to keep flowing, because the moment the energy bar empties there is nothing left to press.

tips.earlyGame: Early mid lane is not the time to force anything. Mai's energy only refunds meaningfully on skill hits, so whiffing repeatedly leaves you unable to act at all. Clear waves with Skill 2's fan — it pierces to the unit behind the first target it hits, so lining it through a minion onto the enemy laner clears and harasses in one throw. Level 4 unlocks the Ultimate, and with rolls woven in, she finally becomes the ambush hero she's meant to be.
tips.midGame: From level 4 on, shove mid quickly and roam the side lanes. Every engage starts with Skill 2 — the 50-point magic defense shred lasts 3 seconds, and the same combo does visibly different damage depending on whether it led. Sliding the stick during an empowered basic or skill triggers a roll, and the small habits pay huge dividends: roll to the wall side to cut off the escape, or roll out of the flight path of their answer skill. One extra input, dramatically better survival.
tips.lateGame: Late game is entirely about timing your entry, not the size of the hit. One CC kills you, so hover the perimeter of frontal fights flashing roll threats, and commit Skill 2 into Skill 1 the instant the enemy's point-and-click CC or lockdown gets spent elsewhere. The Ultimate's knockback and 20% physical attack shred double as insurance — landing it on the enemy marksman buys defense and cuts their damage at once. Having the discipline to leave based on your energy bar is what actually decides your win rate.
tips.teamfight: The ideal teamfight entry is three seconds late, after the scrum has started. Shred a target's magic defense with Skill 2, stack Skill 1's knock-up on top, push with the empowered basic, and finish with the Ultimate. When the full string lands, squishy targets simply disappear — but decide your roll-out path BEFORE you dive. The same input handles both aggressive and escaping rolls on this hero, so the escape route you hold in your head is your actual lifeline.

strengths: Skill 2's 50-point magic defense shred multiplies her entire combo
Two dashes plus rolls deliver elite in-and-out mobility
Knock-up, knockback, and an attack shred give her real self-defense
Energy loops indefinitely as long as skills keep connecting
weaknesses: Whiffed skills drain energy and create dead time where she can't act
Zero defensive tools — a single CC ends her
Misrolled inputs send her the wrong way, straight into danger
High skill floor: her damage tracks directly with practice

name: Marco Polo
title: Marco Polo Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The definitive run-and-gun marksman — his revolver fires on the move, his stacks shred defenses into true damage, and two teleports serve both chase and escape.
playstyle: The definitive run-and-gun marksman — his revolver fires on the move, his stacks shred defenses into true damage, and two teleports serve both chase and escape.
bestFor: players who treat standing still as death — firing on the move, breaking armor into true damage at ten stacks, with two blinks keeping the kiting itself converted into damage.

tips.earlyGame: Until your first attack speed item is finished, farming is the entire job. Skill 1 is your best CS tool — five bullets that clear minions and, when they carry through to your lane opponent, double as free harass. Every three bullets count as one basic attack, so your Passive's armor-break stacks build on their own while you farm. Even when the enemy engages, Skill 2's instant blink buys space immediately, letting you take CS a step further forward than most marksmen dare. Just keep one rule in the back of your mind: burn Skill 2 aggressively and you have no exit for the next several seconds.
tips.midGame: Around 8 to 10 minutes, with your second attack speed item done, the Passive's armor break starts triggering in every single fight. Ten stacks shatter the target's defense, and every follow-up hit adds bonus true damage — the reason you can genuinely shoot it out with fighters and tanks who walk at you. Show up to Tyrant and mid-lane skirmishes, thread Skill 1 into the scrum to farm stacks, and keep an escape budgeted: Skill 2 first, the Ultimate's blink as the emergency reserve. Two dashes' worth of insurance converts directly into extra seconds of firing time — and firing time is Marco Polo's entire game.
tips.lateGame: The closer you get to full build, the more the Ultimate's three-second barrage becomes a fight-deciding weapon. The spray hits every enemy around you, fires faster with attack speed, and late game it cycles armor-break stacks almost instantly. Catch the enemy team clumped on Overlord from a side angle and their frontline's defense simply peels away. The flip side: you crawl while channeling, and one hard stun cancels the whole thing. Who on their team has hard CC, and is it up? Counting that before you channel is the single habit that improves your Marco Polo the most.
tips.teamfight: Your spot is the very back, at maximum Skill 1 range. Don't step up at the opening bell — pour bullets into the enemy frontline to build stacks while their crowd control gets spent. When an assassin dives, answer instantly with Skill 2 and keep shooting from the far side of your blink. Your window opens after their lockdown is committed: blink into a flank with the Ultimate and hose the whole fight down while drifting. Enemies with armor break active simply melt in order, so you don't need fancy target selection — just never stop moving, and never stop firing.

strengths: Armor break plus true damage keeps his output relevant against tanky frontlines
Two blinks across Skill 2 and the Ultimate for total positional freedom
Bullets count as basic attacks, so Passive stacks build extremely fast
weaknesses: Crawls during the Ultimate's channel and loses it all to one hard CC
Underwhelming damage until his attack speed items come online
No burst — deny him sustained firing time and he goes quiet

name: Mayene
title: Mayene Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An eccentric brawler juggling two stamina gauges — slack off and she literally sits down to snack. Weave her cartwheel dodge and pull correctly and her flurries take over the fight.
playstyle: An eccentric brawler juggling two stamina gauges — slack off and she literally sits down to snack. Weave her cartwheel dodge and pull correctly and her flurries take over the fight.
bestFor: players who read resource management as a puzzle rather than a chore, watching two stamina bars and choosing a derivation on the spot — the Very Hard tag is honest.

tips.earlyGame: In a clash-lane 1v1, Mayene is about as scary as it gets. From level 2, with Skill 1 and Skill 2 online, the derivation combos put your opponent in a guessing game they cannot win. Default to Skill 1 → Skill 2 for the punch flurry and its healing to win repeated trades; when they back off, switch to Skill 2 → Skill 1, teleporting behind them for bonus damage equal to 15% of their missing HP. Fist and Leg charges refill one every 8.5 seconds, so the one house rule is: after dumping both, take half a step back and don't eat the counter-swing. In quiet moments, let the Passive kick in — she sits down, snacks, and heals.
tips.midGame: Once the lane is broken, spend minutes 8 to 13 split-pushing a side lane as bait. Whoever comes to collect you eats Skill 2 → Skill 2: the flying kick's crowd control immunity, damage reduction, and healing let you tank the attempt outright, and against two or fewer pursuers it often flips into a kill. One player bending multiple enemies around her while the team takes the Tyrant or towers — that is the Mayene win condition. She is helpless if jumped at zero charges, so make checking for two full gauges before every fight a reflex.
tips.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, cast the Ultimate first, not last. Its serious mode instantly refunds one Fist and one Leg charge and raises the cap to three, letting you chain derivations without pausing for breath. Hunt the backline: flank, lift them with Skill 1 → Skill 1, then finish with Skill 2 → Skill 1's missing-HP bonus. Takedowns with that finisher refund 50% energy (doubled for hero kills), so every kill reloads the next combo. When the 10-second window closes, your output falls off a cliff — overstaying is the one unforgivable sin.
tips.teamfight: Hold the flank and wait for the enemy's CC to be aimed at someone else. Enter with Skill 2 → Skill 2 — crowd control immunity carries you straight through their counters. On landing, refill with the Ultimate and pick the derivation the moment demands: Skill 1 → Skill 1 to lift, Skill 1 → Skill 2 to sustain, Skill 2 → Skill 1 to execute. And honestly, the moment you stop running fixed sequences — reading "they're retreating: 2 into 1" and "they're standing their ground: 1 into 2" on reaction — is the moment Mayene actually begins.

strengths: Four derivations cover engages, sustain, defense, and executions
Crowd control immunity and healing mid-combo make her 1v1 among the best in the game
The Ultimate's instant charge refund unlocks explosive teamfight chains
Takedown energy refunds let momentum turn her nearly unstoppable
weaknesses: Useless with empty gauges — charge accounting never stops
Split-second derivation choices back up her Very Hard difficulty rating
The Passive's lazy healing shuts off in combat, leaving mid-brawl sustain thin
The window right after serious mode ends is where she gets punished

name: Meng Ya
title: Meng Ya Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A gatling marksman whose attack speed converts into cooldown reduction — the faster he fires, the faster everything reloads. At full fury his rounds pierce, and his zone control jumps a tier.
playstyle: A gatling marksman whose attack speed converts into cooldown reduction — the faster he fires, the faster everything reloads. At full fury his rounds pierce, and his zone control jumps a tier.
bestFor: players who like builds that change the feel of a kit — attack speed pays for cooldowns as well as fire rate, and with no dash anywhere, positioning comes before the trigger.

tips.earlyGame: In the farm lane, Meng Ya's job starts with grinding Fury off every basic attack and skill from minute zero. Bounce Skill 2 off a wall and let the shrapnel chip your lane opponent — that's your safe poke, and each pellet packs 100% of your bonus physical attack, with several landing in tight spaces. You have zero mobility skills, so stay away from the riverside bushes whenever the enemy jungler is missing from the minimap. His whole design revolves around skills only being empowered at full Fury, so never wander into a fight with an empty gauge — always start the fight topped up.
tips.midGame: From around 7 minutes, once your first attack speed item is finished, Meng Ya's barrage becomes the real thing — his Passive converts every 5% attack speed into 1% cooldown reduction, so his skills cycle faster with every item. For Tyrant fights and mid-game skirmishes, layering the Ultimate from the backline is ideal: allies' attacks mark enemies and missiles rain down for up to 8 seconds, letting you join fights without stepping forward. Hold the back row, sweep Skill 1 across the fight, and let the full-Fury overflow healing keep you on the front.
tips.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, Meng Ya's spot is two steps behind your frontline. At full Fury, Skill 1's bullets pierce and still deal 50% to the enemies behind the first, so anyone stacked in a line melts together — narrow corridors are where he defends best. Strafing slows him by 50 and he has no dash. Never be caught alone while the enemy assassin's position is unknown. Strafing can also be paused to fire another skill: when someone dives you, break off, land Skill 2's slow, and re-open the gap. With a wall at your back, the splinters ricochet into whoever is in your face. Splinters that hit the same target within 1s only deal 25% damage, so this is no way to dump a whole spread into one hero. Each splinter stops at the first enemy it hits, and with 9 of them at full Fury, spreading them across several bodies is what keeps every hit at full damage.
tips.teamfight: Open every teamfight by firing the Ultimate. Hold the button to widen the search area, mark everyone your teammates touch, and let the missile rain begin. From there, spray Skill 1 from the very back and tag divers with Skill 2's slow to keep them off you. At full Fury, overflow keeps converting into healing, so you win plenty of extended shootouts even while taking damage. Your positioning rule of thumb: stand where no enemy can reach you with a single skill. Keep that true and Meng Ya is still standing when the teamfight ends.

strengths: Full Fury empowers every skill and overflow converts into constant healing
Attack speed feeds cooldown reduction and fire rate, so no stat goes to waste
The Ultimate supports fights from far outside enemy reach
Wall-bounced Skill 2 spikes to absurd damage in tight corridors
weaknesses: No mobility skill whatsoever — once reached, he cannot escape on his own
Skills underperform on an empty Fury gauge, so pre-fight ramp-up is mandatory
Spraying Skill 1 slows him, making enemy skillshots hard to dodge
The Ultimate depends on allies attacking and does little in a solo fight

name: Menki
title: Menki Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A fighter who stacks mass through skills, literally growing heavier and tougher. Manage the bubble's round trip and your mass economy, then plant your inflated self in the enemy team.
playstyle: A fighter who stacks mass through skills, literally growing heavier and tougher. Manage the bubble's round trip and your mass economy, then plant your inflated self in the enemy team.
bestFor: players who would rather prepare than react — every cast adds mass that raises attack and defense, and it drains every second the fight runs, so you arrive already big.

tips.earlyGame: Menki is a clash lane fighter who brawls while banking Mass. Every skill cast adds Mass, and each 10 points grants +6 physical attack and +8 to both defenses, so the golden rule is cycling skills to charge up before you commit. It drains 5 per second while in combat, so the longer a brawl drags, the more you fizzle — keep that in mind. Open trades behind Skill 1's shield: every basic attack shaves 0.5 seconds off its cooldown, so as long as you keep swinging, you can keep re-shielding. Lane opponents hate it.
tips.midGame: Skill 2 carries your mid-game damage. The bubble flies out and returns, then launches at a nearby enemy and returns again — after two retrievals it becomes the Dream Bubble, which at 5.5 seconds of flight time detonates for up to 550 plus 132% magic attack. In a 1v1, stack the bubble's slows while punching, then slam the grown bomb onto their escape path. Push the side lane, and when a river fight breaks out, join with your Ultimate's roam. The crowd control immunity at activation lets you start the rotation straight through enemy CC — quietly one of his best tools.
tips.lateGame: Your late game changes faces with your build: physical items make you a backline diver, defensive items make you a frontline wrecking ball. Either way, cycle skills on jungle camps and minions to top off your Mass before joining any fight. Entering at zero Mass versus full Mass is a difference of dozens of points of attack and both defenses — literally a different hero. At Overlord standoffs, your job is arriving from an unexpected angle with the Ultimate and splitting their formation with its ending knockup.
tips.teamfight: Enter deliberately. First, send Skill 2 bubbles through their line to spread slows while the bomb grows. Once your team commits, roam to their backline with the Ultimate and time the reactivation knockup right under their marksman's feet. The instant you land, press Skill 1 — shield plus 30 Mass in one cast — then cycle basic attacks to reset it and squat in their backline through a second and third shield. Overstaying until your Mass runs dry makes you crumble fast, so the moment it starts dropping, back out and recharge.

strengths: His stats at full Mass rank among the best of any fighter in the game
A fully grown Dream Bubble detonates for up to 550 plus 132% magic attack
Skill 1's shield recycles constantly thanks to basic-attack cooldown reduction
Crowd control immunity on the Ultimate makes rotations and backline dives reliable
weaknesses: Fighting at zero Mass leaves both his damage and durability below average
Mass drains every second in combat, so long fights taper off badly
The bomb needs travel time to grow, so he has no instant burst on demand
The Ultimate's crowd control immunity only covers the start; CC catches him mid-roam

name: Mi Yue
title: Mi Yue Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A dark mage attended by auto-attacking shadow claws, weakening enemies through her draining link. Her ultimate phases her out of existence entirely, buying a reset near the frontline.
playstyle: A dark mage attended by auto-attacking shadow claws, weakening enemies through her draining link. Her ultimate phases her out of existence entirely, buying a reset near the frontline.
bestFor: players who like layering a summon's pressure over their own — shadow claws pile up while the tether drains enemy attack into your Health, and the ultimate's two untouchable seconds are the only exit.

tips.earlyGame: Mi Yue hits her stride at level 1 with Skill 2. In the clash lane, tether the enemy laner: while linked you siphon their physical and magical attack while your chip damage and healing tick together — a one-sided trade. Holding the link for the full 4 seconds spawns an extra shadow servant, so pick fights early and build toward the six-servant cap. The chain snaps at range, though, so when they back off, don't chase — use Skill 1's recast movement to return to the wave safely.
tips.midGame: Mid-game Mi Yue rules the side of the map by forcing 1v1s. From around 8 minutes, push the clash lane wave and welcome whichever fighter comes to answer with a Skill 2-led war of attrition. Even when their jungler makes it 2v1, the Ultimate's 2-second shadow form negates everything — eat their burst, come back out, and the turnaround is more realistic than it looks. Train the reflex: enemy assassin commits, then you press Ultimate, and you stop dying. Skip coin-flip Tyrant fights and take the tower they left behind instead.
tips.lateGame: A straight 5v5 is still not your arena, so keep the side pressure up through the late game. With four items done, no single enemy stops you, and two enemies coming means numbers advantages everywhere else. When you do join Overlord or Shadow Tyrant fights, work the edge: tether their frontline with Skill 2 to drain attack damage, indirectly cutting what your team takes. Treat the Ultimate as a reactive dodge, not an escape — hold it until you see the enemy's big cooldown, then make it whiff.
tips.teamfight: Never enter from the front. Open from a flank by tethering their key fighter or marksman with Skill 2 — a drained enemy hits nowhere near their listed numbers, and 4 seconds of link restocks a servant. When heads turn your way, double-dash out with Skill 1; if they chase, answer with the Ultimate's immunity and let their skills hit nothing. With six servants up, Mi Yue heals back damage just by walking around, so dragging the fight out is itself the win condition.

strengths: Skill 2 drains enemy attack, and with shadow servant healing she's a top-tier duelist
Ultimate's 2 seconds of full immunity and cleanse make enemy ace cooldowns whiff

A skirmish specialist whose influence thins in full frontal teamfights

name: Milady
title: Milady Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A commander mage who spawns robots on takedowns and merges them into stronger units. Her own damage is modest — the army's upkeep and placement is the real weapon.
playstyle: A commander mage who spawns robots on takedowns and merges them into stronger units. Her own damage is modest — the army's upkeep and placement is the real weapon.
bestFor: players who would rather command than carry — the robots multiply with every takedown and Skill 3 fires straight at towers, though nothing in the kit gets you out of trouble.

tips.earlyGame: Milady's job from the first wave is simple: drop robots with Skill 2 and shove everything into the enemy tower. Skill 2 banks a charge roughly every 15 seconds up to three stocks, so resist the urge to dump all of them — with no mobility skill in her kit, a robot dropped at your own feet is the only gank insurance you have. When the enemy jungler vanishes from the minimap, hug your tower. Skip the 4-minute Tyrant fight entirely and keep shoving mid instead; the pressure you generate is what lets your teammates rotate freely.
tips.midGame: Around the 10-minute mark, the moment the enemy mid laner drifts to a side lane is your cue to take the tower. Your Ultimate fires directly at towers and crystals, ticking damage while the mark lasts and detonating for an extra 25% of the damage dealt when it expires — stack that with your robots and towers evaporate. Never cross an unwarded river alone; a caught Milady is a dead Milady. After the tower falls, don't chase. Wait for the next wave and your Skill 2 stocks to recover before stepping up again, and the throws stop happening.
tips.lateGame: You lose the burst race against traditional mages late, so win with siege instead. Nobody else can chip high-ground towers while robots soak the tower shots — you don't even need a minion wave to start the job. If the enemy turtles, don't force a dive; grind them down with Skill 1 fighter jets and endless robot waves and win the patience war. Before Overlord or Shadow Tyrant spawns, bank all three Skill 2 stocks about 30 seconds early and the standoff practically plays itself.
tips.teamfight: Your spot in teamfights is the very back. Keep Skill 2 rolling to feed robots forward, and recast Skill 1 to split the fighter jet in two — enemies clipped by both take a 25% slow that lets your team close the gap. When an assassin jumps you, land your Ultimate on them for the 0.75-second stun, sic your frenzied robots on the target, and walk away. Milady doesn't win face-to-face damage races, so hold your position until you've seen at least one enemy dash hit the ground.

strengths: Robots soak tower shots, letting her break towers without minions
Ultimate fires directly at towers for the fastest siege of any mage
Every kill spawns another robot, so long brawls tilt numbers her way
Skill 2 stocks keep the shove pressure running nonstop
weaknesses: No mobility skill; once gap-closed she cannot shake pursuers alone
AoE mages that clear her robots in one cast gut her damage
Enemies who kite outside robot range blunt her kill threat
Weak personal burst; loses head-to-head damage races

Frozen Breath, Twilight Stream and Savant's Wrath stack magic attack after that, with equipment and arcana closing at +917.4 magic attack and 44.9% cooldown reduction. Seven Tribute slots pay for cooldown, which leaves magic defense penetration at +43.2 - about half of build 2. Mask of Agony only arrives sixth, so the percent-HP damage against tanky targets comes online late.

builds.title: Mask of Agony second for percent damage
builds.condition: When the enemy draft has two or more tanks or high-HP heroes.
builds.notes: Mask of Agony comes second here: 2,780 gold buys +900 max HP and 3% current-HP damage, four times over three seconds. Ten Mind's Eye slots put magic defense penetration at +88 against build 1's +43.2. Stacked magic defense gives way, and the totals edge ahead as well, at 47.5% cooldown reduction and +922 magic attack. Venomous Staff closes the build, cutting enemy HP regeneration and lifesteal by 35% for 2.5 seconds.

name: Ming
title: Ming Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A support who links to one ally and pours attack power into them — a carry-amplification device. He plays the supporting role completely, manufacturing his partner's prime.
playstyle: A support who links to one ally and pours attack power into them — a carry-amplification device. He plays the supporting role completely, manufacturing his partner's prime.
bestFor: support players happy to play second fiddle — one link feeds an ally attack power, the other strips enemy defenses, and the ultimate spends your own health to keep the carry up.

tips.earlyGame: Open the game by linking Skill 1 to your jungler at their first buff — the attack and attack speed boost speeds up the clear — then follow your marksman to lane. Ming's link directly pumps an ally's main attack stat, so any 2v2 next to your linked partner is numerically in your favor. Play forward and push that edge. Skill 2 links to an enemy and cuts both their defenses by 10%, or an extra 25% on a direct hit. Stick it on the lane opponent right before a trade and the exact same combo from your carry chunks visibly harder.
tips.midGame: From here on, the default is gluing yourself to your most fed teammate. Keep the link alive and weave in the Passive's empowered basic attack every 5 seconds — on hit it drains HP and heals both you and your linked ally, and that quiet little hit decides wars of attrition. Skill 2 doubles as a vision tool: if the link is still attached when an enemy ducks into a bush, their position stays lit up. Tag the enemy jungler with it before a Tyrant fight and you're moonlighting as the team's gank alarm.
tips.lateGame: Late game, become the carry's shadow. Your Ultimate, after a 0.75-second cast, changes with your links: linked to one ally, you burn 600 plus 125% magic attack of your own HP to instantly heal them the same amount; linked to both an enemy and an ally, it drains the enemy to heal your ally with zero self-damage. Time it against the enemy's burst on your carry and it's effectively a second life. The consumed HP does trickle back over 5 seconds, but be very careful about self-damage casts while you're near death yourself.
tips.teamfight: Lock your position half a step behind your linked ally and never open enough distance to break the link. On engage, throw Skill 2 at their ace or the assassin diving in — up to 35% defense shred means your team's focus fire suddenly goes through. The soul chain also damages enemies it touches, so deliberately placing your body so the chain drags across enemies is a real micro-play worth practicing. Hold your Ultimate through the opening exchange and heal reactively after their burst lands. Casting it early is only justified when you're certain you've read the play.

strengths: Skill 1's link permanently boosts one ally's offensive output
Skill 2's defense shred and vision tagging set up focus-fire kills
The Ultimate's instant burst heal acts as a second life for the carry
The Passive's drain attack heals both Ming and his linked partner at once
weaknesses: Nearly zero solo combat power or self-peel; dies instantly when isolated
Link range is limited, so highly mobile allies can leave him behind
No hard CC of his own to stop an enemy engage
The Ultimate can self-damage; a mistimed cast gets both of you killed

The only item that differs is Succubus Cloak, slotted fourth at 6,950G. Magic defense totals +400 and max HP climbs to +4387, while Ming himself picks up a 400-800 (+7% of bonus HP) magic damage shield every 15 seconds. Fate arcana x10 feeds HP and physical defense, so magic attack stops at +700.

The one differing item is Venomous Staff, bought last, cutting enemy healing and lifesteal by 35% for 2.5 seconds on hit. Saint arcana x10 brings the totals to +983 magic attack, +22.5% cooldown reduction and +20% movement speed. Max HP is +2950 with only +100 magic defense, so Ming trades durability for damage.

name: Mozi
title: Mozi Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A mobile fortress between mage and fighter, controlling space with cannon fire and a stunning barrier. His skills stack shields, so he pushes forward without a backliner's fragility.
playstyle: A mobile fortress between mage and fighter, controlling space with cannon fire and a stunning barrier. His skills stack shields, so he pushes forward without a backliner's fragility.
bestFor: players who want backline damage and frontline durability in one body — shields stack with every cast, so decide which corridor you want closed before you commit to it.

tips.earlyGame: Mozi's lane is entirely about how you aim Skill 2. The shell detonates on the first enemy it touches, so fire it through gaps in the wave — or the moment your opponent steps forward for a last hit. Land the one-second stun and the follow-up is free: Skill 1 dash into the empowered basic attack, guaranteed. Wave clear is no problem — Skill 1 plus the fourth-hit empowered basic from your Passive handles it, and since every skill cast stacks a shield, you can shrug off some return fire. Tag your opponent with one or two stuns before level 4 and they'll flinch every time they step up. That fear is worth more than the damage.
tips.midGame: This is when Skill 2 turns into gold. A mage who stuns from long range is rare, and the moment your jungler shows up, landing one shell converts directly into a kill. With one AP item and one durability item done around 6-8 minutes, Mozi stops playing like a mage and starts playing like a CC frontliner — stand slightly ahead of your team and let the threat of the stun freeze the enemy's advance. Don't rush your Ultimate barrier out; placed across a narrow corridor or a brush exit, it's far harder to play around.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Mozi is the one who can end a match with a single stun. In the standoffs before Overlord past ten minutes, aim Skill 2 at where the enemy carry will retreat to, not where they stand. One hit and your whole team collapses on the target — that's the objective won on numbers alone. Keep your Passive shield at three stacks and you can eat an assassin's opener, which is exactly why you're allowed to stand a step ahead of any other mage. One warning: your Ultimate roots you while it's deployed, so never lead with it while the enemy still has long-range CC in hand.
tips.teamfight: Your impact swings heavily on whether the opening Skill 2 catch lands. If it misses, don't panic-force anything — chip the frontline with Skill 1 and empowered basics while the cooldown comes back around. Once the fight turns messy, deploy your Ultimate barrier across the path to your carry: enemies who touch it get stunned repeatedly, and in tight quarters it's a genuine wall. And when everything lines up on one target — stun, dash, empowered basic, barrier — Mozi outputs enough damage to kill anything that isn't a tank.

strengths: A one-second stun from long range, backed by the Passive knockback and Skill 3's stunning barrier
Passive shields give him frontline staying power no ordinary mage has
The Skill 2 field and Skill 3 barrier lock down corridors and choke points
Flexible enough to play both mid and the clash lane
weaknesses: Skill 2 flies in a predictable straight line and gets sidestepped by anyone paying attention
The Ultimate roots him during deployment, inviting ranged punishment
His only mobility is the short Skill 1 dash — his escapes are poor

name: Mulan
title: Mulan Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A two-form fighter: agile dual blades that stack a silencing seal, and a heavy greatsword whose charged swings end the fight. Each form demands its own way of fighting.
playstyle: A two-form fighter: agile dual blades that stack a silencing seal, and a heavy greatsword whose charged swings end the fight. Each form demands its own way of fighting.
bestFor: wanting two weapons in one match. Dual blades stack the silence, the greatsword's charged swing finishes it, and the choice between them never stops.

tips.earlyGame: Mulan starts in the clash lane, and the early game belongs to her dual blades. That stance grants 40 Movement Speed and lets every hit from her basic attacks and skills place a stack of Balance, so build your laning around short trades that carry a target to the 5-stack detonation. The thrown sword is dual-blade Skill 2, and walking next to it to retrieve the sword cuts 5 seconds off that same skill's cooldown — which is exactly why you throw it toward your own escape route rather than behind the enemy. Until level 4 unlocks the greatsword, don't force kills; spend the time drilling mark management and sword pickups into muscle memory.
tips.midGame: Level 4 is when Mulan actually starts playing. The core loop: stack five marks in dual-blade stance to detonate them, swap to the greatsword with Skill 3, and follow with a charged slash. The swap also raises her physical attack for 5 seconds, so land the swing inside that window. Mind the crowd control, though — the hit slows but does not root, and the silence itself only locks skills for 1 second. The target keeps walking. A full charge needs 1.5 seconds or more, which the silence cannot cover. The practical version is the 0.75-second charge: 25% slow for 2 seconds, pinning them down again. Greatsword skills grant unstoppable (crowd control immunity) and 45% damage reduction while they are active, so swing through the retaliation. Charge 1.5 seconds or more and the hit launches them for 0.5s — enough to finish any laner already below half HP.
tips.lateGame: Late game, split your time between pushing side lanes and playing silence-bot in teamfights. The silence lasts 1 second. That sounds short, but dropped on a mage the instant they start a cast, it erases that spell outright — treat it as a tool for denying one action, not for muting someone through a fight. At Overlord contests, use dual-blade mobility to flank, then time the greatsword swap onto a marked target the moment fighting starts. Walk in through the front and you'll get surrounded and accomplish nothing; the entry angle is everything.
tips.teamfight: Your job in a teamfight is to silence the one action the enemy most wants to take. Orbit the edge in dual-blade stance spreading marks, and save the fifth stack for the target you need muted. Watching an enemy mage start their cast animation and slamming the silence on top of it feels fantastic — their entire damage output just evaporates. Then swap to the greatsword and lean on the unstoppable frames to land a charged slash in the scrum. Even when you don't kill, the damage reduction gets you out alive more often than it should.

strengths: The 5-stack silence plus slow creates windows where enemies simply can't answer
Unstoppable and damage reduction on greatsword skills shrug off CC-heavy comps
No mana — she trades on cooldowns alone, forever
Swaps between dual-blade mobility and greatsword burst to fit the moment
weaknesses: Charged greatsword swings whiff entirely if the enemy makes distance
Gap-closing leans on the dual-blade Skill 1 dash, so she gets kited hard
Picking the wrong stance leaves her with neither damage nor speed
No built-in sustain — holding lane after getting chunked is miserable

name: Musashi
title: Musashi Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A dual-wielder whose skills build hostility stacks that change his empowered attacks. Skill 1 cuts projectiles out of the air, and his ultimate forces a duel with the healing delayed.
playstyle: A dual-wielder whose skills build hostility stacks that change his empowered attacks. Skill 1 cuts projectiles out of the air, and his ultimate forces a duel with the healing delayed.
bestFor: players who want to be the one issuing the duel, projectile-parries included — Skill 1 cuts arrows out of the air and the ultimate pins one target with their healing delayed.

tips.earlyGame: Jungle start is standard. Skill 2 refunds half its cooldown when it hits, so dashing through camps keeps you moving and puts your level 4 timing among the fastest in the jungle class. From your very first camp, drill the habit of weaving a basic attack after every skill: your Passive's empowered basics refund one second off Skill 1 and Skill 2 each, and that habit alone dictates both your clear speed and your gank quality. There's no need to force anything before level 4 — take river vision and scout your first duel target.
tips.midGame: Once you have your Ultimate, hunt isolated enemies in the side lanes. The lock-on dash cannot miss, grants 50% damage reduction and crowd control immunity while traveling, and slaps a five-second healing delay on the target — the more a fighter relies on sustain, the harder you beat them. At Tyrant fights, Skill 1's hidden strength shows: it destroys enemy projectiles along its path, letting you shield your team in river skirmishes. This is the window to build an item lead through duels and take control of the game's second half.
tips.lateGame: Past four items, the winning pattern is split-pushing a side lane and dueling whoever comes to answer. Against enemies below 50% HP, your empowered basic converts to a missing-HP execute strike, so your damage climbs as fights drag on. When you're needed in a teamfight, come in from a flank and point your Ultimate at the enemy carry — but a failed pick just hands them a reset once the healing delay expires. Before you commit, ask one question: can I kill this target within five seconds? If you hesitate, holding the dash wins more games than forcing it.
tips.teamfight: Musashi is not a front-and-center teamfighter. Open by holding Skill 1 to swat down the enemy's key projectiles, then enter from a flank with Skill 2 once their crowd control is spent. Your ideal victims are overextended marksmen and mages. From the Ultimate's knock-up, alternate skills and empowered basics and the cooldown refunds keep your hands full the entire fight. Two rules: never linger where multiple enemies can hit you, and never waste a single empowered basic. Follow both and even a five-man brawl turns into the duel you wanted.

strengths: One-of-a-kind defense — Skill 1 shoots enemy projectiles out of the air
Top-tier dueling via an unmissable dash with a healing delay attached
Empowered-basic cooldown cycling keeps his output relentless
Missing-HP execute damage closes out targets below half HP
weaknesses: Breaking the skill-into-basic weaving rhythm craters his damage
Struggles in head-on brawls where multiple CC chains land on him
A failed Ultimate pick lets the target heal back up and turn on him

counteredBy.name: Diaochan
counteredBy.reason: Diaochan cycles her skills far faster inside Flowery Potential, so Musashi dives in and she simply blinks away.

counteredBy.name: Liang
counteredBy.reason: Liang's suppression lands the moment Musashi's super armor ends and the trade begins.

synergies.name: Guiguzi
synergies.reason: Guiguzi pulls enemies into one spot, so Musashi's ultimate catches several of them as he lands.

synergies.name: Zhang Fei
synergies.reason: Zhang Fei slows nearby enemies with every skill once he transforms, so Musashi's duel target has nowhere to run.

builds.notes: Pure Sky arrives fifth: land a skill on an enemy hero and incoming damage drops 20% for three seconds. Its active cuts another 30% for three more. Bloodweeper closes the build, taking physical lifesteal to 33% and physical attack to +427. Boots of Resistance, bought second, add +100 magic defense and 25% tenacity, so Miyamoto Musashi can trade in the middle of a magic-heavy fight.
