builds.notes: Boots of Tranquility go in second here, pushing total cooldown reduction to 42.5%. Max HP piles up across Axe of Torment third, Dragon's Rage fifth and Blood Rage last, +2750 in all. Blood Rage adds 1.5% of that bonus HP to every basic attack, and trades 30% of current HP for a shield worth 40% of max HP. Dragon's Rage strips 3.5% of an enemy hero's HP per hit, so the tankier the target, the harder it bites.

name: Nakoruru
title: Nakoruru Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A straightforward, hard-hitting assassin who fights alongside her hawk. Land a skill, follow with an empowered attack, repeat — and her dash heals, giving her more staying power than she looks.
playstyle: A straightforward, hard-hitting assassin who fights alongside her hawk. Land a skill, follow with an empowered attack, repeat — and her dash heals, giving her more staying power than she looks.
bestFor: a first assassin. Land the mark, swing the empowered attack, repeat — and the healing dash forgives a fair number of mistakes.

tips.earlyGame: Nakoruru lives in the jungle. Skill 2 deals 50% bonus damage to monsters and heals on hit, giving her both clear speed and sustain through camps. Take both buffs and head straight to level 4 — the moment the Ultimate's 50% speed boost and terrain hop unlock, the quality of her ganks changes completely. The early trap is mana: detonating Skill 1's mark with any other damage refunds 35 MP, so build the habit of always following up a mark instead of leaving it to expire.
tips.midGame: Mid game, wall-hop ganks from outside vision are your main weapon. Fly in through an unwarded route, mark with Skill 1, and detonate with the charge — with the max HP percent damage included, that string takes most targets to half or lower. At Tyrant and Shadow Tyrant contests, the standard play is landing the Ultimate's charge on the enemy jungler: their damage output drops 30% for 3 seconds, which tilts the entire objective burn in your favor on paper.
tips.lateGame: The mark's max HP percent damage keeps her honest against tanks even late. But she has no exit tool after committing, so opening a fight from the front is off the table. Wait in side bushes and hunt chunked or isolated enemies instead. Her Ultimate's flight passive — activating after 4 seconds out of combat — quietly wins the late game's map movement: reset in a bush after each fight and you'll reach the next one before anybody else.
tips.teamfight: Enter from the flank or the back. Your first job isn't damage — it's landing the Ultimate's charge on the enemy's main damage dealer to shred their output by 30%. Put that debuff on their marksman and your frontline's lifespan visibly stretches. From there, loop Skill 1 marks into detonations while weaving empowered basics onto chunked targets. Each detonation refunds 2.5 seconds of Skill 1's cooldown, so as long as you keep connecting, the pressure never stops.

strengths: Out-of-vision ganks powered by the 50% speed boost and terrain hopping
The mark's max HP percent damage stays relevant against tanks
The charge debuff cuts an enemy ace's damage output by 30%
Skill 2's healing and monster bonus keep clears fast and healthy
weaknesses: An all-in kit with no escape when the dive goes wrong
MP-hungry — missing mark detonations leads to fast burnout
No answer to hard CC; getting caught means dying on the spot
The speed boost decays over time, so prepared enemies blunt the ambush

counteredBy.name: Zhang Fei
counteredBy.reason: Zhang Fei's spear sweep knocks enemy heroes away, so Nakoruru gets shoved back when she dives him head-on.

counteredBy.name: Wukong
counteredBy.reason: Wukong's Protective Shroud eats one of Nakoruru's skills outright and hands him a shield in return.

builds.notes: Rapacious Bite and Boots of Resistance come to 2,860G, then Axe of Torment's 90-180 Physical Pierce and Overlord's Might bring the total to 7,490G. The 30% bonus against enemies below 50% Health is online before the fifth slot is bought. Cuirass of Savagery fills that slot with 210 Physical Defense and 900 Max Health, and each hit taken adds 1% damage and Movement Speed for 3s, up to 10 stacks. Totals: +490 Physical Attack, +2,100 Max Health, +22.5% Movement Speed.

Its Countersiege runs for 3s and reflects 35% of damage taken as true damage, on a 75s cooldown. That is 90 more Physical Defense than Cuirass of Savagery, for totals of +350 Physical Defense, +500 Physical Attack, and +1,900 Max Health.

name: Nezha
title: Nezha Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A fighter who stacks true-damage shields and drops from the sky onto one chosen enemy with Skill 3. Skill 4 stretches that dive across the whole map for five seconds, and the enemies it reveals cannot recall. He is a marksman-catching device — his whole kit erases one target's escape options.
playstyle: A fighter who stacks true-damage shields and drops from the sky onto one chosen enemy with Skill 3. Skill 4 stretches that dive across the whole map for five seconds, and the enemies it reveals cannot recall. He is a marksman-catching device — his whole kit erases one target's escape options.
bestFor: assassins who go and settle 'kill that one and we win' themselves — Skill 4 puts every hero on the map inside diving range for five seconds, and there is no flight home.

tips.earlyGame: Nezha's first four levels are about patience. Do not force wins in the Clash Lane — tag enemies with Skill 1, let the five-second true-damage burn and its healing reduction do the grinding, and settle for short trades. Every skill hit on an enemy hero banks a true-damage shield, so lots of brief touches beat one long slugfest. Skill 2 rolls you behind a target for free hits, but remember it locks out on that same target for three seconds and burns your escape route. Priority number one is simple: reach level 4 without dying.
tips.midGame: Nezha's game starts moving the moment you learn Skill 3, Universe Ring - Skyfall. Spot a low-HP or isolated backliner on the minimap and fly straight to them. The landing knockback breaks their position while an ally collapses from the other side. For four seconds after landing you take 10% less damage at level 1 and gain 20% Resistance, so you can commit harder than it looks. The skill enters only 50%-100% of its cooldown depending on flight distance, so short hops come back fast. Range grows from 2,400 at level 1 to 3,600 at level 4. In a Tyrant standoff, pressuring the opposite side of the map without showing yourself forces the enemy to split bodies. Check the minimap for follow-up before every flight — that one habit erases most of this hero's deaths.
tips.lateGame: After 15 minutes Nezha is the teamfight start button. Skill 3, Universe Ring - Skyfall, is a one-way ticket, so only fly onto targets your team can reach within five seconds. The dream window is the enemy marksman stepping forward. Dive, knock them back out of the formation, then stack Skill 1's Scorching Ember; its 15% healing reduction slows every patch-up the support attempts. Skill 4, Universe Ring, moves nobody. It damages and reveals every enemy hero on the map, and for the next five seconds Skyfall reaches all of them. Revealed heroes cannot recall, so backing off to reset stops being an option. During Shadow Tyrant or Overlord standoffs, simply holding the dive warps the enemy backline's positioning. Great Nezhas save it for the two or three moments per game that actually decide something.
tips.teamfight: Nezha flies first or flies last — nothing in between. If your team has another initiator, the late dive is safer: wait for the enemy CC (stuns and other lockdown) to be spent, then drop on whoever is left carrying. After landing, stack Skill 1's burn to three, keep rolling behind fleeing targets with Skill 2, and let the true damage cook. Your shield rebuilds as long as skills keep connecting, which makes the center of the brawl the safest place you can stand. What you cannot beat is a spread formation kiting you in the open, so push for fights in tight terrain.

strengths: Skill 3 dives straight onto a distant backliner, and Skill 4 stretches its range across the whole map for 5s
True-damage burn plus healing reduction breaks sustain-heavy heroes
Shield stacks off every skill hit, keeping him alive in the scrum
Post-landing damage reduction and resistances make dives stick
weaknesses: Skill 3 has no return trip; without follow-up he dies alone
Lacks burst, so targets can slip away before the burn finishes them
Shield depends on landing skills; whiff and he is suddenly fragile
Minimal self-defense before level 4 and easily bullied in lane

builds.notes: After the 700G boots, Axe of Torment lands second and puts 90-180 physical defense penetration on the board early. Frostscar's Embrace and Pure Sky each stack another 10% cooldown reduction on top of it, and the finished build sits at 41%. Overlord's Might in the fifth slot raises damage against enemies below 50% HP by 30%. Demonsbane closes it out, adding magic defense equal to 50% of physical attack (up to 250), so +476 physical attack and +573 physical defense end up side by side.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Health to hold the line
builds.condition: When the enemy team leans on healing and you want to stay on the front line.
builds.notes: Blazing Cape comes right after the boots: +1100 max HP, plus a burn that cuts enemy healing and lifesteal by 35%. Blood Rage in the fourth slot adds 1.5% of bonus HP as physical damage to basic attacks, so the stacked health feeds the damage too. By Overlord's Platemail the line sits at +4587 max HP and +753 physical defense. Physical attack is 175 lower than the other build, and the 30% bonus against enemies below half HP waits until Overlord's Might arrives sixth.

name: Nuwa
title: Nuwa Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A mage with some of the longest range in the game, dropping judgement from off-screen. Her matrix corridors are paths only she can walk, letting her chip enemies who can never reach her.
playstyle: A mage with some of the longest range in the game, dropping judgement from off-screen. Her matrix corridors are paths only she can walk, letting her chip enemies who can never reach her.
bestFor: players committed to winning from out of reach — walling off the ground the enemy needs to walk, then detonating those walls into a chain from outside their range.

tips.earlyGame: Nuwa's Passive extends her basic attack and skill cast range, so from level 1 she farms mid from a step farther out than her opponent can reach. There is no reason to push up — thread Skill 1 through the spot where the enemy overlaps their minions and let the chip damage add up. Skill 2's walls are insurance before they are offense: block the gank path your jungler is not watching and any dive loses a full beat. Sit on Skill 3. Its warp and shield are the only reason she survives a collapse, so keep it pocketed until the gank threat is genuinely gone.
tips.midGame: The Tyrant spawn at 4:00 begins Nuwa's setup game. Lay two Skill 2 walls in the narrow paths leading to the pit, then thread Skill 1 into anyone touching them — the chain explosions plus the cross's bonus damage carve chunks out of enemies before the fight even starts. Since the matrix blocks only enemy heroes, smart placement seals both their retreat and their reinforcement route. After your first core item, her damage takes a real jump, so cycle between shoving mid and spending time on wall placement until the objective area belongs to you.
tips.lateGame: Once Shadow Tyrant and Overlord are on the line after 10 minutes, a single wall rewrites the geometry of a fight. Seal the pit entrance and the enemy eats a detour while your team pokes them apart. Ideally you bank all three Skill 2 charges before anything starts. Stay at the absolute back, and treat Skill 3's warp and shield as an anti-assassin escape button, never an engage tool. Warp out, drop one more wall behind you, and the chase simply dies. A prepared Nuwa is oppressive; an unprepared one is a minion with a health bar.
tips.teamfight: Nuwa's job starts ten seconds before the fight does. Read the enemy's approach path, pre-lay walls, and thread Skill 1 into the densest clump for chain explosions. Once the brawl is live, wall placement is the judgment call that defines her: cut off a fleeing enemy at the nose, or drop one between their assassin and your carry as a screen. The most painful mistake in practice is walling off your own team's retreat — when in doubt, bias the placement toward the enemy side. Keep Skill 3's warp and shield in reserve as your final card.

strengths: Passive range lets her poke from outside any retaliation distance
Walls become hero-only terrain that dominates every chokepoint
Wall-triggered chain explosions give a setup mage real burst damage
Skill 3's warp and shield answer one dive attempt for free
weaknesses: Needs setup time, so sudden brawls and mobile skirmishes blunt her
Skill 3 is her only escape; she is helpless right after using it
A misplaced wall can seal her own team's retreat
Open ground with no chokepoints devalues her walls sharply

synergies.name: Mozi

The arcana differ too: ten Mind's Eye instead of Tribute, worth 64 magical pierce. The build lands on 37.5% cooldown reduction, +1192 magical attack and +88 magical pierce.

builds.title: MP upkeep, bigger magical attack
builds.condition: When MP runs dry early and you keep leaving the lane
builds.notes: Boots of the Arcane open at 700G with +400 max MP and 10 MP restored every 5 seconds. The arcana take ten Tribute rather than Mind's Eye, adding +22 magical attack and 7% cooldown reduction. The 64 magical pierce dropped with Mind's Eye is covered by the boots' 60-120 pierce passive. Cooldown reduction settles at 29.5%, eight points behind build 1, while magical attack reaches +1214.

name: Pei
title: Pei Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An assassin who shifts between human and tiger stances — poke at range as a human, execute up close as a tiger. You are effectively piloting two kits plus an energy bar.
playstyle: An assassin who shifts between human and tiger stances — poke at range as a human, execute up close as a tiger. You are effectively piloting two kits plus an energy bar.
bestFor: players who judge range fast and enjoy a stance dance — human form does the chipping, tiger form's empowered basics do the killing, and misjudging the gap costs half your damage.

tips.earlyGame: Pei toggles between human and tiger with an Ultimate available from level 1, giving him one of the fastest jungle starts in the game. Shred your first buff with tiger-form empowered basics, and once the second buff is down, start eyeing an invade — almost no jungler beats Pei in a straight early-game scrap. Human form has longer basic attack range, and hitting the same target within 3 seconds scales the damage up to triple the base, so finish camps in human form: the kill is faster and the energy refunds come quicker.
tips.midGame: The gank template is a two-act play: chip in human, execute in tiger. Human form's Skill 1 deals 8% of current HP plus a slow, so even tanks feel the poke, and adding Skill 2's shield plus 30% attack speed makes you genuinely scary at range. Once the target drops below half HP, swap to tiger and pounce with the wall-crossing double dash into empowered basics. Constantly weigh the 4-minute Tyrant against the enemy's buffs — the instant you spot their jungler, steal the resources on the opposite side. Half-map control is the mid-game ideal.
tips.lateGame: Late teamfights are an exercise in patience. Both forms stay fragile, so open every fight in human form from the very back: throw Skill 1, maintain Skill 2's shield, and kite. The only time you swap to tiger is when the enemy's CC is spent and a target below 40% HP is clearly in view. Dive, finish them with empowered basics, and even after the kill, immediately return to human form and re-establish distance. Repeating 'tiger is for executions only' like a mantra puts you at exactly the right level of caution.
tips.teamfight: Your default is playing human form like a marksman: chip the frontline with Skill 1's percent damage, cycle your shield, and kite backward. The reason you never tiger-dive the clump is simple — the instant you transform, multiple CCs come flying. Your go signals are the enemy's stuns being spent and the backline's HP bars. When both line up, swap to Tiger Form, use a side wall for the double dash to erase their reaction time, and get into their carry's face. Secure the kill, skip the chase, and return to human-form range to rejoin the line. That whole loop is one set.

strengths: Form swapping covers both ranged poke and melee burst in one kit
The Ultimate is available from level 1, giving elite early fighting power
Human Form Skill 1's percent damage cuts through even tanks
Tiger Form's wall dashes open up a rich menu of ambush angles
weaknesses: Both forms are fragile; teamfight focus fire melts him quickly
No hard CC of his own, so picks depend on allied lockdown
Fighting at the wrong range for his current form halves his damage
Without an early snowball, his late-game presence thins out fast

counteredBy.name: Diaochan

counteredBy.name: Sun Bin

builds.notes: Frostscar's Embrace moves up to third, so at 4,920 gold the basic attack within five seconds of a skill carries 210-420 bonus physical damage. That same hit cuts enemy movement speed by 15-30%, keeping runners inside your range. The 300 physical defense also lands early, making mid-game skirmishes easier to hold. Axe of Torment's 90-180 penetration drops to the fourth slot and only arrives at 7,010 gold.

name: Sakeer
title: Sakeer Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A forest-keeper who grows his own bushes and sends fireflies to scout and heal. He is the only hero who adds terrain to the map, monopolizing the economy of hiding places.
playstyle: A forest-keeper who grows his own bushes and sends fireflies to scout and heal. He is the only hero who adds terrain to the map, monopolizing the economy of hiding places.
bestFor: anyone who wants to win the vision war — planting bushes where the map has none, hopping between them, and leaving the healing to the fireflies.

tips.earlyGame: Sakeer's early game starts with juggling two jobs: escorting your marksman and sweeping bushes for vision. The fireflies from your basic attacks reveal stealth, and the Passive automatically heals the lowest-HP ally near you, so standing in the right spot alone stabilizes the lane. Skill 2 holds 3 charges — assign roles up front (one for river scouting, one for escape, one for gank follow-up) and your death count drops. Firefly Power builds 1 stack every 1.5 seconds, and Skill 1's radius and healing scale with stacks, so the patience to sit on them until the moment you fire is itself a form of power.
tips.midGame: Once you learn the Ultimate, plant the glowing bush at the entrance to the battlefield before the 4-minute Tyrant and mid-game skirmishes. Fireflies launch every second — damaging enemies, healing allies — and you gain vision of any enemy who steps inside, so the side that placed it fights on terrain that wins both numbers and information. For gank follow-up, fly ahead with Skill 2 to a bush along the enemy's escape route and place Skill 1's knock-up on their exit — a brutal trap. At 9 stacks, Skill 1's radius is a different animal, so burn its maximum size into your muscle memory to sharpen your interceptions.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Sakeer stands half a step behind the carry, focused on one thing: delivering the 1-second knock-up at the perfect moment. The instant an enemy assassin or fighter touches your backline, launch them with a fully stacked Skill 1 and cut the follow-up cold — that single play swings teamfights directly. Firefly healing flies to the lowest-HP ally automatically, so as long as your own position is right, the support never stops. Against stealth heroes, your fireflies' true sight is close to a unique answer — build the habit of pre-firing a basic attack into any suspicious bush.
tips.teamfight: Whether the glowing bush is placed before a teamfight nearly doubles Sakeer's contribution. After setting it, fly with Skill 2 to a bush near your backline and bank Firefly Power while you wait for the engage. Answer enemy dives with Skill 1's knock-up, and let the automatic firefly healing raise your whole team's HP floor through the brawl. Your personal damage is low, so there's no need to chase or step forward. Accept that not dying converts directly into healing output, and keep moving bush to bush, always one step outside the enemy's reach.

strengths: Healing, a knock-up, vision, and stealth detection packed into one support kit
Bush-hopping through Skill 2 and the Ultimate gives him rare mobility for the role
The glowing bush dominates space and scouts around objectives
Fireflies auto-target the lowest-HP ally, so the support never misses
weaknesses: Skill 1 stays thin until Firefly Power builds, so he cannot spam it
Open terrain without bushes cuts his mobility and scouting in half
Low personal damage and no answer to chained hard crowd control
Healing dies when separated from allies — solo play is not an option

counteredBy.name: Liang
counteredBy.reason: Liang's circles hold vision over the brushes, so Sakeer's next hop is read before he takes it.

counteredBy.name: Wukong
counteredBy.reason: Wukong's Protective Shroud simply absorbs Mulberry Power, the one cast Sakeer's setup depends on.

synergies.reason: Luban No.7's scattershot only hits enemies caught in a straight line, and Sakeer's launch pins them in place.

Overlord's Platemail, Eye of the Phoenix and Ominous Premonition follow, taking the totals to +7,937 max HP, +593 physical defense and +270 magic defense. Redemption's shield is 240-480 plus 10% of max HP, so every HP item thickens what Sakeer hands to allies. builds.name: Build 2

builds.notes: Guardian - Redemption opens with 65-130 physical and magic defense on Sakeer, and half of that aura reaches allies within 800 range. Boots of the Arcane bring 60-120 magic penetration by 2,780G, and Breakthrough Robe, moved up to the fourth slot, adds up to 150 more. Totals come to +6,487 max HP, +450 magic attack and 13.5% cooldown reduction - 1,450 less HP than build 1, but 320 more magic attack. Frozen Breath closes it out, adding 75-150 plus 15% of magic attack as magic damage on hit, once every 3 seconds.

name: Shangguan
title: Shangguan Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An ambush mage who detonates intersecting ink strokes. Skill 3 chains a fresh dash every time she clips an enemy or a stroke, up to five; three or more launches her skyward, untargetable while the strikes rain down.
playstyle: An ambush mage who detonates intersecting ink strokes. Skill 3 chains a fresh dash every time she clips an enemy or a stroke, up to five; three or more launches her skyward, untargetable while the strikes rain down.
bestFor: players who plan the route before they move — each dash chains off your own ink and three of them lift you into the air, but hard CC before takeoff ends the combo.

tips.earlyGame: Before level 4, Shangguan is a paper mage who can't take off yet. Use Skill 2's brush and Skill 1's ink for wave clear, and fish for the Passive detonation that triggers where the two trails cross — it chips enemies and heals you at the same time. Simply playing around that intersection roughly doubles your harass output on the exact same casts. Her gank resistance is poor, so sit toward your tower whenever river vision is down, and don't bother showing up for the 4-minute Tyrant before level 4.
tips.midGame: The moment you learn your Ultimate, Shangguan becomes an assassin. Dash three to five times through ink or enemies and you ascend — untargetable, cleansed of all CC, raining ink on everything below, with five dashes granting the maximum number of strikes. You can do this under an enemy tower with total impunity, so the mid-game job is roaming to the farm lane and solo-diving the enemy marksman. With a core item done by around 10 minutes, anyone caught under a clean take-off simply melts.
tips.lateGame: Late game, one failed take-off can be the losing moment of the match. If your dashes get interrupted you are stranded in the middle of five enemies, so before committing, confirm the enemy's lethal lockdown — any suppression-style ultimate — has already been spent. Always enter from a flank. Poke with the Skill 2 into Skill 1 crossing detonation until your target drops below roughly 70% HP and their escape is burned, and your take-off success rate climbs dramatically. The landing recovery is long, so have the discipline to skip take-offs you can't confirm.
tips.teamfight: Spend the fight's opening at the back, scattering crossing detonations and collecting the heals while you read the fight. Two or more enemy CCs down is the take-off signal. You can dash along your own ink trails without touching a single enemy, so pre-draw your approach route in ink. Once airborne, the strikes fire automatically at whatever stands nearby, which makes the launch point everything — land your final dash right beside their carry. Repeat hits on the same unit deal only 25% damage, so a position that catches two or three bodies adds up to more total damage. Land toward your own team, always. Taking off through the enemy frontline is a mistake everyone in the lobby can identify.

strengths: Untargetable and crowd control immune while airborne, dealing unanswerable damage
Crossing brush and ink detonations poke and heal simultaneously
Solo tower dives delete enemy backliners from level 4 onward
Flexible dash routes make her entry angle nearly unreadable
weaknesses: Among the hardest heroes in the game; one missed dash means death
Hard CC before take-off shuts down her entire game plan
Long landing recovery invites the counter-kill if the target survives
Minimal self-defense before level 4 and extremely gankable

counteredBy.name: Liang
counteredBy.reason: Liang's suppression halts the dash chain, so Shangguan never reaches the untargetable leap that cleanses crowd control.

synergies.name: Guiguzi
synergies.reason: Guiguzi pulls enemies into one spot and stuns them, so Shangguan's intersecting brush strokes land on the whole group.

Every 2% of that lifesteal converts to 1% cooldown reduction, stacking 12% on top of the 12.5% the items list. Build 1 reaches Savant's Wrath only at 9,040G and Void Staff at 11,080G. Ardent Dominion, bought fourth, clears crowd control below 30% HP and grants a 4-second shield that carries 30% movement speed. Staves of Sorcery closes out the set at +997.8 magic attack, +32.5% movement speed and +700 max MP.

name: Shi
title: Shi Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A mage whose damage grows with distance — the inverse of every melee rule. Her silk pulls drag enemies while she lands maximum-range hits; letting anyone close is half a loss already.
playstyle: A mage whose damage grows with distance — the inverse of every melee rule. Her silk pulls drag enemies while she lands maximum-range hits; letting anyone close is half a loss already.
bestFor: players with the footwork to hold the untouchable distance, landing Silk Imprint at max range and dragging one enemy out of their formation.

tips.earlyGame: In mid, Shi clears waves quickly before level 4 thanks to Skill 1 dealing double damage to non-heroes, then spends the spare time poking from maximum range. The Passive adds 5% damage per 100 units of distance, capping at 40%, so firing from the very edge of your range is always the better trade. Skill 2's energy orb drifts toward enemies wrapped by Skill 1's silk, so never throw it on its own — always pair the two. Land even one pull-into-kill early and the enemy mid laner will stop standing inside Skill 1 range for the rest of the lane.
tips.midGame: Once you learn the Ultimate, Shi becomes the best gank launchpad your jungler could ask for. Before the 4-minute Tyrant fight, hook an enemy from a river bush with Skill 1 and drag them into your side of the map — that alone locks in a numbers advantage. During the Ultimate you can pull twice per Skill 1 hit and Skill 2's cooldown is halved, so you handle everything from the catch to the sustained damage by yourself. Pull diagonally back toward your team's damage, not straight toward yourself; drag them in a straight line and you're the first one getting hit.
tips.lateGame: In the late game, half the fight is decided the instant Skill 1 connects. Past 15 minutes with three magic core items, simply dropping a hooked enemy onto the center of Skill 2's explosion — which deals double damage there — vaporizes marksmen. But the downtime after a miss is heavier than ever, and the pull fizzles if the target gets far enough away, so resist the urge to chase deep. Don't forget the defensive job either: from behind your frontline, interrupt enemies winding up long channels by tagging them with the bind's crowd control.
tips.teamfight: Shi's teamfight contribution is the pick before the fight ever starts. In the standoffs before Overlord or Shadow Tyrant, catch whoever's positioning is sloppy with Skill 1, drag them into your team, and start the fight 5v4. Once it turns into a brawl, pull diving frontliners away from your carry and roll Skill 2 at their feet to stack sustained damage. Your distance Passive rewards you for orbiting the outer edge of the fight, far from the enemy clump, so hold that perimeter the whole way through.

strengths: Skill 1's forced displacement rips enemies straight out of their formation
The distance Passive makes max-range poke from total safety genuinely painful
The bind's crowd control interrupts enemy channeled skills
Double damage to non-heroes from Skill 1 keeps waveclear fast
weaknesses: Missing Skill 1 leaves her close to useless for several seconds
Almost no self-peel, and the distance Passive dies once enemies close in
The pull fizzles at long range, demanding precise spacing at all times

counteredBy.name: Zhuangzi
counteredBy.reason: Zhuangzi's passive cleanses crowd control and grants immunity, so the hold from Shi's Silk Imprint does not last.

counteredBy.name: Sima Yi

synergies.name: Huang Zhong

builds.notes: Boots of Deftness opens a run of five HP items that ends with Insatiable Tome, taking max HP to +3350. Breakthrough Robe, bought fourth, turns 2% of that bonus HP into magic attack and 3% into magic penetration, capped at +100 and +150. Mask of Agony, the third item, deals 3% of the target's current HP as magic damage four times over three seconds. Magic lifesteal totals 36%, and Splendor closes the build with an active that nullifies all effects for 1.5 seconds, at the cost of being unable to move or act.

builds.notes: Venomous Staff comes second, so the 35% cut to enemy healing and lifesteal is online at 2,740 gold. Every item after it carries magic attack, pushing the totals to +1022 magic attack and 30% cooldown reduction. Savant's Wrath adds 30% magic attack and Void Staff adds 45% magic penetration, percentage boosts that pay off more as the build fills out. Max HP stops at +1300, so safety rests on +25% movement speed and Ardent Dominion, which clears crowd control and grants a shield below 30% HP.

name: Shouyue
title: Shouyue Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A long-range sniper who converts calm into power — focus stacks build while out of combat and spend on single devastating shots. His three vision wards make him a reconnaissance network with a main gun attached.
playstyle: A long-range sniper who converts calm into power — focus stacks build while out of combat and spend on single devastating shots. His three vision wards make him a reconnaissance network with a main gun attached.
bestFor: shooters with patience — focus builds only while you hold fire, three devices widen what you can watch, and the shot is won by taking ground nobody can close on.

tips.earlyGame: Play the farm lane or mid lane, and train yourself to hug walls first. Skill 1's passive turns you camouflaged while out of combat near terrain, adding 15% move and attack speed. The lane phase revolves around Skill 2's snipe — a frankly unfair 750 base plus 8% max HP per shot from level 1, so landing two or three forces your opponent to recall. Practice the flick shot early: keep the laser aimed somewhere else and snap it onto the target at the last instant. Your hit rate becomes a different animal.
tips.midGame: Before the 4-minute Tyrant fight starts, place Skill 1's vision devices at the river junctions and enemy jungle entrances. You can stock up to three and each lasts 300 seconds, so never skimp on replacing them — that vision alone visibly cuts your whole team's gank deaths. On offense, keep sniping tower defenders with Skill 2 until they're at half HP and forced back, then siege with your team. Rounds stack up to three; never fire your last one for poke — always keep a bullet for self-defense.
tips.lateGame: Chipping the enemy carry to half HP before the fight even starts — that's Shouyue's late-game job. The Passive stacks Ambush once per 1.5s out of combat, up to 5 stacks, and while he holds stacks he gains 20% Physical Pierce plus bonus physical damage. A skill hit on an enemy hero spends all 5 stacks at once, so whether you can take one breath between snipes decides how much each shot weighs. Every 1% Critical Rate adds 4 damage to Wild Wind and 2 to Getaway, so his single-shot power keeps climbing as crit items come online. You never need to step forward. The very back, with walls and bushes behind you, is your permanent address.
tips.teamfight: One step further back than your own backline — that's your spot. Once the fight starts, snipe whoever's in your sightline with Skill 2, but prioritize wounded targets. When an assassin dives you, leap backward with your Ultimate while firing (it slows on hit), then follow up with a stocked Skill 2 round. Aiming a snipe leaves you defenseless for about 2 seconds, so fight with basic attacks while the enemy's dash skills are still up, and only settle in to snipe after they've been spent. That patience is what keeps you alive.

strengths: Skill 2's extreme-range snipe adds 8% max HP damage, so every shot hits like a truck
Three Skill 1 vision devices let him build his own safe zones on the map
Terrain camouflage hides his position while he lines up sightlines
Crit converts into snipe damage, so his one-shot power never stops scaling
weaknesses: Aiming a snipe takes about 2 seconds, leaving a huge opening up close
The Ultimate's backward leap is his only escape; chained dives kill him
A run of missed snipes craters his damage contribution
Sustained DPS lags behind rapid-fire marksmen in messy extended brawls

counteredBy.reason: Consort Yu turns immune to physical damage with Protecting Winds, so Shouyue's snipe and basic attacks do nothing.

counteredBy.name: Liu Bang
counteredBy.reason: Liu Bang's Battlefield Command shields the exact target Shouyue is aiming at, so the snipe lands into a shield.

synergies.reason: Mozi's barrier stuns enemies over and over, so Shouyue can finish his long aim before firing.

synergies.name: Lian Po
synergies.reason: Lian Po's Tremor Smash slows and then launches enemies, giving Shouyue time to complete his aim and land Wild Wind.

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: A last item that cuts enemy healing
builds.condition: When the enemy team leans on healing and lifesteal to stay alive
builds.notes: The first five items are shared, so the two builds only split at the sixth. Mortal Punisher costs 2,080G and heals you 375-750 over five seconds once your HP falls under 30%. Enemies hit by a basic attack lose 35% of their healing and lifesteal for 2.5 seconds. With seven Reaver slots and three Hunt, the totals land at 31.2% lifesteal and +128% attack speed, 23 points over build 2.

builds.title: A finisher for wounded targets

builds.notes: The same five items carry the build to 9,520G, then Overlord's Might at 2,540G fills the sixth slot. Targets under 50% HP take an extra 30% damage, and total physical attack sits at +439, fifty above build 1. Dropping Hunt for a full ten Reaver slots leaves lifesteal at 16% and attack speed at +105%. At 12,060G the build costs 460G more than build 1, so that last item lands later.

name: Sima Yi
title: Sima Yi Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A mid-range assassin who sees enemies whenever they cast skills, then dives with a silence attached. Mechanically normal-difficulty, but his real power is converting vision into aggression.
playstyle: A mid-range assassin who sees enemies whenever they cast skills, then dives with a silence attached. Mechanically normal-difficulty, but his real power is converting vision into aggression.
bestFor: anyone who plays off information rather than reflexes. Every enemy cast shows you where they are, and knowing first is what lets you pick the target for the silence.

tips.earlyGame: Sima Yi lives in the mid lane. Before level 4, keep an eye on your Passive: every skill an enemy hero casts nearby feeds you 10 energy, up to 50. When you are near the cap, harass with the empowered basic attack — its first hit teleports you behind the target, so even enemies hugging their minion wave can't hide from it. Into a mage matchup, Skill 2's passive heals you for 25% of magic damage taken, which means you can accept extended trades. One hard rule: never step forward while both your mana and your energy are empty.
tips.midGame: Once the 4-minute Tyrant contest starts, shove mid and rotate for ambushes on the side lanes and jungle. Skill 1 sends out a fast-moving spirit, but the crowd control immunity belongs to Sima Yi himself, not to the spirit. For the 2.5 seconds you probe ahead with it, nothing can lock your body down. Coming in sideways through brush is ideal. A basic attack — or the spirit expiring — pulls you to its position, so the long way around still closes fast. Chip with the behind-the-back empowered basic, then land Skill 2's 0.75-second silence to lock out their blink or CC before finishing the job. Your Passive also grants vision of enemy heroes who cast skills, so anyone charging a skill in brush gives away their position and hands you the ambush.
tips.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, with Savant's Wrath and Void Staff complete, your one-shot threat is real — but you're as fragile as ever. Let teammates take the first hit in teamfights, and move only after the enemy has dumped skills, feeding you both energy and vision. Your Ultimate is a backstep into a long charged dash that works for offense or escape, and since an interrupted charge refunds 90% of the cooldown, deliberately showing the wind-up to bait enemy CC becomes more and more valuable as the game goes on.
tips.teamfight: Your spot in a brawl is second wave. Because enemy skill casts charge your energy, entering from the flank right after their engage beats opening with a full combo — better damage, better safety. Hunt the isolated mage or marksman: the instant the empowered basic teleports you behind them, layer Skill 2's silence so they physically can't press their escape while you shred them. Skill 1 is effectively a blink since you can relocate to the spirit's position, so keep one charge in reserve as an exit — it changes your survival rate completely.

strengths: Energy charged by enemy skill casts plus a behind-the-target teleport gives elite ambush power
Skill 2's silence and 25% magic-damage healing make him a nightmare for mages
Skill 1 grants him crowd control immunity and relocates him to the spirit, working as both gap-closer and escape
An interrupted Skill 3 refunds 90% of its cooldown, so he can always re-engage
weaknesses: Healing is halved against physical damage, so marksmen grind him down
Damage depends on passive energy — enemies who hold their skills starve him
A clear damage trough opens right after his empowered basics are spent
Low base durability; a failed kill attempt invites an instant counter

name: Sun Bin
title: Sun Bin Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A time-keeper who accelerates allies and converts damage they took into healing. His silencing ultimate directly answers enemy channels — an understated kit that touches every critical moment.
playstyle: A time-keeper who accelerates allies and converts damage they took into healing. His silencing ultimate directly answers enemy channels — an understated kit that touches every critical moment.
bestFor: players who like handing out speed as a resource — Skill 2 accelerates the team and refunds a quarter of the damage they take, and with nothing here to lock enemies down, tempo is the contribution.

tips.earlyGame: Sun Bin is a roaming support built around time manipulation. Start by shadowing your marksman and holding the farm lane bushes; when the enemy commits, Skill 2's team-wide speed boost gets everyone out. The boost heals 25% of damage taken during its duration when it ends, so cast it just before enemy skills connect — not after you've started running — and the HP difference is plain to see. Skill 1's bomb is all about the 3-second detonation, so in skirmishes, sandwich the tagged target with an ally and chase until it pops.
tips.midGame: From level 4, ganks built around your Ultimate start connecting at a much higher rate. The field applies a heavy 1-second slow on hit and even silences enemies caught mid-cast, making it the answer to targets holding escape skills. At the 4-minute Tyrant and mid-game rotations, ferrying your whole team with Skill 2's +130 move speed is a job only Sun Bin does. Walking speed converts directly into numbers advantages — arrive at objectives five-strong one beat before the enemy, over and over, and the map tilts your way.
tips.lateGame: Late game, placing your Ultimate is map control in itself. The field detonates 5 seconds after deployment, so drop it in the narrow entrance to Shadow Tyrant or Overlord and the enemy must either fight inside the blast zone or concede the spawn. When fights break out, stick Skill 1 on their key hero and play for the detonation; when your team needs to reset, Skill 2's speed and refund heal rebuild the line. Your personal damage is modest, so operate from behind your team, out of enemy reach, and keep pulling the strings.
tips.teamfight: Open teamfights by placing your Ultimate on the enemy's escape path, not at their feet. The 1-second slow lets your team's follow-up land, and the 5-second delayed blast catches them on the retreat. Attach Skill 1 to a frontliner and the 3-second fuse plus AoE slow completes the trap. Skill 2 works as an engage tool too, but its best use is covering the exact moment enemy burst lands — with 25% of damage taken coming back a few seconds later, it feels like haggling the enemy mage's full combo down to three-quarters price.

strengths: Skill 2 speeds up the entire team, winning rotations and chases before they start
25% of damage taken during the boost returns as healing — a strong burst counter
Ultimate silences on interrupt, and its delayed blast dominates whole areas
weaknesses: No stuns or hard CC, so he can't lock down a kill by himself
Both Skill 1 and the Ultimate have delayed payoffs, lacking instant stopping power
Personal damage and durability are below average — a misused speed boost leaves nothing

name: Sun Ce
title: Sun Ce Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A fighter who sails a ship into the enemy team. The boat opens the fight, then he disembarks and brawls, sustained by empowered-attack healing. Ninety percent of playing him is the entrance.
playstyle: A fighter who sails a ship into the enemy team. The boat opens the fight, then he disembarks and brawls, sustained by empowered-attack healing. Ninety percent of playing him is the entrance.
bestFor: players who want to start every teamfight themselves — the ship carries a teammate across the map and detonates on the first wall it touches, so the steering is the engage.

tips.earlyGame: Sun Ce hunts for lane control with level 2 trades in the clash lane. The core pattern is Skill 1 in, Skill 2, weave a basic attack, then Skill 2 again — each Skill 2 cast hits 25% harder and resets your basic attack cooldown, so punctuating casts with swings hurts far more than mashing. His Passive stacks physical defense every time he takes physical damage, so against AD matchups, brawl freely; the empowered basic attack every 5 seconds heals enough to win the war of attrition.
tips.midGame: From level 4, the boat is Sun Ce's calling card. While sailing you have crowd control immunity — knock-ups and the like never land — and can carry one teammate, so scooping up your mid laner for a gank is a devastating play. The ideal rhythm: sail to a side lane before the 4-minute Tyrant, create a numbers advantage, then arrive at the pit on spawn. The boat detonates on contact with walls and enemies, knocking targets up, so watch your spacing against terrain, not just your target. Winding routes are where boats go to die.
tips.lateGame: Late game, Sun Ce is the team's designated engage. The longer the boat sails, the longer the knock-up — up to 1.5 seconds — but steering gets harder too, so pre-plan the shortest hidden approach before you commit. Aim for their backline. If the hit misses, swallow your pride, hop off mid-route, and join the frontline fight with Skill 1 and Skill 2. A boat that connects cleanly on the right target ends the teamfight before it begins; a solo boat launched beyond your team's reach is Sun Ce's single most common way to lose.
tips.teamfight: Launch from bushes or from behind walls. Hop off just before impact so only the boat connects — you stay free to act during the knock-up, letting you layer a max-range Skill 1 for the second knock-up in the chain. With the target locked down, unload all three Skill 2 casts with basic attacks in between. While enemy Flashes are still up, holding the boat and firing it as the follow-up to an ally's CC is the disciplined play. With his defense stacks rolling, Sun Ce is far harder to kill than he looks.

strengths: The boat crosses the map and ferries an ally straight into ganks
Boat explosion plus Skill 1 chains two knock-ups back to back
Stacks physical defense when hit, winning drawn-out AD brawls
Empowered-attack healing outlasts lane wars of attrition
weaknesses: The boat detonates on walls, so one steering error wastes the engage
Missing both the boat and Skill 1 leaves no CC and easy kiting
Solo engages without follow-up lock enemies down but kill nothing
Noticeably soft at fight start before his defense stacks build

name: Ukyo Tachibana
title: Ukyo Tachibana Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A swordsman defined by spacing: his draw-cut rewards hitting at the very tip of its range, so every fight is measured in single steps. His backward leap makes enemies whiff at the moment they commit.
playstyle: A swordsman defined by spacing: his draw-cut rewards hitting at the very tip of its range, so every fight is measured in single steps. His backward leap makes enemies whiff at the moment they commit.
bestFor: footsies. Damage, healing and the stun all hinge on connecting at the very tip of the range, so every duel is measured one step at a time.

tips.earlyGame: Ukyo is primarily a jungler, though his dueling power makes clash lane workable. Clear camps around the Ultimate's four slashes and Skill 1, weaving the Passive's iai slash into every camp — skill damage refunds 0.5 seconds of its cooldown per hit, so clean rotations alone speed up your route. What matters before level 4 is internalizing tip range: both the iai slash and Skill 2 only pay their bonuses when they land at the very edge of their reach.
tips.midGame: Around 10 minutes, with two physical items done, Ukyo wins almost any small-scale fight he takes. The ideal engage starts with Skill 2's tip stun — pour the Ultimate's four slashes into the 0.75-second lock, and the healing per enemy hero hit lets you out-sustain the brawl. He has genuine 1v2 potential, but he also folds instantly to CC, so while enemy lockdown is still up, measure the fight from one step back.
tips.lateGame: Late game, his bait game on side lanes shines. Shove the wave; if one enemy comes, cook them at tip range — if two come, double-jump out with Skill 1. Repeat, and you're feeding your team a permanent numbers advantage. Never enter teamfights through the front: the CC-saturated middle is a death zone for Ukyo. Flank, wait for the formation to crack, and enter on a chunked target with the tip stun.
tips.teamfight: Ukyo's teamfight is a continuous act of measuring tip distance inside the chaos. Too close and the bonus vanishes; too far and nothing lands. Watch for the enemy's dash, jump backward with Skill 1, and land the iai slash at the tip as they arrive — when that counter connects, the aggressor is the one who gets shredded. Angle the Ultimate through as many enemy heroes as possible: the healing stacks per hit, so slashing through two or three from the side actually keeps you healthier than dueling one target point-blank.

strengths: Tip hits pay out damage, healing, and a stun all at once
The Ultimate's multi-hit healing wins extended small-scale brawls
Skill 1's double jump covers both aggression and clean exits
Skill hits refund the Passive's cooldown, keeping his output constant
weaknesses: Everything depends on spacing — wrong range means no damage and no healing
Fragile at baseline; getting CC'd is his number one cause of death
Skill 1's unusual movement takes real practice to stop misplaying
Struggles to show his strengths in CC-heavy frontal teamfights

name: Umbrosa
title: Umbrosa Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An honest fighter whose basic attacks adapt to range, throwing rebounding blades at distance. There is one trick — tapping basic attack just before the blade comes home sends it straight back out — but at heart she is a straightforward brawler, and the easy rating is accurate.
playstyle: An honest fighter whose basic attacks adapt to range, throwing rebounding blades at distance. There is one trick — tapping basic attack just before the blade comes home sends it straight back out — but at heart she is a straightforward brawler, and the easy rating is accurate.
bestFor: learning the fighter role from scratch — the only mechanic worth drilling is tapping Basic Attack just before the blade comes home, and the rest is honest brawling.

tips.earlyGame: Clear speed is the calling card. Umbrosa's Passive changes shape with range — a spinning featherblade at distance, a fast three-hit string up close — and tapping basic attack just as the blade returns bounces it back out with 5% more damage and projectile speed per bounce (up to three). Drill that timing on jungle camps until it's muscle memory. Everything changes at level 4: the Ultimate's temporary HP equal to 50% of your health turns invades and slightly greedy ganks into genuine options.
tips.midGame: This is a snowball hero, so from 8 to 12 minutes you're prowling the map for anyone farming alone. Open with Skill 1's 50% attack speed steroid, stack marks with the close-range strings, then Skill 2's dash into the multi-hit dance to spend them — healing on every hit while the damage pours in. You can move during the dance, so literally sidestep enemy skills mid-combo while you keep carving. If the fight turns, recast Skill 2 to cancel the dance and leave. There is always another target.
tips.lateGame: Five-on-five head-on collisions are not her format, so play the late game as a pure flanker. A few seconds into the fight, when every enemy eye is fixed forward — that's your cue. Cast the Ultimate for the 50% temporary HP and its AoE damage, dive the backline, and one squishy dies before the buffer runs out. Even if you fall, dying while the Ultimate is off cooldown triggers a revival with another AoE burst, so you force the enemy to pay one-and-a-half deaths' worth of resources for one of yours. That math is the whole terror of this hero.
tips.teamfight: Never take the opening engage. Sit on the perimeter, flick featherblades in to pre-stack marks, and watch for the enemy's key CC to be spent. Then commit: Skill 1 into Skill 2's dance to detonate the marks, healing through the chaos at the center of the fight. The dance strikes ten times and its final hit carries 100% bonus damage, so the more marks banked before entry, the heavier a single dive lands. And from live play: revive right when the enemy has forgotten the mechanic exists, drop the AoE on their heads, and watch entire fights flip.

strengths: Range-shifting basics let her fight at whatever distance the enemy picks
Skill 2's dance moves and heals, so she out-sustains extended exchanges
50% temp HP plus a death revival forces better-than-even trades
Skill 2's cooldown halves when the dance whiffs, keeping the kit fast
weaknesses: The blade-bounce timing takes real practice to internalize
With the Ultimate on cooldown she loses the license to dive
Comps that instantly burst the temp HP break her trade math
No hard CC of her own — catching dedicated runners is on her team

name: Wang Wei
title: Wang Wei Guide: Combos, Counters & Strategy - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An area mage that drops a mountain on the target spot, then pulls enemies into its center with Endless River and detonates it. Official difficulty: Easy.
playstyle: An area mage that drops a mountain on the target spot, then pulls enemies into its center with Endless River and detonates it. Official difficulty: Easy.
bestFor: players who can send Endless River into the mountain before it explodes. Keep that order and the area combo comes together quickly. One With All also changes what Skill 1 and Skill 2 do for 9 seconds, so steering the mist takes some practice.

tips.earlyGame: Misty Mountain is cheap: a 6-second cooldown and 35 Mana. It hits for 400 damage (plus 80% of your magical attack) the moment it appears and slows by 20% for 0.75s. For the next 1.5s it deals 45 every 0.4s, then explodes for 180. Drop it where enemies and minions overlap, and one cast both clears the wave and chips your opponent. Shifting Mists gains 1 mark every 5 seconds at Level 1, so a full 5 marks takes 25 seconds. Standing inside your own mountain puts you in the Misty Mountain state and speeds up mark gain. Check that your dodge is ready before stepping forward.
tips.midGame: In the mid game, Misty Mountain into Endless River becomes your main tool. Place the mountain first, then hit it with the river before its 1.5 seconds of damage run out. The river circles the mountain once, pulls enemies to its center and detonates it. Endless River's cooldown is 10 seconds (8 at Level 6), longer than the mountain's 6, so you can't pair them every time. Treat the extra mountains as poke. When the river hits an enemy, up to 2 streams split off to chase nearby enemies and slow them by 15% (Level 1).
tips.lateGame: At Level 3, One With All's cooldown drops to 45 seconds. Landing deals 800, and the follow-up deals 500 every 1/3s for 3 seconds (both at Level 3, plus a share of your magical attack). Repeat hits on the same enemy fall to as low as 1/3. The follow-up locks on to a random enemy in range, so if only the frontline is near your landing spot, the frontline takes it. Carry the mist close to the backline before you recast. By Level 15, Shifting Mists can dodge up to 500 damage, and marks come every 4 seconds.
tips.teamfight: Fights start with Misty Mountain the moment enemies bunch up. Run Endless River through it to pull them together and stack the detonation on top. One With All's mist deals 150 (Level 1) to enemies in its path. Repeat hits on the same enemy drop to 1/3, so sweep across as many different enemies as you can. While steering, Skill 1 becomes Mist Rider and Skill 2 becomes Churning Mists. Decide in advance whether to cast the mountain and river before the mist or after landing. For 3 seconds after landing, Wang Wei is in the Misty Mountain state and gains marks faster.

strengths: Misty Mountain costs 35 Mana on a 6-second cooldown and follows its 400 initial hit with damage over time and a 180 explosion (Level 1)
Running Endless River into the mountain pulls enemies to its center before detonating it
One With All lets Wang Wei steer the mist for 9s and land somewhere far away for 400 damage (Level 1)
At 5 marks, Shifting Mists dodges the next instance of damage (up to 250 at Level 1)
weaknesses: No stun or launch; Wang Wei can only hinder enemies with slows and Endless River's knockback and pull
One With All's follow-up damage locks on to a random enemy in range, so Wang Wei can't pick the target
One With All is Wang Wei's only movement skill; during its 55-second cooldown (Level 1), Endless River's knockback is the only skill that pushes a diver away
Shifting Mists gains 1 mark every 5 seconds at Level 1, so outside the Misty Mountain state a full 5 marks takes 25 seconds

counteredBy.name: Zhuangzi
counteredBy.reason: Zhuangzi's Butterfly Effect grants teammates crowd control immunity, so Wang Wei's Endless River cannot pull them into the mountain.

counteredBy.name: Sima Yi
counteredBy.reason: Sima Yi heals from magical damage taken, and every Wang Wei skill is magical, so the poke struggles to finish him.

synergies.reason: Wang Zhaojun's Frigid Prison freezes enemies in place, so they cannot dodge the Misty Mountain Wang Wei conjures at the target location.

synergies.name: Guiguzi
synergies.reason: Guiguzi's The Animist pulls enemies to him and stuns them, so Wang Wei's Misty Mountain hits the whole group at once.

name: Wang Zhaojun
title: Wang Zhaojun Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A slow-acting lockdown mage who layers chill until enemies freeze solid. Her out-of-combat shield keeps her alive while her blizzard gradually strangles the enemy formation.
playstyle: A slow-acting lockdown mage who layers chill until enemies freeze solid. Her out-of-combat shield keeps her alive while her blizzard gradually strangles the enemy formation.
bestFor: anyone who prefers certainty to speed. The freeze is slow and rarely lands alone, so you layer it over ally crowd control and chokepoints until there is nowhere left to step.

tips.earlyGame: In the mid lane, Skill 1 is your everything until level 4. It clears waves, and since it grants 2 seconds of vision at the impact point, firing scout shots into the river brush warns you of ganks before they happen. Your Passive shield regenerates out of combat and chills any physical attacker who breaks it, so trade confidently whenever the shield is up. Skill 2 has a long delay before it triggers, so at this stage only aim it at enemies rooted in place clearing the wave — anything else is a coin flip.
tips.midGame: Wang Zhaojun's setup game begins with the 4-minute Tyrant. Drop your Ultimate's blizzard on the river entrance and that path is closed for 5 seconds — anyone forcing through eats chill that strips both movement and attack speed. When a gank arrives, pre-place Skill 2 on the enemy's escape route — more precisely, on the spot where they'll stand after using their blink. Land the 2.5-second freeze with your jungler present and the kill is all but booked. The Ultimate also refreshes your Passive shield, which is exactly the license you need to play forward.
tips.lateGame: With Savant's Wrath and Void Staff done after 15 minutes, the blizzard's ticks turn genuinely heavy. Before Shadow Tyrant and Overlord fights, seed the chokepoint with your Ultimate early, warp their formation, and give your team the signal to commit. If the freeze → Skill 1 → empowered third basic sequence reaches their backline, the numbers advantage ends the game on the spot. You have zero mobility, so live in the deepest position — and when the enemy assassin vanishes from the map, your first thought should be about your own feet.
tips.teamfight: Your contribution is decided by who you chill. Cooling down their frontline tank moves nothing. The target is their marksman: chill strips up to 50% of both movement and attack speed, which functionally disarms a carry — damage and kiting gone in one status effect. The ideal opening: blizzard on their backline's heads, Skill 2 on the retreat path, then Skill 1 and empowered basics to follow. Frozen enemies also take bonus damage, so tell your team before the fight to focus whoever's frozen first — it visibly changes the results.

strengths: Skill 2's 2.5-second freeze converts into a near-guaranteed kill with follow-up
Chill strips movement and attack speed at once — brutal against marksmen
The Ultimate refreshes her Passive shield, making her tougher than she looks
Skill 1's vision grant makes her excellent at scouting and dodging ganks
weaknesses: Skill 2's trigger delay makes it nearly impossible to land unassisted
No movement skill — once an enemy reaches her, she rarely gets away
Damage lives in placed zones, so constantly moving enemies out-trade her
Enemies who step out of the blizzard halve her teamfight output

builds.name: Build 1
builds.title: Survive-and-cast core
builds.condition: When the enemy has divers and you need to keep casting under pressure.
builds.notes: Boots of Deftness goes down first at 700G, so the +70 movement speed is there from the opening. Twilight Stream, the fifth pick, stacks 20-40 magic defense penetration for four seconds each time you damage an enemy hero, up to six stacks. Splendor closes the build with 12% magic lifesteal and an active that nullifies every effect for 1.5 seconds, though moving and attacking stop for that window. Equipment and arcana together come to +2200 max HP, +882 magic power and 40% cooldown reduction, 300 more HP than Build 2.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Penetration first, then burn
builds.condition: When two or more enemy frontliners are stacking magic defense.
builds.notes: Boots of the Arcane in the first slot buys 60-120 magic defense penetration for 700G. Mask of Agony moves up to second and lands at 2,780G total, chipping 3% of the target's current HP four times across three seconds whenever a skill connects. Void Staff raises penetration by a further 45%, and Sage's Tome brings equipment and arcana to +1112 magic power. That is 230 more magic power than Build 1, and 300 less max HP.

name: Wukong
title: Wukong Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A crit assassin built around parrying: Skill 1 blocks an enemy skill, and a successful block grants invincibility and a shield that flows into his knock-up combo. The whole kit is a mind game.
playstyle: A crit assassin built around parrying: Skill 1 blocks an enemy skill, and a successful block grants invincibility and a shield that flows into his knock-up combo. The whole kit is a mind game.
bestFor: reading the opponent one step ahead. Bait a key skill, block it, punish — and accept that a wrong guess is the reason you die.

tips.earlyGame: Wukong owns one of the fastest jungle clears in the game. Skill 2 deals true damage to monsters and outright executes any monster below 15% HP (Tyrant and Overlord excluded), so his full clear beats most junglers by a camp. The catch: his crit damage starts capped at 150%, so his early dueling is weaker than the highlight reels suggest. Farm to level 4 without greed, and keep one eye out for the enemy jungler's invade — that's the only real threat.
tips.midGame: Everything changes around 8-10 minutes with one or two attack speed and crit items done. His post-skill empowered basics always crit, which means every point of crit damage on your items is pure scaling. Gank by entering with Skill 2's dash, then empowered basic into the Ultimate's knock-up into detonating brands with basics. Hold Skill 1 in reserve as insurance against their answer skill instead of burning it for movement — your success rate climbs immediately.
tips.lateGame: At full build, a single empowered basic deletes backliners. His body stays soft, though, so never walk in through the front. Wait in side bushes or behind walls and strike from behind the moment enemy eyes face forward. One trick: pre-channel Skill 1 right before you dive. Catching their reaction skill is far easier that way than pressing it reactively, and a successful block's shield plus 0.2 seconds of immunity transforms your odds of walking out alive.
tips.teamfight: Opening the teamfight is a mistake. Wukong's job is spotting the handful of seconds when the enemy backline's peel thins out. Enter with Skill 2's speed, empowered basic, Ultimate knock-up, then detonate the brands with basics while another guaranteed crit lands. Everything crits, so squishy targets die before the knock-up ends. Finish, then take Skill 2's second dash to complete the exit. Whether you chase a second kill comes down to one question: is Skill 1 still up?

strengths: Post-skill empowered basics always crit, giving elite late-game burst
Skill 1 can nullify one key enemy skill and flip entire duels
The monster execute makes his jungle clear among the fastest anywhere
40% speed from Skill 1 and 90% from Skill 2 start both his engages and his exits fast
weaknesses: His damage stays modest until crit items actually come online
Whiffing the Skill 1 block exposes just how soft his defenses are
Reliant on empowered basics — attack-dodging enemies blank him
The knock-up is his only CC, so fleeing targets are hard to pin

builds.title: Crit damage stacked high
builds.condition: When the enemy draft fields two or more squishy backline heroes.
builds.notes: The buy order matches Build 2: Rapacious Bite at 2160G, then Boots of Fortitude at 700G to get moving early. Eternity Blade and Shadow Ripper alone carry crit rate to 40%. Ten Unparalleled slots add another 7% and pile on 36% critical damage from arcana alone. Attack speed and health are left to the Fate setup; this one buys the size of the hit.

builds.title: Attack speed and health
builds.condition: When the enemy fields durable frontliners that no single burst can drop.
builds.notes: The same six items in the same order as Build 1. Swapping the ten slots to Fate lifts the totals to +48% attack speed, +1337 max health and +123 physical defense. Crit rate stops at the 40% the items provide, and no arcana critical damage sits behind it. Both builds carry the same 36.2% physical lifesteal from Reaver and Bloodweeper; the extra 10% attack speed is what turns it over faster.

name: Wuyan
title: Wuyan Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A heavy bruiser whose every hit has a chance to petrify. Wide hammer swings and a shield make her a brawl monster, and the random stone gaze poisons every enemy calculation.
playstyle: A heavy bruiser whose every hit has a chance to petrify. Wide hammer swings and a shield make her a brawl monster, and the random stone gaze poisons every enemy calculation.
bestFor: players who wield randomness as pressure — anything that lands, attack or skill, petrifies the target half the time, so keep swinging and take the coin flip that comes up wrong at the worst moment.

tips.earlyGame: In the clash lane, treat everything up to level 4 as target practice for Skill 2. One cast clears the wave, and center hits deal 50% bonus damage, so aim at the enemy's feet the instant they step up for a last-hit. Open trades with Skill 1's dash and its empowered basic attack; when the 50% petrify chance procs, stack Skill 2 onto the frozen target to win the exchange outright. Your Passive shield refreshes every 3 seconds, so the more short trades you take, the further ahead you get.
tips.midGame: Once your Ultimate unlocks at level 4, make sure you walk to the 4-minute Tyrant fight in time. During the 3.2-second spin, damage ticks every 0.4 seconds and each tick rolls the petrify check, so simply parking it in a brawl freezes enemies one after another. The spin also ramps your move speed in steps and stacks shields, so you can chase fleeing targets too. One caveat: casting Skill 1 during the Ultimate slows the dash — dash first, then spin, and you'll whiff far less.
tips.lateGame: With three defensive items done around 15 minutes, your role is holding the front and stopping enemies on repeat. Enter fights with Skill 1 into their clump, then Ultimate immediately. The spin's outer edge deals 50% bonus damage, so a half-step of positioning to keep enemies on the rim turns your damage into something else entirely. Petrify is still a dice roll, though — don't stake everything on it against the one target you absolutely must stop. Keep Skill 2 in reserve for after the spin, and a petrified backliner becomes a free kill to carry home.
tips.teamfight: Your teamfight job is to spin in the middle of their team and wreck the formation. Skill 1 in, Ultimate out: ticks every 0.4 seconds scatter petrifies across multiple enemies, leaving them unable to fight back or retreat cleanly. Petrify has an 8-second cooldown per target, so rather than chasing someone already frozen, walk your spin onto enemies you haven't stopped yet — total lockdown time goes up. The window right after the spin ends is your biggest opening, and whether Skill 2 goes onto their backline or stays for self-defense there swings the result.

strengths: Every instance of damage carries a 50% petrify chance — keep hitting and enemies stop moving
Skill 2 center hits deal enough damage to delete backliners even on a tanky build
Passive and Ultimate shields keep cycling, making her tougher than her stats suggest
weaknesses: Petrify is RNG — it can fail at the decisive moment and invite a counterattack
Skill 2's long wind-up makes it hard to land raw on mobile targets
Her only mobility is Skill 1's short dash, so kiting shuts her out completely

name: Xiang Yu
title: Xiang Yu Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A tank who becomes hardest to kill at the brink — 40% damage reduction kicks in below 30% Health. His knockbacks and attack-down debuff dull the enemy's edge exactly when late-game fights peak.
playstyle: A tank who becomes hardest to kill at the brink — 40% damage reduction kicks in below 30% Health. His knockbacks and attack-down debuff dull the enemy's edge exactly when late-game fights peak.
bestFor: tanks who are fine being the one whose health bar drains. Drop the attack-down debuff onto the enemy's engage and hold the line; the lower you go, the harder you are to kill.

tips.earlyGame: The lane badge at the top of this page reads Clash, following the official stats. The advice below assumes a roaming pick. On the global server, roam is his standard assignment. Attach to your marksman from level 1 and play the bodyguard: in skirmishes, Skill 1's knockback exists to bat divers away from your carry. In trades, Skill 2 is quietly vicious — it cuts the attack damage of every enemy in range by 30% for 3.5 seconds, so slapping it on top of the enemy's engage simply deletes their trade math. Maintain HP with the empowered basic's healing, rush tank items above all else, and be there when your jungler moves for the 4-minute Tyrant.
tips.midGame: Through the mid game, with one or two defensive items done, Xiang Yu's value is measured in gank follow-ups. Skill 1's dash carries enemies with its knockback, so the trick is angling it to shove a fleeing target back toward your team — connect the knock-up and your side's full damage lands during it. In Tyrant and mid-lane collisions, stand at the very front and stop fearing a shrinking HP bar: drop below 30% and the Passive's 40% damage reduction triggers on its own, wrecking the enemy's damage math. Weaken overchasers with Skill 2 and swallow them whole — that's the mid-game pattern.
tips.lateGame: The late game belongs to Xiang Yu. Right when enemy damage peaks, his kit peaks harder: 40% damage reduction below 30% HP, and an Ultimate that makes him unkillable — HP cannot drop below 1 — while it's active. The tank who was supposed to die first simply doesn't, and that stolen time becomes your team's counterattack window. The Ultimate also deals more and heals more the lower your HP sits, so a near-death swing hits harder than some fighters' full combos. At Overlord, soak every enemy cooldown at the front, then look for the answering blow.
tips.teamfight: The job description is short: stand at the front, get hurt, then hit back. Your opening is a choice between shoving their frontline into your team with Skill 1 or batting an assassin off your carry. Fire Skill 2 the instant enemies clump — a 30% attack cut across their whole team visibly shrinks the damage your side takes. The Ultimate is for stepping into the enemy team on low HP: crowd control immunity and the unkillable effect mean you cannot die during the charge, and the slash stuns with 50% bonus damage on connect. The moment the Xiang Yu they thought was dead swings back is the moment fights flip.

strengths: Gets tougher as he gets lower via the unkillable Ultimate and 40% damage reduction
Skill 2's 30% attack cut suppresses an entire team's damage
Excellent peel with knockback and knock-up to protect his carries
The low-HP Ultimate hits far harder than a tank has any right to
weaknesses: Skill 1 is his only movement and can't cross walls — kiting ruins him
The Ultimate's charge-up is telegraphed and easy to sidestep
Missing the blade's edge means no stun and no bonus damage
Low damage and low pressure while his HP bar is still full

name: Xiao Qiao
title: Xiao Qiao Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The entry point to ranged mages: poke with a returning fan, protect yourself with a knock-up, and speed up on every hit so you're never caught. Simple, but every fundamental of range control lives here.
playstyle: The entry point to ranged mages: poke with a returning fan, protect yourself with a knock-up, and speed up on every hit so you're never caught. Simple, but every fundamental of range control lives here.
bestFor: learning the mage role properly — with no dash to bail you out, every fight comes down to spending the knock-up on offense or saving it to protect yourself.

tips.earlyGame: In the mid lane, Xiao Qiao can run her whole laning phase off Skill 1. The fan flies out and boomerangs back, so after the first hit, sidestep so the return path crosses the same target — one cast, two hits, and it clears the wave at the same time. You'll be tempted to use Skill 2 for damage; don't. Before level 4, that 1.5-second knock-up is your only answer to a jungle gank, and Xiao Qiao has no dash to fall back on. Watch your mana, and when the 4:00 Tyrant fight starts, lob fans in from the edge of the river rather than committing to the pit.
tips.midGame: From level 4 onward, a simple rule keeps you alive: only go all-in when Skill 2 actually lands. During the 1.5-second knock-up, stacking your Ultimate meteors and Skill 1 on top deletes any mage or marksman outright. When Skill 2 is down or missed, go back to fan poke and nothing else. Once your first one or two AP items finish around 7-9 minutes, use the movement speed from your Passive and Ultimate to shove mid and show up in the farm lane — you rotate faster than your lane opponent, and that creates free numbers advantages.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Xiao Qiao does half her job before the fight even starts. Thread fans into the enemy clump during the standoff — a double-hit strips 20-30% off a frontliner, and your team fights noticeably braver with that lead. Whether Skill 2 opens fights or saves your life depends entirely on the enemy comp: if they run a dash-heavy assassin, it stays in your pocket, no debate. Your Ultimate lets you move while it channels, so walk backward toward your team as the meteors fall. That one habit fixes most deaths where you got dropped before your damage finished.
tips.teamfight: Hold the backline, chip with Skill 1, and the moment someone jumps you, knock them up with Skill 2 — an assassin diving into your Ultimate mid-knock-up has simply traded their life. If you're flipping to offense, the window is when the enemy collides with your frontline and their feet stop: drop Skill 2 into the pile, then Ultimate, then Skill 1, and you're cooking several people at once. Your Passive grants a burst of speed on every skill hit, so keep the rhythm — hit, move, hit. A Xiao Qiao who never stands still is remarkably hard to catch.

strengths: Skill 1's range and damage let her win the lane poke war one-sidedly
Skill 2's knock-up comes out fast and starts plays on both offense and defense
She accelerates on every skill hit, staying slippery as long as she keeps landing them
Straightforward kit that doubles as an excellent introduction to mage fundamentals
weaknesses: No blink or dash — a targeted stun with no escape tools means death
Skill 1 loses damage each time it passes through a minion, blunting poke through waves
She constantly wrestles with saving Skill 2 for defense versus spending it on offense
