You cannot move or attack while it runs, but an opening burst lands on nothing. Without Savant's Wrath magic power sits at +1142, with 36% magic lifesteal and 22.5% cooldown reduction.

name: Xuance
title: Xuance Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An assassin built entirely around his chain-sickle: hook one target, bind them, and never let go. When the hook lands the kill is nearly scripted; when it misses he has little else.
playstyle: An assassin built entirely around his chain-sickle: hook one target, bind them, and never let go. When the hook lands the kill is nearly scripted; when it misses he has little else.
bestFor: skillshot players ready to stake a fight on one throw — a landed hook hands you the chase and the kill, a miss takes your damage and your mobility with it.

tips.earlyGame: You're the jungler. The moment you hit level 2 off your first buff, start planning the opening gank — Xuance's game is decided by whether he moves one beat faster than the enemy and steals first blood. Everything revolves around Skill 2's hook, and its 50% bonus damage to monsters keeps your clear speed respectable too. One detail worth memorizing: canceling the charge partway refunds 50% of the cooldown. If the angle feels wrong, don't throw it — cancel and rotate to the next bush. The discipline to hold the hook is often worth more than a kill.
tips.midGame: The mid game is about erasing isolated enemies one at a time. Charge Skill 2 from outside their vision (you gain 30% move speed while charging) and release the instant a sightline opens. On hit, reactivate to hurl the target behind you — deliver them straight to your team. While your Ultimate carries you through an enemy you take 50% reduced damage, so diving under towers is safer than it looks. Every kill or assist triggers the Ultimate's passive attack speed and move speed surge, which even speeds up your travel to the next victim.
tips.lateGame: A head-on 5v5 is your worst-case scenario — even full-build Xuance is made of paper. During the standoff before Shadow Tyrant, keep orbiting the perimeter. Your cue is seeing the enemy's stuns get burned on your teammates. Then hook a chipped backliner out of their formation, throw them, and finish with the Ultimate. Xuance's real terror is the chain reaction: one kill stacks the Ultimate's passive and the snowball starts rolling. Focus entirely on taking the first pick safely and the rest falls into place on its own.
tips.teamfight: Never, ever take the job of engaging first. Sit on the edge of the fight with Skill 2 charged, waiting for a lane to open toward their marksman or mage. When the hook lands, pull yourself in with Skill 1 and the empowered basic attack, then reactivate Skill 2 to throw them into your team's kill zone. If you miss, back off immediately and wait out the cooldown. Playing hit and miss as two completely separate game plans — that discipline is what decides Xuance's winrate.

strengths: A self-sufficient pick machine: hook, throw, and follow-up all live in one kit
Kill-and-assist stacking passive makes his snowball terrifyingly fast
50% damage reduction while the Ultimate is in motion keeps dives safe
The charge-cancel cooldown refund lets him attempt hooks again and again
weaknesses: Missing Skill 2 silences both his damage and his mobility at once
Paper-thin base durability; a single stun or hard CC deletes him
Cannot play the frontline role in a head-on teamfight
Hook accuracy takes practice, so results swing wildly before mastery

counteredBy.name: Liu Bang
counteredBy.reason: Liu Bang teleports onto an ally and lands with a stun, cutting in before Xuance can finish the kill.

counteredBy.name: Sima Yi
counteredBy.reason: Sima Yi gains vision of nearby enemies who cast skills, so Xuance is spotted the moment he starts charging.

synergies.name: Liang
synergies.reason: Liang's suppression freezes a target, giving Xuance time to charge Nightmare Hooks and land it cleanly.

synergies.name: Zhuangzi
synergies.reason: Zhuangzi grants crowd control immunity, so Xuance can dive the enemy line and shrug off the stuns that follow.

Doomsday at slot five adds 80–160 plus 7% of the target's extra health to every basic attack, and Pure Sky at the end takes physical defense to 200. Eight Red Moon slots finish the arcana: together with the items, +57.8% attack speed and +24% crit rate.

name: Yang Jian
title: Yang Jian Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A fighter who grows more resistant the longer he brawls, transforming into a towering form that sweeps the frontline. Missing-Health damage plus true damage lets him melt tanks head-on.
playstyle: A fighter who grows more resistant the longer he brawls, transforming into a towering form that sweeps the frontline. Missing-Health damage plus true damage lets him melt tanks head-on.
bestFor: brawlers who plant their feet instead of backing off — resistances climb the longer the fight drags, and the Skill 2 stun runs twice as long while you are the one lower on health.

tips.earlyGame: Yang Jian wants to fight in the Clash Lane before level 4, not after. Skill 2's stun doubles in length when the target's HP percentage is higher than yours, so trading back after eating some damage is where he shines — never fear an even exchange. If a bush looks suspicious, send in Skill 1's War Hound first; five seconds of vision on whatever it touches exposes any ambush before it springs. Once the Ultimate arrives at level 4, its built-in healing transforms your staying power, so start forcing 1v1s and take the lane by the throat.
tips.midGame: When the Tyrant spawns at 4:00, shove your wave before rotating. Landing Skill 1 pre-fight applies the mark and vision, and the recast dash adds missing-HP damage that finishes chases. Against enemy heroes, the Passive shifts into its empowered mode with bonus HP and resistances, which makes small skirmishes Yang Jian's home turf. Around 7-8 minutes, with one core item done, run a loop: pick a 1v1 on the side, and when two enemies collapse, use the hound's vision to back off clean. That XP gap compounds fast.
tips.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, baiting enemies out in a side lane beats standing in the middle of every 5v5. Your 1v1 stays strong even at even items, and when you cannot secure the kill, the Ultimate's healing still lets you hold ground. Always shove a wave before Shadow Tyrant or Overlord starts — every defender the enemy sends is a body missing from the objective fight. Since your resistances stack into crowd control immunity, entering brawls two or three seconds late means less CC (stuns and other lockdown) aimed your way and a much longer rampage.
tips.teamfight: Yang Jian's teamfight is a flank job: circle the edge and delete enemies who are already chipped. The five-second true-damage window after Skill 2 connects is the core of your output, so squeeze in every basic attack you can while the stun holds. The Ultimate's lasers heal more when they strike multiple enemies — the moment you get surrounded is exactly when to fire. One habit worth stealing: hold the Skill 1 recast until the enemy burns their blink, and the dash almost never whiffs. As long as the mark is up, you can always re-chase.

strengths: Skill 2's stun doubles when he is lower on HP, making counter-trades brutal
Passive resistances stack into crowd control immunity, winning long brawls
Ultimate and Passive healing let him hold ground through item deficits
War Hound's vision exposes bush ambushes while he engages
weaknesses: Missing Skill 1 removes his only gap closer until the cooldown returns
Anti-heal items gut the sustain his whole game plan leans on
Fishing for the doubled stun by staying low on HP is a risky gamble
Long-range poke that never lets him close distance leaves him without a play

name: Yango
title: Yango Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A one-of-a-kind puppeteer who fights through his puppet while keeping his real body safe. You manage two positions at once, trading mind games with the enemy's vision.
playstyle: A one-of-a-kind puppeteer who fights through his puppet while keeping his real body safe. You manage two positions at once, trading mind games with the enemy's vision.
bestFor: players who enjoy complexity for its own sake — piloting two positions at once, where losing the puppet stuns your real body for two seconds and knowing when to recall is what practice buys.

tips.earlyGame: Yango's opening minutes are about collecting shards and getting comfortable on the puppet. Shards accrue passively over time, but basic attacks on enemy heroes have a chance to grant extras, so roam between lanes and harass from safe range. Skill 1's puppet doubles as a bush scout, but if it's destroyed, your real body is stunned for 2 seconds and locked out of resummoning for roughly 20 — don't toss it carelessly at enemies with skills still up. Without his puppet, Yango is just a squishy melee hero.
tips.midGame: Once you bank 50 shards, the Passive's hero transformation widens your playbook. The copy matches the original's kit exactly, so the standard play is borrowing an enemy with CC or a dash as your engage tool. Ganks start with Skill 1's puppet launch: the 0.5-second knock-up on hit, whittling through puppet control, then the recall — its purify and shield transfer to your body as you finish with Skill 2's hidden weapons. Keep the real body behind walls and bushes, showing the enemy only the puppet. That habit separates Yango players.
tips.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, the puppet is the perfect decoy. Walk it into the enemy's path before the fight; when they burn skills on it, that's your cue. It takes 100% extra damage and breaks easily, so recall early when threatened and convert the purify and shield into your own engage. For the finish, chain Skill 2's four paper birds into Skill 3's strings, which pull you back out as they land. The 13% of lost Health only applies to a target hit by both strings — land one and it's chip damage, nothing more. Line up the angle before you fire, especially on a target already low. Once your real body is caught, the fight is basically lost, so check your exit before anything else.
tips.teamfight: The rule is simple: the real Yango doesn't fight. Send the puppet in from a flank to pressure their backline, and only move your body once you've confirmed their CC and big cooldowns have gone into the doll. The moment they spend a major skill on the puppet is the only window where you're allowed forward. Start with Skill 1's knock-up, and once a target is pinched between puppet and body — with 50 shards turning that puppet into a copy of an enemy hero — you are effectively more than two attackers. Skill 3's strings can cap a combo or buy your spacing back. When a collapse actually lands on you, the answer is Skill 4: it cleanses every crowd control effect and drops you somewhere else. Hold it for that, and remember it cannot clear the 2-second stun from a destroyed puppet.

strengths: The puppet leads, soaking enemy skills and attention while his body stays hidden
50 shards turn the puppet into a copy of an enemy hero, borrowing their ace card for 10 seconds
Skill 1's knock-up plus the recall's purify and shield cover offense and defense
Skill 3 adds 13% of lost Health when both strings connect, and creates distance as it lands
weaknesses: The puppet takes double damage, and its destruction stuns the real body for 2 seconds
Controlling the puppet leaves the real body exposed to a pincer
Extremely demanding to pilot — below mastery, you get half the hero

name: Yao
title: Yao Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A swordsman who heals on skill hits and unleashes empowered versions at full star power. His signature is the rewind — returning to where he stood two seconds ago, letting him dive deep and walk out untouched.
playstyle: A swordsman who heals on skill hits and unleashes empowered versions at full star power. His signature is the rewind — returning to where he stood two seconds ago, letting him dive deep and walk out untouched.
bestFor: players who treat the way home as part of the technique — Skill 3 only returns you to where you stood two seconds ago, so the dive has to be planned before it starts.

tips.earlyGame: In the jungle, Yao lives on repeated short engagements powered by the Passive, which heals you every time a skill connects. Touch with Skill 2's arcing dash, land Skill 1's full-circle slash, and back off immediately — repeat this loop and your HP bar drains slower than your opponent's. Star Power management is the key detail: your skills are only empowered for 3 seconds at max stacks, so never commit while the buff is down. Unlocking the Ultimate at level 4 lets you delay 40% of incoming damage and snap back to where you stood 2 seconds ago, erasing it — which is when shallow tower dives start to work.
tips.midGame: The mid game is about shoving side waves and winning skirmishes with your in-and-out mobility. From around 6 to 8 minutes, once your first physical core item is finished, combos built around the empowered Skill 2 knock-up start killing squishy targets outright. The single biggest habit on this hero: always track where you stood 2 seconds ago, and step through a safe spot before you commit. As long as your return point is secured, even getting collapsed on by the enemy jungler and support isn't fatal — the Ultimate wipes the delayed damage and carries you out.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Yao is a second-wave diver whose job is touching the enemy backline. Don't burn skills at the start of a teamfight; watch the enemy's targeted crowd control get used on someone else, then enter with Skill 2. Going in at max Star Power lets you pile on pressure with empowered skills and the charging empowered basic attack. Even when you soak heavy damage, returning 2 seconds back with the Ultimate cancels it — but returning into the middle of the enemy team is worthless, so design your entry path as your route home from the start.
tips.teamfight: The ideal teamfight is a cycle: dart in, heal off skill hits, dart out, and do it again. Leave the first engage to your tank, sweep in from a flank with Skill 2 into Skill 1, layer empowered skills, and disengage. One piece of hard crowd control is your death sentence — the delayed Star Split damage collapses on you all at once — so never stop respecting the enemy support's stun. And if you spend the Ultimate aggressively, you lose the safety net for the next burst you eat, so take a breath before every cast.

strengths: Healing on every skill hit wins the war of repeated short trades
Max Star Power spikes hard with empowered skills and the charging basic attack
The Ultimate delays 40% of damage taken and can erase it entirely
Skill 2's mobility gives you the initiative on both chase and escape
weaknesses: Individual skills hit softly, so full combo execution is the price of damage
The Ultimate returns you to a fixed spot from 2 seconds ago — unplanned casts get you killed
Hard crowd control stops the loop and stacked Star Split damage deletes you

name: Yaria
title: Yaria Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A guardian who possesses an ally and becomes their shield — protection in its final form. Her deer transformation cleanses CC on reflex, and her chosen hero simply does not die alone.
playstyle: A guardian who possesses an ally and becomes their shield — protection in its final form. Her deer transformation cleanses CC on reflex, and her chosen hero simply does not die alone.
bestFor: players who never hesitate to be someone else's armor — riding an ally hands them a true-damage shield, and choosing the wrong ally wastes the whole thing.

tips.earlyGame: Start the game standing behind your mid laner or marksman, letting Skill 2's auto-targeting bolts help with the chip damage while you fire Skill 1 into bushes for safety checks. The energy orb homes in and knocks up any hero it detects, so one cast tells you whether an ambush is waiting. Until Yaria learns her Ultimate attach at level 4, she is honestly just a soft target — take river vision only inside your allies' range, because nothing in her kit justifies walking ahead alone.
tips.midGame: From level 4 on, the default play is attaching to your best-fed carry — usually the jungler or the marksman. What you hand them is a shield that negates 1,000 true damage, rising to 1,500 and 2,000 as Skill 3 levels up. Attaching immediately cuts your active skills' cooldowns by 30%. That is a one-time reduction at the moment you attach, not a discount that lasts while you ride. What does last for the whole attachment is 20% more tracking range on Skill 1 and 20% more attack range on Skill 2. The key habit: detach yourself before the shield breaks. A manual detach cuts 50% off Skill 3's cooldown, which beats eating the full downtime every time. Hold the attach in reserve right before the 4-minute Tyrant or any Shadow Tyrant fight after 10 minutes.
tips.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, your one shield decides whether the carry lives. Assassin burst is instant — reacting after the dive starts is usually too late, so climb on as soon as a fight looks likely. Watch the shield's remaining health, hop off just before it shatters to collect the cooldown refund, then climb right back on. The window immediately after you detach is your most dangerous moment; hard CC triggers your Deer form (once per 60 seconds), but it will not save you from the second stun.
tips.teamfight: Stay mounted on your carry, spread Skill 2's sustained damage, and knock up divers with Skill 1 to blunt their momentum. Your Passive Deer form only triggers on hard CC like knock-ups and knock-backs, making you untargetable while slowing everyone nearby — trading it for one wasted enemy engage tool is a clean win. Picking the right host is part of the job, too. Sitting on an ally nobody is attacking wastes the shield, so identify the one player actually being focused and move.

strengths: Her all-damage shield cancels one lethal burst on a carry
Manual detach refunds half the cooldown for high shield uptime
Deer form absorbs hard CC and wastes enemy engage tools
Skill 1 scouts bushes and knocks up in a single cast
weaknesses: Zero solo damage or durability; helpless once her team collapses
Deer form runs once per 60 seconds and loses to chained CC
No healing in her kit; drawn-out poke wars wear her down
Attaching to the wrong host throws the entire shield away

name: Ying
title: Ying Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A spear fighter who banks resonance through skills and spends it on basic attacks, triggering one of three arts depending on the count. Stack management is combo selection.
playstyle: A spear fighter who banks resonance through skills and spends it on basic attacks, triggering one of three arts depending on the count. Stack management is combo selection.
bestFor: players who want stack-counting to become second nature, since the count decides which of the three spear arts a Basic Attack brings out.

tips.earlyGame: Ying lives in the jungle, though she can hold the clash lane in a pinch. Every skill cast banks one Resonance stack and your next basic attack spends them all, so drill the skill-into-basic-attack rhythm on camps from your very first clear — the one-stack sweep is what keeps your clear speed honest. Once you hit level 4 and unlock your Ultimate, start showing up to river 2v2s: layering its knock-up with Skill 1 lets you flip counter-ganks even at a numbers disadvantage. Just keep deep invades to a minimum before your stacks are flowing, because she is easy to shut down early.
tips.midGame: Skirmishes around the Tyrant (the buffed boss that spawns at 4:00) are where Ying spikes. Finish one attack speed item and her resonance skills come out noticeably faster — attack speed feeds their animation at a 50% ratio — so your hit count climbs in a hurry. Approach from a side bush with Skill 2's charged dash, pop enemies up with Skill 1, then weave in a basic attack: the two-stack rapid thrusts chunk hard. Every resonance proc also refunds 1.5 seconds on Skill 1 and Skill 2, which is exactly why the longer a fight drags on, the faster she spins.
tips.lateGame: Past the 10-minute mark, fights hinge on when you commit Skill 3. Crowd control immunity runs for the whole cast and damage taken drops by 30% at rank 1, so the ideal pattern is to watch one key piece of enemy CC (crowd control) get spent, then dive in with the back-and-forth knock-ups. Cycling all three skills builds three stacks, and your next basic attack becomes Zenith - Wildfire: she leaps into the air, ignores terrain, and unleashes a sweeping strike across a wide area — exactly what you want against enemies who back off. Her actual durability is only fighter-average; do not chase deep while Skill 3 is down.
tips.teamfight: Resist the urge to lead the charge — stacking Skill 3 on top of an ally's engage is far more reliable. Knock the clump around with the back-and-forth passes, fire the second phase, Roaring Sun, and fight on top of the burn zone it leaves behind. From there, keep the loop simple: one skill, one basic attack, over and over, so the resonance sweeps and cooldown refunds never stop. Against runners, build three stacks first and release Zenith - Wildfire — she ignores terrain on the approach and unleashes a wide sweeping strike. One habit that pays off: aim the second-phase sweep at the spot where knocked-up enemies will land — it almost never misses.

strengths: Resonance cooldown refunds make her output snowball the longer a fight runs
Multiple knock-ups from Skill 1 and the Ultimate dominate skirmishes and brawls
Crowd control immunity plus 30% damage reduction on the Ultimate makes her hard to stop
Attack speed also accelerates resonance skills, so her items never go to waste
weaknesses: Demands constant skill-and-basic-attack weaving; the execution bar is high
Burst lags behind true assassins, letting targets slip away half-dead
Her teamfight presence drops sharply while the Ultimate is on cooldown
Only average durability — getting chain-CC'd before stacking up is lethal

counteredBy.reason: Lady Sun keeps shaving time off Rolling Raid with every Basic Attack, so Ying struggles to close the gap.

name: Yixing
title: Yixing Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A mage who plays the fight like a board game — placing stones, drawing a board that traps enemies inside, pulling them toward the center. He builds inescapable positions, one move at a time.
playstyle: A mage who plays the fight like a board game — placing stones, drawing a board that traps enemies inside, pulling them toward the center. He builds inescapable positions, one move at a time.
bestFor: players who lay groundwork one move at a time — stones first, then a formation that drags enemies inward, then a board they cannot leave for four seconds.

tips.earlyGame: Yixing is a mid-lane setup mage who builds a board across the battlefield. Take Skill 2 at level 1 — it deals 180% bonus damage to non-heroes, so dropping the formation on a wave finishes your minion clear by itself. That clear speed is your early edge: it frees you to show at the river, and spare Skill 1 stones tossed into enemy jungle bushes buy 3 seconds of vision. Your durability is paper, but the Passive negates fatal damage for 1 second as a once-per-150-seconds insurance policy — if you get ganked, don't panic; use its speed boost and walk out.
tips.midGame: This is where formation play separates good Yixing players from great ones. Skill 2 drags enemies near its center and slides any Skill 1 stones inside the area toward the middle for multi-hits, so burn the order into your hands: stones first, formation on top. Marks from skill hits and accumulated stones grow your magic attack for the entire game, which means from 6 to 10 minutes, every skill you land is literally banking late-game damage. The narrow river paths before Tyrant are the formation's best terrain — whoever lays their board first owns the fight.
tips.lateGame: Past 10 minutes, the clumped fights over Shadow Tyrant and Overlord are your Ultimate's showcase. It has a 1.5-second formation delay, so overlap it on moments the enemy cannot back away — mid-attack on an objective, or right after allied CC lands. Trapped enemies can't leave the board for 4 seconds while marks stack on them automatically. The smaller you draw the board, the shorter its cooldown (up to 25% off), so cycling quick, small boards that lock down just two enemies is a genuinely strong late-game pattern.
tips.teamfight: Anchor yourself in the backline and start laying Skill 1 stones along the enemy's approach path. The instant they push in, drop the Skill 2 formation on top — the pull plus stone multi-hits shreds their shape. If you smell a dive coming, drawing a small Ultimate around your own feet is a defensive play you'll use constantly in real matches. Blink users tend to escape during the 1.5-second windup, so don't burn the Ultimate on a single target — hold it until the enemy is clumped with nowhere to retreat. That's the win condition.

strengths: The Ultimate's inescapable board is a lockdown no other hero can replicate
Stone accumulation grows his magic attack automatically across the whole game
Skill 2's 180% bonus damage to non-heroes makes wave clear effortless
The Passive's 1-second fatal-damage negation insures against burst deaths
weaknesses: Low instant burst; his damage needs setup time before it comes online
The Ultimate's 1.5-second formation delay lets blink users walk out
No regular mobility skill, making him a favorite assassin target
The stones-then-formation sequencing takes real practice to master

name: Yuhuan
title: Yuhuan Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A musician mage who switches between an offensive and a healing stance, capped by an untargetable ultimate that both dodges the enemy's aim and restores her team.
playstyle: A musician mage who switches between an offensive and a healing stance, capped by an untargetable ultimate that both dodges the enemy's aim and restores her team.
bestFor: players who want to decide the split between damage and healing themselves, switching between the War and Peace stances as the fight turns.

tips.earlyGame: Mid lane Yuhuan starts with learning the Passive toggle. Clear waves in the damage stance for the bonus minion damage, and flip to the healing stance the moment you take poke — that one habit alone transforms her lane sustain. Skill 1's notes home in on enemies, and deal bonus damage to minions, so the pre-level-4 gameplan is simply notes, empowered hit, repeat. Even when the enemy jungler collapses on you, Skill 2's speed boost and delayed stun turn the gank around — she can push the lane far more confidently than she looks.
tips.midGame: From level 4, everything hinges on one decision: is the Ultimate for healing, or for dodging? While performing, Yuhuan is untargetable and cleansed of CC, so timing it against enemy burst makes their biggest cooldowns hit air. Wait until you see the enemy assassin's ult animation before you rise — wasting their entire combo never stops feeling great. At Tyrant and Overlord fights, your job is holding the line: patch up chipped teammates with the healing stance and the post-performance area heal. From around eight minutes, your second magic item brings real poke damage online too.
tips.lateGame: After ten minutes, Yuhuan plays the unkillable back-liner. You don't have the burst to delete anyone, so during Shadow Tyrant standoffs, chip away with the homing notes and answer dives with Skill 2 first, Ultimate second. Simply having the Ultimate available is deterrence — enemy assassins hesitate to jump a target who can vanish mid-combo. When your front line runs low, stabilize them with the healing stance and the area heal, and drag the fight into the long, grinding version that favors you. The only way Yuhuan loses is panicking and stepping forward at the wrong moment.
tips.teamfight: Your teamfight spot is half a step behind the front line. Once it starts, flip to the damage stance for the bonus area damage and keep cycling Skill 1's notes into empowered basic attacks. When a diver turns onto you, drop Skill 2's soundwave, speed away, and let the stun land 1.5 seconds later as they chase — lockdown over your shoulder. If burst stacks onto you, rise with the Ultimate: the enemy wastes their damage, then eats your area heal on the way down. Leave the kills to your teammates; your job is making the enemy's math stop working, over and over.

strengths: Passive toggle covers damage and healing in a single kit
Ultimate's untargetability and cleanse make enemy burst whiff
Empowered basic attacks refund cooldowns for relentless uptime
Area healing sustains her team through long teamfights
weaknesses: Low burst damage — she rarely finishes kills alone
Skill 2's stun lags 1.5 seconds behind and isn't guaranteed
Thin self-defense against dives while the Ultimate is down
Can't carry alone; her impact depends on allied damage

builds.notes: The first buy is Crimson Shadow - Radiance at 2080G, a roam-only item carrying 1200 HP that also feeds gold to whichever ally has the least. Max HP stops at +2000 against build 1's +5112, so Yang Guifei picks her fights from further back.

name: Zhang Fei
title: Zhang Fei Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A guardian with a monster inside: he hands out shields until his ultimate transforms him into a roaring demon that scatters the enemy team. The shift from protector to terror is theatrical.
playstyle: A guardian with a monster inside: he hands out shields until his ultimate transforms him into a roaring demon that scatters the enemy team. The shift from protector to terror is theatrical.
bestFor: playing two roles in one game. Hand out shields, bank Madness, then turn into the thing that scatters the enemy team across the map.

tips.earlyGame: The lane opens with you swinging basic attacks next to your marksman. It looks menial, but every pre-transformation swing adds 3 Madness, and how fast you fill that bar is quite literally how strong you are. Skill 2's landing shield covers multiple allies at once, and it pays 3 Madness for the cast plus 1 more for every ally it shields — so time it for the instant a teammate is about to eat damage. In trades, cut off enemy chases with Skill 1's knockback; landing it on an enemy unit is another 3 Madness. Bank a full Madness bar before the Tyrant spawns at four minutes and the transformation is ready for the first skirmish.
tips.midGame: Whether your Ultimate is available defines mid game Zhang Fei — with it up, he's a different hero. The roar carries 1.25 seconds of invincibility and crowd control immunity, so its strongest use is a head-on counter to enemy engages. Enemies caught at the far edge of the storm are stunned for 1.5 seconds, which means the clean blast comes from half a step back rather than point-blank. Around Tyrant and Overlord, sit on the transformation and answer whoever moves first. While transformed, your basic attacks carry bonus damage, so you can moonlight as a damage threat too.
tips.lateGame: In teamfights after ten minutes, Zhang Fei's reason to exist is entering the fight holding a shield worth 40% of his max HP. During Shadow Tyrant standoffs, stand one step forward so the enemy initiation lands on you, absorb it, then answer with the roar. Just manage the knock-away direction carefully — launching the enemy carry toward your team is game-winning, while launching them to safety makes you the villain instantly. Remember that Skill 1 auto-casts when the transformation ends, so you can factor that final knockback into your closing sequence.
tips.teamfight: Zhang Fei's teamfight is a checklist. Pre-shield your team with Skill 2, answer the enemy's dive with the roar, split their formation with the storm — and only then start swinging. The 1.25 seconds of invincibility exists to make enemy ultimates whiff, so firing it early with nothing to counter is a waste. Watch for the enemy ult animation, then blow them away, and the battlefield goes quiet in an instant. While transformed, every skill you cast also slows nearby enemies, so you can even run down the stragglers yourself.

strengths: A 40% max HP shield and an invincible roar create massive comeback power
Skill 2 shields multiple allies with a single leap
The storm's knock-away and edge stun wreck enemy formations
Bonus damage and constant slows while transformed make him a real threat
weaknesses: Low damage and only a knockback for CC until Madness is charged
A misdirected blast saves enemies and betrays your team's follow-up
Mobility depends entirely on Skill 2's leap, limiting self-defense
No ranged tools — he spectates during poke wars

Dawnlight, Frigid Charge and Sage's Sanctuary follow, putting both physical defense (+683) and cooldown reduction (43.5%) ahead of build 1. Frigid Charge's ice field slows enemies by 30-60% and freezes them for 0.75 seconds, on a 75-second cooldown. Sage's Sanctuary revives Zhang Fei on the spot 2 seconds after death with 2000-3000 HP, twice per match, so he keeps showing up for the next fight.

name: Zhou Yu
title: Zhou Yu Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: An area-denial mage who pre-burns the ground enemies want to stand on, stacking ignition marks until they catch fire. He wins not by aiming at enemies but by removing their real estate.
playstyle: An area-denial mage who pre-burns the ground enemies want to stand on, stacking ignition marks until they catch fire. He wins not by aiming at enemies but by removing their real estate.
bestFor: players who shape the ground before the fight reaches it — burn the lanes enemies need, heal while standing in your own fire, and take the corridors early, since only a burn-fed ultimate stuns.

tips.earlyGame: Zhou Yu's lane is a placement puzzle for Skill 2's fire arrows. They restock every 9 seconds up to three, and each burn zone lasts 6.5 seconds, so budget one for the wave and one for pressure. The core habit is placing flames where the enemy wants to retreat, shrinking their playable space. You heal while standing in your own fire thanks to the Passive, so trading on top of your flames is a fight you're happy to take. Your Ultimate only stuns when it passes through a burn zone, so even past level 4, everything starts with Skill 2.
tips.midGame: The 4-minute Tyrant kicks off Zhou Yu's setup game. Thirty seconds before it spawns, push mid and reach the pit first, laying two arrows across the entrance. The enemy detouring around your flames is zoning working exactly as intended. When the fight starts, spread the burn with Skill 1's wind field, knock their formation loose, then send the Ultimate through the widened flames for a multi-man stun. The Passive's 4-stack ignition ticks hard too — in tight corridors, enemies sometimes sit at half HP off placement alone.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Zhou Yu wins fights before they start. Carpet the approach to Overlord or Shadow Tyrant with burn zones: your team gets the wind field's speed while the enemy is forced through flames and slows. With items done, overlapped flames in a narrow path melt even tanks off pure damage over time. The weakness is self-defense — no dash means a read on your position is a death sentence. Stay behind your team, always within reach of your own fire, and keep shooting.
tips.teamfight: Run the same teamfight script until it's muscle memory. Open with two Skill 2 arrows layered between the teams, push the flames enemy-ward with Skill 1's wind and knockback, then fire the Ultimate through the extended flame line for a clustered 1-second AoE stun. From there, keep feeding restocked arrows onto their escape paths and backline — the enemy is forever choosing between burning and backing off. New and old burn zones stack their damage, so deliberately doubling them on one spot builds a genuinely lethal firepit — a veteran's move.

strengths: Overlapped burn zones melt even tanks with sustained damage in narrow terrain
Ultimate through flames becomes an AoE 1-second stun — real CC on a zone mage
Heals while standing in his own fire, making him stubborn on claimed ground
Skill 1's knockback doubles as self-peel and engage-breaking
weaknesses: Setup takes steps, so he reacts poorly to sudden skirmishes and flanks
The Ultimate only stuns through a burn zone — on its own it stops no one
No mobility skill; once his position is read and dived, there's no answer

Totals land at +1172 magic attack, 110 above build 1, with max HP 400 lower at +1500.

name: Zhuangzi
title: Zhuangzi Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The complete answer to crowd control: he cleanses himself every six seconds and his ultimate purges the whole team. Enemy engage plans dissolve into paper against him.
playstyle: The complete answer to crowd control: he cleanses himself every six seconds and his ultimate purges the whole team. Enemy engage plans dissolve into paper against him.
bestFor: players who find beauty in cancellation rather than damage — he shrugs off his own crowd control every six seconds and frees the team with the ultimate, so the job is waiting for the enemy to commit.

tips.earlyGame: Zhuangzi's default assignment is glued to his marksman. In lane, your job is landing Skill 1's butterflies on the enemy — the slow scales up to 60%, and every second of it is free damage for your carry. Your Passive cleanses your own CC every six seconds, which is exactly why you can afford to stand one step further forward than most supports and menace the enemy laners. Skill 2 even auto-casts every seven seconds, so simply being near enemies keeps feeding speed stacks to your allies at zero cost. Before the 4:00 Tyrant spawns, face-check the river brush yourself so your jungler starts it safely.
tips.midGame: Mid-game Zhuangzi is judged on one thing: when, and for whom, the Ultimate comes out. Cleanse plus 1.5 seconds of crowd control immunity plus a shield can void an entire enemy engage — but cast it early and they'll simply hold their skills and wait it out. The rule is to react: the moment enemy stuns or knock-ups land on your carry, layer it on top. Once your HP items finish around 7-8 minutes, work the frontline of objective standoffs with butterfly slows, and quietly count the enemy's CC. Deciding in advance where your Ultimate goes wins teamfights before they start.
tips.lateGame: The deeper the game goes, the heavier Zhuangzi's power to undo things becomes. Fights past ten minutes are decided by a single landed CC chain, and the ability to erase one wholesale makes your Ultimate a second life for the entire team. In the standoffs before Overlord, stay welded to your carry at reaction distance from any enemy engage. Skill 1 does double duty — closing the net on runners or buying seconds for a retreating ally. There's no highlight reel here, but the moment the enemy engage hero hesitates because Zhuangzi is standing there, you're already halfway to winning.
tips.teamfight: Position half a step in front of your carry. When enemy CC comes in, erase it with the Ultimate, then flip the fight with the butterfly slow. On the timing: let it land first. The 1.5 seconds of crowd control immunity whiffs when cast on prediction, so watching the enemy's key skill actually connect before you answer is the higher-percentage play. Your own Passive cleanse means you can tank a few skills yourself — baiting the enemy into wasting CC on you is legitimate work. And the longer the brawl runs, the more Skill 2's stacking damage and speed support quietly tilts it your way.

strengths: The Ultimate's area cleanse and crowd control immunity turn enemy engages into whiffs
His Passive periodically cleanses his own CC, hard-countering lockdown comps
Skill 1's 30% slow for 2s serves both the chase and the rescue
Periodic healing and damage reduction keep him working the frontline for ages
weaknesses: No hard CC of his own — he almost never creates kills singlehandedly
Only a shield stands between his team and raw burst, so heavy dive can power through
Against low-CC enemy comps, the Ultimate's value drops off a cliff

synergies.reason: Lady Sun only speeds up when she rolls beside an enemy, while Zhuangzi's marks keep her quick everywhere else.

Dawnlight third adds 10% cooldown reduction, taking the build to 16%. Damaging an enemy hero puts out a shield of 250-500 plus 4% of max HP on Zhuangzi and the lowest-health ally nearby, once every 10 seconds. Blazing Cape slips to slot five, so the 35% anti-heal arrives 4,060 gold later than in build one.

name: Zilong
title: Zilong Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: A fighter who gets tankier as his Health drops, hitting his stride exactly when he looks finished. His dash and healing spear flurry let him win fights the enemy thought were already over.
playstyle: A fighter who gets tankier as his Health drops, hitting his stride exactly when he looks finished. His dash and healing spear flurry let him win fights the enemy thought were already over.
bestFor: players who live on a broken health bar — Zilong hardens as he drops, so the craft is judging how deep you can go and healing back out with the spear flurry.

tips.earlyGame: Zilong lives in the jungle. Max Skill 2 first — the healing on the five-thrust combo keeps your clear healthy — and grab both buffs on the way to level 4. Keep his Passive in mind while you farm: each time your HP drops past 70% and then 40%, your damage reduction steps up and Skill 1 gets a charge refunded, which means a wounded Zilong is a stronger Zilong. The catch is that none of that protects you at full HP, so don't pick a coin-flip fight during a level-1 invade. Whatever else happens, walk into the 4:00 Tyrant fight with your Ultimate available.
tips.midGame: From level 4, Skill 3 is your gank button. If it doesn't hit an enemy hero, half the cooldown comes back — so stop treating it as precious and throw it with conviction. What the leap itself applies is the induction mark, nothing more. The knock-up only happens when another skill connects on a marked target within 5s, and only enemies standing at the center of the area get launched. So chain fast after you land: Skill 2's five thrusts, then the Skill 1 dash, cashing in the bonus magic damage on every connect. Around seven minutes, with your first core item done, Zilong is one of the nastiest duelists on the map; he genuinely wins fights that start at half HP. Welcome the scrap. Being damaged is your Passive working as intended.
tips.lateGame: Unless he gets bursted first, late-game Zilong is the last man standing in every teamfight. The 20% damage reduction, Skill 2 healing, and overheal-to-shield conversion all stack up, and every second a brawl drags on tilts it further his way. At Shadow Tyrant and Overlord fights past ten minutes, don't be the first one in — go second, and leap onto the backline with your Ultimate after the enemy has dumped CC on your frontline. From the enemy's perspective, the worst part of fighting Zilong is watching him heal back up mid-fight with Skill 2. The one real counter is anti-heal: respect anyone who built it.
tips.teamfight: Play the late pick. Let your team take the opening exchange, watch the enemy burn their stuns and knock-ups, then use Skill 3 on the softest target you can reach. The leap applies the induction mark and nothing else. Everything after that comes from what you land inside the next 5 seconds — Skill 2's five thrusts and the Skill 1 dash each cash in bonus magic damage, and a connecting skill launches whoever is standing at the center of the area for a second. That's the reason to jump at the side where their backline is stacked. If your HP crosses a Passive threshold mid-fight, the refunded Skill 1 charge is your exit ticket or your chase tool, whichever the moment demands. Zilong is at his best in the red — just don't get cocky into a team stacking anti-heal.

strengths: Damage reduction scales up as his HP drops, making him monstrously hard to finish off
The Ultimate refunds half its cooldown on a miss, so ganks can be thrown freely
Skill 2 healing plus overheal-to-shield conversion wins extended trades
The shock effect's bonus magic damage keeps him relevant against armor stackers
weaknesses: Thin defenses at full HP leave him vulnerable to opening burst
As a melee physical fighter, slows and stuns that deny his approach shut him down
Anti-heal items strip away most of what makes him durable

Blood Rage adds physical damage equal to 1.5% of bonus HP on every basic attack, and that bonus grows another 25-50% once Zhao Yun drops below half HP. For three seconds after a skill lands on an enemy hero, incoming damage drops 20%, and the active cuts another 30% for three seconds. Succubus Cloak adds 300 magic defense plus a shield every 15 seconds, lifting total magic defense to +400.

name: Ziya
title: Ziya Build Guide: Items, Combos & Counters - Honor of Kings (HoK)
description: The mage whose level cap extends to 25 — growth itself is his identity. He fights with seals and shockwaves, and by the late game his raw stats leave other mages behind.
playstyle: The mage whose level cap extends to 25 — growth itself is his identity. He fights with seals and shockwaves, and by the late game his raw stats leave other mages behind.
bestFor: the long game. Survive a rough start, spike after 15, and own the single biggest call in the match: which ally gets Sanctification.

tips.earlyGame: Ziya holds the mid lane, and until level 15 the job description reads: survive and soak experience. Place Skill 1 where the wave and the enemy overlap and it handles clearing, harass, and defense shred in one cast. Your Passive drops EXP balls from kills you've damaged, so pick them up religiously to build a level lead. With no blink, never leave tower range while the enemy jungler is dark. Skill 2's knock-up is your self-defense — waste it on offense and the bill arrives with the next gank.
tips.midGame: Level 15 — roughly the 10-minute mark — is Ziya's turning point. Reaching it lifts your level cap to 25 on its own, and every level after that adds 20 magical attack. The same moment grants Sanctify, a one-time skill you aim at a teammate, never at yourself. Whoever you pick gains 1,200 EXP, breaks through their own level cap, and has a chance at EXP orbs; from the roam slot they also collect an extra Sanctification effect matched to their class. Hand it to the carry whose next level changes the most. Skill 3 shifts at level 15 as well, but only on a roll — 20% to enter the Sanctifier state, climbing 20% per level, which works out to every cast from level 19. Only in that state can you fire a shockwave while moving, charging up to 2s to stretch the range out to 1,800. Step up in Shadow Tyrant standoffs when the state procs, and settle for the standard three-shockwave cast when it doesn't. Shockwaves pass just 10% damage to towers and crystals, so leave the siege to your teammates.
tips.lateGame: Late-game Ziya stands behind the backline — the deepest position on the map. Past level 20, your magic attack ranks among the game's highest, and two charged Ultimates connecting is enough to halve an enemy formation. Before Overlord, start seeding the chokepoints with Skill 1 thirty seconds ahead of the spawn to strip defense and speed until the fight favors you. Track the enemy assassin at all times, and when they're missing, hold the charge. If you get touched mid-channel, the lost fight is mostly on you.
tips.teamfight: Seventy percent of Ziya's teamfight happens before the fight. Skill 1 walls off approach paths, and Skill 2 goes down early on the spot where their diver will land — press it before they jump, because pressing it after never connects. That's the field lesson worth remembering. Once the brawl starts, thread charged Ultimates in from maximum range and drive the lowest-HP enemies out of the fight one by one. While your blessed teammate rampages up front, you conduct the battle from beyond anyone's reach.

strengths: Sanctification is a one-of-a-kind buff that raises an ally's level cap
1800-range charged Ultimate enables safe poke and siege from another zip code
Skill 1's slow and defense shred dominates pre-objective standoffs
Passive EXP balls make building a level lead easy
weaknesses: No blink — self-defense rests entirely on predicting with Skill 2
Charging the Ultimate leaves him wide open, a gift for assassins
Power spikes at level 15, so falling behind early is hard to repair
Misusing the Sanctification target or timing halves his late game

builds.notes: Boots of the Arcane open at 700G, putting 60-120 magic defense penetration on the board with the very first purchase. Venomous Staff lands third and cuts an enemy's HP recovery and lifesteal by 35% for 2.5 seconds on hit. Void Staff sits fifth here, so its 45% penetration is live at 8,960G, 2,140G earlier than in build 2. Venomous Staff also carries the totals to 37.5% cooldown reduction and +17.5% movement speed, both 7.5 points above build 2.

builds.name: Build 2
builds.title: Percent chip early, 45% pierce last
builds.condition: When the enemy fields high-HP frontliners and your chip damage has to land early
builds.notes: Boots of Deftness come first at 700G for +70 movement speed, plus another 35-70 after five seconds out of combat. Mask of Agony moves up to third, so its 3% current-HP hit, four times over three seconds, is online at 4,880G. That is 2,040G earlier than in build 1, and the trade is Void Staff: its 45% magic defense penetration waits until 11,100G. Savant's Wrath lands fifth and raises magic power by 30%, stacked on top of the +902 total.
